这本书献给约翰——我的弟弟，

我的挚友，也是我非常敬佩的人。兄弟，我爱你。

This book is dedicated to John—my little brother,

a big friend, and a guy I admire greatly. I love ya, man.

前言
 

距离我撰写《健身游泳》第一版已经十年了。我对这本书的成果非常满意。就在我写下这些文字的时候，第一版英文版的第三版也即将售罄。它已被翻译成西班牙语、法语、中文和土耳其语，并已出版发行。大学教师已将《健身游泳》选为多门游泳和教练课程的教材。游泳教练们也围绕书中阐述的技巧和训练原则设计了训练计划。最令人欣慰的是，自本书初版发行以来，我收到了数百位读者的来信。我衷心感谢每一位抽出时间告诉我他们喜欢这本书的哪些方面，更重要的是，如果将来有机会出版第二版，他们希望看到哪些改进或补充。

It has been 10 years since I wrote the original Fitness Swimming. I’ve been quite pleased with the results of that endeavor. As I write this, that first edition is selling out the last bits of its third English-language printing. It has been translated into, and has been published in, Spanish, French, Chinese, and Turkish. College instructors have adopted Fitness Swimming as a textbook for a number of swimming and coaching courses. Swim coaches have built programs around the techniques and training principles espoused therein. Most satisfying of all, I’ve heard from hundreds of readers since the book’s original release. I am indebted to everyone who has taken the time to tell me what they liked about the book and, more to the point, what they’d like to see changed or added if a second edition were ever considered.

游泳教练这个职业还处于起步阶段。武术大师们历经一万余年的发展，才逐渐完善了他们的技艺。相比之下， “游泳”和“教练”这两个词同时出现不过短短几十年，简直是沧海一粟。培养高效游泳运动员的方法也在飞速发展。在我执教成人游泳的25年里，我一直坚持一个原则：如果五年后我回首往事，发现自己还在用同样的方式教授同样的东西，那就该考虑换个工作了。目前为止，一切进展顺利。

The profession of coaching swimming is in its infancy. Martial arts masters have evolved their discipline over 10,000 years or so. The handful of decades in which the words swimming and coach have been uttered in close succession are a comparative blink of an eye. Methods of producing highly effective swimmers are evolving rapidly. Throughout the 25 years I’ve coached adults, I have maintained that if at any point I were to look back 5 years and realize that I was still teaching the same things in the same way, it would be time to find another line of work. So far, so good.

然而，这种说法让原版《健身游泳》陷入了某种困境。要知道，自从第一版出版以来，我书页上的文字一直公开且一成不变，而我实际教授给运动员的内容和教学方法却一直在变化。因此，十年之后，《健身游泳》亟需升级。在接下来的篇章中，您将看到我对游泳原理的最新理解，以及如何才能最好地提高您的游泳水平。虽然原版《健身游泳》的基本概念保持不变，但我表达和应用这些概念的方式已经发生了变化——在某些情况下，变化幅度相当大。我扩展了许多技术和训练主题的讨论，增加了一些新的练习，并收录了60个新的练习——所有这些都是为了帮助您尽可能高效地游泳，提高体能，并享受游泳的乐趣。保持活力，智慧游泳。

That statement, however, paints the original Fitness Swimming into a bit of a corner. You see, from the moment the first edition was published, my words on the page have remained both public and static, while what I teach my real-life athletes and how I teach it to them have changed. So, after a decade, a Fitness Swimming upgrade is due. In the following pages, you will find my current understanding of how swimming works—and of how best to improve your swimming. While the basic concepts in the original Fitness Swimming are the same, the way I express and apply them has changed—by a great deal, in some cases. I’ve expanded my discussions of many technique and training topics, added a number of new drills, and included 60 new practices—all to help you swim as effectively as possible, improve your conditioning, and enjoy the journey. Stay wet and swim smart.

致谢
 

游泳既是一项个人运动，也是一项团队运动。一支队伍的成功取决于每位游泳运动员的发挥。而这些运动员又依赖于团队——包括游泳运动员、教练、管理人员以及其他人员——为他们提供训练、场地、指导、激励、启发以及其他一切有助于他们备战和发挥最佳水平的资源。教练的工作也并非孤立进行。在此，我要感谢并感谢以下各位（排名不分先后），感谢他们一路以来（迄今为止）给予我的帮助、支持和启发：

Swimming is both an individual sport and a team sport. A team’s success depends on the performances of its individual swimmers. Those swimmers, in turn, rely on the team—i.e., swimmers, coaches, managers, and others—for training, facilities, instruction, motivation, inspiration, and everything else that helps them prepare for, and rise to, the competitive occasion. Neither do coaches work in a vacuum. I thank and acknowledge the following people in no discernable order, each of whom has helped, supported, or inspired me along the way (so far):

比尔·布默教练，他特立独行，却又无私地允许他人追随他，并时不时地向他学习；迈克·柯林斯教练，他始终激励着我，是我的榜样；菲尔·汉塞尔教练，他让我有机会在他身边学习；乔尔·布鲁姆博士，他激励我投身教育事业；克莱·埃文斯教练，他向我展示了如何将大师级教练工作发展成一项职业；马克斯·泽勒教练，他帮助将人才培养的艺术传播到世界各地；迪克·鲍尔教练，他提出了巡航间歇的概念；特里·劳克林教练，他让一切都变得清晰易懂；肯·福斯特博士，他既是我的朋友，也是我的合作伙伴；斯科特·拉巴莱斯教练，他给予了我鼓励、友谊和榜样；格伦·米尔斯教练，他提供了前沿的教学方法和视频影像；理查德·奎克教练，他通过技术不断突破运动表现的极限；作家菲尔·惠顿，他给予了我友谊和启发；宇航员斯科特·帕拉津斯基博士，他帮助我在微重力环境下验证了我的一些游泳理论。

Coach Bill Boomer, who goes his own way and who unselfishly allows others to follow him and to look over his shoulder from time to time; Coach Mike Collins, who is a constant inspiration and role model; Coach Phil Hansel, who let me hang around and learn from him; Dr. Joel Bloom, for inspiring me to make a career of teaching; Coach Clay Evans, for demonstrating how to turn Masters coaching into a profession; Coach Max Zeller, for helping to spread the art of talent development around the world; Coach Dick Bower, for the cruise interval concept; Coach Terry Laughlin, who makes it all make sense; Dr. Ken Forster, for being a friend and co-conspirator; Coach Scott Rabalais, for his kind words, friendship, and example; Coach Glenn Mills, for his cutting-edge instruction and video imagery; Coach Richard Quick, for pushing the performance envelope through technique; author Phil Whitten, for his friendship and inspiration; astronaut Dr. Scott Parazynski, for testing some of my swimming theories in microgravity.

我尤其要感谢 H 2 Ouston Swims 的游泳运动员们，感谢他们激励了我，感谢他们信任我，让我把他们当作小白鼠，感谢他们乐于接受新想法。

I must especially acknowledge the swimmers of H2Ouston Swims for motivating me, for trusting me to use them as guinea pigs, and for being receptive to new ideas.

我的妻子、孩子和父母应该受到热烈的公开表扬，因为他们一直很有耐心，并且在我努力拯救世界（或者至少是拯救游泳世界）的时候一直容忍我。

My wife, children, and parents are due loud and public acclaim for being patient and for continuing to put up with me while I try to save the world (or at least the swimming part of it).

第一部分
 
准备游泳
 

游泳是最受欢迎的健身活动之一。它不仅能带来愉悦的体验，还能展现身体的流畅性和优雅，以及力量、速度和耐力。游泳可以锻炼心肺系统，增强体质，塑造强健体魄。因此，它是提升和保持终身健康体魄的绝佳方式。

Swimming is one of the most popular of all fitness activities. It can be pleasurable, allowing for the physical expression of fluidity and grace as well as of power, speed, and stamina. Swimming conditions the cardiorespiratory system and it tones and strengthens the body. As such, it can be an excellent tool for improving and maintaining lifelong fitness.

然而，如果游泳姿势不正确，就会变成一场令人精疲力竭、痛苦不堪的挣扎，仿佛快要溺水一般。据估计，在美国自称游泳者的人中，只有不到百分之二的人能够一口气游完500码以上。限制大多数游泳者的并非体能，而是游泳技巧。他们的游泳技巧导致能量消耗过大，很快就会感到疲惫，在获得任何有氧运动益处之前就不得不停止。对这些人来说，游泳与其说是一种健身方式，不如说是一种生存技能。

Improperly done, though, swimming can be an exhausting and excruciating struggle that makes you feel like you are almost drowning. It is estimated that fewer than two percent of Americans who call themselves swimmers are able to swim more than 500 yards without stopping. It is technique, not physical conditioning, that limits most swimmers. Their technique causes them to waste so much energy that they fatigue quickly and must stop long before they receive any aerobic benefit. For these people, swimming is more of a survival skill than a fitness tool.

或许你能长时间游泳，但仍有提升空间。或许你游泳是为了健身，或是为了备战铁人三项或大师赛，又或许只是享受在水中的乐趣。无论如何，你很可能羡慕那些游得更快、效率更高，或者看起来更像专业游泳运动员的人。

Perhaps you can swim for extended periods but you still have room for improvement. Perhaps you currently swim for fitness, or to train for a triathlon or for Masters competition, or perhaps just for the pleasure of being in the water. Regardless, chances are that you envy certain swimmers who are faster, more efficient, or simply look more like real swimmers.

游泳是一项对技巧要求较高的运动。在这方面，它更像高尔夫，而不是跑步或骑自行车。和高尔夫一样，几乎任何人只要愿意投入足够的时间和精力练习，就能学会并保持流畅优美的游泳技巧。这样的练习带来的健身益处是巨大的。很少有其他运动能像游泳一样，提供如此全面的全身锻炼，而且人们即使到了远超其他运动年龄的年纪，也能全身心地投入其中。

Swimming is a technique-limited sport. It is more like golf in this respect than running or cycling. As with golf, almost anyone who is willing to spend enough time and effort practicing can learn and maintain the skills necessary for fluid, graceful swimming. The fitness payoff for such practice can be enormous. Few other activities offer a full-body workout that people can fully participate in even when they are well beyond the age at which participation in other sports is unthinkable.

然而，很少有游泳者能在不遵循教练、指导员、观看视频、阅读书籍或结合多种方式的指导下，达到流畅优美的游泳水平。我希望这本书能成为一份路线图，帮助你开启或保持与水之间终身愉悦且有益的关系。

Few swimmers, however, reach the fluid, graceful stage without following the plan of a coach, an instructor, a video, a book, or a combination thereof. My hope is that this book will serve as a kind of road map that will start or keep you on course to a lifelong, pleasurable, and beneficial relationship with the water.

前三章的内容为您的训练奠定了基础。第一章将游泳介绍为一项终身运动，并阐述养成游泳习惯的益处。第二章帮助您选择适合自身需求的游泳装备，并提供寻找最佳游泳场所的建议。第三章定义了游泳体能的概念，并帮助您评估当前的游泳技能和体能水平。这些章节的内容将帮助您明确自己的起点，启发您未来的发展方向，并确保您拥有开启游泳之旅所需的一切。

The information in the first three chapters lays the groundwork for your training. Chapter 1 introduces you to swimming as a lifelong sport and covers the benefits of making a habit of swimming. Chapter 2 helps you choose the proper swimming equipment to fit your needs and offers suggestions on finding the best places to swim. Chapter 3 defines what swimming fitness is and helps you determine your current swimming skill and conditioning level. The information in these chapters will help you identify where you are starting, give you ideas for where you might want to go, and ensure you have what you need to start the journey.

第一章
 
终身游泳
 

游泳——没有其他运动能真正伴随孩子一生。婴儿天生就对水有着亲近感，水能给他们带来如同子宫般的安全感。从婴儿第一次洗澡开始，他们就有很多机会与水建立联系。从六个月大开始，亲子游泳课程会教家长如何让孩子在与水的早期接触中感到安全、舒适和充满鼓励。真正的游泳课程最早可以从三岁开始。在全国许多地区，孩子们早在五岁就开始参加夏季游泳联赛。孩子们可以通过社区夏季联赛和美国游泳协会（USAS）的青少年组队等项目继续参与游泳，然后进入高中游泳队，再到大学校队和校内游泳队。美国大师游泳协会（USMS）是青少年组游泳的延伸，为18岁及以上、各种水平的游泳运动员提供有组织的训练和比赛。大师赛的规模从只有几十名游泳运动员参加、持续几个小时的小型地方赛事，到吸引数千名选手齐聚一堂、持续一周或更长时间的国际赛事，不一而足。老年奥运会为50岁及以上、各种水平的游泳运动员提供了颇受欢迎但参赛机会相对有限的竞技平台。当然，基督教青年会（YMCA）的课程和社区游泳课也是不错的选择。许多成年人甚至会一直游泳到生命的最后一刻。我们经常可以看到六七十岁甚至八十岁的老人与二三十岁的游泳运动员在泳道中并肩畅游。1993年，美国游泳大师协会（USMS）修改了比赛规则，增设了百岁及以上年龄组的比赛！

Swimming—there is no other truly lifelong sport. Babies are born with a natural affinity for water and its womblike feeling of security. Beginning with a baby’s first bathtub experiences, there are numerous opportunities to develop a relationship with the water. From six months, parent-and-tot programs teach parents how to make their children’s formative experiences with water safe, comfortable, and encouraging. Real swimming lessons begin as early as age three. In many areas of the country, children start racing in summer swim leagues as early as age five. Kids can stay involved in swimming through programs such as community summer leagues and USA Swimming’s (USAS) age-group teams, then move on to high school swimming and then to college varsity and intramural swimming. United States Masters Swimming (USMS) is an extension of age-group swimming that offers organized training and competition for swimmers of all abilities age 18 or older. Masters competitions range from small local meets with a couple dozen swimmers lasting just a couple hours all the way up to international meets that draw thousands of competitors together for a week or more. Senior Olympics offers popular, though more limited, competitive opportunities for swimmers of all abilities age 50 and over. Of course, YMCA classes and community lap-swim classes are always an option. Many adults continue swimming literally until the day they die. It is common to see people in their 60s, 70s, or 80s swimming laps in lanes next to 20- or 30-year-old swimmers. In 1993, USMS amended its competition rules to add age groups for swimmers 100 years of age and up!

在本章中，我们将探讨您在成人游泳爱好者群体中可能扮演的角色。接下来，我们将讨论加入“游泳爱好者”行列后，您能从中获得哪些益处。最后，我将破除一些常见的误解，这些误解有时会让一些原本想游泳的人犹豫不决。

In this chapter we’ll explore where you might fit into the broad spectrum of adult swimmers. Next we’ll talk about the variety of benefits you can derive from claiming your rightful place among the chronically wet. Finally, I’ll dispel the common myths that sometimes give an otherwise would-be swimmer pause.

游泳运动员的类​​别

Categories of Swimmers

 

在美国，游泳是最受欢迎的运动。当然，在问卷调查中表示自己参与游泳的6000万美国人中，肯定有一些人指的是去年夏天在海水中涉水一周，弄湿了沙滩裤。然而，如果你在早上、午餐时间或下班后去游泳池，看到众多健身游泳者争抢泳道，你很快就会意识到，这6000万美国人中很大一部分实际上是经常认真游泳的人。如果你曾经在水中游过，超过膝盖的深度，那么你很可能属于以下几种情况之一：

Swimming is enjoyed by more Americans than any other sport. Certainly some of the 60 million Americans who indicate on questionnaires that they participate in swimming are referring to one week last summer when they waded knee-deep in the ocean and got their beach-baggies wet. Yet, if you visit a lap pool in the morning, during lunch, or after work and see the numerous fitness swimmers vying for lane space, you’ll quickly come to appreciate that a large percentage of those 60 million Americans are, in fact, regular, serious swimmers. Chances are, if you ever immerse yourself farther than knee-deep into water, you fall into one of the following categories:

游泳新手：你可以一口气游完一两个泳池长度。你用的是自由泳或蛙泳，就算掉进深水区也不会溺水。事实上，如果拼了命，你甚至可以游几百码，但你可能一天之内游不到500码。

Novice Swimmer You can swim one or two lengths of the pool without stopping. You use the crawl stroke or breaststroke, and you wouldn’t drown if you were to fall into the deep end. In fact, you could swim a couple hundred yards if your life depended on it, but you probably have never swum more than 500 yards in one day.

游泳爱好者：状态好的时候，你一天能游一英里甚至更远。最后几圈游得很快，这样你既能保持状态又能感到疲惫；或者，如果泳池有计时，你也会计时游几个50米。你的自由泳游得很好，或许还能再练一种泳姿，足以在公共场合游。我们通常把这部分健身游泳爱好者称为游泳爱好者。每天，数以百万计的人前往附近的泳池，独自游上一两个小时。

Lap Swimmer You swim a mile or more on a good day. You swim your last few lengths pretty fast so that you feel good and tired, or you time a couple of 50s if the pace clock is on. You swim freestyle well and maybe one more stroke well enough to do in public. We commonly refer to this largest segment of the fitness-swimming public as lap swimmers. Every day, millions of people head to a nearby pool to swim an hour or so of solitary laps.

前参赛选手：您曾参加过一些比赛——例如美国游泳协会 (USAS)、业余体育联盟 (AAU)、高中或大学比赛。您（或曾经）精通所有四种竞技泳姿。虽然您很少游超过 1000 码，但您通常能在泳池派对上参加几场比赛。

Former Competitor You have some competitive background—USAS, Amateur Athletic Union (AAU), high school, or college. You swim (or swam) all four competitive strokes. Although you rarely swim more than 1,000 yards, you are usually good for a couple of races at pool parties.

参赛者：您是一名铁人三项运动员或游泳大师赛选手。您经常或偶尔参加比赛。您定期训练，训练日游泳距离为 1500 至 5000 码。您进行专项训练和间歇训练，并且可能与水平相近的选手一起游泳，或者您是游泳大师赛俱乐部的成员。

Competitor You’re a participating triathlete or a Masters swimmer. You compete often or occasionally. You work out regularly and swim 1,500 to 5,000 yards on a workout day. You do drills and interval work and probably swim with others whose ability is similar to yours or you belong to a Masters swim club.

无论你属于哪个群体，本书都能帮助你更深入地参与游泳运动，无论是为了健身还是竞技。如果你是游泳新手，你将学习水对身体的影响，以及如何运用生理原理让游泳更轻松。你还将学习如何将游泳作为一种健身方式。如果你是游泳爱好者，你将学习如何像专业游泳运动员一样，运用更高效的姿势和动作。你将发现新的训练方法，让你的训练更加高效。

Whichever group you are in, you can use this book to increase your involvement in swimming, whether for fitness or competition. If you’re a novice swimmer, you will learn how the water affects your body and how you can use physical principles to make swimming easier. You will also learn how to use swimming as a fitness tool. If you’re a lap swimmer, you will learn what it takes to look and move like an accomplished swimmer, using more efficient positions and motions. You will discover new ways to focus your training time so that it’s more productive.

如果您曾是一名竞技游泳运动员，您会发现一些关于游泳技术和体能训练的新信息，这些信息在您早期的游泳生涯中是无法获得的。作为一名现役运动员，您将学习到一些关于技术和训练的前沿知识，这些信息您可能之前只能从杂志文章、教练或训练伙伴那里零星了解到。本书还将为您提供一些方法，帮助您在独自训练时，无论是在家还是外出，都能高效地利用泳池时间。

If you’re a former competitive swimmer, you will find new information about swimming technique and conditioning that was not available during your earlier swimming years. As an active competitor, you will learn cutting-edge information about technique and training that you might have caught only snippets of from magazine articles, coaches, or training partners. This book will also give you ideas for using pool time efficiently when training on your own, whether at home or on the road.

无论您从哪个水平开始练习游泳，您都有着广阔的提升空间。只要您坚持执行技能提升计划和循序渐进的训练结构，您的能力就能远远超出您最初的想象。即使是游泳新手，只要愿意努力训练并遵循行之有效的方案，也能进步到足以体验国际比赛的激情，或者掌握一项终身受益的健身技能。

No matter what level you are starting at with Fitness Swimming, you have a wide-open opportunity for improvement. By faithfully following a skill-building program and a progressive structure of workouts, you can develop your abilities far beyond what you might initially think possible. Even novice swimmers can improve to the point where they can experience the thrill of international competition or gain a lifelong fitness tool if they’re willing to work hard and follow a proven plan.

游泳的好处

Benefits of Swimming

 

游泳被健康和健身专家广泛认为是提高有氧运动能力、柔韧性、身体力量、肌肉张力和协调性的近乎完美的运动。任何比随意浏览电视频道更剧烈的运动都会对身体造成损耗，这几乎是普遍存在的问题。而游泳的独特之处在于，它是对身体损耗最小的运动，尤其是在采用正确技巧的情况下。

Swimming is widely recognized by health and fitness professionals as a nearly perfect activity for improving aerobic fitness, flexibility, body strength, muscle tone, and coordination. Wear and tear on the body is an almost universal problem with any activity more strenuous than channel surfing. Swimming has the distinction of being the sport lowest in wear and tear, particularly if you use proper technique.

几乎所有运动项目的教练和训练员都认可各种形式的水中运动作为运动员训练辅助手段的有效性。无论是职业拳击手利用水的自然阻力来增强拳击力量，还是奥运会百米短跑运动员利用水中跑步来加强短跑训练，亦或是职业足球或篮球运动员将水中运动作为物理治疗方案的一部分，各运动项目的运动员都在利用水中运动来提升他们的主要运动表现。

Coaches and trainers in virtually every sport acknowledge the efficacy of water exercise in various forms as an adjunct to their athletes’ training. Whether it’s a professional boxer using the natural resistance of water to make his punches more powerful, an Olympic 100-meter runner using water running to augment her sprint training, or a professional football or basketball player using water exercise as part of a physical therapy regimen, athletes in all sports are coming to water to improve their primary sports.

游泳，简而言之，是水上运动的最佳形式。它既能挑战身心，又能提升精神和体魄，是一项令人着迷的运动，它能让你爱不释手，并让你终生保持健康。《华尔街日报》的伦纳德·古德曼曾说过：“世上有两样东西，没人会认为它们对你有害——游泳和酸奶。 ”

Swimming, quite simply, is the supreme form of water exercise. Challenging to the mind and the body, uplifting to the spirit and the flesh, swimming is a fascinating sport that can grab you, hold you, and keep you healthy for the rest of your life. “There are two things in existence that nobody thinks are bad for you—swimming and yogurt,” says Leonard Goodman in the Wall Street Journal.

有氧训练

Aerobic Conditioning

 

如果你调查一下健身游泳爱好者，你会发现他们几乎都以提高有氧运动能力为目标。旨在提高有氧运动能力的锻炼会影响两个不同但又相互关联的系统——心肺系统和肌肉系统——而这两个系统各自包含不同的训练要素。

If you canvas the ranks of fitness swimmers, you will find that a nearly universal goal is to improve aerobic fitness. Exercise intended to improve aerobic fitness affects two different yet related systems—the cardiorespiratory system and the muscular system—each of which has different conditioning components.

任何能使心率超过每分钟 120 次并持续 20 分钟以上的运动都能改善心肺系统。心肺系统是由心脏、肺和血管组成的众所周知的系统，它负责将吸入的空气中的氧气输送到肺部，并输送到各个肌肉细胞供其使用。氧气进入肺部后，扩散穿过毛细血管壁，然后进入红细胞。心脏将这些携带着宝贵氧气的红细胞泵入由各种大小血管组成的迷宫，最终到达环绕肌肉细胞和肌纤维的毛细血管。在这里，氧气从心肺系统输送到肌肉系统。

Any exercise that raises your heart rate higher than 120 beats per minute for longer than 20 minutes improves the cardiorespiratory system. The cardiorespiratory system is the well-known system of heart, lungs, and blood vessels that takes oxygen from the air you breathe into your lungs and transports it to the individual muscle cells where it will be used. Oxygen enters the lungs, diffuses through the capillary walls, and then enters your red blood cells. Through a maze of various-sized blood vessels, the heart pumps these red blood cells, which are carrying their precious cargo of oxygen, to the capillaries that surround the muscle cells and fibers. Here, the transition from the cardiorespiratory system to the muscular system takes place.

当心肺系统将红细胞输送到肌肉细胞后，氧气会扩散穿过肌肉细胞膜进入细胞，帮助肌肉收缩产生能量。有氧代谢是指利用脂肪、碳水化合物和氧气产生运动能量的一系列复杂的化学反应。有氧训练会引起肌肉细胞内多种适应性变化，从而提高细胞长时间工作的能力。与其他任何热门运动相比，游泳运动中参与有氧运动的肌肉比例更高。越野滑雪是唯一能与之匹敌的运动。

Once the cardiorespiratory system delivers the red blood cells to a muscle cell, the oxygen diffuses across the muscle cell membrane and into the cell, where it helps produce energy for muscle contractions. The term aerobic metabolism identifies a complex set of chemical interactions that use fat, carbohydrate, and oxygen to produce energy for exercise. Aerobic conditioning causes a variety of adaptations within the muscle cell that improve the cell’s ability to perform work for extended periods. Swimming properly involves a greater percentage of your body’s muscle mass in aerobic exercise than any other popular activity. Cross-country skiing is the only other sport vying for this position.

只有当运动使特定肌肉在整个锻炼过程中反复持续收缩时，才能实现对特定肌肉的有氧训练。难怪跑步者或骑行者在开始游泳时，尽管他们的心肺功能良好，游几圈后仍然会感到疲惫。他们花费时间进行腿部专项肌肉的有氧训练，但很少或根本没有进行上半身的训练。

Aerobic conditioning of any specific muscle occurs only when an exercise causes that particular muscle to contract repeatedly and consistently throughout the workout. It is no wonder that runners or cyclists who take up swimming find that, despite their excellent cardiorespiratory conditioning, swimming a few laps leaves them fatigued. They have spent time aerobically conditioning the sport-specific muscles of the legs but have done little or no conditioning of the upper body.

 

游泳是保持健康体型和柔韧性的绝佳方式。

Swimming is a great way to attain a healthy body composition and maintain flexibility.

© Icon Sports Media

© Icon Sports Media

 

肌肉力量：虽然游泳并不能练出健硕的肌肉，但即使是中等强度的长距离游泳也能有效增强多块肌肉的力量和线条，尤其对躯干、肩部和手臂肌肉的锻炼效果显著。经验丰富的游泳运动员会采用高强度间歇训练和冲刺训练来提升整体身体力量。游泳的优势之一在于，这项运动本身就包含大幅度的运动，因此能够有效增强身体各部位的功能性力量。

Muscular Strength Although swimming does not build huge, rippling muscles, even moderate-intensity distance swimming is excellent for improving strength and tone in several muscles, especially in the torso, shoulder, and arm. More experienced swimmers use high-intensity interval and sprint training to increase overall body strength. One of swimming’s advantages is in developing functional strength throughout the large ranges of motion inherent in the sport.

提高柔韧性可能是游泳最大的益处之一。它能让人们在其他运动项目因年龄限制而不得不停止参与时，依然能够充分享受游泳的乐趣。由于游泳时身体需要做出各种姿势和大幅度的运动，几乎所有经常游泳的人都能提高柔韧性。

Flexibility Improving flexibility may be one of the greatest benefits of swimming. It is an important factor that allows people to participate fully in swimming well past ages where they must discontinue participation in other sports. Because of the positions and large ranges of motion that swimmers ask the body to move through when making proper strokes, virtually all people who swim regularly become more flexible.

多年来，关于游泳是否是减脂的好方法一直争论不休。和任何运动一样，你对待这项运动的强度在很大程度上决定了最终的效果。你只需看看游泳比赛中那些站在出发台上的选手们匀称健美的身材，就能明白高强度的游泳训练可以打造出令人艳羡的体型。同样，也有很多人去游泳池只是漫不经心地游来游去，几乎不费吹灰之力地从一端游到另一端。这些人很可能会抱怨游泳对他们毫无益处。如果他们把同样的精力投入到跑步、骑自行车或其他任何运动中，他们很可能也会有同样的抱怨。

Body Composition Much has been said over the years about whether swimming is a good way to get leaner. As with any form of exercise, the intensity with which you approach the sport determines, to a large extent, the results. You need only look at the evenly-toned, long-muscled bodies of swimmers mounting the blocks at any swimming competition to know that intense swim training can produce a body a person would be proud to wear almost nothing on. By the same token, there are plenty of people who go to the pool and just piddle around, applying the bare minimum of effort to slowly move from one end to the other. Those people are likely to complain that swimming does nothing for them. If they were to put the same amount of effort into running, cycling, or any other sport, those people would most likely have the same complaint.

游泳常见误区

Common Swimming Myths

 
以下是一些关于游泳的常见误解，我必须一一澄清。

•在冷水中游泳会导致身体储存脂肪。有一种被称为冷水浸没反应的现象，它倾向于将身体脂肪用于保暖。然而，一旦你开始进行强度足以提升核心体温的运动，这种现象就不再重要了。大多数游泳池的水温都保持在 78 华氏度（约 26 摄氏度）或更高，足以让除极瘦的人以外的所有人都能提升核心体温。事实上，如果泳池水温过高，游泳者可能会过热，从而降低运动能力和脂肪代谢。与在过热的空气中进行的任何运动相比，在冷水中游泳可以带来更大的运动量和强度。即使是横渡英吉利海峡的游泳者，在 55 华氏度（约 13 摄氏度）的水温下也会经历显著的脂肪减少。迄今为止，运动强度和持续时间对脂肪代谢的影响最大。

• Swimming in cold water causes your body to store fat.There is a phenomenon called the cold-water immersion response that tends to spare body fat for insulation. As soon as you begin exercising at an intensity great enough to elevate your core temperature, however, this becomes a moot point. Most swimming pools are kept at 78 degrees or warmer, plenty warm to allow all but the thinnest people to elevate core temperature. In fact, if a pool is too warm, a swimmer can become overheated, which decreases work capacity and fat metabolism. Swimming in cool water allows greater exercise volume and intensity than does any exercise that is performed in air that is too hot. Even English Channel swimmers experience significant fat loss during their 55 ˚F (13 ˚C) ordeal. By far, intensity and duration most greatly influence fat metabolism.

游泳时身体呈俯卧姿势，这意味着训练期间的心率会比其他运动低。因此，游泳的锻炼强度可能不如其他运动。仅仅是待在水中就能减轻心脏泵血的负担，因为它不再需要克服重力。虽然这会降低你的静息心率，但并不会影响你的训练强度。无论训练强度和持续时间如何，游泳的锻炼效果并不逊于你投入相同强度和时间进行其他运动。

• Swimming is performed in a prone position, which means that your heart rates during training will be lower than in other sports. You therefore don’t get as much of a workout.Just being in the water reduces the amount of work that the heart must do to circulate your blood, because it no longer must pump against the force of gravity. While this does reduce your resting pulse rate, it has no influence over how hard you can push yourself. Regardless of training intensity and duration, the workout you can get in swimming is no less effective than if you invested the same intensity and time in another sport.

•游泳会让你感到饥饿。好吧，你猜对了。的确，大多数游泳运动员在训练后都会感到饥饿。几乎所有运动项目都是如此。但是，运动后饥饿感出现的时间与体温的关系比与运动类型的关系更为密切。当你的核心体温远高于正常静息水平时，你不太可能感到饥饿。跑步者和骑行者在运动后通常会保持较高的体温较长时间，从而推迟饥饿感的出现。而游泳运动员在剧烈训练后通常会在凉爽的水中待足够长的时间，使体温降低到足以让饥饿感与运动本身直接相关的程度。

• Swimming makes you hungry. Okay, you got me. It is true that most swimmers tend to be hungry after workouts. The same is true in nearly every sport. But the timing of after-exercise hunger is more directly related to body temperature than to the type of exercise. You are less likely to be hungry when your core temperature is far above normal resting levels. Runners and cyclists generally have elevated body temperatures for longer periods after their workouts, postponing hunger. Swimmers, on the other hand, generally spend enough time in cool water after intense training to lower their body temperature enough that hunger seems more directly linked to the workout.

 

现在你心动了吗？游泳将成为你人生下一个挑战和挚爱。现在你只需要一套泳衣和其他一些装备，就可以出发寻找游泳的好去处了！

So now are you convinced? Swimming will be your next life challenge and passion. Now you need a swimsuit and a few other goodies and you’re off to find a swimmin’ hole!

第二章
 
做好准备
 

游泳的一大魅力在于它所需的装备很少。然而，对于那些喜欢拥有所有运动装备的人来说，市面上也提供了各种各样的可选装备。要学习本书中介绍的训练方法，你需要的装备会比最低要求略多一些。本章将详细介绍所有你需要的装备，并就如何在有多种选择的情况下做出正确的决定提供一些建议。此外，你还将了解到如何最好地利用这些新装备。

An appealing thing about swimming is that it requires very little equipment. Yet, for those who like to own every conceivable bit of paraphernalia that could be used in a sport, a variety of optional equipment is available. To follow the drills and workouts presented in this book, you’ll need a bit more than the minimum. This chapter explains all the equipment you’ll need and gives some hints about making the right selections when options exist. In addition, you’ll learn about where it is best to put all your new stuff to use.

必备设备

Essential Equipment

 

花费比一次廉价约会还少，你就能拥有参与这项运动所需的一切——泳衣、泳镜、泳帽、毛巾和水壶。有了这套极简装备，你可以在任何合适的水域进行锻炼，甚至参加比赛。而且，当你需要旅行时，你也不用担心，因为毛巾和水随处可得，你的泳衣、泳镜和泳帽就足以让你在世界任何地方畅游。当然，随着你不断追求更多样化的体验和更短的学习曲线，你最终可能会拥有比这更齐全的装备，但这套最基本的配置仍然非常实用。

For less than the cost of a cheap date, you can have all the necessities for full participation in the sport—swimsuit, goggles, cap, towel, and water bottle. With this minimal outfit, you can get a workout or even compete in any suitable body of water. And when it’s time to travel, you can take comfort in knowing that, with towels and water available everywhere, your suit, goggles, and cap are all you need in order to swim anywhere in the world. As you search for variety and shortened learning curves, you’ll probably end up with more than the bare essentials, but this minimum configuration will come in handy.

泳装

Swimsuit

 

在所有你需要的装备中，泳衣是最重要的。一般来说，泳衣分为五种类型——比赛泳衣（你正在寻找的那种）、高性能泳衣（选手在重要比赛中穿的）、时尚泳衣（你在《体育画报》上看到的那种）、休闲泳衣（时髦人士在海滩上穿的那种）以及奇形怪状的泳衣（我奶奶在海滩上穿的那种）。

Of all the pieces of equipment you’ll need, your suit is the most important. There are, in general, five types of suits in the swimsuit universe—competition suits (what you are looking for), high-performance suits (what competitors wear for important competitions), fashion suits (what you see in Sports Illustrated), casual swimwear (what cool people wear at the beach), and monstrosities (what my grandmother wears at the beach).

“比赛泳衣”这个词并不意味着这种泳衣只能用于比赛。它指的是一系列能在水中最大限度减少阻力的泳衣。如果你经常游泳，这一点就非常重要。关键在于选择一件既舒适又贴身的泳衣，避免任何松散的布料在水中飘动。

The term competition suit doesn’t mean that the suit should be used only for competition. It is a term that describes a variety of suits that offer a minimum of drag in the water. If you swim laps, this is important. The key is to wear a suit that is comfortable but that snugly fits your body, leaving no loose fabric to flap around in the water.

两种常见的泳衣面料是莱卡和涤纶。如果选择知名品牌，就能买到128级莱卡面料，这种面料比便宜的莱卡泳衣更耐氯、更防霉——绝对物有所值。莱卡泳衣在最初几次游泳后会撑大一个尺码。如果拿不准，宁可买小一号也不要买大一号的。而涤纶泳衣则不会随着穿着而撑大，所以它在商店里的合身程度就是它实际穿着时的合身程度。涤纶泳衣在含氯水中的使用寿命比莱卡泳衣更长，但很多人觉得它的舒适度不如莱卡泳衣。并非所有款式的泳衣都有涤纶面料可选。如果你每天都游泳，至少要准备两套泳衣。穿上冰冷潮湿的泳衣，尤其是在清晨，简直就像看着猫吐毛球一样难受。

Two common workout-suit materials are Lycra and polyester. If you stick with major brands, you’ll get a 128-grade Lycra fabric that is more resistant to chlorine and mold than cheaper Lycra suits—well worth the extra expense. Lycra suits will stretch one full size within your first few sessions in the pool. If in doubt, buy one that is a bit small rather than too big. Polyester, on the other hand, will not stretch with use, so how it fits in the store is how it will continue to fit. It will last longer in chlorinated water than Lycra will, but many people find that it is not as comfortable. Not all suit styles are available in polyester. If you swim daily, get at least two suits. Putting on a cold, wet suit, especially first thing in the morning, is about as much fun as watching a cat cough up a fur ball.

对于女性来说，选择泳衣不仅仅是看尺码标签。由于游泳需要手臂和肩膀进行大幅度的运动，泳衣背部和肩带的贴合度会直接影响你的动作。试穿不同款式和品牌的泳衣，确保充分伸展身体，摆出流线型姿势，并做出游泳动作，以判断泳衣是否会妨碍你的动作。尤其要注意不要选择过大的泳衣。过松的泳衣会积水，增加阻力。一般来说，如果肩带可以拉到耳朵以上，那么泳衣可能就太大了。女性可以选择连体泳衣（图 2.1）或分体式比基尼泳衣。

For women, choosing a suit only begins with the size printed on the tag. Because swimming involves so much range of motion of the arms and shoulders, the way the back and strap configuration fits you will influence the way you move. Try on suits of various styles and manufacturers, making sure to stretch yourself into a full streamline position and to move your arms through swimming motions in order to see if the suit will hamper your movement. It is particularly important to not get too big a suit. A suit that is not snug enough will catch large amounts of water and act as a drag chute. In general, if the shoulder straps can stretch higher than your ears, the suit might be too big. Women have the option of a one-piece workout suit (figure 2.1) or a two-piece workout bikini.

 

图 2.1女士连体运动服和男士运动短裤。

Figure 2.1 Women’s one-piece workout suit and men’s Jammers.

 

对男士来说，泳衣大体上都差不多。一旦确定了最合适的尺码，你很可能对任何主流品牌的泳衣都满意。有些男士就是无法接受穿着过于暴露的比赛泳衣。一些品牌推出了一系列剪裁更宽松的泳衣，侧边拼接部分为 4 英寸或 5 英寸（10 或 13 厘米），而不是标准的 3 英寸（8 厘米）。紧身泳裤（图 2.1）能够紧贴大腿，在健身游泳中越来越受欢迎。不过，三角泳裤（图 2.2）仍然是健身游泳中最受欢迎的款式。

For men, for the most part, a suit is a suit is a suit. Once you decide which size fits you best, you will likely be happy with any suit from any of the major manufacturers. Some guys just can’t bring themselves to wear skimpy little racing suits. Several manufacturers offer a line of fuller-cut suits with 4- or 5-inch (10 or 13 cm) side panels instead of the standard 3-inch (8 cm) side panels. Jammer suits (figure 2.1) that snugly cover the thighs are gaining popularity for workout swimming. Briefs (figure 2.2) are still the most popular style for workout swimming, however.

如果以上方法都不奏效，你非要买一条沙滩裤，那就给自己一个机会，把口袋缝起来，这样当你沿着沙滩小道蹒跚而行时，它们就不会像泄力伞一样鼓起来了。

If none of these will suffice and you just have to have a pair of beach baggies, do yourself a favor and sew the pockets shut so that they don’t balloon up like drag chutes as you plod down the lane.

女士顶级泳衣，尤其是最新款印花款式，通常售价在 50 到 75 美元之间；男士泳衣则根据款式不同，售价在 35 到 45 美元左右。在许多泳装店，你会发现一些已经停产的同款高品质泳衣，价格可能只有最新款的一半。此外，现在的高性能泳衣采用高科技材料制成，据制造商称，这种材料的水阻比皮肤还要小。不同款式的泳衣覆盖的身体部位也各不相同，有些款式甚至覆盖了除头部、手部和脚部以外的所有部位。许多竞技选手在高水平比赛中都会穿着这种泳衣。由于这类泳衣的价格从 150 美元到 500 美元甚至更高，而且只能穿几次，因此并不适合日常训练游泳。不过，谁知道呢——如果你遵循本书中的建议，说不定哪天你也需要一件！

Women’s top-quality suits in the latest prints usually cost $50 to $75 U.S., and men’s suits cost about $35 to $45, depending on style. In many swim shops you’ll find a rack of discontinued prints of the same high-quality suits for as little as half the price of the latest prints. Additionally, now performance suits are made from high-tech materials that, according to the manufacturers’ claims, offer less resistance to water flow than your skin does. Different styles of these suits cover different amounts of the body, up to full-body suits that cover all but the head, hands, and feet. Many competitors wear these for high-level competition. Because they cost anywhere from $150 to $500 or more and can be worn only a few times, these suits are not for workout swimming. But who knows—if you follow the advice in this book, you might one day need one!

 

图 2.2男士三角裤。

Figure 2.2 Men’s briefs.

 

风镜

Goggles

 

泳镜在眼睛前方形成一个小型气囊，其透明镜片能让使用者拥有接近正常的视力。此外，泳镜还能保护游泳者的眼睛免受氯气刺激带来的不适。

Goggles maintain a small pocket of air directly in front of the eyes, and they have a transparent lens that allows for nearly normal vision. They also protect swimmers’ eyes from the discomfort of chlorine exposure.

现代材料的进步以及越来越多愿意花钱购买泳镜的游泳爱好者，催生了大量价格低廉、轻便舒适、小巧便携的泳镜款式。然而，其中真正适合你的款式却寥寥无几。除了泳衣之外，没有什么比一副合适的泳镜更能影响你的游泳舒适度和乐趣了。以下是选择完美泳镜时需要考虑的一些因素。

Modern materials and a growing swimming population that is willing to part with its cash have spawned an abundance of inexpensive, compact, lightweight, comfortable goggle styles. Only a few of those styles, however, are likely to be right for you. Aside from your swimsuit, there is nothing within your control that will more greatly affect your comfort and appreciation for swimming than the right pair of goggles. Here are a few things to consider when choosing your perfect pair of goggles.

形状：护目镜有两种基本形状，我称之为“半圆形”和“椭圆形”。如果你找到一副适合你的椭圆形护目镜，那么很可能任何适合你的护目镜都是椭圆形的。同样的道理也适用于你发现一副半圆形护目镜很适合你的情况。

Shape The two basic shapes for goggles are what I refer to as “sort of round” and “more oval.” If you find one pair of oval goggles that works well for you, then most likely any goggle that works well for you will be more oval in shape. The same kind of thinking also applies if you find that a pair of sort-of-round goggles works well.

鼻托大多数护目镜都配有可调节的鼻托，材质通常为塑料、硅胶或绳子。一旦正确调整，几乎无需再次调整。有些型号的鼻托是不可调节的一体成型鼻托，与镜框融为一体。如果您鼻梁和眼位正常，这种鼻托也适用。

Nosepieces Most goggle styles come with an adjustable nosepiece that is made of plastic, silicone, or string, which, once properly adjusted, will seldom, if ever, need readjustment. Some models have nonadjustable, molded nosepieces that are part of the frame. These are fine if you have average nose and eye placement.

泳镜带：一副合适的泳镜即使不用带子也能贴合在脸上。它们之所以能固定住，仅仅是因为吸力和良好的密封性。不过，带子确实能让泳镜在游泳时更加稳固。宽大、浅色的带子，上面有足够的空间写上你的名字，万一泳镜丢失，这无疑是个加分项。双带或分体式带子可能比单带更牢固，因为受力点分散在头部更多部位。

Straps A good-fitting pair of goggles will stick to your face without the strap. They stay on simply because of a bit of suction and a good seal. Nevertheless, the strap keeps your goggles in place while swimming. A wide, light-colored strap that allows plenty of space to write your name on it is a plus in case you lose your goggles. A double or split strap may stay in place better than a single strap because the forces are spread around more parts of the head.

绑带调节：在结账前，您可以先判断一副泳镜的好坏，其中一项就是绑带和扣环系统是否方便调节。患有关节炎或其他影响灵活性的游泳者尤其应该注意这一点。在泳池边调节泳镜可不是件容易的事。

Strap Adjustment One of the things you can judge about a pair of goggles before you reach the checkout counter is whether the strap and buckle system allows for easy adjustment. Swimmers with arthritis or any other dexterity-limiting condition should pay particular attention to this. It doesn’t get any easier to adjust the goggles when you’re poolside.

密封圈密封圈是护目镜眼罩周围的柔软材料，用于填充护目镜与面部连接处的缝隙。密封圈有多种类型可供选择：泡沫、硅胶、聚乙烯或无密封圈。就简洁性、易保养性和使用寿命而言，“无密封圈”是最佳选择。流行的瑞典式护目镜没有密封圈，因此能够实现最贴合面部的流线型佩戴效果。但是，如果您的脸型与护目镜的轮廓不完全吻合，那么带密封圈的护目镜会更适合您。如果护目镜的形状适合您的脸型，实心硅胶或聚乙烯密封圈可以形成良好的密封，并且具有出色的抗菌性能。泡沫密封圈虽然更容易形成防漏密封，但如果保养不当，容易滋生微生物。

Gaskets The gasket is the soft material around the goggle’s eyecup that fills the voids at the goggle-to-face union. There are several types to choose from: foam, silicone, polyvinyl, or none. For simplicity, ease of care, and length of service, “none” tops the list. Popular Swedish-style goggles have no gasket, allowing for the most streamlined, face-hugging fit. If, however, your face doesn’t have the same contours as the goggle, you will be happier with a gasketed goggle. Solid silicone or polyvinyl gaskets make a good seal if the goggle is the correct shape for your face, and they offer excellent resistance to microbial growth. Foam gaskets, although more forgiving in making a leakproof seal, are prone to grow low-order life-forms if not properly maintained.

泳镜镜片有多种颜色和色调可供选择。如果您计划在白天户外游泳，建议选择颜色较深且具有紫外线防护功能的泳镜。

Lens Color Goggle lenses come in a variety of colors and shades. If you plan to swim outdoors in daylight, you should stick with darker goggles that have UV protection.

防雾性能：泳镜起雾的原因是眼罩内温暖空气中的水分凝结在泳镜内壁上，而泳镜内壁已被周围的水冷却。市面上许多泳镜都标榜具有防雾功能。此外，还有防雾喷雾或液体可供选择。您也可以自己制作，只需将等量的婴儿洗发水和水混合即可。就我个人经验和听说的而言，我还没发现比游泳者的唾液更好的防雾方法。在眼罩内壁涂抹一层薄薄的唾液，就能在游泳的大部分时间里防止起雾。或者，在眼罩内滴几滴泳池水，水量刚好能让水滴自由滚动，这就像给挡风玻璃装了雨刷一样，可以有效防止长时间游泳时起雾。

Antifog Properties Goggles fog up when moisture in the warm air trapped in the eyecup condenses on the inside surface of the goggle, which has been cooled by the surrounding water. Many goggles on the market tout antifog properties. In addition, antifog sprays or liquids are available. You can make your own by mixing equal parts baby shampoo and water. I have yet to encounter, through experience or anecdote, any better antifog system than good ol’ swimmer’s spit. A thin coating of saliva on the inside of the eyecup keeps it from fogging for a good portion of your workout. Alternatively, a few drops of pool water in the eyecup, just enough to roll around freely, works a bit like windshield wipers for a long swim.

戴眼镜或隐形眼镜的人不必盲泳。许多隐形眼镜佩戴者害怕戴着隐形眼镜和泳镜。然而，游泳时丢失隐形眼镜的几率远低于摘戴隐形眼镜时丢失的几率。游泳时戴着隐形眼镜会让你看得更清楚，心情也会更愉悦。如果你戴眼镜，可以咨询验光师，了解是否有合适的近视泳镜或近视镜片可以适配你常用的泳镜。此外，游泳用品商店和网站也出售现成的矫正镜片泳镜。你很可能找到一副可以让你在泳池对面也能看清计时器的泳镜。

People who wear glasses or contacts need not swim blind. Many contact-lens wearers are afraid to wear their lenses with goggles. You are less likely to lose lenses while swimming, however, than you are while taking them out and putting them back in. You will be much happier if you keep your lenses in while swimming because you’ll be able to see. If you wear glasses, check with your optometrist about prescription goggles or prescription inserts for your favorite goggles. There are also off-the-rack corrective-lens goggles available through swim shops and Web sites. You likely can find a pair that allows you to read a pace clock from across the pool.

价格与哪款泳镜适合游泳者无关。你的泳镜可能是你泳包里最便宜的物品，也可能是最贵的。大多数游泳者都能在价格较低的泳镜中找到舒适且不漏水的款式。然而，许多游泳者却执着地用“不惜一切代价”的态度去摆弄昂贵的泳镜，试图让它们达到完美状态，但往往徒劳无功。有些人花了30多美元买了一副最新的高科技泳镜后，却舍不得放弃这笔投资，去买一副他们认为更合适的5美元泳镜。一旦你找到了完美的泳镜，就多买几副吧。墨菲定律总是有规律可循的。我记不清确切的措辞了，但它大致是指，在未来的某个时候，唯一适合你脸型的泳镜款式可能永远不会出现。

Price has nothing to do with which goggle is right for a given swimmer. Your goggles could easily be the least expensive item in your swimming bag—or they could just as easily be the most expensive. Most swimmers are able to find a comfortable, leak-free fit in the low end of the price range. Yet many a swimmer doggedly applies the “whatever it takes” attitude to fussing with an expensive pair of goggles, trying in vain to coax perfection from them. After spending $30-plus on a pair of the latest high-tech goggles, some people are loath to abandon their investment for a pair of $5 goggles that they know will fit better. Once you find your perfect goggle, buy several pairs. Murphy has a law. I don’t recall the exact wording, but it has something to do with the availability, at any point in the future, of the only goggle style that fits your face.

泳帽

Swimming Cap

 

对于头发超过几英寸的人来说，泳帽是必需品。泳帽均为均码，用途广泛，包括防止头发遮挡眼睛、鼻子和嘴巴；比头发更防水；防止头发吸收过多氯；与泳装搭配；以及彰显你的身份。

For anyone whose hair is more than a few inches long, a swimming cap is a necessity. Caps are one size fits all and serve multiple purposes, including keeping your hair out of your eyes, nose, and mouth; affording less water resistance than hair; keeping your hair from absorbing too much chlorine; coordinating with your swimming ensemble; and proclaiming your affiliation.

泳帽的三种常见材质是乳胶、硅胶和莱卡。乳胶泳帽最受欢迎，价格也最便宜，而且适合大多数游泳者。硅胶泳帽价格更高，也更耐用（除非出现哪怕是最轻微的破损，一旦破损就报废了）。硅胶泳帽比较难固定，而且不太适合所有人。莱卡泳帽最不受欢迎，价格也最高。它们看起来很奇怪，而且根本无法保护头发。我不明白为什么会有市场。

The three common materials for caps are latex, silicone, and Lycra. Latex caps are the most popular and the least expensive, and they fit most swimmers. Silicone caps are more expensive and they last longer (unless they get even a slight tear, in which case they are instant history). Silicone caps are harder to keep in place, and they work well for fewer swimmers. Lycra caps are the least popular and most expensive. They look funky and they don’t protect your hair at all. I’m not sure why there is a market for them.

无论使用哪种瓶盖，每次使用后都要彻底晾干。存放前，轻轻扑上一层婴儿爽身粉。避免将其揉成一团放在包底或高温的车内。最好多带几个，以防万一损坏。

Regardless of what kind of cap you use, dry it thoroughly after each use. Dust it lightly with baby powder before you store it. Avoid leaving it wadded up in the bottom of your bag or in a hot car. Carry several, in case one becomes damaged.

水瓶

Water Bottle

 

即使浸泡在凉爽的水中，游泳时身体仍然会出汗，呼吸时也会不断排出水蒸气。及时补充水分对于安全高效的锻炼至关重要。在感到口渴之前就喝水，并且要比你认为需要的量多喝一些。你需要一个带盖的容器，以防止泳池中的水溅入。如果你在烈日下进行户外训练，最好使用保温水瓶，或者可以提前一晚将半瓶一升装的水放入冰箱冷冻。在前往泳池前，将水瓶装满水，这样你就能在整个锻炼过程中随时补充水分。即使只是一个装满自来水的旧牛奶罐，也要把这宝贵的生命之水带到泳池边。

Despite being immersed in cool water, your body still perspires when you swim, and you are constantly blowing off water vapor as you breathe. Replenishing that water is vital to a safe and productive workout. Drink before you get thirsty and drink more than you think you need. You will want a container with a cap on it that will keep out water that could be splashed into the container from the pool. If you train outdoors in the hot sun, you will want an insulated water bottle, or you can freeze a half-full liter-size water bottle overnight. Just before you head to the pool, fill the bottle the rest of the way with water, which will provide you with cold water throughout your workout. Even if it is just an old milk jug full of tap water, bring this precious elixir of life to the pool with you.

辅助设备

Supplemental Equipment

 

对于那些非得被各种器材和装备包围才觉得训练完整的人来说，市面上有很多额外的产品可以作为基础装备的补充。本书中的训练计划和练习需要用到比基本装备更多的器材。有些器材可以提升体能，有些可以帮助你更快地掌握技能，还有一些可以帮助你保持动力、条理清晰、步入正轨。以下这些器材将为你的训练增添多样性、实用性和趣味性。

For the person who doesn’t feel complete until he is surrounded by equipment and gadgets, there are plenty of additional products available to complement the basics. The drill progressions and workouts in this book call for the use of several more pieces of equipment than just the essentials. Some offer fitness benefits, others help you master skills more quickly, and others will help keep you motivated, organized, and on track. The following equipment will add variety, utility, and a bit of fun to your training.

训练脚蹼如果您按照本书中的训练计划进行练习，您至少需要一副训练脚蹼。脚蹼可以伸展您的脚部和腿部，使您的踢腿更快更高效。它们有助于提高脚踝的灵活性和腿部力量，还能激活更多肌肉群，所有这些都将缩短您学习许多游泳技巧的学习曲线。此外，您还会发现，它们带来的额外速度在游泳时会带来很多乐趣。

Training Fins If you follow the workouts in this book, you will want at least one pair of training fins. Fins extend your feet and legs, making your kick faster and more efficient. They help increase ankle flexibility and leg strength, and they also activate more muscle mass, all of which will shorten the learning curve for many of the skills you’ll be working on. Plus, you’ll find that the extra speed they provide when you swim is simply lots of fun.

大多数脚蹼由天然橡胶制成，如果保养得当，可以使用数年。有些脚蹼由硅胶制成，比橡胶更耐用。还有一些脚蹼由几乎坚不可摧的高密度热处理聚氨酯制成，可以永久使用。您可能需要两副脚蹼：一副短款训练脚蹼（蹼长 1 或 2 英寸，或 2.5 或 5 厘米）和一副标准尺寸的训练脚蹼（蹼长与您的脚大致相同）。避免使用硬质脚蹼、蹼宽超过脚宽 1.5 倍的脚蹼以及蹼长超过脚长的脚蹼，因为这些都会影响您的游泳技术。此外，还要避免使用容易浮到水面或容易下沉的脚蹼。理想情况下，您的脚蹼应该接近中性浮力。除非你的脚踝非常灵活（只有极少数成年人拥有这种灵活性，跑步者几乎不可能拥有），否则请选择你能找到的最灵活的脚蹼。

Most fins are made of natural rubber and give good service for several years if properly cared for. Some are made of silicone, which lasts longer than rubber. Others are made of a nearly indestructible high-density, heat-treated polyurethane that will last forever. You might want two pairs of fins: a pair of short training fins (with a blade length of 1 or 2 inches, or 2.5 or 5 cm) and a pair of normal-size training fins (with a blade that is roughly the same length as your foot). Avoid rigid fins, blades that are more than one-and-a-half times wider than your foot, and blades that are longer than your foot, because any of these will be detrimental to your technique. Also avoid fins that float quickly to the top of the pool or that sink quickly. Ideally, your fins should be almost neutrally buoyant. Unless you have very flexible ankles (a very small percentage of adults do, and runners almost never do), opt for the most flexible fins you can find.

训练呼吸管如果您按照本书中的训练计划进行练习，您将需要一根训练呼吸管。这种呼吸管专为游泳训练而设计。它固定在前额中央，并弯曲覆盖头顶，以确保头部处于正确的位置。对于本书中描述的许多练习、技巧和大部分游泳动作，合适的呼吸管可以消除转身换气的干扰，让您专注于技术的其他方面。如果您不习惯使用呼吸管，请理解需要一段时间才能适应，但这绝对值得。Finis 公司（www.finisinc.com）提供两种型号的呼吸管。一种是游泳呼吸管（图 2.3），是大多数游泳者的最佳选择；另一种是自由泳呼吸管，使用起来稍微复杂一些，但有助于技能更熟练的游泳者进一步提升技能。

Training Snorkel If you follow the workouts in this book, you will want a training snorkel. This type of snorkel is designed specifically for swim training. It mounts in the center of your forehead and curves over the top of your head to allow for a proper head position. For several of the drills, many of the skills, and much of the swimming described herein, a proper snorkel will remove the distraction of turning to breathe so that you can concentrate on other aspects of your technique. If you are not used to snorkels, understand that it takes a while to get comfortable with one, but it is well worth the effort. Two models are offered by Finis (www.finisinc.com). One is called the Swimmer’s Snorkel (figure 2.3), which is the best choice for most swimmers, and one is called the Freestyle Snorkel, which is a bit harder to use but promotes further skill refinement in more skilled swimmers.

电子心率监测器在游泳领域越来越受欢迎。只有配备手表式显示屏和胸带式传感器的监测器才能准确测量游泳时的心率。心率监测器对女性来说非常实用，因为它们可以佩戴在泳衣内，而且不易移位。然而，有些男性会觉得长时间佩戴心率监测器不太舒服，因为它必须足够紧，才能防止在蹬壁时下滑。如果您按照本书中的训练计划进行训练，强烈建议您使用心率监测器。有关如何在训练中使用监测器的详细信息，请参阅第6章。

Heart-Rate Monitor Electronic heart-rate monitors for swimming are becoming more popular. A monitor with a watch-style display and a sensor that straps around the chest is the only accurate way to get heart-rate readings for swimming. Heart-rate monitors work very well for women because they are worn under the suit and they stay in place well. Some men, however, find a heart-rate monitor uncomfortable for extended use because it must be tight enough to not slip down the body when pushing off from the wall. If you follow the workouts in this book, a heart-rate monitor is strongly recommended. See chapter 6 for details on using a monitor in your training.

配速计时器或训练手表大多数训练都采用间歇训练模式，需要使用可见的计时设备。如果您常去的游泳池没有配速计时器，则需要自行准备一个。理想的设备是便携式 15 英寸（38 厘米）模拟配速计时器，带有扫秒针和分针。表盘上的数字从 5 到 60，以 5 秒为单位递增，中间还有小刻度线表示每一秒。更便携的解决方案是个人配速计时器，它可以放置在泳道末端，无论是在池边还是在池沿。对于难以远距离看清配速计时器的人来说，这可能是一个可行的选择。另一种选择是带有计时器的运动手表。选择一款具有多种秒表功能的手表，包括带有倒计时和正计时功能的单圈分段计时记忆功能。一些心率监测器在其手表部分也集成了运动计时器功能。使用手表式计时器有两个缺点：一是游泳时必须停下来才能看清时间；二是记录分段计时需要用另一只手去按按钮，这很不方便。然而，手表的便携性是其他计时器难以匹敌的。

Pace Clock or Training Watch Most workouts are organized in an interval-training format that requires a visible timing device. If the pool you frequent does not have a pace clock, you will want to provide a timing device. The ideal device is a portable 15-inch (38 cm) analog pace clock with a sweeping second hand and minute hand. The face is numbered from 5 to 60 in 5-second jumps, with small tick marks for each second in between. A more portable solution is a personal pace clock or timer that is designed to sit at the end of your lane, either on the deck or in the gutter. This can be a workable option for people who have a hard time seeing a pace clock at a distance. Yet another alternative is a sports watch with a timer. Look for one with multiple stopwatch functions, including lap-split memory with countdown and count-up interval timers. Some heart-rate monitors include sports-timer functions in the watch portion of their system. Two drawbacks to using a watch-type timer are that you can’t see it without stopping your swim, and that recording lap splits requires reaching over with your other hand to press a button, which is awkward at best. It is difficult, however, to beat the portability of a watch.

节奏蜂鸣器：这种小型电子节奏设备可以滑入泳帽下方或固定在泳镜带上。您可以设置一个特定的蜂鸣节奏来配合您的划水动作，然后通过骨传导将声音传递到您的内耳。Tempo Trainer 和 Wetronome 是常见的游泳节奏蜂鸣器。

Tempo Beeper These small electronic-pacing devices slide under your cap or attach to your goggle strap. You set a specific beep tempo to match your stroke to, and then bone conduction transmits the tones to your inner ear. Tempo Trainer and Wetronome are common tempo beepers for swimming.

防水笔记本：泳池边的笔记本可以让你记录时间、记下训练笔记，还能记录那些“灵光乍现”的时刻（甚至还能记下一两个电话号码），而无需离开水面。可以看看 Wet Notes 和 Wet Log 的防水笔记本。如果实在没有防水笔记本，你也可以把 Tyvek 信封裁成几张，然后用铅笔在泳池边写字。

Waterproof Notebook A poolside notebook allows you to keep track of times, jot down training notes, and record those “Aha!” moments (and maybe even capture a phone number or two) without getting out of the water. Look for Wet Notes and Wet Log waterproof notebooks. In a pinch, you can cut Tyvek envelopes into sheets and then use a pencil to write on them poolside.

装备包你拿着这本书去了当地的游泳用品店，说：“每样都要一个，有些要两个。”现在你得来回搬运一大堆东西。不如把剩下的几块钱投资到两个好用的游泳包上。首先，买一个尼龙网眼抽绳包，用来装湿漉漉的泳池玩具（比如脚蹼、呼吸管等等）。然后买一个普通的运动包，用来装更衣室里常用的东西。这种包应该有一两个外部网眼口袋，可以放湿泳衣和泳镜，还有一个防水隔层可以放湿毛巾。防水底在经常潮湿的泳池边也很有用。

Equipment Bags So you took this book to the local swim shop and said, “I’ll have one of each, two of some.” You now have a pile of stuff to schlep back and forth. Invest your last couple of sawbucks in two good swim bags. First, get a nylon-mesh drawstring bag for wet pool toys (fins, snorkel, and the like). Then get a conventional workout bag for the usual locker-room stuff. It should have one or two external mesh pockets for damp suits and goggles and a waterproof compartment for wet towels. A waterproof bottom also comes in handy around constantly wet pool decks.

虽然你会看到游泳者在泳池里使用其他辅助器材，但它们并非提高游泳水平的必要条件。事实上，有些器材甚至可能适得其反。在你掌握本书中的技巧和训练方法之前，请远离浮板、踢水板、手蹼、腕部负重、游泳手套等类似器材。我敢肯定，一旦你掌握了这套健身游泳训练计划，你就会发现自己既不需要也不想使用它们。

Though you’ll see swimmers use other items at the pool, they aren’t necessary for improving your swimming. In fact, some of them could indeed be detrimental. Until you have mastered the skills and workouts in this book, stay away from pull buoys, kickboards, hand paddles, wrist weights, swimming gloves, and the like. My bet is that once you have mastered the Fitness Swimming program, you’ll find that you have no need or desire to use them.

哪里可以游泳

Where to Swim

 

你打算把所有新装备都放在哪里才能物尽其用呢？和任何活动一样，环境会影响你游泳的乐趣，进而影响你参与游泳的频率和坚持的时间。有时候，你只能选择游泳的地点。如果只有一个水潭，而且一天只有一小时可以游泳，那你只能将就了。不过，通常情况下，你会有很多游泳选择。在不同的泳池、不同的时间段、和不同的人一起游泳，有时甚至在开放水域游泳——所有这些都能带来更充实的游泳体验。时刻留意那些与你日常游泳习惯不同的体验吧。

Where do you go to put all your new stuff to best use? As with any activity, the environment affects your enjoyment of swimming, influencing how often you participate in it and how long you stick with it. Sometimes you have little choice over where you swim. If there’s only one swimming hole available and only one hour of the day for lap swimming, then you have to make due. Usually, though, you will have a variety of swimming options from which to choose. Swimming in different pools, at different times of day, with different people, sometimes in open water—all these things tend to make for a fulfilling swimming experience. Always be on the lookout for a swimming experience that’s different from your normal routine.

泳池游泳

Pool Swimming

 

在美国，大多数标准泳池的长度为25码或25米，被称为短池。许多酒店、汽车旅馆和健身场所由于空间限制，泳池的长度通常只有20码，有时甚至只有15码。长池的泳道长度为50米（这是奥运会标准泳池的长度），宽度大多为25码或25米，这样在某些时期或季节，可以在泳池中划线，以适应短池游泳的需求。

Most lap pools in the United States are either 25 yards or 25 meters in length and are referred to as short-course pools. In many hotel, motel, and fitness facilities, space limits a pool’s size to 20 yards in length, sometimes even to 15 yards. Long-course pools have 50-meter lanes (this is the length of an Olympic-size pool), and most are either 25 yards or 25 meters wide so that, during certain periods or seasons, the lane lines can be installed across the pool to allow for short-course swimming.

标准的游泳训练池只需满足以下条件：水质干净清澈，水深至少一米，以及能够抑制波浪的泳道标记。泳道标记由绷紧的缆绳组成，缆绳上系有直径 8 至 13 厘米（3 至 5 英寸）的浮标和圆盘，贯穿整个泳池。它们划定并控制游泳训练区域，并吸收大部分水面波浪。理想情况下，泳池最好有一段深水区——你将学习的几个训练动作就需要用到深水区。

The only requirements for a lap pool are clean, clear water that is at least a meter deep and wave-quelling lane markers, which are tightly stretched cables with 3- to 5-inch (8 to 13 cm) diameter floats and discs that run the length of the pool. They define and control the space for swimming laps and absorb most surface waves. Ideally, you’ll find a pool that has a section with deep water—there are a couple of drills you will learn that will require it.

华氏78度到82度（摄氏25.5度到27.8度）被认为是游泳训练的最佳温度范围。华氏78度一开始可能会感觉有点冷，但游一会儿之后就会觉得很舒服。在华氏82度以上的水中进行剧烈运动会让人感觉过热，而在华氏85度（摄氏29.4度）以上的水中则有过热的风险。另一方面，只要坚持锻炼以维持体温，大多数人都能逐渐适应华氏60多度（摄氏十几度到二十几度）的水温。室内游泳池的温度通常控制在一两度以内。室外游泳池的温度受天气影响更大，但在某些地区，室外游泳池全年开放。冬季，它们使用燃气、太阳能或地热系统加热；夏季，则使用曝气或地热系统冷却。

78 to 82 degrees Fahrenheit (25.5 to 27.8 degrees Celsius) is considered an optimal temperature range for lap swimming. 78 degrees will likely seem cold at first, but once you have been moving for a while, it’ll feel fine. A strenuous workout in water over 82 degrees can get uncomfortably warm, and in water over 85 degrees Fahrenheit (29.4 degrees Celsius), you can risk overheating. On the other end of the spectrum, most people can adapt over time to temperatures in the high 60s Fahrenheit (upper teens to low 20s Celsius) as long as they continue working hard enough to maintain body temperature. Temperature in indoor pools is usually controlled within a degree or two. Outdoor pool temperatures are affected more by the weather, but in some parts of the country, outdoor pools operate year-round. They are heated with gas, solar, or geothermal systems in the winter and they are cooled by aeration or geothermal systems in the summer.

游泳者经常抱怨氯，因为它会顽固地附着在皮肤和头发上。长期接触氯还会使头发变得像稻草一样干枯毛躁。皮肤和头发会吸收水分，尤其是在刚沾水的时候。如果先淋浴，让自来水先被吸收，就能有效阻隔泳池水的氯含量，而泳池水的氯含量通常是自来水的2到10倍。戴泳帽效果更佳，尤其是在湿发上涂抹少量护发素之后。

Swimmers commonly complain about chlorine, which tenaciously attaches itself to the skin and hair. Consistent exposure can also make hair feel and act like straw. Your skin and hair absorb water, mostly when you first get wet. If you take a shower, so that tap water is absorbed first, it tends to block out pool water, which typically has 2 to 10 times as much chlorine as tap water. A cap will help even more, especially if you rub a dab of conditioner into your wet hair first.

游泳礼仪
 

无论你是参加团体游泳训练，还是独自一人在拥挤的泳道游泳，你都难免会不时地与他人共用泳道。如果每个人都了解并遵守基本的游泳礼仪，那么大家的游泳时光都会更加愉快。你肯定不想在几乎赤身裸体的时候被指控行为不端吧？

请阅读标牌您的泳池可能设有标牌，上面列有当地游泳礼仪、泳道速度、圈泳路线、器材使用等方面的规定。如有，请遵守张贴的规则。

请将所有个人物品整齐地堆放在泳池边，以便为其他游泳者的物品留出空间，并尽量减少绊倒的风险。请在您的个人物品上做好标记，以免混淆。

香水、护发产品、护肤品：一小部分人对各种护发和护肤品中的香料过敏。运动时深呼吸以及水中氯气引起的鼻腔刺激，往往会导致更多游泳者在运动过程中对这些香料格外敏感。含香料的护发和护肤品会随水流进入泳池，并在水面聚集，正好在人们的鼻子下方。即使是无香型产品最终也会进入泳池——进而进入其他游泳者的耳朵、眼睛、鼻子和嘴巴。因此，请在下水前淋浴。

口腔卫生：您会和其他呼吸急促的人一起游泳。为了避免尴尬，也为了让他人感到舒适愉快，请在游泳前刷牙并使用漱口水。

运动饮料和咖啡：拥挤的泳道尽头通常会摆放着许多饮料瓶。务必清楚地标记你的饮料，以免在运动过程中造成混乱。即使盖上盖子，咖啡也绝不适合在泳池边饮用。咖啡气味浓烈，很容易飘过好几条泳道。许多人深呼吸时会觉得这种气味令人不适（甚至恶心）。（关于咖啡口气，请参见上一段。）

选择和进入泳道：切勿贸然进入已有其他游泳者的泳道。找到一条与你速度相近的泳道，并与他们沟通，让他们知道你即将加入。如果他们不停地游，请先将脚滑入泳道右侧角落，并在那里停留足够长的时间，让所有泳者都游过一遍，并确认有新的泳者即将加入。然后，以与该泳道其他泳者相同的速度开始游动。

环形泳道：泳道内三名或三名以上游泳者必须以环形泳道游动，以避免正面碰撞——每位游泳者都应保持在泳道右侧。每位游泳者之间应至少保持五秒钟的距离。如果您因任何原因停止游泳，您有责任避开仍在游泳的其他人。

就像骑自行车一样，游泳时紧跟在别人身后可以让你受益于对方的努力。你或许会想挤在别人身后，让对方承担大部分的体力，但这被认为是不礼貌的，而且可能会引发更衣室里的闲言碎语。

即使在水平相当的泳道中，在环形游泳时，超车和被超车有时也难以避免。一般来说，超车者应该游到泳道中央，加速，并迅速完成超越。速度较慢的游泳者应该预判被超越，靠近泳道绳，稍微减速，让速度较快的游泳者快速通过。在泳道角落短暂停留，让速度较快的游泳者转身领先也是可以的。如果有人轻拍你的脚，表示他想超越你——请相应地做出反应。如果你频繁地超车或被超越，你可能应该换一条泳道。

靠墙处：无论泳道内有多少游泳者，每个人都有责任保持泳道中间三分之一区域畅通，以便其他正在转身或冲线的游泳者通行。当你在靠墙处停下时，请迅速移动到泳道角落。

己所不欲，勿施于人。尊重你的同车道伙伴，并期望他们也同样尊重你。即使车道拥挤，只要每个人都秉持这种态度，也能带来愉悦的体验。

派对结束后，锻炼结束后请立即离开泳道，让其他人使用。

Lap-Swimming Etiquette
 

Whether swimming as part of a group workout or just by yourself during a crowded lap-swim session, you are likely to share lane space with others from time to time. Everyone’s water time is more enjoyable when everyone knows and lives by the basic rules of swimming etiquette. You don’t want to be charged with antisocial behavior while nearly naked.

Read the Signs Your pool may have signs with the local guidelines for swimming etiquette, lane speed, circle patterns, use of equipment, and the like. If so, follow the posted rules.

Equipment Neatly stack any personal equipment at the pool’s edge in order to leave room for other swimmers’ equipment and to minimize tripping hazards. Mark your personal equipment to avoid confusion.

Fragrances, Hair Products, Skin Products A small percentage of people are adversely sensitive to the fragrances in various hair and skin products. Deep breathing during exercise and nasal irritation from chlorine in the water tend to make a larger percentage of swimmers ultrasensitive during workouts. Fragrant hair and skin products rinse off in the pool and become concentrated at the surface, right under people’s noses. Even fragrance-free products end up in the pool—and thus in other swimmers’ ears, eyes, noses, and mouths. Please, take a shower before you hit the water.

Oral Hygiene You will be breathing heavily near other heavy breathers. Avoid embarrassment and make your presence a joy to others by brushing your teeth and using mouthwash just before hitting the water.

Sports Drinks and Coffee A crowded lane usually has a number of beverage bottles at the end of it on the deck. Be sure to mark yours plainly to avoid midworkout confusion. Coffee is never an appropriate pool-edge beverage, even with a lid on your cup. It has a strong odor that easily wafts across several lanes. Many people find the odor unpleasant (or downright nauseating) when breathing deeply. (As for coffee breath, see the previous paragraph.)

Selecting and Entering a Lane Never dive into a lane that has people swimming in it. Find a lane where swimmers of your speed are doing their laps and communicate with them so that they know that you are about to join them. If they are swimming nonstop, slip feet-first into the right-hand corner of the lane and stay there long enough for everyone to cycle through the lane and to see that a new swimmer is about to join the fray. Then begin swimming at the same speed as the rest of the people in that lane.

Circle Pattern Three or more swimmers in a lane must swim in a circle pattern in order to avoid head-on collisions—each swimmer stays to the right of the lane. Each swimmer should leave at least a five-second gap between himself or herself and the next swimmer. If you stop for any reason, it is your responsibility to stay out of the way of everyone who is still swimming.

Drafting Just as in cycling, swimming close behind somebody allows you to benefit from the effort of that swimmer. It may be tempting to tuck in behind someone and let that swimmer do most of the work, but it is considered bad form and can lead to ugly locker-room gossip.

Passing and Getting Passed Even in well-matched lanes, passing or getting passed is sometimes unavoidable when circle swimming. In general, the person doing the passing should move to the center of the lane, speed up, and finish the pass quickly. The slower swimmer should anticipate being passed, stay close to the lane rope, slow down a bit, and let the faster swimmer pass quickly. Stopping briefly in the corner to allow a faster swimmer to turn and take the lead is okay. A tap on your foot means someone wants to pass you—act accordingly. If you are frequently passing people or being passed, you probably belong in another lane.

At the Wall Regardless of how many swimmers are using a lane, it is everyone’s responsibility to keep clear the center third of the wall for other swimmers who are either turning or finishing. When you stop at the wall, move quickly to a corner of the lane.

Do Unto Others Treat your lane partners with respect and expect the same from them. Even a crowded lane can be a joy when everyone has this attitude.

When the Party’s Over As soon as you’ve finished your workout, leave the lane and let someone else use it.

 

公开水域游泳

Open-Water Swimming

 

许多游泳爱好者更喜欢在更自然的水域游泳，而不是沿着黑线游泳。几乎在任何水温高于华氏55度（摄氏12.8度）的洁净水域，都能找到开放水域游泳爱好者的身影。专家一致认为，您应该始终在有专人监管的开放水域游泳。如果您独自游泳，尤其是在不熟悉的水域或不习惯的环境下，很容易遇到危险。在有专人监管的开放水域游泳是积累长距离游泳经验的绝佳方式，它能赋予这项运动全新的体验。不妨尝试一下在海洋、湖泊或采石场游泳。这才是真正长距离游泳的场所——其他一切都只是练习而已。

Many swimmers eschew the black line for a more natural setting. Virtually anywhere you can find clean water warmer than 55 degrees Fahrenheit (12.8 degrees Celsius), you will find open-water swimming enthusiasts. Experts agree that you should always swim in a properly supervised open-water swimming area. You can easily get into trouble if you swim on your own, especially if you are swimming in an unfamiliar area or in conditions you aren’t used to. Properly supervised, open-water swimming is a great way to log many unfettered miles, and it gives the sport a whole new feel. Try an ocean, lake, or quarry swim sometime. This is where true distance swimming takes place—everything else is just practice.

第三章
 
评估您的游泳体能
 

你已经向凯撒献上贡品，换取了一整袋游泳装备，并且找到了一处近乎完美的游泳胜地。在你纵身跃入碧蓝的海水中尽情畅游之前，还有一项任务需要完成：你必须了解自己目前的游泳水平。本章将定义什么是游泳水平，并介绍两种游泳测试方法，这两种方法结合起来可以精确地评估你的游泳水平。

You have rendered unto Caesar in return for a full bag of swim goodies, and you have located a near-perfect swimming hole. There remains one task to complete before you launch yourself into the blue and start stroking with abandon. You must get a feel for your current level of swimming fitness. This chapter defines what swimming fitness is and describes two types of swimming tests that, in combination, will pinpoint your level of swimming fitness.

定义游泳健身

Defining Swimming Fitness

 

我对游泳体能的定义如下：体能是指能够根据自身情况，在任意强度和时长内，运用已掌握的游泳技巧。体能水平因具体任务而异。一个人可能擅长长跑或骑行，但可能完全不适合游泳。一个人可能擅长长距离游泳，但却无法完成泳池一圈的冲刺。

My operating definition of fitness for swimming is as follows: Fitness is the ability to express the technique you have developed over whatever time you choose, at whatever intensity you choose. Fitness is specific to the task at hand. A person may have a high level of fitness for distance running or for cycling yet be completely unfit for swimming. A person might be fit for swimming long distances yet be unfit for sprinting one length of the pool.

健康与健身这两个词经常被放在一起提及，仿佛它们密不可分。虽然体能水平高的人更有可能保持健康，但反过来却不一定成立。你可能身体健康，没有疾病和伤痛，但却完全无法承受任何长时间或高强度的体力活动。在开始游泳训练计划之前，请咨询医生，确保自己能够承受各种强度运动带来的额外压力。

The terms health and fitness are often used in the same breath, as if they were inseparable. Although it is true that if you have a high level of fitness, you have a greater likelihood of being healthy, the converse is not necessarily true. You can be healthy in the sense of being illness and injury free, yet be completely unprepared for any prolonged or intense physical exertion. Before you start your swimming training program, check with your physician to be sure that you can handle the added stress of exercise at a variety of intensities.

如果您身体健康，并且经常进行高强度锻炼，那么您或许可以以中等速度进行45分钟（或更长时间）的游泳训练，并配合相对较短的休息时间。如果您只是偶尔锻炼或运动强度适中，则可能需要在训练过程中延长休息时间。如果您是NEBAB（从未进行过任何运动），则可能需要更频繁、更长时间的休息，并放慢游泳或练习的速度。如果您体能水平较低，并且期望过高，那么开始一项新的体育活动可能会令人沮丧。即使您很容易感到疲倦或筋疲力尽，也应该将最初几次游泳视为重大成就。从相对不运动的状态转变为一项健身活动是一个巨大的改变，您的身体需要一段时间来适应。坚持下去。您的初始体能水平越低，您在不久的将来获得的益处就越大。

If you are in good health and already exercise vigorously on a regular basis, you can probably handle 45-minute (or longer) swim-training sessions at a moderate pace with relatively short rest periods. If you exercise only occasionally or only at moderate levels, you may need to take longer rest breaks during a training session. If you are a NEBAB (never ever been athletic before), you may need to take frequent, longer breaks and swim or drill more slowly. Beginning a new physical activity when you are at a low fitness level can be frustrating if your expectations are too high. You should count your initial trips to the pool as major accomplishments even if you get tired easily or feel pooped. Moving from relative inactivity into a fitness activity is a big change that takes a while for your body to get used to. Keep after it. The lower your initial fitness level, the greater your rewards will be in the near future.

测试游泳体能

Testing Swim Fitness

 

高效游泳的技巧约占70%，体能仅占30%。一个人可能拥有出色的体能，适合多种运动，但如果缺乏有效的游泳技巧，他无法游得远或快。无效的划水动作会浪费大部分能量，且推进力微乎其微。另一方面，想想一位曾经的精英级竞技游泳运动员，他已经十年没有运动，如今体能状况不佳。尽管他精力有限，但他仍然可能比许多体能更好的人游得更远更快，因为他很久以前养成的良好技术习惯仍然让他能够做出流畅、有力且推进力强的划水动作，从而最大限度地减少能量浪费。

Highly effective swimming is considered to be roughly 70 percent technique and only about 30 percent conditioning. A person may have a high fitness level for a variety of sports, but if he lacks effective swimming technique, he will be unable to swim very far or very fast. His ineffective stroke wastes most of the energy he puts into the effort and produces minimal forward motion. On the other hand, consider the former elite-level competitive swimmer who has been sedentary for 10 years and is now in poor condition. Though he doesn’t have much energy to spare, he’ll likely be able to swim farther and faster than many people who are in better shape, because the excellent technique habits he ingrained long ago still allow him to take long, smooth, effective strokes that are highly propulsive and waste little energy.

要想让游泳训练计划既有趣又高效，训练方案必须同时提升游泳技巧和体能。我鼓励你将本书视为通往高效游泳之路的详细路线图——高效游泳是指将精湛的技巧与良好的体能储备相结合的游泳。在路线图发挥作用之前，你必须先找到“你在这里”的标记。本书介绍的两项游泳测试将作为你通往高效游泳之路的起点。它们将从两个方面精准地测试你当前的游泳水平。在你参与健身游泳计划的过程中，这些测试将不时用于记录你的进步。每次测试后记录的进步将激励你继续前进。是时候穿上你的新泳衣了。你的入学考试即将开始。

For a swimming training program to be enjoyable and productive, the training regimen must enhance both elements of swimming effectiveness—technique and conditioning. I encourage you to think of this book as a detailed roadmap leading to highly effective swimming—swimming that combines the efficiency of great technique and the fitness and energy reserves of great conditioning. Before a map can help you get anywhere, you must locate the “You are HERE” mark. The two swimming tests described here will mark your starting point on the road to highly effective swimming. They will precisely test, in two ways, the effectiveness of your current swimming. And as you engage in the Fitness Swimming program, these tests will be used from time to time to mark your progress along that road. The improvements you chart after each test will help motivate you to continue. It’s time to get your new swimming suit wet. Your entrance exam is about to begin.

T-20 游泳

T-20 Swim

 

T-20游泳测试的目的是测试你在20分钟内能游多远。这项测试是衡量你游泳能力的绝佳实用指标，也是同时评估你的技术和体能水平的理想方法。

The idea of the T-20 swim test is to see how far you can swim in 20 minutes. This test is an excellent practical indicator of your swimming ability and is an ideal way to assess both your technique and conditioning levels at the same time.

1. 在20分钟内，尽可能游得更远，可以使用任何泳姿或泳姿组合。你需要计算游的圈数。（泳池中的一圈是两个泳池长度，也就是说，就像在跑道上一样，游回起点。在25码的泳池中，一圈是50码；在50米的泳池中，一圈是100米。）尽量保持匀速游完整个过程。不要在最后两分钟加速。游泳过程中，如果你需要停下来休息片刻，可以这样做。但是，时间会一直走，这些休息时间也会计入你的游完时间。

1. Swim any stroke or combination of strokes as far as possible in 20 minutes. You must count your laps. (A lap in a pool is two lengths, which means, as on a running track, returning to where you started. In a 25-yard pool, one lap is 50 yards; in a 50-meter pool, one lap is 100 meters.) Strive for an even pace throughout the swim. Do not speed up in the last two minutes of the swim. During the swim, if you need to stop and rest for short periods, you may do so. The clock keeps ticking, however, and these rest periods are part of your elapsed time.

2. 游泳结束时，当计时器显示 20:00 时，完成你当前游的那一圈。记录下你完成这一圈所用的时间。这意味着你的总用时会略超过20:00。（例如，在游泳接近尾声时，你到达池边，计时器显示你已经游了 19:40。你还需要再游一圈。当你完成这一圈时，计时器显示 20:30。现在你完成了。）

2. At the end of the swim, finish the lap you are on when 20:00 ticks by. Note your elapsed time when you complete that lap. This means you will have an elapsed time that is a bit over20:00. (For example, near the end of the swim, you arrive at the wall and the pace clock shows that you have been swimming for 19:40. You need to swim one more lap. When you complete that lap, the clock shows 20:30. Now you are finished.)

3. 游泳结束后，立即测量您的心率（IHR）。如果您有心率监测器，请使用游泳结束后立即显示的读数。否则，请手动测量心率（有关心率及其测量方法的更多信息，请参见第二部分）。

3. Upon completing the swim, take your immediate heart rate (IHR) reading. If you have a heart-rate monitor, use the reading that appears immediately after you finish swimming. Otherwise, take a manual heart rate (more about heart rates and how to take them is included in part II).

 

游泳结束后，请在防水笔记本上记录三项信息，如下例所示。请注意，这些数据仅提供 T-20 测试可能结果的示例，并非您的目标标准。

Once you complete your swim, record in your waterproof notebook three pieces of information, as shown in the following example. Note that these figures provide a sample of possible outcomes for the T-20 test and are not a guideline for you to shoot for.

 

记录完信息后，轻松地游泳或踩水至少五分钟以降温。

Once you have recorded the information, swim or tread water easily for at least five minutes in order to cool down.

游泳结束后，你需要查看并记录你的T-20巡航配速——即你在游泳过程中每100码（或米）的平均配速（参见第206页）。这是你能长时间游出的最快速度，它反映了你的游泳体能和能力水平（在上述例子中，巡航配速为1分38秒4）。之后，你将在本书训练章节的某些练习中学习如何利用巡航配速来确定训练速度和间歇时间。

After your swim, you will look up and record your T-20 cruise pace—your average pace per 100 yards (or meters) during the swim (refer to page 206). This is the fastest pace you can swim for an extended time, and it indicates your combined swimming fitness and ability level (in the above example, it would be 1:38.4). Later you will learn to use your cruise pace to determine training speeds and intervals during some of the practices in the workout section of the book.

您可以经常重复进行T-20游泳测试，比如每周一次。有三种方法可以体现您T-20成绩的提升：平均配速加快（参见附录A中的T-20百米巡航配速表）；配速不变但心率降低；或者平均划水次数减少（随着您阅读本书并开始练习，您会逐渐意识到自己游完一个泳池长度需要多少划水）。长期来看，提升T-20成绩的最佳方法是专注于提高技术和效率。

You can repeat the T-20 swim test often, perhaps once per week. There are three ways to note an improvement in your T-20 performance: if you swim at a faster average pace (T-20 Cruise Pace Per 100 Chart in appendix A), if you swim the same pace but show a lower IHR, or if you have a lower average stroke count (as you read this book and start doing some practices, you will become aware of how many strokes you take to swim a length of the pool). Over the long haul, the best way to make the largest improvements in your T-20 swims is to focus your efforts on technique and efficiency.

完成几次 T-20 测试后，您就会有足够的信心进行 T-30 测试。T-30 测试的原理和执行方式与 T-20 测试相同，只是游泳时间从 20 分钟延长至 30 分钟。请使用附录 B 中的 T-30 测试记录表来记录您在 T-30 测试中的进步。第 202 页提供了一个空白表格，您可以复印后用于记录您的 T-20 和 T-30 测试成绩，以便轻松查看您的进步情况。

After you have swum a few T-20s, you will feel confident enough to do T-30 swims. The concept and execution are the same as with the T-20, except that you swim for 30 minutes instead of 20 minutes. Use the T-30 chart in appendix B to chart your progress in the T-30 tests. See page 202 for a blank chart that you can photocopy and then use to keep track of your T-20 and T-30 swim performances, which will allow you to easily see your progress over time.

 

完成 T-20 游泳测试后，务必立即测量心率。

Be sure to take your heart rate immediately after finishing the T-20 swim test.

 

游泳高尔夫

Swimming Golf

 
游泳高尔夫更考验技术能力而非体能，它可以作为衡量一段时间内技术进步的基准。规则如下：

1. 游50码（或米），数出你划水的总次数——每只手入水时都算一次。（如果你在短池泳池，第一趟划水21次，回程划水22次，总共划水43次。）

1. Swim 50 yards (or meters), counting the total number of strokes you take—count once for each hand as it enters the water. (If you are in a short-course pool and you take 21 strokes on the first length followed by 22 strokes coming back, your total is 43.)

2. 游泳结束后，记录下你用了多少秒。（假设游泳用了 47 秒。）

2. At the end of the swim, note your elapsed swim time in seconds. (Let’s say the swim took 47 seconds.)

3. 将划水次数加上时间（秒数）。总和就是你这次游泳的得分。（例如，43 次划水加上 47 秒，总共是 90 分。）

3. Add the number of strokes to the number of seconds. The total is your score for that swim. (Add the 43 strokes to the 47 seconds for a total of 90.)

4. 尽情休息，然后从第 1 步重复，这次尝试获得更低的分数——因此得名“游泳高尔夫”。

4. Take as much rest as you want, and repeat from number 1, this time attempting to get a lower score—hence the name “swimming golf.”

5. 重复此步骤四次，并计算平均分。下次将游泳高尔夫练习加入训练计划时，这个分数就是你的标准杆。（例如，你的分数分别为 90、89、89、88，那么你的平均分，也就是新的标准杆，就是 89。）

5. Do this four times and average your scores. This is your par the next time you include a swimming golf set in your workout. (Say your scores are 90, 89, 89, 88. Your average, or new par, is 89.)

 

在50码的自由泳中，水平更高的游泳者比水平较低的游泳者划水次数更少，用时更短。在典型的高尔夫大师赛中，50码自由泳的成绩很容易从40多杆到100多杆不等。想要降低杆数，首先要减少划水次数。一旦你适应了较低的划水次数，就尝试在不增加划水次数的情况下提高划水节奏（划水频率）。每次你游出新的、更低的杆数，你的游泳水平就提高了一分。

Over 50 yards, better swimmers take fewer strokes in less time than less-accomplished swimmers. In a typical Masters group, 50-yard freestyle golf scores can easily range from the high 40s to more than 100. Start lowering your scores by lowering your stroke count. Once you get comfortable with a lower stroke count, try to increase stroke tempo (how often you take strokes) without adding any strokes. Every time you hit a new, lower score, you have become a better swimmer.

如果你和别人一起游泳，游泳高尔夫可以让不同水平的人进行一对一的较量。两位经验丰富的游泳高尔夫选手可以轮流游50米，然后将每次的成绩与自己的标准杆进行比较，并记录几个50米的成绩。在游泳间隙用防水笔记本记下数字，可以轻松追踪你的成绩。你可以复印第203页上的空白游泳高尔夫（SGolf）成绩表，以便记录你的游泳高尔夫成绩，从而轻松查看你的进步情况。

If you swim with others, swimming golf allows people of different abilities to compete head to head. Two experienced swimming golfers can take turns swimming 50s and then compare their score for each swim to their personal par, keeping score over several 50s. Jotting down numbers in your waterproof notebook between swims makes it easy to keep track of your scores. You can photocopy the blank Swimming Golf (SGolf) Performances chart, found on page 203, in order to to keep track of your swimming-golf performances so that you can easily see your progress over time.

第二部分
 
正确的游泳方式
 

说实话，人类的身体并非为游泳而生。人类并非天生就该一头扎进河里追逐猎物。上帝赋予了最伟大的猿类以理性，于是飞钓竿应运而生。如果一个人不慎落入河中，本能地抬起头仰望天空，拼命挣扎，最终将毛茸茸的身体爬回岸边，这足以满足眼前的生存需求。然而，文明的进步使得我们这些处于食物链顶端的生物得以在闲暇之余改造自然。因此，我们在水上旅行领域取得了一些进展。

Let’s face it: The human body wasn’t designed for swimming. Human beings were not intended to leap headlong into a river and chase after their dinner. God gave the greatest of the apes the power of reason and thus the fly rod came to be. If a person should fall into that river, the instinct to lift his head toward the heavens, thrash about wildly, and scrabble his hairy carcass back onto the shore would serve immediate survival needs well enough. The advance of civilization, however, has allowed those of us at the top of the food chain to spend our idle time tinkering with nature. As such, we have made modest progress in the area of aquatic travel.

迄今为止，最受欢迎的泳姿是自由泳。在竞技游泳中，有四种正式泳姿——蝶泳、仰泳、蛙泳和自由泳。前三种泳姿都有非常具体且严格的规则，规定了运动员如何完成动作。相比之下，根据规则，自由泳比赛允许运动员以任何方式完成，只要其在游完规定距离的过程中，不能借助池底、池壁或泳道绳来推进即可。

By far, the most popular swimming stroke is the freestyle stroke. In competitive swimming, there are four regulation strokes—butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke, and freestyle. The first three have very specific and constraining rules that govern how you perform the strokes. In contrast, according to the rules, a freestyle event may be swum in any manner the swimmer chooses as long as she or he completes the distance without using the bottom or sides of the pool or the lane ropes for propulsion.

大多数游泳运动员在自由泳比赛中都会选择某种形式的自由泳。这是因为，如果游得当，自由泳是水中移动速度最快、效率最高的泳姿。因此，“自由泳”一词已成为自由泳的标准术语。除了速度最快之外，自由泳也是最容易学习的泳姿，因此深受健身游泳者的喜爱。本书将完全专注于自由泳的技巧提升和训练。然而，我在本书中描述和融入训练计划的许多概念、基本原理和练习方法也适用于其他三种泳姿中的一种或多种。

Most swimmers choose some variation of the crawl stroke for freestyle events. This is because, when swum properly, the crawl is the fastest, most efficient method of moving through the water. Thus, the term freestyle has become the standard term for the crawl. In addition to being the fastest stroke, freestyle is the easiest to learn and is therefore the overwhelming favorite of fitness swimmers. I concentrate entirely on refining and training the freestyle stroke in this book. Nevertheless, many of the concepts, fundamentals, and drills that I describe and build into the workouts in this book also apply to one or more of the other three strokes.

跑步和骑行在很大程度上都涉及相对简单且本能的运动模式和动作幅度。运动员发现，在这两项运动中，速度、耐力和技巧都能通过增加训练量或加大训练强度而显著提高。因此，大多数跑步和骑行训练计划主要侧重于体能训练而非技术训练。游泳则完全不同。它包含一系列复杂的重复性、节奏性动作。流畅高效的游泳动作所需的协调性几乎难以想象。而且，由于游泳的动作和姿势绝非自然，我们发现“多做”并不足以提高技术。

Running and, to a large extent, cycling involve relatively simple and instinctive patterns and ranges of motion. Athletes have found that in both sports, speed, endurance, and technique all improve dramatically by simply training more or harder. This is why most running and cycling training regimens concentrate chiefly on conditioning rather than on technique. Swimming is an entirely different animal. It involves a complex set of repetitive, rhythmic motions. The level of coordination required to execute fluid, efficient swimming strokes is almost beyond comprehension. And because swimming motions and positions are by no means natural, we find that “just doing it” isn’t enough to improve technique.

当我们观看运动员表演时，我们的目光，以及由此而来的注意力，自然会被吸引到动作幅度最大的部位——投手投球的手臂、高尔夫球手的手臂和球杆、空手道大师的手臂和腿。因此，我们往往以四肢为起点来描述和学习这些运动。然而，在这些运动中，最关键的动作和姿势都始于身体的核心，并由此向外辐射。如果不能掌握中线姿势、平衡以及四肢相对于核心的协调性，投手就会投出软绵绵的球，高尔夫球手就会把球切短到水草丛里，空手道选手最终也会摔倒在地。游泳也是如此，我们往往几乎完全专注于手臂的动作，而对腿部的关注则相对较少。因此，大多数自学游泳的人往往只关注手臂和腿部的动作。他们用力向后划水，希望以此推动自己前进；他们依靠蹬腿的力量像快艇一样推动身体前进，并像拖着货物一样拖着上半身前进。结果通常是费力地在泳道上挣扎，而不是流畅优美的划水。

When we watch athletes perform, our eyes, and thus our attention, are naturally drawn to where we see the largest motions—a pitcher’s throwing arm, a golfer’s arms and club, a karate master’s arms and legs. As a result, we tend to describe and then learn these sports using the appendages as a starting point. Yet in each of these sports, the most critical actions and postures begin in, and radiate from, the body’s core. Without mastery of central-line posture, balance, and coordination of the appendages relative to the core, the pitcher tosses cream puffs, the golfer slices short into the weeds, and the karateka winds up on the mat. Similarly with swimming, we tend to focus almost entirely on the motions of the arms and, to a lesser degree, the legs. Thus, most self-taught swimmers tend to swim by focusing on just their arms and legs. They yank their arms backward through the water with the hope that this will move them forward; they rely on their kick to push them forward like a motorboat and to haul their torso along like cargo. The result is usually an effort-filled struggle down the lane rather than a flow of graceful strokes.

第二部分采用由内而外的教学方法，旨在提高游泳的有效性。在第四章​​中，你将学习如何运用核心肌群，将身体的关键部位协调起来，形成一个适合游泳的“船”。接下来，你将学习并掌握在各种姿势和动作中保持完全支撑的水中平衡。你将学习如何运用身体最大的肌肉群来驱动自由泳的基本动作。第五章介绍了完整的划水动作，并提供了练习方法来提升你的划水技巧。这种方法先奠定概念和技能的基础，然后以逻辑清晰、循序渐进的方式逐步提升。
