Part II employs an inside-out approach to teaching highly effective swimming. In chapter 4, you’ll learn how to use your core muscles to organize your critical body masses into a water-worthy vessel. Next, you’ll learn and master fully-supported aquatic balance in a variety of positions and through a variety of motions. You’ll learn how to drive the fundamental motions of freestyle swimming with the largest muscles in the body. Chapter 5 introduces full-stroke swimming and provides drills for building your stroke. This approach lays down a foundation of concepts and skills, then builds on that foundation in a logical sequence of manageable steps.

认真练习游泳技巧能让你不断进步，而体能训练则是练习这些技巧的自然结果。相比之下，漫无目的地在泳池两端来回游动，就像试图通过在网球底线之间来回奔跑来提高球技一样。你凭直觉就知道，要想成为一名优秀的网球运动员，你需要练习反手击球、正手击球、落点控制、发球等技巧，然后在比赛中运用这些技巧。游泳也是如此。

Carefully practicing the skills of swimming allows you to continually improve, while conditioning becomes a by-product of the effort spent practicing those skills. In contrast, mindlessly plodding back and forth between the end walls is like trying to improve your tennis game by simply running back and forth between the baselines of the court. You know intuitively that in order to become an excellent tennis player, you need to practice backhand drills, forehand drills, shot-placement drills, serving drills, and then to use those skills as you play the game. So too with swimming.

我的体能训练计划围绕着练习展开，每个章节的难度都会逐渐增加，但这些练习旨在锻炼肌肉并扩大运动范围，从而为长距离重复这些技能做好准备。每个练习都配有一个或多个反馈工具，帮助你判断自己的动作是否正确。

My conditioning program is built around practicing drills and exercises that become increasingly complex with each chapter but that condition the muscles and ranges of motion that are required for repeating those skills over long distances. Each drill has one or more feedback tools that will help you determine whether you are doing the drill correctly.

本书的这一部分也运用了许多重点，每个重点都将一个复杂的概念提炼成几个简单的词语。请特别注意这些重点，因为我在正文和训练中会反复提及它们。这些概念不仅在本书的其余部分中至关重要，而且在你继续游泳的整个过程中都将发挥重要作用。

In this part of the book, I also use numerous focus points, each of which distills a complex concept down to a few words. Pay special attention to these points, because I refer to them repeatedly throughout the text and workouts. The concepts will be important not only throughout the rest of the book but for as long as you continue swimming.

第四章
 
姿势与平衡
 

了解人体与水的相互作用至关重要。这包括了解你所处介质的特性，以及如何调整和控制身体，从而最大限度地发挥水的益处，同时最大限度地减少其不利影响。本章将介绍水中运动的各种阻力，以及如何通过调整姿势和平衡来避免大部分阻力。接下来，本章将详细介绍各种练习和重点，帮助你改善姿势和平衡能力。后续章节将教授有效的划水技巧。在潜入水中之前，让我们先来探索一下这片陌生的水环境以及我们与它之间的关系。

It is important to understand how the human body interacts with the water. This involves understanding the nature of the medium through which you are moving and understanding how to orient and control your body to maximize the beneficial effects of water while minimizing its detrimental effects. This chapter covers various types of resistance to aquatic motion and how posture and balance can help you avoid much of that resistance. Then it details a variety of drills and focus points that will help you improve your posture and balance skills. Subsequent chapters teach you effective stroke technique. Before diving in, let’s explore the alien aquatic environment and how we relate to it.

对水流运动的阻力

Resistance to Aquatic Motion

 

游泳者的大部分能量都用于克服阻力。即使是世界级游泳运动员，超过90%的能量也用于克服阻力，只有不到10%的能量转化为前进的动力。对于水平较低的游泳者来说，可能只有2%的能量能够转化为前进的动力。你的游泳水平的提升很大程度上取决于你如何应对（或者更准确地说，是如何避免）各种类型的阻力。但要做到这一点，你需要更深入地了解阻力，以及如何运用各种策略来最大限度地减少阻力的影响。

Most of a swimmer’s energy is used to overcome resistance. Even world-class swimmers spend more than 90 percent of their swimming energy overcoming resistance, and less than 10 percent translates into forward motion. For less accomplished swimmers, as little as 2 percent of expended effort yields forward progress. Much of your swimming improvement will come from learning how to combat (or, more accurately, avoid) several types of resistance. To do this, though, you need to understand more about resistance and about the general strategies you’ll employ to minimize its effects.

外部电阻

External Resistance

 

由于水的密度大约是空气的800倍，因此会对在其中运动的物体产生很大的阻力。游泳者会受到三种主要的阻力：形状阻力、波浪阻力和表面阻力。形状阻力是指物体在水中运动时由于其形状而产生的阻力（图4.1a ）。减少与迎面而来的水接触的前表面面积可以降低形状阻力（图4.1b ）。这意味着在游泳时要始终保持身体平衡，尽可能接近水平，并保持身体修长。这也意味着要避免不必要的动作。如果你的体态非常流线型，那么任何动作都会增加形状阻力，因此要避免任何除了推进自身所需的最小动作之外的动作。就像造船师会为赛艇设计细长的锥形船体而不是扁平的方形船体一样，你也需要调整身体的形状和轮廓，以便在水中游动——并且要在游泳时保持这种形状。理解并运用平衡和流线型概念的游泳者可以显著降低形状阻力。

Because water is roughly 800 times denser than air, it offers strong resistance to a body moving through it. There are three major types of resistance, or drag, acting on a swimmer: form drag, wave drag, and surface drag. Form drag is the resistance that results from the shape of an object moving through the water (figure 4.1a). Reducing the front surface area that meets the oncoming water reduces form drag (figure 4.1b). This means always keeping the body balanced as close to horizontal as possible, as well as keeping it long and narrow, while swimming. It also means eliminating unnecessary motions. If you are perfectly streamlined, any motion you make increases form drag, so avoid any movement other than the minimum necessary to propel yourself. Just as a boat builder shapes long, tapered hulls instead of flat, square hulls for a racing boat, you want to taper the form and profile of your body for traveling through the water—and you want to maintain that form as you swim. A swimmer who understands and applies the concepts of balance and streamlining can dramatically reduce form drag.

波浪阻力是产生尾流的结果。为了在水面上前进，身体必须划开挡路的水流。这会形成一个向外传播的波浪。划开更宽的路径意味着必须更远、更快地推动水流才能将其推开，从而产生更大的波浪。波浪越大，游泳者消耗在水流上的能量就越多。在自由泳中，你需要尽可能多地保持身体两侧的姿势，而不是平躺在水面上，从而尽量在水面上划出一条狭窄的路径。

Wave drag is the result of creating a wake. For the body to move forward through the surface of the water, it must move water out of the way. This creates a wave that travels away from the body. Cutting a wider path through the surface means that the water must be pushed further and faster to get it out of the way, which creates a bigger wave. The bigger the wave, the more energy the swimmer gives away to the water. In freestyle, you try to cut a narrow path through the surface by maximizing the time you spend on the sides of your body rather than flat on the belly.

水面阻力是指物体在水中运动时因摩擦力而产生的阻力。减少水面阻力并非依靠技术，而是通过准备和装备来实现。合身的泳衣和泳帽有助于达到这一目的。在比赛中，剃除体毛并穿着特制的高科技低阻力泳衣是常见的做法。

Surface drag is the resistance caused by the frictional force of a moving body in water. You can reduce surface drag not through technique but through preparation and equipment. Properly fitting swimsuits and swimming caps help achieve this result. For competition, shaving body hair and wearing special high-tech, low-drag swimsuits are common practices.

运用你的感官来感知身体哪些部位在与水搏斗。仔细聆听是否有水花四溅或扑通作响的声音，并努力消除这些声音。尝试让身体的每个部位都做出流畅、平稳的动作，而不是像推土机一样横冲直撞。观察周围水中是否有大气泡或大量气泡。它们是造成水流湍急的明显标志。

Use your senses to give you feedback about places on your body where you are fighting the water. Listen for splashing or kerplunking sounds and try to eliminate them. Try to make smooth, flowing movements, instead of bulldozing movements, with every part of your body. Look for large or numerous bubbles in the water around you. They are a sure sign that you are causing turbulence.

 

图 4.1游泳时最大的阻力来源是形状阻力(a)。减少与来流水接触的前表面面积(b)可以显著降低形状阻力。

Figure 4.1The largest source of resistance in swimming is form drag (a). Reducing the front surface area that meets the oncoming water (b)can dramatically reduce form drag.

 

本书介绍的技术将帮助你减少或消除这些阻力因素，从而停止浪费能源。

The technique work presented in this book will help you reduce or eliminate these drag indicators and thereby stop wasting energy.

内阻

Internal Resistance

 

阻力并非游泳者面临的唯一阻力。还有三种内部阻力：被动阻力、主动阻力和惯性。被动阻力是由关节周围的软组织造成的，这些软组织限制了游泳者的运动范围。优秀的游泳者能够游到或伸展到运动范围的极限，此时结缔组织开始阻碍并限制进一步的运动。

Drag is not the only type of resistance with which a swimmer contends. There are three kinds of internal resistance as well: passive resistance, active resistance, and inertia. Passive resistance is caused by the soft connective tissues that surround joints and restrict a swimmer’s range of motion (ROM). Effective swimmers move through, or stretch to, the ends of their ranges of motion, where connective tissues begin to oppose and limit further motion.

主动阻力是指肌肉之间相互对抗。在学习新技能或提升现有技能时，神经肌肉系统会激活比完成所需动作多得多的肌纤维。这些额外的肌纤维中有很多会相互拮抗——就像一群人试图把一辆车往几个不同的方向推一样。此外，有些人天生或性格就比其他人更容易紧张。那些总是像绷紧的弹簧一样，浑身充满蓄势待发的能量的人，往往会有很多肌纤维相互对抗。

Active resistance occurs when muscles work against each other. When first learning new skills, or when improving established skills, your neuromuscular system fires many more muscle fibers than are necessary to complete the desired actions. Many of these extra fibers work antagonistically against each other—a bit like a bunch of guys trying to push one car in several different directions. In addition, some people are, by nature or disposition, tenser than others. The person who is always wound up like a tight spring, bouncing and vibrating with just-waiting-to-be-unleashed energy, will have lots of muscle fibers working against others.

惯性是指身体静止在沙发上时倾向于保持静止状态，而不是拿起泳包走向游泳池。无需多言。

Inertia is the tendency for a body at rest on the couch to remain at rest on the couch—instead of grabbing the swim bag and heading to the pool. ’Nuff said.

随着你不断改进划水技术，避免无效的动作幅度，并通过定期拉伸来提高柔韧性，从而减少不必要的肌肉紧张或活动范围不足带来的内在阻力。当你能够以放松流畅的方式完成动作时，神经肌肉系统会减少不必要的肌肉纤维激活，从而降低因肌肉阻力而损失的能量。如果你像大多数运动员一样，制定了训练计划，那么对进步的预期将极大地帮助你克服“沙发惰性”。

The internal resistance of unwanted muscle tension or of poor range of motion will be reduced as you refine your stroke technique to avoid ineffective ranges of motion and improve your flexibility by regularly stretching into effective ranges. As you get better at performing skills in a relaxed and fluid manner, the neuromuscular system will fire fewer unnecessary muscle fibers, thus reducing the amount of energy lost to active muscular resistance. If you are like most athletes who undertake a planned program, the anticipation of improving will do wonders for overcoming couch inertia.

本书中的练习和训练方法将帮助你最大限度地减少游泳时遇到的各种阻力。阻力越小，你的训练效率就越高。你将更好地掌控自己的训练，展现更专业的游泳技巧，享受更多乐趣，并乐于再次投入训练。

The drills and training approach in this book will help you to minimize resistance of all kinds in your swimming. The less resistance you work against, the more efficient you will be. You will have greater control over your workout, look more proficient as a swimmer, have more fun, and feel better about doing it all again.

水中姿势与平衡

Aquatic Posture and Balance

 

人类进化成能够在陆地上直立行走并有效活动。在孩提时代，你就学会了陆地上的姿势和平衡，并终生运用这些技巧。然而，这些在陆地上行之有效的姿势和平衡在水中却远非如此。你明白平衡在陆地上至关重要——在陆地上，你做任何事情之前都会先保持平衡。然而，大多数游泳者的姿势和平衡都很差，因为在水中保持良好姿势和平衡所需的技能既非本能也非直觉。在水中，正如在陆地上一样，不良的姿势和平衡会妨碍你正确地完成其他游泳技巧。本节将教你什么是有效的水中姿势和平衡，以及如何做到它们。

Human beings have evolved to function effectively on land in an upright position. Early in childhood, you learned land-based posture and balance that you have subsequently used throughout your life. The posture and balance that serve you well on land, however, do not serve you nearly as well in the water. You understand that balance is essential on land—you simply never choose to do anything on land without first getting balanced. Yet most swimmers swim with poor posture and balance, because the skills needed for good posture and balance in the aquatic environment are neither instinctive nor intuitive. In the water, just as on land, poor posture and poor balance will prevent you from correctly performing other swimming skills. This section teaches you what effective aquatic posture and balance are and how to achieve them.

姿势

Posture

 

我把游泳的人比作皮划艇。皮划艇是一种高效的水上交通工具。它前进起来毫不费力，一旦开始前进，就能保持前进的势头。现在想象一下，把这艘皮划艇切成三段——前部、中部和后部——然后用弹力绳松松地绑在一起。很明显，你会得到一艘效率低得多的皮划艇——稳定性更差，划起来更费力，而且根本无法操控。

I liken a swimming human being to a kayak. A kayak is an efficient design for an aquatic vessel. It takes little effort to make it move forward, and once it is moving, it wants to keep moving. Now imagine cutting that kayak into three pieces—front, center, and rear—then tying them back together loosely with bungee cords. It is clear that you’d have a much less effective kayak—less stable, tougher to paddle, and positively impossible to maneuver.

游泳的人也是一艘水上交通工具。为了学会塑造和控制这艘“船”，游泳者必须专注于身体的三个部分——头部、胸部和臀部。如果没有良好的姿势，尽管有脊柱、肌肉、肌腱、韧带和筋膜等结构和组织将它们连接起来，这三个部分仍然会各自独立运动，就像一艘由三段式结构和弹力绳连接的皮划艇。但是，当这三个部分被拉成一条笔直且紧密相连的线时，人体就更像一艘整体式的皮划艇了。

A swimming human being is also an aquatic vessel. In learning to shape and control that vessel, a swimmer must focus on three bodily sections—the head, thorax, and hips. Without good posture, each of these sections will move somewhat independently of the others, despite the structures and tissues—the spinal column, muscles, tendons, ligaments, fascia—connecting them, somewhat like a three-piece, bungee-connected kayak. But when the three sections are drawn into a straight and tightly connected line, the human body behaves more like a solid kayak.

你可以背靠墙站立，感受一下正确的水中姿势。如果你的头发扎在脑后（发髻、马尾辫，或者只是把一团头发塞进泳帽里），先放下来。将脚后跟放在离墙几英寸的地方。你的臀部、肩胛骨和头部应该贴着墙。放松时，你的腰椎（下背部）会形成一个弧度，但不会贴着墙（图 4.2a ）。现在，通过收缩下腹部肌肉，将肚脐向脊柱方向拉，来减小或消除这个弧度。这会使你的骨盆倾斜，就像把尾巴缩到身下一样。你要完全用腹部肌肉来完成这个动作，不要用到臀肌。然后，用上腹部肌肉收紧下肋骨（图 4.2b ）。保持腹部肌肉的收紧状态，稍微收下巴，并尝试将后颈靠近墙面。这样可以拉长你的颈线，使你的头顶略微抬高。其目的是使你的三个部分（头部、胸部和臀部）从骨盆底部开始，沿着脊柱向上，一直到头顶，呈一条紧绷的直线（图 4.2 c）。

You can get a feel for good aquatic posture by standing with your back against a wall. If your hair is bunched at the back of your head (a bun, a ponytail, or just a tangle of hair stuffed into your swim cap), first let it down. Place your heels a few inches away from the wall. Your butt, shoulder blades, and head should touch the wall. When you are relaxed, your lumbar spine forms an arch (the small of your back), which does not touch the wall (figure 4.2a). Now decrease or eliminate this arch by contracting your lower abdominal muscles to draw your navel toward your spine. This will tilt your pelvis, as if tucking your tail under. You want to do this entirely with abdominal muscles without involving your gluteal muscles. Then use your upper abdominal muscles to tuck in your lower ribs (figure 4.2b). While holding this abdominal tension, tuck your chin in a bit and try to bring the back of your neck closer to the wall. This should lengthen your neckline, pushing the top of your head a bit higher. The idea is to align your three sections (head, thorax, and hips) in a tight line from the floor of your pelvis, up your spine, and through the top of your head (figure 4.2c).

现在你的身体各部分协调一致，让你比以往任何时候都更高。注意你用哪些肌肉来保持这种挺拔、笔直、高挑的姿势，并克制住想要弯腰驼背的冲动。保持这个姿势，离开墙壁，尝试走动，保持你的身高。尝试深呼吸。先尝试将一只手臂举过头顶，然后再尝试将双臂举过头顶。尝试将头尽可能地转向两侧，但不要让头顶偏离脊柱的直线。一开始，你会发现，在行走和呼吸的同时保持身体各部分紧密排列是一个复杂的任务，但坚持练习——你会越来越容易。学习如何在水中正确地协调身体的三个部分，并在不同强度的游泳中保持这种姿势也需要时间。幸运的是，掌握并保持身体的紧绷线条是少数几种你可以在陆地上有效练习的水上技能之一。此外，普拉提训练可以极大地增强你对如何有效地连接核心肌群和四肢的理解，并可以帮助你加强和锻炼那些在游泳时保持良好姿势的肌肉。

Your body parts are now organized so that you are taller than you have been in a long time. Note what muscles you are using to hold this tight, straight, tall position, and resist the urge to schlump back down to normal height. While continuing to hold this posture, step away from the wall and try walking around, maintaining your full height. Experiment with breathing fully. Experiment with first extending one, then both arms overhead. Experiment with turning your head as far as possible to each side without letting the crown of your head move off your spine line. At first, you will find that keeping your body parts organized in a tight line while walking and breathing is a complex task, but keep practicing—it will get easier. Learning to properly organize your three sections in the water and to maintain that posture as you swim at various intensities also takes time. Luckily, acquiring and keeping a tight line is one of the few aquatic skills you can practice effectively on land. In addition, Pilates training can greatly enhance your understanding of how to effectively link your core and extremities, and it can help you strengthen and condition the muscles that maintain excellent posture while swimming.

 

图 4.2良好的游泳姿势所形成的紧凑线条，比松散、松弛的游泳姿势所形成的线条，能使身体在水中发挥更大的作用。(a)松散的姿势，身体各部分错位；(b)良好的陆地姿势，身体各部分基本对齐；(c)组织良好的水上紧凑线条姿势，身体三个部分完全对齐。

Figure 4.2 The tight line of a well-organized swimming posture creates a far more effective aquatic vessel than the disorganized, relaxed line of a schlumpy swimming posture. (a) Schlumpy posture with body sections out of alignment, (b) good land-based posture with body sections somewhat aligned, (c)well-organized, aquatic tight-line posture with all three body sections fully aligned.

 
 
重点➤紧绷的鱼线
 

本书中，我们将不断强调，保持挺拔的泳姿和紧绷的体态，而不是懒散地游动，能让你更快、更远地滑过水面，同时节省体力。保持体态紧绷所需的肌肉张力，能让你的平衡和推进机制协同运作（而不是像你放松身体姿势时那样相互对抗）。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Tight Line
 

Throughout this book, we’ll keep reinforcing the fact that swimming tall with a tight line, rather than swimming schlumpy, allows you to slip faster and farther through the water with less energy. And the muscular tension used to keep your line tight will allow your balancing and propelling mechanisms to work together (rather than against each other, as they will when you allow yourself to revert to a schlumpy posture).

 

平衡

Balance

 

水中的平衡取决于水中的姿势。一般来说，自由泳的平衡姿势是指头部、胸部、臀部和腿部呈一条直线，与水面平行。这种姿势可以最大限度地减少正面阻力，而正面阻力是游泳者遇到的最大阻力。

Aquatic balance is dependent on aquatic posture. In general, a balanced position for the freestyle stroke is one in which the head, thorax, hips, and legs are all in one line, parallel to the surface of the water. This position allows for minimal frontal resistance, the strongest of the resistance forces a swimmer encounters.

许多游泳者都明白保持身体与水面平行的重要性，但他们的方法却错了——他们用强劲的踢腿将臀部和双腿抬出水面。踢腿会消耗大量的能量。优秀的游泳者采用不同的方法，这种方法只需更少的能量就能达到并保持这种平衡的姿势。它首先要保持良好的水面姿势，同时还要保持头部与水面平行，并压紧浮板（胸部）。

Many swimmers understand the need to have their whole body parallel to the surface, but they go about it the wrong way—by using a strong kick to lift the hips and legs up to the surface. Kicking uses a tremendous amount of energy. Great swimmers use a different approach that requires much less energy to achieve and maintain this balanced position. It starts with maintaining a tight line of good aquatic posture but adds keeping the head in line and pressing the buoy (chest).

你的头部重约10磅，它的位置对你在水中的身体平衡有着很大的影响。你的头顶需要与脊柱保持在一条直线上，并且在不呼吸时，你的鼻子需要正对着泳池底部（图4.3a ）。抬起或倾斜头部偏离这条直线会给你的臀部施加很大的向下压力，导致臀部下沉（图4.3b ）。（你可以很容易地感受到这一点：面朝下躺在地上，双手放在身体两侧，然后抬起头。你会感觉到臀部向下压。）如果你的姿势挺拔，你的头部就会处于正确的位置。但是，抬头向前看的本能会一直很强烈，直到你养成更牢固的习惯，保持头顶与脊柱在同一条直线上。当你保持平衡时，无论是俯卧、侧卧还是仰卧，你的头部只有大约四分之一到三分之一会露出水面，其余部分都会在水下。

Your head, weighing 10 pounds or so, and its position have a great influence on the balance of your body in the water. The crown of your head needs to be in line with your spine, and your nose needs to be pointed straight toward the bottom of the pool when not breathing (figure 4.3a). Lifting or tilting your head off this line puts a large downward force on your hips, causing them to sink (figure 4.3b). (You can easily feel this by lying facedown on the ground, hands at your sides, and lifting your head up off the ground. You will feel your hips press toward the ground.) If your posture is organized tall, your head will be in the right position. But the instinct to lift your head to look forward will remain strong until you have developed an even stronger habit of keeping the crown of your head on your spine line. When balanced, whether on your belly, side, or back, only about one-quarter to one-third of your head will be exposed above the surface. The rest will be under water.

 

图 4.3水中平衡，虚线表示脊柱线。(a)保持头顶与脊柱在一条直线上有助于保持平衡。(b)即使头部稍微离开脊柱线，也会立即且剧烈地使臀部下沉，破坏平衡。

Figure 4.3 Aquatic balance, dotted line depicting the spine line. (a) Keeping the crown of your head in line with your spine will help you stay balanced. (b)Lifting your head off the spine line, even a little bit, will immediately and dramatically drive your hips toward the bottom of the pool, destroying balance.

 

按压浮标也有助于保持平衡。你的肺就像一个浮标，能够托起上半身。相反，你的重心位于肚脐附近，会使你的臀部和腿部下沉（图 4.4a ）。想象一下，一块踢水板放在水面上。如果你将踢水板的一端向下按压，另一端就会上升。同样地，如果你拉紧钓线，那么用力按压浮标使其向下，就能抬高臀部（图 4.4b ）。你用力按压浮标的力越大，水产生的浮力也就越大。拉紧钓线时肌肉的张力会将浮力从浮标传递到脊柱上的其他所有部位。当你按压浮标时，你应该感觉到整个身体略微向下倾斜，完全被水支撑着。

Pressing your buoy will also help keep you balanced. Your lungs are a buoy that tends to float the upper body. By contrast, your center of mass, which is located near your navel, tends to sink your hips and legs (figure 4.4a). Imagine a kickboard placed on the water’s surface. If you press one end of the kickboard toward the bottom, the other end rises. Similarly, if you are holding a tight line, then leaning on your buoy to press it toward the bottom raises the hips (figure 4.4b). The greater the force you lean on your buoy with, the greater the buoyant force the water exerts in response. The muscular tension used to hold a tight line transmits the buoyant forces from your buoy to all other points along your spine line. As you press your buoy, you should feel your entire body tilting slightly downhill, fully supported by the water.

 

图 4.4按压浮标。(a)即使你的姿势正确，如果没有足够的浮标压力，你的身体重心也会下沉到水面以下，双腿也会随之下沉。(b)用胸部倚靠浮标会使你的臀部和双腿抬升到水面附近。

Figure 4.4 Pressing the buoy. (a) Even if your posture is good, without sufficient buoy pressure, your body’s center of gravity will sink below the surface, taking your legs with it. (b)Leaning on your buoy (chest) will raise your hips and legs toward the surface.

 
 
重点➤浮标压力
 

在练习本书中的技巧和游泳训练时，你始终应该努力获得足够的浮力，以完全依靠水的支撑。如果浮力过小，你将被迫使用手臂或腿部来获得额外的支撑。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Buoy Pressure
 

As you practice the drills and swim the workouts in this book, you always should seek to have enough buoy pressure to be completely supported by the water. If there is too little buoy pressure, you will be forced to work with either your arms or legs for artificial support.

 

静态姿势和平衡练习

Static Posture and Balance Drills

 

以下是一系列技巧练习，旨在帮助你在各种姿势下保持正确的身体姿势和平衡。你将练习正确的动作，这些动作最终将成为高效自由泳划水动作的一部分。在开始进行完整训练之前，建议你花一些时间练习这些动作。我还提供了一些练习方法，可以帮助你更好地了解自己与水的关系。

Following are a series of skill drills that teach your body correct posture and balance in a variety of positions. You will practice the correct motions that will eventually be part of an efficient freestyle stroke. You will want to spend some time on each of these drills before you begin doing full workouts. I have included some ways to experiment with the drills that will help you learn more about your relationship with the water.

所有这些练习都应以轻松的踢腿方式进行。建议您在练习任何动作时都穿上脚蹼，直到熟练掌握为止，尤其是在轻松踢腿时进步甚微的情况下。许多游泳者发现，除了全尺寸脚蹼外，一副短脚蹼也能帮助您更好地掌握某些动作。理想情况下，您最终能够赤脚完成所有动作。然而，有些人，特别是那些跑步基础较强的人，脚踝灵活性较差，可能永远无法获得像快艇推水那样直接的推进力。这并不是什么大问题，因为我们的游泳模式并不依赖踢腿来获得这种推进力。但有些练习确实需要以踢腿作为唯一的或主要的推进方式。对于这些练习，如果您踢腿几乎没有或完全没有推进力，那么最好始终使用短脚蹼或全尺寸脚蹼。

Do all these drills with easy kicking. You are encouraged to wear fins as you practice any drill until you master it, especially if you make very little forward progress with easy kicking. Many swimmers find that, in addition to a pair of full-size fins, having a pair of short fins provides a stepping stone on the way to mastering some of the drills. Ideally, you will eventually master all the drills with bare feet. Some people, however, especially those with a strong running background, have poor enough ankle flexibility that they will likely never get much direct propulsion of the motorboat-pushing-you-forward variety. That’s not a large problem, because our paradigm does not rely on the kick for this sort of propulsion when swimming. But some of the drills do use kicking as the sole or primary source of propulsion. For these drills, if you get little or no propulsion from your kick, you may be best served by always using either short or full-size fins.

学会站立和保持平衡是学会走路的前提。同样，学会保持泳姿笔直并在踢腿时保持平衡是高效游泳的前提。本章的静态姿势和平衡练习将帮助你的身体感受良好的水中姿势，并在几种静态姿势下保持平衡，这些姿势下你唯一的动作就是轻柔地踢腿。动态姿势和平衡练习将帮助你学习如何在进行除踢腿以外的其他简单动作时，保持良好的水中姿势和平衡。

Learning to stand up and to be in balance is a prerequisite to learning to walk. Similarly, learning to establish a tight line and to stay balanced while simply kicking is a prerequisite to highly effective swimming. The static posture and balance drills in this chapter will teach your body what it feels like to have good aquatic posture and to be balanced in several static positions where the only motion you’ll make is gentle kicking. Dynamic posture and balance drills will help you learn how to maintain good aquatic posture and balance while performing simple movements other than just kicking.

垂直踢腿（VK）

Vertical Kicking (VK)

 

大多数成年游泳者在踢腿上浪费大量能量。他们往往出于错误的目的踢腿，这导致腿部动作不正确，例如蹬自行车式踢腿或主要依靠膝盖踢腿。垂直踢腿练习可以帮助你学习有效的踢腿动作，同时精准地锻炼相关肌肉。学习这项练习时，请使用全尺寸的训练脚蹼。

Most adult swimmers waste a great deal of energy on kicking. They tend to use the kick for the wrong reasons, which encourages incorrect leg motions, such as bicycle kicking or kicking mainly from the knees. Vertical kicking will help teach you effective kicking motions while it conditions precisely the right muscles. As you are learning this drill, use full-size training fins.

顾名思义，这是一个垂直姿势的踢腿练习。前往泳池较深的区域，确保你的双脚无法触底。将一只手叠放在另一只手上，置于胸前，开始踢腿。目标是保持头部露出水面，水面略低于下巴，并且鼻子始终指向正前方（图 4.5）。检查你的水中姿势——挺拔紧绷，就像你在陆地上练习行走时那样。保持臀部位于肩膀正下方；不要向前或向后倾斜。

As the name indicates, this is a kicking drill in a vertical position. Go to a deep section of the pool where your feet cannot touch the bottom. Place one hand on top of the other on your chest and start kicking. The goal is to keep your head above the surface, with the water just below your chin and with your nose pointed straight forward (figure 4.5). Check your aquatic posture—tall and tight, just as you practiced while walking on land. Keep your hips directly under your shoulders; do not lean forward or backward.

自由泳的标准打腿动作，也是本次练习中使用的动作，称为蝶泳打腿。打腿指的是将腿从身体后方向前蹬出，到达身体前方等距位置的动作——就像踢球一样。一条腿打腿的同时，另一条腿也随之收回——也就是说，收回的腿从身体前方移动到身体后方，从而处于正确的打腿位置。双腿交替进行相反方向的打腿和收回动作，形成连续的节奏。每次打腿主要发力于髋部，膝盖在腿部向前蹬出时可以略微弯曲以适应水压。在打腿动作的收回阶段，膝盖完全不能弯曲。

The standard kick used for freestyle swimming, and for this drill, is called flutter kicking. The word kick refers to the action of driving your leg forward from behind your body plane to an equidistant point in front of your body plane—like kicking a ball. As one leg kicks, the other leg recovers—that is, the recovering leg moves from in front of your body plane to behind your body plane, thus putting it in the correct position to kick. The legs alternate their opposing kick and recovery motions in a continuous rhythm. Each kick should come predominantly from your hips, allowing the knee to yield slightly to the pressure of the water as the leg kicks forward. There should be no knee bend at allon the recovery portion of the kick cycle.

 

图 4.5垂直踢球练习。

Figure 4.5 Vertical kicking drill.

 

踢腿时主要用髋部发力，保持脚踝放松。小而快的踢腿比大而慢的踢腿更好。这样踢腿15秒，然后休息（可以扶住泳道绳或泳池边）。一开始可以少做几次，比如每次15秒，然后休息15秒或更长时间。等熟练后，再增加次数和时间，减少休息时间。

Kick mainly from the hips and keep your ankles loose. A small, fast kick is better than a larger, slower kick. Kick in this manner for 15 seconds and then rest (hold the lane rope or side of the pool). Start with small doses of this drill, perhaps just a few repetitions of 15 seconds, followed by 15 seconds or more of rest. After you gain confidence, add more and longer repetitions with less rest.

虽然垂直踢水对体能要求较高，但它是训练初期非常有效的练习。求生本能会迅速引导你的神经肌肉系统找到最有效的保持呼吸孔干燥的动作。一旦你熟练掌握了使用全尺寸脚蹼的垂直踢水，尤其是紧绷脚蹼的部分，就可以尝试使用短脚蹼。最终，你应该努力练习赤脚垂直踢水。在过渡到赤脚练习时，你可能会发现，在胸前握住一个小型漂浮物（例如浮板）可以提供足够的额外浮力，让你无需仰头就能保持呼吸孔干燥。注意不要倚靠在浮板上；而是要悬挂在浮板上。

Though it is physically demanding, vertical kicking is an excellent drill to do early in your training. Survival instincts will quickly tell your neuromuscular system which motions are most effective for keeping your blowhole dry. Once you master VK with full-size fins, particularly the tight-line part, you can try short fins. Eventually, you should work toward doing VK with bare feet. In moving to bare feet, you may find that holding a small, floating object (a pull-buoy works well) against your chest will give you enough extra buoyancy to allow you to avoid tilting your head back to keep your blowhole dry. Be careful not to lean on the float; instead, hang from it.

反馈工具

Feedback Tools

 

• 如果你的鼻子指向的不是正前方、与水面水平的方向，那么你的头就偏离了紧绷的绳索。

• If your nose is pointed anywhere but straight forward, horizontal to the surface, then you have tilted your head off your tight line.

• 如果你发现自己每次踢腿时身体都会上下晃动，那么你的踢腿幅度就太大了——保持踢腿动作紧凑。

• If you find yourself bobbing up and down a bit with each kick, then your kicks are too large—keep the kicks compact.

 

做个小实验

Experiment a Bit

 

在练习VK（垂直踢腿）一段时间后，保持良好的腹部和颈部肌肉张力以维持身体的稳定，然后刻意放松身体，保持一种松散的姿势一段时间，并注意这种姿势如何影响你的姿势和动作。之后，再恢复到正确的姿势。你可能会发现，松散的姿势会让你感觉支撑力不足，或许需要花费更多精力来保持头部和呼吸孔干燥。你也可能发现，将头部、躯干和臀部重新调整回挺拔的水上姿势可以迅速解决这些问题。你可以通过以下方式增加练习的难度和训练价值：在踢腿时，将双手放在水面上方、头顶上方，或者保持完全流线型姿势（双臂笔直伸过头顶）。每种姿势都需要你加快踢腿速度才能保持头部露出水面。

After you have spent some time with the VK drill, using good abdominal and neck tension to keep a tight line, purposely relax into a schlumpy posture for a while and note how this affects your position and efforts. Then draw yourself back into good posture. You will likely find that with schlumpy posture you feel less supported, perhaps having to spend more energy to keep your blowhole dry. You will also likely find that reorganizing your head, torso, and hips back into tall aquatic posture quickly solves those problems. You can increase the difficulty and training value of the drill by holding your hands just above the surface of the water, on top of your head, or in full streamline position (arms extended straight above your head) during the kicking. Each of these positions will require you to kick faster to keep your head above the water.

前轮平衡 (FB)

Front Balance (FB)

 

俯卧撑在池壁上，双臂自然垂于身体两侧，开始轻松踢腿。确保你的姿势挺拔——记住要保持身体紧绷。头顶应与脊柱成一条直线，鼻子指向池底。轻轻将浮力板向下压，这样可以抬高臀部，使其靠近水面。调整浮力板的压力，使臀部刚好露出水面。不要把脸部而不是浮力板向下压——你可能需要有意识地稍微收下巴，使脸部远离池底，以保持挺拔的姿势。当需要换气时，将头部向前抬起，吸一口气，然后低头，使头顶与脊柱成一条直线。再次向下压浮力板，并确保下背部保持平直，尽可能地挺直身体。每次抬头时，你的臀部和腿部都会迅速下沉。一旦你恢复到正确的姿势并按压浮标，你就能重新获得平衡。

Push off from the wall on your belly with both arms at your sides and begin kicking easily. Check to be sure your posture is organized tall—remember the tight-line focus point. The crown of your head should be in line with your spine, nose pointed toward the bottom of the pool. Lightly press your buoy toward the bottom. This will raise your hips toward the surface. Adjust the amount of buoy pressure so that the cheeks of your butt just break the surface. Don’t make the mistake of pushing your face, instead of your buoy, toward the bottom—you may need to consciously tuck your chin a bit and draw your face away from the bottom to maintain your tall posture. When you need to take a breath, lift your head straight up in front and get a breath of air, then put your head down so that the crown is in line with your spine. Press your buoy again and make sure to re-flatten your lower back, making yourself as tall as possible. Each time you lift your head, your hips and legs sink rapidly toward the bottom. As soon as you return to good posture and press your buoy, you regain balance.

通往脸书的垫脚石

Stepping-Stone to FB

 

使用训练呼吸管进行这项练习可以避免抬头呼吸的干扰，从而使您能够完全专注于绷紧绳索的姿势和平衡等基本技能。如果您是呼吸管新手，请预留大约半小时的时间来适应脸部浸入水中呼吸，并学习如何通过用力呼气来排出呼吸管内的气体（在每次游完一段距离后蹬墙时，您可能需要这样做）。

Using a training snorkel for this drill eliminates the distraction of lifting your head to take a breath, thus allowing you to focus completely on the basic skills of tight-line posture and balance. If you are new to snorkel use, plan on spending a half hour or so getting used to breathing with your face in the water and learning to purge the snorkel by exhaling forcefully (which you may need to do after pushing off the wall at the beginning of each length).

反馈工具

Feedback Tools

 

• 当你的姿势正确且身体平衡时，你的后脑勺四分之一和大部分背部（包括肩胛骨和臀部）会暴露在空气中，而你的脚后跟会在踢腿时刚好离开地面。

• When your posture is correct and you are in balance, the back quarter of your head and most of your backside (including your shoulder blades and the cheeks of your butt) will be exposed to the air, and your heels will just break the surface as you kick.

• 当你低头俯视时，你应该看到的是脸正下方的毛球和创可贴，而不是你很快就会从它们身上碾过的那些。

• In your nose-down position, you should see the hairballs and Band-Aids that are directly under your face, not the ones you will soon cruise over.

• 如果在练习过程中水进入训练呼吸管，通常表明你把头埋进了水里（这意味着你把脸朝下压向泳池底部，而不是保持头部处于绷紧的姿势），或者你因为对浮标施加了过大的压力而把整个前端都埋进了水里。

• If water enters the training snorkel as you do the drill, it usually indicates that you have buried your head (which means that you’ve pushed your face toward the bottom of the pool instead of keeping your head in tight-line posture) or that you have buried your whole front end by putting too much pressure on your buoy.

 

做个小实验

Experiment a Bit

 

在以良好的紧绷姿势练习FB练习一段时间后，刻意放松身体，以略显松垮的姿势游半个身位左右，并注意这种姿势对你的动作和用力程度的影响。你可能会发现，松垮的姿势会导致速度减慢、支撑力下降、呼吸后难以恢复平衡，并且消耗更多能量。将头部、躯干和臀部重新调整回良好的、挺拔的、水生姿势，应该可以迅速解决这些问题。

After you have spent some time with the FB drill using good tight-line posture, purposely relax into a schlumpy posture for a half length or so and note how this affects your position and efforts. You will likely find that with schlumpy posture you slow down, feel less supported, have trouble regaining balance after breaths, and spend more energy. Reorganizing your head, torso, and hips back into good, tall, aquatic posture should quickly solve those problems.

后平衡 (BB)

Back Balance (BB)

 

仰卧蹬壁，双臂自然下垂于身体两侧，头部与脊柱保持一条直线，鼻尖向上，呼吸顺畅。开始轻松踢腿。轻轻地将身体的支撑点（肩胛骨之间的某个点）向下压向水底。检查身体是否保持良好的水中姿势。仰卧时的感觉可能与俯卧时有所不同。你可能会注意到自己有仰头和拱背的倾向——这两个动作都会破坏身体平衡。运用腹部肌肉的力量来收紧下背部，并伸展颈部和身体线条，这乍听起来可能有些反直觉，但练习几次后就会习惯。

Push off from the wall on your back with both arms at your sides, head aligned with your spine, and nose pointed up and breathing freely. Begin kicking easily. Lightly press your buoy (lean on a spot between your shoulder blades) toward the bottom. Check for the tight line of good aquatic posture. This may feel different when you’re on your back than it did when you were on your belly. You may notice a tendency to tilt your head back and to arch your back—both motions will work against balance. Using abdominal tension to flatten your lower back and extending your neck and bodyline may seem counterintuitive until you have practiced them a few times.

反馈工具

Feedback Tools

 

• 保持平衡时，请注意只有大约四分之一的头部（即面部）会露出水面。您的耳朵应该完全浸没在水中。头部周围的水线应该位于下巴尖、前额最高点，并且两侧泳镜的交界处大致相同。

• When you are in balance, note that only about one quarter of your head (i.e., just your face) will be exposed above the water’s surface. Your ears should be underwater. The waterline around your head should be at the tip of your chin, at the crest of your forehead, and equally on both sides of your goggles.

• 你的骨盆应该与地面齐平，或者距离地面一英寸以内。

• Your pelvis should be at, or within an inch of, the surface.

• 踢水时，你的膝盖和脚趾应该只是略微露出水面。

• Your knees and toes should barely break the surface of the water as you kick.

 

做个小实验

Experiment a Bit

 

在用良好的水中姿势练习一段时间的BB练习后，像练习FB练习那样，故意放松身体，摆出一个松垮的姿势，并观察其效果。然后，重新调整姿势，保持笔直。你可能会遇到与FB练习中相同的松垮姿势带来的问题，同时也会感受到恢复良好挺拔姿势带来的益处。

After you have spent some time with the BB drill using good aquatic posture, experiment as you did with the FB drill—purposely relax into a schlumpy posture and note the effects. Then draw yourself back into a tight line. You will likely experience the same problems with schlumpy posture as you did in the FB drill, as well as the benefits of regaining good, tall posture.

侧滑机头向下（SGND）

Side-Glide Nose-Down (SGND)

 

如前所述，在水中划出较窄的路径时，阻力会更小。这意味着你应该尽可能多地侧身游自由泳，避免长时间俯卧。高效自由泳的基础是左右交替的侧卧滑行，并通过身体从一侧快速转向另一侧来衔接。这个练习可以帮助你保持侧卧的平衡和舒适度。

As mentioned before, the water offers less resistance when you cut a narrower path through it. This means that you want to swim freestyle as much on your side as possible and avoid spending time on your belly. The foundation of an efficient freestyle stroke is a series of alternating right and left side-lying glides, connected by snappy rotations of the body from one side position to the other. This drill will get you balanced and comfortable on your sides.

侧滑练习最好使用训练用呼吸管，这样可以让你游完整个泳池长度而无需担心转头呼吸。侧身站立，从池壁蹬水，下侧手臂大致伸向泳池远端，略微向下倾斜。开始轻松踢腿。另一只手臂紧贴身体。鼻子朝下。身体靠在浮标上（胸侧或腋窝）。保持良好的水姿势。保持这个侧滑姿势（图 4.6）游完整个泳池长度。身体两侧都要进行此练习。

SGND is best done with a training snorkel, which allows you to swim complete lengths of the pool without worrying about turning your head to breathe. Push off from the wall while turned on your side, with your lower arm extended generally toward the far end of the pool, but at a slight downward angle. Begin kicking easily. Press your other arm firmly against your side. Point your nose straight down. Lean on your buoy (the side of your chest or armpit). Maintain a tight line of good aquatic posture. Stay in this side-glide position (figure 4.6) for the length of the pool. Do this drill on both sides of your body.

与其他平衡练习一样，在这个练习中建立正确的水中姿势可能需要一些尝试，但尽可能保持挺拔姿势的基本要点仍然适用。

As with the other balance drills, establishing correct aquatic posture in this drill may require some experimentation, but the fundamental point of drawing yourself into as tall a posture as possible still applies.

反馈工具

Feedback Tools

 

• 侧卧保持平衡时，你会感觉到从肩膀到手腕，手臂上有一条裸露的皮肤。稍微用腋窝用力，增加浮标的压力，可以让更多皮肤暴露在空气中。这条皮肤可以指示你的臀部位置。如果你的手臂紧贴身体，手腕干燥，那么你的臀部就位于水面。

• When you are balanced on your side, you will be able to feel a strip of flesh exposed to the air all the way down your arm from your shoulder to your wrist. Putting a bit more pressure on your buoy by leaning in on your armpit will help expose more of your arm to the air. That strip of flesh is an indicator of the position of your hips. If your arm is firmly pressed to your side and your wrist is dry, then your hips are right at the surface.

• 你的手臂伸直时应该始终感觉不到重量。

• Your extended arm should feel weightless at all times.

• 注意，当你的姿势正确且保持平衡时，你的头部应该几乎与前平衡练习中的位置完全相同——鼻子直直向下，只有后脑勺暴露在空气中。

• Note that when your posture is correct and you are balanced, your head should be in almost exactly the same position as in the front-balance drill—nose pointed straight down and just the back of your head exposed to the air.

• 如果在练习过程中水进入呼吸管，通常意味着你的头埋进了水里（这意味着你把脸朝下压向泳池底部，而不是保持绷紧的姿势并靠在浮标上），或者你的整个前部都埋进了水里（因为对浮标施加了过大的压力）。

• If water enters the snorkel as you do the drill, it usually means that you have buried your head (which means that you’ve pushed your face toward the bottom of the pool instead of keeping it in tight-line posture and simply leaning on your buoy) or that you have buried your whole front end (by putting too much pressure on your buoy).

 

做个小实验

Experiment a Bit

 

在用绷紧的绳索进行一段时间的SGND练习后，像之前的练习一样进行实验——故意放松身体，保持一个略显臃肿的姿势游几码，然后再恢复到正确的姿势。和之前一样，注意每种姿势带来的积极和消极影响。同时，尝试调整浮力，找到能够让你感受到水面完全支撑的阻力。你可能会发现，当你放松核心肌群的姿势张力时，支撑感会变得难以捉摸甚至完全消失。

After you have spent some time with the SGND drill with a tight line, experiment as you did with the previous drills—purposely relax into a schlumpy posture for a few yards, then draw yourself back into good posture. As before, note the effects, both positive and negative, of each of these postures. Also experiment with the amount of buoy pressure you need to use in order to feel fully supported by the water. You will likely find that when you relax the posture tension in your core, the sensation of support is elusive or non-existent.

 

图 4.6侧滑机头向下钻探。

Figure 4.6 Side-glide nose-down drill.

 

侧滑抬头（SGNU）

Side-Glide Nose-Up (SGNU)

 

侧卧俯卧平衡与侧卧仰卧平衡同样重要。这项练习建立在你之前练习的侧卧俯卧平衡（SGND）技巧之上，旨在帮助你在侧卧时保持平衡和舒适，同时保持呼吸孔暴露。但在尝试侧卧仰卧平衡（SGNU）之前，你应该先练习侧卧俯卧平衡，直到你能够保持平衡并感到非常舒适为止。

Just as important as side-lying nose-down balance is side-lying nose-up balance. This drill builds on the skills you learned in SGND and will get you balanced and comfortable on your sides while your blowhole is exposed. But you should practice SGND until you are balanced and very comfortable with it before trying SGNU.

这次不要使用呼吸管。以侧卧抬头姿势（SGND）蹬离水面。一旦保持平衡，只需转动头部，直到鼻子朝上，可以自由呼吸（图 4.7）。转动头部时，身体其他部位不应有任何变化。不要翻身仰卧。转动头部时不要抬起头——即使是轻微的抬头也会破坏平衡。检查一下你的水中姿势是否正确。保持侧卧抬头的姿势游完泳池全程。身体两侧都要进行此练习。

Eschew the snorkel this time. Push off in SGND position. As soon as you are balanced, turn just your head until your nose points straight up and you can breathe freely (figure 4.7). Nothing else should change when you turn your head. Don’t roll onto your back. Don’t lift your head as you turn it—even the slightest lift will undo your balance. Check for good aquatic posture. Stay in this side-lying nose-up position for the length of the pool. Do this drill on both sides of your body.

如果你一转头呼吸就失去平衡，可以尝试以下方法：从仰卧抬头（SGND）姿势开始，确保转头时肺部充满空气，使鼻子露出水面。不要立即呼气；而是屏住呼吸，保持鼻子抬起的姿势，同时在脑海中检查身体的平衡感。一旦你确认身体平衡良好，就可以缓慢呼气，开始正常呼吸。

If you are losing your balance as soon as you turn your head to breathe, try the following strategy: Starting in SGND position, make sure that your lungs are full of air when you turn your head to take your nose out of the water. Do not exhale immediately; instead, hold your breath in the nose-up position while you mentally check your feedback tools. Once you are satisfied that you are well balanced, exhale slowly and begin breathing normally.

反馈工具

Feedback Tools

 

• 使用与 SGND 相同的反馈工具，但当您保持平衡时，您的头部位置应与后平衡练习中的位置几乎完全相同——耳朵在水下，鼻子直指上方，水线位于下巴尖和额头顶。

• Use the same feedback tools you would use for SGND, except that when you are balanced, your head should be in almost exactly the same position as in the back-balance drill—ears under the water, nose pointed straight up, and water line at the tip of the chin and crest of the forehead.

 
 

图 4.7侧滑机头上翘练习。

Figure 4.7 Side-glide nose-up drill.

 

做个小实验

Experiment a Bit

 

在用绷紧的绳索进行SGNU练习一段时间后，像之前的练习一样进行实验——交替进行紧绷-松弛-再紧绷的姿势，并记录每种姿势带来的积极和消极影响。同时，尝试调整浮力压力，直到你感受到水的完全支撑。和之前一样，放松姿势的紧张感可能会消除支撑感。

After you have spent some time with the SGNU drill with a tight line, experiment as you did with the previous drills—alternate between tight-schlumpy-tight, noting the effects, both positive and negative, of each of these postures. Also experiment with varying the amount of buoy pressure you need to feel fully supported by the water. As before, relaxing your posture tension may erase the sensation of support.

 
重点➤向下角度手臂伸展
 
在侧滑练习的说明中，我指出伸出的手臂应该略微向下倾斜。这与通常将引导臂笔直伸向泳池远端的做法有所不同。大多数成年游泳者的肩部活动范围有限，这会影响手臂伸展位置的选择。以下几点原因强烈建议将伸出的手臂略微向下倾斜，无论是在这个练习中，还是在大多数自由泳练习中。

•避免受伤。将手臂水平伸向泳池远端（或以任何向上角度）都可能导致肩部肌腱在肱骨和肩关节窝之间受到挤压。每天重复数千次这样的动作是许多游泳者慢性疼痛的根源。但即使手臂以很小的角度向下伸展，也能大大降低肩部肌腱受到挤压的风险。

•机械优势。肩关节活动范围接近或达到极限时，机械优势较差（换句话说，虽然肌肉力量很大，但实际做功很少）。手臂略微向下伸展，可以使肩关节远离活动范围的极限，从而在划水动作的初始阶段增加机械优势。

•上坡滑雪。当游泳者在水中向前滑行时，手臂向上伸展任何角度，都会使涌入的水流冲击手和手臂的底部，从而抬升手臂。由于伸展手臂的杠杆作用较长，这会抬起上半身（同时臀部下沉）——有点像上坡滑雪。相反，手臂略微向下伸展则有助于臀部紧贴水面。

•能量消耗。选择接近肩关节活动范围末端的伸展线（水平或向上角度）需要大量的额外内部张力来维持该位置。选择略微向下的角度可以大大降低所需的内部张力（以及相应的能量消耗）。

•疲劳引起的髋部下沉。水平或向上伸展所需的额外内部张力虽然可以短时间维持，但长时间下来很快就会导致疲劳。通常的反应是放松一些核心肌群的张力，让髋部下沉，从而打破平衡的流线型姿势。这可以减轻一些肩部压力，但会大大增加正面阻力。如果让你在纤细的小手略微偏离流线、位于身体下方，和沉重的髋部下沉之间做出选择，你会选择哪一个？

 

自己判断手臂伸展角度通常比较困难。可以请泳伴反馈你手臂伸展的位置。然后尝试不同的手臂向下角度，同时注意肩部及周围肌肉需要多大的张力来支撑这个姿势。你需要找到的向下角度恰到好处，既能保持良好的水中姿势，又能让臀部紧贴水面。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Downward Angle Arm Extension
 
In the side-glide drill descriptions, I indicated that the extended arm should be at a slight downward angle. This is a departure from the conventional wisdom of extending the lead arm straight toward the far end of the pool. Most adult swimmers have range of motion issues in their shoulders that affect the choice of the arm extension position. Several considerations strongly favor having the extended arm at a downward angle, both in this drill and throughout most of your freestyle endeavors. They are as follows:

• Avoiding injury.Extending the arm horizontally toward the far end of the pool (or at any upward angle) can pinch the shoulder tendons between the upper-arm bone and the shoulder socket. Doing this thousands of times per day is a cause of chronic pain for a large number of swimmers. But extending the arm at even a small degree of downward angle greatly reduces the risk of an impingement.

• Mechanical advantage.A shoulder joint at or near the end of its ROM has poor mechanical advantage (in other words, you exert lots of muscular force but get very little work done). Extending your arm at a bit of a downward angle keeps the shoulder away from the end of its ROM, increasing mechanical advantage during the first part of the stroke.

• Skiing uphill.As the swimmer glides forward through the water, an arm extended at any degree of upward angle will mean that the onrush of water will hit the bottom surface of the hand and arm, which will tend to raise them. Due to the long lever of the extended arm, this will lift the upper body (and drop the hips)—a bit like skiing uphill. Alternatively, extending the arm at a bit of a downward angle will help your hips hug the surface.

• Energy use.Choosing an extension line near the end of your shoulder ROM (horizontal or upward angle) requires lots of extra internal tension to maintain the position. Choosing a bit of a downward angle greatly decreases the internal tension (and, consequently, the energy) required.

• Fatigue-induced hip drop.While the extra internal tension required by a horizontal or upward angle extension is sustainable for short durations, for longer durations it soon results in fatigue stress. The usual response is to release some core body tension and break out of the balanced streamline position by letting the hips drop. This relieves some of shoulder stress but greatly increases total frontal resistance. If you had to choose between having a spindly little hand a bit out of streamline below the rest of the body or your big ol’ hips dragging deep, which would be your preference?

 

It is often hard to judge your arm extension angle yourself. Have a swim partner give you feedback about your extended arm position. Then experiment with various amounts of downward angle in your arm extension line while monitoring how much tension is required in and around your shoulder to support the position. What you are looking for is just enough downward angle to allow you to maintain good aquatic posture and to keep your hips glued to the surface.

 

动态姿势和平衡训练

Dynamic Posture and Balance Drills

 

侧滑呼吸（SGB）

Side Glide With Breathing (SGB)

 

这个练习是SGND和SGNU练习的交替进行。开始时，动作与SGNU练习相同。保持良好的姿势和平衡，在鼻尖朝上的姿势下呼吸几次，然后将头转向泳池底部，在水下呼出少量空气。之后，将头转回鼻尖朝上的姿势。在这个姿势下呼吸几次，然后再转头在水下呼气。在这个练习中，除了腿部之外，你唯一要移动的部位就是头部。整个练习过程中，身体应保持平衡的侧滑姿势。练习时，每次鼻尖朝下时尝试呼出更多空气，每次转头回到鼻尖朝上的姿势时尝试减少呼吸次数，直到你能在水下正常呼气，并且在鼻尖朝上时只需吸一口气。身体两侧都要进行这个练习。

This drill is an alternation between the SGND and SGNU drills. Start as you would for the SGNU drill. With good posture and balance, take several breaths in the nose-up position, turn your head so that your nose points toward the bottom of the pool, and exhale a little bit of air underwater. Then turn your head back to the nose-up position. Take several breaths in this position before turning your head to exhale again underwater. The only thing you move in this drill, besides your legs, is your head. The body should stay in a balanced, side-glide position throughout the drill. As you practice this drill, work toward exhaling more air each time you are nose down and try to take fewer breaths each time you turn your head to the nose-up position until you can exhale normally underwater and until you can take just a single breath when nose up. Do this drill on both sides of your body.

反馈工具

Feedback Tools

 

• 当你的鼻子朝上时，你的头部位置应该和SGNU练习中一样——耳朵在水下。当你的鼻子朝下时，只有后脑勺会露出水面。关键是要像绕着一根烤肉串（一根穿过脊柱并向上延伸到头顶的烤肉串）一样转动头部，但烤肉串不能弯曲。

• When your nose points up, your head should be in the same position as in the SGNU drill—ears under the water. When your nose points toward the bottom, just the back of your head is exposed to the air. The idea is to rotate your head as if it were on a skewer (one that runs through your spine and up through your crown) without bending the skewer.

• 在练习过程中，始终要感受从肩膀到手腕，沿着侧臂向下延伸的那条干燥的皮肤带。许多游泳者在转身仰头时，往往会稍微抬起头部，这会导致臀部下沉。你会感觉到水线沿着侧臂向上移动，靠近肩膀，这表明你失去了平衡。在转身仰头时，你可能需要稍微将身体侧面和后脑勺向下压向泳池底部，以避免头部抬起。

• Feel for that dry strip of flesh all the way down your side arm, from your shoulder to your wrist, at all times during this drill. Many swimmers tend to lift the head a bit when turning to the nose-up position. This causes the hips to drop. You’ll feel the water line creep up your side arm toward your shoulder, indicating that you have lost your balance. You may need to press your side and the back of your head slightly toward the bottom of the pool in order to avoid lifting it as you rotate it to the nose-up position.

• 这项练习中另一个常见的倾向是，在转头换气时，身体会倚靠伸出的手臂，将其向下压向泳池底部。这是为了人为地支撑略微抬起的头部。正确的做法是更多地依靠浮板支撑身体，并保持伸出的手臂略微向下倾斜。在整个练习过程中，这只手臂应该感觉不到重量。

• Another common tendency with this drill is to lean on the extended arm, pressing it toward the bottom of the pool as the head turns for a breath. This is an attempt to artificially support a slightly lifted head. The cure is to support yourself by leaning on your buoy more and by keeping the extended arm at a slightly downward angle. This arm should feel weightless throughout the drill.

 

做个小实验

Experiment a Bit

 

与之前的所有练习一样，花时间有意识地在保持紧绷的泳姿和放松的懒散泳姿之间来回切换很有帮助。了解这两种不同姿势对游泳的影响，将有助于你养成良好的泳姿习惯。

As with each of the other drills so far, it is helpful to spend time consciously shifting back and forth between holding a tight-line posture and relaxing into a schlumpy posture. Becoming aware of how the two different postures affect your swimming will help motivate you to make a habit of good posture.

 
重点➤危险呼吸
 

为了换气，缺乏游泳经验的游泳者会本能地抬起头，确保吸入的只有空气，不会呛水。这会导致臀部和腿部下沉——下沉的幅度可能不大，也可能很大。头部垂直抬高5厘米（2英寸），臀部就会下沉10到15厘米（4到6英寸），进而导致双脚下沉20到30厘米（8到12英寸）——这足以使阻力几乎翻倍。意识到这个问题后，缺乏游泳经验的游泳者会更加用力地踢腿，以支撑臀部和腿部保持在水面附近。这个过程变得异常艰难，浪费了大量能量。

另一方面，你在换气时必须冒险，尽量把头放低到足以呛水的程度。提示：如果你从未呛过水，那就说明你冒险的程度还不够。转动头部，使鼻子更多地指向天空而不是侧方。鼻子越接近垂直向上，吸气时头部就可以放得越低。如果你养成每次呼吸都保持这种冒险的深头姿势的习惯，就能减少额外踢腿支撑所消耗的能量。你的目标是：头部零抬升，躯干零抬升，以及零额外能量消耗。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Risky Breathing
 

To take a breath, the uneducated swimmer instinctively lifts his head to a position where he is absolutely sure he’ll get nothing but air, with no risk of swallowing water. This causes the hips and legs to sink—maybe a little, maybe a lot. A 2-inch (5 cm) vertical lift of the head can cause a 4- to 6-inch (10 to 15 cm) drop of the hips, which shows up as an 8- to 12-inch (20 to 30 cm) drop of the feet—enough to nearly double form drag. Sensing this problem, the uneducated swimmer then uses extra kicking to support his hips and legs near the surface. The process becomes a struggle that wastes a lot of energy.

You, on the other hand, must be risky about how low you keep your head when going for air—risky enough that you might take in some water. Hint: If you never ever take in water, then you are not being risky enough. Rotate your head far enough that your nose is pointed more skyward than sideways. The closer you come to a nose-straight-up position, the deeper your head can be when you take a breath. If you create a habit of going for a risky-deep head position every time you breathe, you will decrease the amount of energy you waste in extra support kicking. You goal is zero head-lift, zero torso-lift, and zero extra-energy consumption.

 

平衡身体滚动（BBR）

Balanced-Body Rolling (BBR)

 

这个练习最好使用训练用呼吸管。以与做FB练习时相同的姿势——俯卧，双臂自然下垂，鼻尖朝下——从池壁蹬出，开始轻松踢腿。保持绳子绷紧，并对浮标施加足够的压力以保持平衡。一旦保持平衡，翻身侧卧。保持鼻尖朝下，双手自然下垂。如果在翻身过程中保持绳子绷紧并对浮标施加压力，那么侧卧时你已经处于平衡状态。保持侧卧姿势的平衡。由于双臂下垂，你可能需要比单臂伸直时更大的浮标压力才能保持平衡。保持平衡后，再次翻身俯卧，翻身过程中保持绳子绷紧并对浮标施加压力。向两个方向翻身练习。

This drill is best done with a training snorkel. Push off from the wall in the same position you used for the FB drill—on your belly and with both arms at your sides, nose pointed toward the bottom of the pool—and begin kicking easily. Keep a tight line and keep enough pressure on your buoy to stay balanced. Once you are balanced, roll onto your side. Keep your nose pointed straight down and keep your hands at your sides. If you keep a tight line and keep pressure on your buoy as you roll, you will already be in a balanced position when you reach your side. Stay balanced while on your side. With your arms at your sides, you’ll likely need a bit more buoy pressure to be balanced than when you had one arm extended in front. After you are well balanced, roll again to your front, keeping a tight line and pressure on your buoy as you roll. Do this drill rolling in both directions.

反馈工具

Feedback Tools

 

• 当你从前滚翻到侧滚时，你应该能感觉到从肩膀到手腕的那条肉带一下子暴露在空气中，而无需调整你的平衡。

• As you roll from the front position to the side position, you should feel the strip of flesh from your shoulder to your wrist become exposed to the air all at once without having to adjust your balance.

• 当你向后滚动到前位时，你应该感觉到臀部两侧暴露在空气中，而无需调整你的平衡。

• As you roll back to the front position, you should feel the cheeks of your butt become exposed to the air without having to adjust your balance.

• 为了保持平衡，您可能会发现，侧卧时需要对浮标施加比俯卧时更大的压力。

• To stay balanced, you may find that you need to keep a bit more pressure on your buoy when you are on your side than when you are on your front.

 

做个小实验

Experiment a Bit

 

再次强调，要花时间有意识地在保持挺拔姿势和放松慵懒的姿势之间来回切换。如果你坚持这样做，就会逐渐建立一个自动反馈机制，一旦你开始偏离良好姿势，它就会在你脑海中发出警报。

Again, spend time consciously shifting back and forth between holding a tight-line posture and relaxing into a schlumpy posture. If you do enough of this, you will begin to set up an automatic feedback cycle that will set off alarm bells in your head whenever you begin to break out of good posture.

 
焦点➤红点
 

在许多游泳练习和全程划水练习中，想象头顶中央有一个直径 5 厘米（2 英寸）的红点，并始终保持它在水下，会很有帮助。当你游向水下观察者时，他应该看不到这个红点随着你的身体旋转或划水而上下或左右移动。他只能看到红点在你转头换气时转动。这个重点结合了之前讨论过的三个与头部相关的概念：水中姿势的颈部紧张、不换气时保持鼻子朝向池底，以及危险换气时头部完全不抬起。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Red Dot
 

In many swimming drills and in full-stroke swimming, it can be helpful to imagine a 2-inch (5 cm) red dot in the center of the top of your head that you keep underwater at all times. A person watching you from a vantage point under the water as you swim toward him should not be able to see that red dot move up, down, or side to side as your body rotates or as you take strokes. They would only see the dot rotate as you turn your head to breathe. This focus point combines the three head-related ideas discussed thus far: the neck tension of aquatic posture, keeping your nose pointed toward the bottom of the pool when not breathing, and the zero head-lift of risky breathing.

 

垂直旋转踢 (VKR)

Vertical Kick With Rotation (VKR)

 

自由泳的动力来源于身体围绕长轴的节奏性旋转。VKR 练习可以教会你如何启动全身旋转，以及如何有节奏地交替进行旋转。

Freestyle swimming is powered by rhythmic rotations of the body around its long axis. The VKR drill teaches you how to initiate full-body rotations and how to alternate them in a rhythmic fashion.

VKR练习的起始姿势与标准的VK练习相同——在深水中，双手放在胸前，肘部紧贴身体两侧，保持紧绷的姿势。建立起舒适的垂直打水-打腿节奏后，用一次打腿将身体向右旋转约四分之一圈，然后在新的位置继续打水。几次打水后，用一次打腿将身体向左旋转四分之一圈回到起始位置。用于旋转身体的打腿动作——一次打腿使身体向右旋转，之后再一次打腿使身体向左旋转——称为旋转打腿。

The VKR drill starts like the standard VK drill—in deep water with your hands on your chest, elbows tucked in at your sides, and a tight-line posture. After you have established a comfortable vertical-flutter-kick rhythm, use one of your kicks to rotate your body roughly a quarter turn to the right and then continue flutter kicking in this new position. After a handful of flutter kicks, use one of your kicks to make a quarter turn back toward the left where you started. The kicks you use to rotate yourself—one kick to turn you to the right and, later, one kick to turn you to the left—are called rotation kicks.

旋转踢腿时，右腿向前踢出会使右髋向后摆动（牛顿反作用力）。同时，左腿向后摆动，带动左髋向前摆动（同样是牛顿反作用力）。左髋向前、右髋向后摆动，就相当于向右转动髋部。要向右转动髋部，在左腿摆动的同时踢出右腿。要向左转动髋部，在右腿摆动的同时踢出左腿。这听起来很简单，但要真正掌握却需要一定的意识和专注力。旋转并不需要特别用力或幅度特别大。只需放松髋部，让它们旋转四分之一圈，然后保持这个姿势，继续打腿。每次髋部旋转时，让上半身随着髋部一起转动（如果你拉紧了绳子，这会自动发生）。你可能会想在踢腿时耸肩来帮助旋转。千万不要这样做。耸肩没有任何帮助。一点帮助都没有。就算是为了你，也别怪我没提醒你。相信我，你就放心吧。

With a rotation kick, kicking your right leg forward drives your right hip backward (Newton’s equal and opposite reaction). Simultaneously, the left leg recovers backward, which drives the left hip forward (Newton again). Left hip forward and right hip back equals turning your hips to the right. To rotate your hips to your right, kick your right leg as you recover the left leg. To rotate your hips to your left, kick your left leg as you recover the right. It sounds simple, but it takes some real awareness and focus to grasp. It does not take an extra-hard or extra-large kick to rotate. Simply release your hips and let them rotate that quarter turn, then hold them in place as you continue to flutter kick. Each time your hips rotate, allow the top part of your body to take a ride along with your hips (which will happen automatically if you are holding a tight line). You may be tempted to try to help the rotation by throwing your shoulders around as you kick. Don’t. Throwing your shoulders doesn’t help. Not at all. Not even for you. Just take my word for it.

当你能够轻松地进行偶尔的旋转后，就可以为旋转加入节奏。你会用到一种叫做六拍旋转模式的动作，它很简单：先是两次轻踢（F），然后是一次旋转踢（R），使你向右转，接着是两次轻踢，再是一次旋转踢，使你回到起始的左侧。完成一个包含两次旋转的循环（FFRFFR），总共需要六个踢腿节拍，之后便开始一个新的循环，节奏保持不变（……FFRFFRFFRFFRFFR……）。你可以大声数拍子来辅助练习，每只脚向前踢出一个节拍。保持头部静止，鼻子直指前方，继续进行这个六拍旋转模式——只需让你的身体在头部下方旋转即可。

Once you are comfortable with making occasional rotations, add rhythm to the rotations. You’ll use what is called a six-beat rotation pattern, which is simply two flutter kicks (F) followed by one rotation kick (R), which turns you to the right, followed by two flutter kicks and another rotation kick that turns you back to the left, where you started. That’s a total of six kick beats to complete a cycle of two rotations (FFRFFR), after which a new cycle starts without breaking rhythm (. . . FFRFFRFFRFFRFFR. . .). It helps to count these beats out loud, one for each foot as it kicks forward. Continue this six-beat rotation pattern while keeping your head still, nose pointed straight forward—just let your body rotate under your stationary head.

即使你已经掌握了标准的无蹼垂直跳（VK），我仍然强烈建议你在初学垂直跳旋转（VKR）时使用脚蹼。脚蹼可以让你放慢踢腿的节奏，从而更清晰地感知每一次踢腿的节奏，更容易分辨哪些是打水踢腿，哪些是旋转踢腿。脚蹼还能让你更好地感知每次旋转时使用的肌肉群。一旦你熟练掌握了使用全尺寸脚蹼的垂直跳旋转，就可以尝试使用短脚蹼，最终甚至可以赤脚练习。在过渡到赤脚练习时，你可能会发现像练习垂直跳时那样，用一个小型漂浮物贴近胸口悬挂会很有帮助。

Even if you have mastered standard VK without fins, I strongly encourage you to use fins when you are first learning VKR. Fins will allow you to slow the tempo of your kick. This allows distinct awareness of each beat, making it easier to pinpoint which kicks should be flutter kicks and which should be rotation kicks. Fins will also improve the feedback you get about which muscles you are using to drive each rotation. Once you master VKR with full-size fins, you can try short fins and, eventually, bare feet. In moving to bare feet, you may find that hanging from a small floating object held against your chest is helpful, as it was with VK.

反馈工具

Feedback Tools

 

• 每次转动髋部时，你应该意识到肩膀的转动与髋部完全同步，幅度也完全相同。紧绷的体态能立即将髋部的转动沿着脊柱传递，使腿部的动作能够带动整个上半身作为一个整体进行转动。如果你发现肩膀落后于髋部，或者肩膀的转动幅度小于髋部，那么你的紧绷体态就出现了问题。如果你发现髋部落后于肩膀，那么你试图通过将肩膀向前顶到髋部来辅助髋部旋转（但令人惊讶的是，这样做反而会阻碍髋部的旋转，而不是帮助它）。

• Each time you rotate your hips, you should be aware that your shoulders rotate at exactly the same time as, and exactly as far as, your hips. Your tight-line posture instantly transmits the rotation of your hips along your spine, allowing the action of your legs to drive the rotation of the entire upper body as a single unit. If you find that your shoulders lag behind your hips or that they don’t turn as far as your hips, you have lost your tight line. If you find your hips lagging behind your shoulders, then you are trying to help the rotation by throwing your shoulders ahead of your hips (which, surprisingly, works to hinder hip rotation instead of helping it).

• 检查一下，在准备旋转踢腿时，你是否弯曲了支撑腿的膝盖，试图将脚向后拉得更远，以便踢出更大更有力的踢腿来带动旋转。这样做是不可取的——它只会将旋转的支点从髋部转移到膝盖，有效地将力臂缩短了一半，从而大大降低你的发力效果。

• Check to see if, in preparation for a rotation kick, you are bending your knee on the recovering leg to bring that foot a bit farther back for a bigger or more forceful kick to drive the rotation. It is important not to try to help the rotation by doing this—it simply moves the rotation fulcrum from your hips to your knees, effectively cutting your lever length in half and making your effort much less effective.

 

做个小实验

Experiment a Bit

 

当你熟练掌握简单的六拍旋转节奏后，可以尝试加快速度。如果保持六拍节奏，加快踢腿节奏也会加快旋转节奏。旋转速度加快时，你可能会发现需要稍微拉紧腹部，才能保持上半身作为一个整体独立旋转。此外，和往常一样，一定要尝试不同的姿势，比如放松的姿势和紧绷的姿势。

After you are comfortable with an easy six-beat rotation pattern, experiment with increasing the tempo. If you maintain the six-beat pattern, a faster kick tempo will result in a faster rotation tempo. With faster rotations, you may find that you need a bit more tension on your tight line to keep the upper body rotating as a separate unit. And, as usual, be sure to experiment with schlumpy vs. tight-line postures.

长轴旋转（LAR）

Long-Axis Rotations (LAR)

 

这个练习会将你刚刚在垂直旋转（VKR）练习中学到的长轴旋转技巧运用到水平位置，并结合你的平衡技巧。一旦你熟练掌握了垂直旋转，就可以通过缓慢前倾，让臀部和腿部浮出水面，过渡到长轴旋转（LAR）。在过渡到水平位置的过程中，保持身体呈直线，并继续保持六拍的旋转节奏。将浮板压向平衡点，并确保你的鼻子朝下。一旦身体水平，就将双臂向前伸展，指向泳池的尽头。你的打腿动作会轻柔地推动你前进，而旋转打腿动作则会使你的肚脐从大约向右45度旋转到大约向左45度。不要试图完全旋转到侧滑位置。一旦你熟练掌握了水平位置的六拍旋转节奏，就可以开始从池壁蹬水，而不是从垂直旋转开始。

This drill takes the long-axis rotation skills you just learned in the VKR drill and puts them to use in a horizontal position, where you will add your balance skills to the mix. Once you are comfortable with VKR, you can transition to LAR by slowly leaning forward and allowing your hips and legs to rise to the surface. Keep a tight line as you transition to a horizontal position, and keep the same six-beat rotation pattern going. Press your buoy to the balance point and be sure your nose is pointed straight down. Once you are horizontal, extend your arms forward toward the end of the pool. Your flutter kicks will propel you gently along while your rotation kicks will result in quarter turns that swing your navel from pointing roughly 45 degrees to the right to pointing roughly 45 degrees to the left. Do not try to rotate all the way to the side-glide position. Once you are comfortable with the six-beat rotation pattern in a horizontal position, you may begin by pushing off from the wall instead of by starting from VKR.

换气时，转动头部的同时转动身体，让呼吸侧的手肘滑回胸前，同时该手的指尖仍指向泳池末端（图 4.8）。这样，手臂就能避开头部，无需划水，也无需向下压水。转回时，将手臂向前伸直。转身时，可以稍微超过 45 度角，以避免抬头（记住红点和呼吸风险点）。每次换气之间至少要完成三次，最好是五次旋转——至少要等到你能在不影响平衡且旋转节奏的情况下完成一次换气为止。

When it is time to grab a breath, turn your head as you rotate and allow the elbow on the breathing side to slide back to your chest while the fingers on that hand remain pointed toward the end of the pool (figure 4.8). This gets the arm out of the way of your head without taking a stroke and without pushing down on the water. As you rotate back, extend that arm back out in front of you. You may want to go a bit beyond the 45-degree mark when rotating to the air to avoid lifting your head (remember the red dot and risky-breathing focus points). It is important to have at least three, and preferably five, rotations between breaths—at least until you are able to take a breath with no effect on your balance and no change in your rotation rhythm.

使用训练呼吸管可以大大缩短学习LAR基本技能的周期，因为它消除了转头呼吸的干扰。在训练中需要长时间进行LAR练习时，持续使用呼吸管有助于进一步提升技能，但你仍然需要掌握在不方便使用呼吸管的情况下如何呼吸。如果没有深水区可以让你以VKR作为起始点，你仍然可以从靠墙蹬腿开始学习LAR练习。只是要做好花费更多时间的准备。

Use of a training snorkel can greatly shorten the learning cycle for the basic skills of LAR by eliminating the distraction of having to turn your head to breathe. Continued use of the snorkel is valuable for further refinement when long segments of LAR are called for in the workouts, but you’ll still need to know how to take a breath when the snorkel is not convenient. If you have no deep water in which to use VKR as a starting point, it is still possible to learn the LAR drill by starting from a wall push-off. Just plan on it taking a bit longer to accomplish.

 

图 4.8长轴旋转练习的呼吸姿势。

Figure 4.8 Breathing position for the long-axis rotations drill.

 

反馈工具

Feedback Tools

 

• 利用臀部来感知平衡——始终要保持一侧臀部或另一侧臀部暴露在空气中。这样做表明你的臀部始终紧贴地面。

• Use your butt for feedback about balance—at all times you should have one butt cheek or the other exposed to the air. Doing so indicates that you are keeping your hips glued to the surface.

• 你应该知道，每一次旋转都是由一个鼓点引起的，而不是由两个或三个鼓点引起的。

• You should be aware that each rotation happens with and because of a single kick beat, rather than two or three beats.

• 将你的旋转节奏与节奏提示器（或脑海中一段节奏鲜明的熟悉旋律）相匹配，可以帮助你判断自己旋转的节奏是否发生了变化。目标是在整个练习过程中（即使在呼吸时）保持稳定的旋转节奏。

• Matching your rotation tempo to a tempo beeper (or to a familiar tune with a distinctive beat in your head) can help you determine whether you are changing the tempo of your rotations. The goal is to set and keep an uninterrupted rotation tempo throughout the drill (even when breathing).

• 注意你是否使用了更大或更有力的踢腿来驱动旋转。所有踢腿的幅度和力度都应该相同。

• Be aware of whether you are using a bigger or more forceful kick to drive the rotation. All the kicks should be the same size and force.

• 使用红点和危险呼吸重点来帮助你时刻注意自己是否正在抬头呼吸。

• Use the red dot and risky-breathing focus points to help you stay aware of whether you are lifting your head for air.

 

做个小实验

Experiment a Bit

 

当你熟练掌握简单的LAR动作后，尝试不同的踢腿节奏，从非常慢到非常快，始终以髋部和胸廓作为一个整体旋转为目标。尝试仰卧和侧卧进行LAR练习。此外，除了通常的紧绷-放松-紧绷姿势切换实验外，还可以进行类似的平衡实验：偶尔放松身体的浮力，使其失去平衡，观察这会如何影响旋转、稳定性和前进速度。

After you become comfortable with easy LAR, try a variety of different kicking tempos, from very slow to very fast, always with the goal of making the hips and thorax rotate as a single unit. Try doing LAR on your back and on your sides. Also, supplement the usual tight-schlumpy-tight posture-switching experiment with a similar balance experiment: occasionally release buoy pressure to become unbalanced and see how this affects rotation, stability, and forward progress.

第五章
 
笔画整合与转弯
 

如果您在水中感觉舒适，并且已经花足够的时间练习上一章的技巧，对自己的姿势和平衡能力充满信心，那么您就可以开始学习一些新的泳姿了。本章将介绍如何打造一台高效的游泳机器（您很快就能成为其中一员），并介绍一种易于掌握的概念——前象限游泳，许多世界级游泳运动员都在使用这种方法。一些泳姿整合练习将帮助您构建自己的游泳机器，并将前象限游泳融入其中。这些练习将帮助您把在姿势和平衡练习中学到的各项技巧融会贯通，整合手臂划水动作，从而形成一套协调的动作，让您轻松地游向泳池的另一端。在您练习这些练习一段时间后，我们将再次讲解整个划水周期，并提供一些微调技巧，帮助您改进练习，弥合练习和实际游泳之间的差距。最后，您将学习两种最有效的触壁转身方法。

If you are comfortable in the water and have spent enough time with the drills in the previous chapter to feel confident about your posture and balance skills, you are ready to add a few stroke skills to your repertoire. This chapter describes how an effective swimming machine (soon to be you) works, and I introduce an easy-to-incorporate concept used by many world-class swimmers called front-quadrant swimming. Several stroke-integration drills will help you assemble your swimming machine and incorporate front-quadrant swimming. These drills help you put together the discreet skills you learned in the posture and balance drills, integrating arm strokes to create a coordinated set of motions that propels you easily down the pool. After you’ve spent some time with the drills, the whole stroke cycle is covered again, offering some fine-tuning tips that will help improve your drills and bridge the gap between drilling and swimming. Finally, you will learn about the two most effective ways to turn when you come to a wall.

按照本章及后续章节的顺序进行练习，你将逐步从零开始建立一种新的自由泳泳姿。在一段时间内，当你游泳而不是练习时，你可能会倾向于回到阅读本书之前的泳姿。但是，你越熟悉这些技巧和练习，就越容易将它们融入到你的日常游泳中。后续章节的训练计划围绕着循序渐进地练习这些技巧而设计，首先加入少量、逐渐增加的完整泳姿练习。

As you follow and practice the drills in the order presented in this and later chapters, you will progressively build a new freestyle stroke from scratch. For a while, when you swim rather than practice drills, you will tend to revert to whatever stroke style you had before you read this book. The more comfortable and relaxed you become with these skills and drills, though, the easier they will be to incorporate into your everyday swimming. The workouts in subsequent chapters are built around progressively practicing the drills while first mixing in small and later larger amounts of full-stroke swimming.

你的游泳机

Your Swimming Machine

 
我之前提到过，自由泳是由一系列交替的侧滑和推进划水动作组成的。正确的旋转，良好的起跳和手臂的正确配合，可以让游泳者调动更多的肌肉力量，比旋转不正确、手臂配合不当或只是平游时更能发挥力量。在解释其中的原理之前，我们先来了解一些术语。我将单臂划水周期分为三个部分——划水、回转和入水及伸展。

1. 划水动作是指在水下将手从身体前方完全伸展的位置移动到大腿附近的结束位置的推进动作。划水动作始于身体开始从一侧侧卧姿势旋转，止于身体完成旋转到另一侧侧卧姿势。

1. The stroke is the propulsive underwater action of moving the hand from the fully extended position in front of the body to the finish position somewhere by your thigh. The stroke starts as the body begins to rotate from one side-lying position, and it ends as the body finishes rotating to the other side-lying position.

2. 回旋动作是指将手臂从大腿附近伸出水面，并向上滑行至手掌与头顶齐平或略微超过头顶，整个过程不涉及推进力。手臂回旋时，身体保持侧卧姿势——完全不旋转，只是滑行——另一只手臂则保持向前伸展，略微向下倾斜，以帮助身体在整个回旋过程中保持舒展。

2. The recovery is the non-propulsive action of taking the arm out of the water from the spot by your thigh and carrying it through the air to a point where the hand is even with or just past the top of the head. The body stays on its side while the arm recovers—no rotation at all, just gliding—and the other arm simply remains extended out front at a bit of a downward angle, helping keep the body long throughout the recovery.

3. 入水和伸展是指手臂和手从头顶上方一点到完全伸展的运动。入水始于身体开始从一侧侧卧位旋转，止于身体完成旋转到另一侧侧卧位。对于观察者来说，身体的旋转应该是手臂入水并向前伸展的原因。你应该感觉到手臂像是随着旋转的身体自然伸展，而不是像手从肩膀猛地向前刺出。从这里开始，回到步骤1（划水），开始一个新的划水循环。

3. The entry and extension is the movement of the arm and hand from the point just past the top of the head to full extension. The entry starts as the body begins to rotate from one side-lying position and ends as the body finishes rotating to the other side-lying position. To an observer, it should appear that body rotation is the reason that the arm enters the water and then extends in front of the body. You should feel as if the arm is de-spooling off the rotating body rather than as if the hand is stabbing forward from the shoulder. From here, go back to step 1, the stroke, to start a new stroke cycle.

 

请注意，你的手臂动作会随着核心身体的每一次旋转而交替。在一次旋转中，右臂参与上述动作1，而左臂参与上述动作3；下一次旋转则相反——这就引出了我们之前讨论的问题：如何完成这些旋转，以及如何将你的划水动作与这些旋转动作衔接起来。

Note that your arm motions alternate with each core body rotation. With one rotation, the right arm is engaged in 1 above while the left arm is engaged in 3, and vice versa on the next rotation—which brings us back to the topic of how you create those rotations and how you connect your strokes to them.

在上一章中，你学习并练习了VKR和LAR练习中以腿部驱动的核心旋转技巧。在游泳中，你需要利用这些以腿部驱动的核心旋转作为推进的主要动力，让肩膀、手臂和手部更多地扮演传动装置的角色，而不是发动机，从而将工作分配给多个肌群。那么，绕身体长轴旋转（髋部和肩膀在一个与你的预期运动方向垂直的平面上旋转）如何能推动你游向对岸呢？要回答这个问题，你可以把你的身体想象成一台游泳机器——就像你的汽车是一台驾驶机器一样。

In the previous chapter, you learned and practiced leg-driven core-rotation skills in the VKR and LAR drills. In swimming, you want to use these leg-driven core rotations as the main engine of propulsion and to allow the shoulders, arms, and hands to act more as transmissions than engines, distributing the work among many muscle groups. How can rotating around the long axis of the body (rotating the hips and shoulders in a plane at right angles to your intended motion) propel you toward the far wall? To answer that, think of your body as a swimming machine—much as your car is a driving machine.

汽车有发动机，发动机通过曲轴产生旋转力。游泳机的“发动机”则由你的腿部和下半身核心肌群组成。正确运用这些肌肉，可以带动髋部、脊柱和肩部的旋转。

The car has an engine, which produces rotational forces by way of its crankshaft. Your swimming machine’s engine encompasses your legs and core lower-torso muscles. Used properly, they initiate the rotations of your hips, spine, and shoulders.

汽车的变速器和差速器将曲轴的旋转动力传递到轮胎。在你的游泳机中，背部、肩部和手臂的肌肉就如同变速器和差速器一样发挥作用。它们通过支撑和稳定上臂、前臂和手部，将核心肌群的旋转力传递到水中。

The car’s transmission and differential transmit the rotation of the crankshaft to the tires. In your swimming machine, muscles of the back, shoulders, and arms act as the transmission and differential. They do this by supporting and stabilizing the upper arm, forearm, and hand in order to direct the core’s rotational forces through them to the water.

发动机产生的旋转力最终通过轮胎传递到路面，产生直线运动。轮胎抓住路面上的某个点，使施加的力转化为推进力。由于你的游泳机是水上交通工具，所以你用的是桨——你的手臂和手——而不是轮胎。从某种意义上说，你手臂和手的大面积桨叶抓住水面，使身体核心旋转产生的力转化为直线推进力。

What began as rotational force from the engine is finally applied to the road through the tires to produce linear motion. The tires grip a spot on the road so that the applied force becomes propulsion. Because your swimming machine is an aquatic craft, you have paddles—your arms and hands—instead of tires. The large surface area of your arm-plus-hand paddle, in a sense, holds onto a spot in the water so that the force of core body rotation produces linear propulsion.

汽车要正常行驶，三个部件必须协同工作——发动机带动曲轴转动，变速箱啮合，轮胎抓地。如果其中任何一个部件运转不正常，车辆就会停止——游泳机也是如此。

For your car to work properly, all three components must work together—the engine turns the crankshaft, the transmission is engaged, and the tires grip the road. If any one of the components is not operating properly, the vehicle will come to a halt—so too with your swimming machine.

想象一下，你的游泳机正在运转，侧身滑行，此时你左臂的划水手已经越过头部。你的右臂向前伸展。你可以在第53页的图5.4b中看到这个姿势。踢动你的右腿，启动整个身体围绕紧绷的绳索（曲轴）的旋转（引擎）。随着身体开始旋转，你通过旋转上臂来调动背部、肩部和手臂肌肉（传动装置），使前臂和手（桨）尽可能地向前伸展，并保持肘部不下垂（图5.4c ，第53页）。这个动作可以强化从脊柱到手部的整个肌肉通路。此时，在旋转的早期阶段，你的传动装置已经完全启动。一旦前臂和手与垂直方向成45度角，桨就找到了一个可以抓握的摩擦点。为了保持划水时的抓水力，请尽可能保持桨杆垂直，并在身体旋转经过桨杆时使其紧贴水面（图 5.4 d，第 53 页）。如果肘部下沉或仅仅依靠手臂和肩部肌肉向后猛拉手，就会打滑——就像汽车车轮空转一样。在核心身体旋转的同时，保持身体的动力传递，只需施加足够的肩部和手臂力量，使划水动作与核心身体旋转同时完成即可。

Imagine that your swimming machine is in motion, gliding on your right side just as the hand on your recovering left arm has passed your head. Your right arm is extended out front. You can see this position in figure 5.4b on page 53. Kick your right leg to initiate rotation (the engine) of your entire body around your tight line (the crankshaft). As your body begins to rotate, you engage your back, shoulder, and arm muscles (the transmission) by rotating your upper arm to get your forearm and hand (the paddle) moving toward vertical and as far out in front as possible without dropping your elbow (figure 5.4c, page 53). This action firms the entire muscular path from the spine to the hand. At this point, early in your rotation, your transmission is fully engaged. Once the forearm and hand are at a 45-degree angle toward vertical, the paddle has established a traction spot to hold onto. Maintain traction by keeping your paddle as vertical as possible and glued to that spot as your body rotates past it (figure 5.4d, page 53). If you drop your elbow or simply use your arm and shoulder muscles to yank your hand backward in the water, you’ll be slipping water—the same as spinning your wheels in your car. Keep your transmission engaged as your core body rotation continues by applying only enough shoulder and arm force to finish the stroke at the same moment that core body rotation finishes.

腿部驱动的身体旋转能使你的游泳动作更强劲流畅，减少局部肌肉疲劳，并带来显著的健身益处。与主要依靠手臂和肩部肌肉发力相比，这种方法能调动多达五倍的肌肉量。这能显著增加高强度运动后数小时内的脂肪燃烧量。

Leg-driven body rotation makes your swimming more powerful and fluid, reduces local muscle fatigue, and has great fitness benefits. You involve as much as five times more muscle mass as you would when using primarily arm and shoulder muscles to do the work. This greatly increases the amount of fat that is burned during the few hours following a high-intensity workout.

前象限游泳

Front-Quadrant Swimming

 

现在您已经了解了划水臂如何与旋转引擎连接并同步，接下来需要了解回旋臂和划水臂是如何连接的。任何船只在水中的形状，包括您的游泳机，以及其长、宽、深的比例，决定了该船只在任何给定速度下所受到的波浪阻力。这就是为什么各种赛艇都修长流线型的原因。对于您的游泳机而言，这意味着当身体在每个划水周期中尽可能保持较长的划水姿势时，阻力和克服阻力所需的功率都会显著降低。想象一下，在一场帆船比赛中，两艘实力相当的赛艇和船员进行比赛。再想象一下，每秒钟，其中一艘船会短暂地变成拖船的形状，持续半秒钟，然后再变回赛艇的形状。您会押注另一艘船，因为它始终保持着修长流线型的船身。

Now that you’re acquainted with how the stroking arm is connected and timed to the rotation engine, you need to understand how the recovering arm and stroking arm are connected. The shape of any vessel in the water, including your swimming machine, and the ratios of length, width, and depth determine the amount of wave drag that that vessel has at any given speed. This is why racing boats of all kinds are long and sleek. The implication for your swimming machine is that drag and the power required to overcome it are significantly reduced when the body stays as long as possible throughout each stroke cycle. Imagine a sailing event in which two evenly matched racing boats and crews are pitted against one another. Also imagine that once every second, one of the boats morphs into a tugboat shape for half a second, then morphs back into a racing-boat shape. You would bet on the other boat because it keeps its long, sleek shape.

现在想象一个身高 6 英尺（近 2 米）的人，当他伸展到完全流线型姿势时，在水中就变成了一艘 8 英尺长（2.4 米）的船。我们称之为他的赛艇形状（图 5.1）。

Now imagine a 6-foot-tall (almost 2 m) person who, when stretched to full streamline position, becomes an 8-foot-long (2.4 m) vessel in the water. We’ll call this his racing-boat shape (figure 5.1).

 

图 5.1细长的流线型赛艇形状。

Figure 5.1 Long, streamlined racing-boat shape.

 

假设他同时开始划水和恢复动作，因此他的恢复臂和划水臂几乎同时越过肩膀。这样，他的船身就缩短到了6英尺。我们称之为他的拖船形（图5.2）。这位游泳运动员每次划水都会在8英尺的竞速艇形和6英尺的拖船形之间交替变化。

Say that he begins his recovery and his stroke at the same time and that his recovering arm and pulling arm are therefore passing the shoulders at about the same time. He has shortened his vessel back to 6 feet. We will call this his tugboat shape (figure 5.2). This swimmer alternately morphs from the 8-foot racing-boat shape to the 6-foot tugboat shape and back with every stroke he swims.

 

图 5.2较短的拖船形状，划水手和回收手在肩部附近交错。

Figure 5.2 Shorter tugboat shape with stroking hand and recovering hand passing each other near the shoulders.

 

隔壁泳道的女选手（身高相同，体型也与她相同）学习了一种叫做前象限游泳的技巧。如下图所示，她并没有像通常那样同时开始划水和收臂，而是保持侧卧姿势，前臂伸直，直到收臂手越过头部。图中的大圆圈表示，当划水手仍处于前象限时，收臂手即将入水。另一种理解方式是，想象她的交接区——即向前移动的收臂手越过向后移动的划水手的区域——位于她的头部前方（图 5.3）。这样，她几乎在整个划水周期中都能保持流线型的侧卧姿势，并尽可能地保持身体长度。在每个划水周期中保持身体长度，可以显著减少波浪阻力，并使手臂划水和核心旋转同步进行。划水整合练习将教会你如何保持身体长度，并正确地控制手臂动作的时机。

The woman in the next lane (same height, same racing-boat shape) has learned a technique called front-quadrant swimming. In the following figure, you can see that instead of starting her recovery and pull together, she stays on her side with her lead arm extended until her recovering hand has passed her head. The large circle shows that the woman’s recovering arm is about to enter the water while her stroking hand is still in the front quadrant. Another way of thinking about this is by imagining that her passing zone—the area where the recovering hand, which is moving forward, passes the stroking hand, which is moving backward—is in front of her head (figure 5.3). In this way, she maintains her streamlined, side-lying position and most of its length for nearly the entire stroke cycle. Keeping her vessel long throughout each stroke cycle reduces wave drag dramatically and allows the arm stroke and core rotation to begin together. The stroke-integration drills will teach you to keep your swimming machine long and to properly time your arm motions.

 

图 5.3前象限游泳。这位游泳运动员仍然保持着修长流线型的赛艇体态。她的划水手会从头部前方越过她的回水手。

Figure 5.3 Front-quadrant swimming. This swimmer is still in a long, streamlined racing-boat shape. Her stroking hand will pass her recovering hand in front of her head.

 

击球整合练习

Stroke-Integration Drills

 

那么，如何将侧身游泳、以腿部驱动身体旋转作为主要推进力以及前象限游泳等概念融入到日常游泳中呢？你需要进行一些泳姿整合练习。不过，在学习这些练习之前，你应该已经熟练掌握了所有姿势和平衡练习。即使在学习后续更复杂的练习时，也应该继续练习这些基础的姿势和平衡练习。

So how do you integrate all these concepts—swimming on your sides, using leg-driven body rotation as your primary source of propulsion, and front-quadrant swimming—into normal swimming? You will use several stroke-integration drills. Before you begin learning these drills, however, you already should have become comfortable with all the posture and balance drills. And you should continue practicing them even as you add the more complex drills that follow.

练习这些动作时，请注意，不使用呼吸管呼吸时，你大约会一半的呼吸用在身体的一侧，一半用在另一侧。两侧呼吸都要顺畅。这个原则适用于所有练习，也适用于完整的划水动作。

As you practice these drills, notice that when you breathe without a snorkel, you will be taking roughly half your breaths to one side of your body and half to the other side. It is important to breathe well to either side of your body. This idea applies to all of the drills and to full-stroke swimming as well.

侧滑单桨（SGSS）

Side-Glide Single Strokes (SGSS)

 

这个练习最好使用呼吸管进行，它旨在培养你从身体一侧侧滑姿势转身到另一侧侧滑姿势的技巧。首先，蹬墙起跳。以侧滑姿势（鼻尖朝下）轻松踢腿（图 5.4 a）。检查你的姿势和平衡反馈工具。将侧臂收回水面以上。当这只手越过你的头部时（图 5.4 b），利用一次踢腿开始旋转身体，保持鼻尖朝下。随着核心旋转的开始，收回侧臂的手应该入水，另一只手臂开始划水（图 5.4 c）。你的双手应该在交错区交错。继续划水（图 5.4 d），同时向另一侧侧滑姿势旋转。你希望在手臂划水结束于大腿时，身体也旋转到另一侧侧滑姿势。现在你应该处于侧滑姿势，头部朝下（图 5.4 e）。继续轻松踢腿，同时深呼吸几次。继续侧滑踢腿一段时间，并检查你的姿势和平衡反馈工具。重复以上动作，每只手臂都要踢满整个泳池长度。

This drill, best learned with a snorkel, introduces the skill of taking a single stroke to turn from a side-glide position on one side of your body to a side-glide position on the other side. Start by pushing off from the wall. Begin kicking easily in a side-glide nose-down position (figure 5.4a). Check your posture and balance feedback tools.
