Recover your side arm above the surface of the water. As that hand passes your head (figure 5.4b), use one of your kicks to begin rotating your body, keeping your nose pointed down. As your core rotation begins, your recovering hand should enter the water and the other arm should begin the stroke (figure 5.4c). Your hands should pass each other in the passing zone. Continue the stroke (figure 5.4d) while rotating toward the other side-glide position. You want your rotation to reach the other side-glide position just as the arm stroke finishes at your thigh. You should now be in a side-glide nose-down position (figure 5.4e). Take a few breaths as you continue to kick easily. Check your posture and balance feedback tools as you continue kicking on your side a little longer. Repeat these actions for each arm for the entire length of the pool.

 

图 5.4侧滑单次划水练习。(a)起始姿势为平衡的侧滑姿势，头部朝下。(b)你的支撑臂刚好越过头部。(c)随着核心开始旋转，支撑手刺破水面，同时另一只手臂开始划水。双手在交错区交错。(d)旋转和划水继续进行，另一只手臂在身体前方完全伸展。(e)身体旋转结束的同时，手臂划水也结束于大腿处。此时你的头部仍然朝下，你已侧滑到另一侧。

Figure 5.4 Side-glide single strokes drill. (a) Begin in a balanced, side-glide nose-down position. (b) Your recovering arm just passes your head. (c) As core rotation begins, your recovering hand pierces the surface as your other arm begins the stroke. Your hands pass each other in the passing zone. (d) Rotation and stroke continue as your other arm reaches full extension in front of your body. (e) Body rotation finishes just as your arm stroke finishes at the thigh. With your nose still pointed down, you are now side-gliding on your other side.

 

要想将手臂动作与旋转打腿完美配合，关键在于让手在对侧腿向前踢水的同时入水（打腿的下拍）。或者，你也可以专注于让手在同侧腿向后收回的同时入水（打腿的上拍）。单侧入水与打腿的配合会比另一侧更容易。现在就掌握这两种配合方式，或者其中一种，将有助于你日后将多种划水动作与节奏性旋转动作连接起来。

The key to properly timing the arm’s motion with a rotation kick is to have your hand enter the water just as the leg on the opposite side kicks forward (the downbeat of the kick). Alternatively, you can focus on your hand entering the water just as the leg on the same side recovers backward (the upbeat of the kick). It will be easier to pair a hand entry with a kick on one side than on the other. Getting a feel now for either or both of these pairings will help you later when you start connecting multiple strokes to rhythmic rotations.

当你熟练掌握了使用呼吸管的练习后，就可以加入真正的呼吸动作了。摘掉呼吸管，侧身滑行，鼻尖朝下，像之前一样开始练习。但是，在开始旋转和划水时，让你的头部随着身体转动，而不是保持鼻尖朝下。这样，划水结束时，你的身体会变成侧身滑行，鼻尖朝上，而不是鼻尖朝下。继续轻松踢腿，同时深呼吸几次。检查你的姿势和平衡。将头部转回鼻尖朝下的位置。现在你回到了与起始位置相反的一侧。再次检查你的姿势和平衡，保持侧身姿势再踢几下。重复以上动作，每只手臂都要踢完泳池的整个长度。

Once you’ve mastered this drill while using a snorkel, it’s time to add real breathing motions. Without the snorkel, start side-gliding with your nose down and begin the drill as you did before. As the rotation and stroke begin, however, allow your head to turn with your body instead of remaining nose-down. You will end up in a side-glide nose-up position at the end of the stroke instead of in a nose-down position. Take a few breaths as you continue to kick easily. Check your posture and balance feedback tools. Turn your head back to a nose-down position. You are now in a starting position on the opposite side from where you started. Check your posture and balance again as you remain on your side for a few more kicks. Repeat these actions for each arm for the entire length of the pool.

尽管你在SGB练习中已经尽力，但在身体旋转到抬头姿势时，你可能仍然会不自觉地抬起头部或上半身。单独转动头部会使这种情况更加糟糕。相反，你应该主动利用红点瞄准点来保持头部低垂，以便转身换气。同时，尝试使用你在SGNU练习开始时所采用的策略，屏住呼吸直到你确信自己保持平衡且感觉舒适。反复练习，直到你能稳定地直接旋转到平衡的抬头姿势，而无需重新调整或“安顿”。

Despite the work you did in the SGB drill, you may still tend to lift your head or upper body as your body rotates to the nose-up position. Turning your head separately makes this situation even worse. Instead, proactively use the red-dot focus point to keep your head low as you turn for air. Also try using the strategy that you used to start the SGNU drill, holding your breath until you are sure that you are balanced and comfortable. Practice until you consistently rotate directly to a balanced nose-up position without having to readjust or “settle.”

练习侧滑划水时要有耐心。你的大脑和身体可能很想立刻进行下一次划水。要克制这种冲动。相反，每次到达下一个侧滑位置时，都要暂停足够长的时间，通过以下方式进行评估、纠正和提前计划：

• 评估你完成旋转时的位置——姿势、平衡、前导臂角度——以及你是如何达到这个位置的。在开始SGSS练习之前，你应该已经进行了足够的侧滑练习，并花足够的时间检查每个反馈工具，从而知道自己是否以完美的水平紧绷线完成了旋转。

• Assess the position you finished the rotation in—posture, balance, lead arm angle—and how you got there. By the time you start the SGSS drill, you should have done enough side-gliding and spent enough time checking each of the feedback tools to know whether you have finished with an impeccable, horizontal tight line.

• 纠正你的姿势、平衡或位置上的任何缺陷。

• Correct any flaws in your posture, balance, or position.

• 为下一次重复练习做好计划。决定是否需要做出任何改变，并在继续之前在脑海中预演下一步动作。

• Plan ahead for the next repetition. Decide whether you need to make any changes, and mentally rehearse your next step before continuing.

 

随着你在 SGSS 练习中不断进步，你会对自己在旋转时保持姿势和平衡的能力更有信心，在评估自己的表现后，很少或根本不需要进行纠正。

As you improve at the SGSS drill, you will gain confidence in your ability to maintain your posture and balance as you rotate, seldom or never needing to make corrections after assessing your performance.

通往SGSS的垫脚石

Stepping-Stone to SGSS

 

如果你发现很难保持前导臂和头部前方传球区域的平衡，可以尝试以下方法：不要完全从一侧旋转到另一侧，而是旋转到一半时停止，此时身体平躺在水面上，双臂向前伸直。保持这个姿势踢腿几秒钟，直到你确定自己保持平衡。然后继续旋转并向另一侧踢腿。

If you find it difficult to stay in balance with your lead arm and your passing zone in front of your head, try the following: Instead of rotating completely from one side to the other, stop halfway, when you are flat on your front, with both arms extended in front of you. Continue kicking in this position for several seconds until you are sure that you are balanced. Then continue the rotation and stroke to your other side.

反馈工具

Feedback Tools

 

• 你已经知道并且应该使用所有关于侧滑姿势的反馈工具。

• You already know, and should use, all the feedback tools for your side-glide positions.

• 旋转时要保持对浮标的压力，确保臀部在整个旋转过程中始终保持在水面。如果在旋转过程中臀部没有保持在水面，并且在侧滑姿势开始时感觉不到侧腹（或从侧臂到手腕的干燥皮肤），那么你可能出现了以下三种情况之一：(1) 绳索松脱；(2) 浮标压力过低；(3) 头部抬起。头部抬起是最可能的原因，几乎肯定会导致你失去对浮标的压力和绳索的紧绷感。

• Keep pressure on your buoy as you rotate so that your hips stay at the surface throughout the rotation to your other side. If your butt does not remain at the surface of the water as you rotate and if you are not able to feel your flank (or the dry strip of flesh on the side arm all the way to your wrist) exposed just as you get to the side-glide position, then you have either (1) lost your tight line, (2) lost buoy pressure, or (3) lifted your head. A lifted head is the most likely culprit, and it will almost certainly cause you to lose your buoy pressure and your tight line.

• 不使用呼吸管时，检查你的头部和身体是否作为一个整体旋转，而不是头部先转动或身体先转动。记住，头部和臀部要一起移动。

• When you are not using a snorkel, check that your head and body rotate as a single unit rather than head first or body first. Think, Head and hips move together.

 

做个小实验

Experiment a Bit

 

通过练习，你会逐渐减少在每个侧滑姿势上检查平衡和姿势的时间。之后，你可以尝试在不转头呼吸的情况下重复一些动作，保持鼻子朝下。常见的呼吸模式包括每两次或每三次重复呼吸一次。当然，现在你应该已经习惯在宽松和紧绷的姿势之间切换了。

With practice, you will gradually spend less time in each side-glide position checking your balance and posture. You can then experiment by performing some of the repeats without turning your head to breathe, remaining nose down. Common breathing patterns include breathing every second repeat or every third repeat. Of course, experimenting with shifting between schlumpy and tight-line postures should be a habit by now.

SGSS 练习是学习各种概念和技能的绝佳工具，这些概念和技能最终会应用到其他练习和全泳姿中。反过来，这些概念和技能也会提​​升你 SGSS 练习的执行水平。在进行下一个练习之前，请花些时间，一次练习一个重点，专注于 SGSS 练习中的以下每个要点。

The SGSS drill is a great tool for learning a variety of concepts and skills that you’ll eventually apply to other drills and to full-stroke swimming. Each of these concepts and skills will, in turn, refine your execution of the SGSS drill. Before moving on to the next drill, spend some time working on each of the following focus points, one at a time, in the SGSS drill.

 
重点➤向下刺入（而非推入）至延长线
 

在水中向下伸展手臂的角度非常重要。开始旋转时，指尖应刺破水面，然后沿着一条直线以略微向下的角度继续伸展，直到手臂完全伸直。同时，前臂也应该像手掌一样滑过同一个小孔。一个常见的错误是将手臂笔直向前伸展，刚好在水面上方或下方，然后再将手和手臂向下推到所需的角度。这样做会给肩膀带来不必要的压力，迫使身体前部抬起、臀部下沉，并浪费能量。

 
重点➤手套
 

大多数初级和中级游泳者都是后肢划水。为了过渡到前肢划水，有时可以稍微夸大一下手臂划水的节奏。想象一下，伸出的手戴着一副宽松的手套。在开始旋转时保持伸出的手伸直，同时另一只手向前向下划水，靠近伸出的手的顶部。当指尖滑入手套的袖口下方时，手套的掌心就会打开，伸出的手臂就可以开始划水，而收回的手则继续向前滑入手套内。这样做的目的是在伸出手的瞬间，将想象中的手套从一只手转移到另一只手。请注意，这只是为了教学目的而夸大的动作，正常游泳时，两只手实际上不会接触。但是，你需要让收回的手在伸出的手臂开始下一次划水之前几乎追上伸出的手——这就是“传递区”的概念。

 
焦点➤宽追踪
 

手套焦点能让你很好地感知手臂纵向的位置，但这样一来，每只手的进出路线都沿着头部正前方的一条直线——就像在单轨列车上行驶一样。而当你不使用手套焦点时，理想的情况是每只手的进出路线都位于自身肩膀的正前方——就像在标准的双轨轨道上行驶，轨道间距大致与肩宽相同。如果想要更进一步，你还希望笔画的大致间距也与肩宽相等。

 
重点➤斑驳的脸颊
 

良好的平衡意味着始终保持水平姿势，臀部始终位于水面。游泳或进行任何涉及身体旋转的练习时，要始终保持一侧臀部或大腿（紧贴泳衣下方）的皮肤，或者一侧或两侧臀部，暴露在空气中——尤其是在呼吸时。这需要紧绷的姿势和足够的浮力支撑。抬头或用手向下推身体前方的水都会迅速使臀部下沉。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Pierce (Not Push) Down to Extension
 

It is important how you extend your arm at a downward angle in the water. As you begin to rotate, your fingertips should pierce the surface of the water and then continue along a straight line, at a slight downward angle, until your arm is fully extended. You also want your forearm to slide through the same small hole that your hand did. A common error is to extend the arm straight forward, either just above or just below the surface, and to then push the hand and arm down to the desired angle. This puts unnecessary stress on the shoulder, forces your front end up and your hips down, and wastes energy.

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ The Glove
 

Most novice and intermediate swimmers are rear-quadrant swimmers. To make the change to front-quadrant swimming, it is useful to sometimes exaggerate the arm timing a bit. Imagine that the extended hand has a loose-fitting glove on it. Leave it extended as you begin to rotate and as the other hand pierces the surface of the water forward and down toward the top of the extended hand. As soon as the fingertips slip under the cuff of the glove, the palm of the glove opens, allowing the extended arm to start stroking while the recovering hand continues to slide forward fully into the glove. The idea is to transfer the imaginary glove from hand to hand out in front at the extension point. Note that this is an exaggerated movement for instructive purposes only, and that when swimming normally, the two hands will not actually touch. You will, however, want the recovering hand to almost catch up to the extended hand before the extended arm begins the next stroke—hence, the passing-zone concept.

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Wide Tracking
 

The glove focus point gives you a good feeling for where your arms should be longitudinally, but it has each hand entering and extending along a line directly in front of your head—as if you were moving along a monorail. What you want at any time you are not using the glove focus point is for each hand to enter and extend directly in front of its own shoulder—as if you were moving along a standard two-rail track with rails roughly shoulder-width apart. Taking wide tracking a step further, you want the general lines of the strokes to be shoulder-width apart as well.

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Patches and Cheeks
 

Good balance means keeping a horizontal position at all times with your hips right at the surface. When swimming or when doing any drill that involves body rotation, focus on keeping a patch of skin on one hip or thigh just below your suit, or one or both butt cheeks, exposed to the air at all times—especially when breathing. A combination of tight-line posture and sufficient buoy pressure is required. Lifting the head or using a hand to push down on the water in front of the body will quickly sink the hips.

 

三冲程与滑翔（3S&G）

Three Strokes & Glide (3S&G)

 
当你对SGSS练习中的重点动作练习足够熟练，感到舒适自信后，就可以开始增加划水次数了。这项新练习将帮助你更快地掌握游泳技巧。顾名思义，它的意思是先划三下，然后滑行。虽然听起来很简单，但要正确掌握，你需要分几个步骤来学习：

1. 使用训练呼吸管，首先从右侧蹬水，以侧滑姿势（头部朝下）踢腿。一旦身体保持直线平衡，将后侧（左侧）手臂收回水面，然后像在SGSS练习中那样，旋转身体并划水至左侧。立即开始收回后侧（右侧）手臂；当手臂越过头部时，在进行第二次划水的同时旋转身体至右侧。一旦身体完全侧卧，立即收回后侧（左侧）手臂。当手臂越过头部时，再次旋转身体，在进行第三次划水的同时旋转身体至左侧。当身体完全侧卧后，停止除踢腿以外的所有动作。在侧滑姿势中停留足够的时间，以评估和纠正你的姿势和平衡，并计划任何可能改善接下来三次划水的调整。请注意，你现在滑行的侧方与你开始时的侧方相反。再做一组三次划水（这将使你回到右侧的初始侧滑姿势）。再次评估、纠正并提前计划。重复此动作直至游完泳池全程。每次三次划水循环都要保持连续的游泳节奏。在SGSS练习中手部入水到腿部的协调性基础上，现在你需要有节奏地在每个三次划水循环中连续进行手部入水。反复练习此步骤，直到你能以良好的姿势和平衡完成每组三次划水，且无需任何调整。

1. Using your training snorkel, start by pushing off on your right side and kicking in the side-glide position, nose down. As soon as you are in a tight line and in balance, recover the trailing (left) arm over the water, and rotate and stroke onto your left side as you did in the SGSS drill. Immediately begin to recover the trailing (right) arm; then, as it passes your head, rotate onto your right side while taking the second stroke. As soon as you are on your right side, recover the trailing (left) arm. As it passes your head, rotate again while taking your third stroke onto the left side. When you are fully on your side, stop all action except kicking. Spend as much time as you need in the side-glide position to assess and correct your posture and balance and to plan for any changes that might improve the next set of three strokes. Note that you are now gliding on the left side of your body, opposite the side you started on. Go through another set of three strokes (which will return you to your original side-glide position on your right side). Again assess, correct, and plan ahead. Repeat for the length of the pool. Each cycle of three strokes is done in a continuous swimming rhythm. Expanding upon the hand-entry-to-kick coordination from the SGSS drill, you now want to rhythmically execute that coordination with successive hand entries in each three-stroke cycle. Practice this step until you can complete each set of three strokes with good posture and balance and without having to adjust anything.

2. 学习进阶的第二步与第一步类似。但这次，你不再需要使用呼吸管并将鼻子向下，而是在每组划水的第三划时转动头部换气。练习开始时，动作与之前相同，但在开始第三划时，像在SGSS练习中那样，让头部随着身体转动。完成这一划并到达侧滑位置时，你的鼻子会抬起。评估并调整你的姿势和平衡。吸一口气（如果需要，可以吸几口），然后将头部转回鼻子向下的位置，再次评估并调整你的姿势和平衡，并为下一个循环做好准备。重复此步骤，直至游完泳池长度。反复练习，直到你能以完全平衡、侧滑抬头的姿势完成每组三划，并且无需任何调整。

2. The second step in the learning progression is similar to the first step. But instead of using the snorkel and keeping your nose down, you will now rotate your head to breathe on the third stroke of each set of strokes. Start the drill as you did before, but as you begin the third stroke, let your head turn with your body just as it did in the SGSS drill. As you finish that stroke and reach your side-glide position, your nose will be up. Assess and correct your posture and balance. Take a breath (or several, if needed) and turn your head back to the nose-down position, assess and correct your posture and balance again, and plan ahead for the next cycle. Repeat for the length of the pool. Practice this step until you can complete each set of three strokes fully balanced, in the side-glide nose-up position, and without having to adjust anything.

3. 学习三桨滑行（3S&G）的最后一步是在每组划水动作的第二个划水动作时吸气，并在每组三个划水动作之间的滑行阶段保持头部向下的姿势。和之前一样，在滑行过程中评估并纠正姿势和平衡，并在继续下一组三个划水动作之前提前做好计划。这一步的目标是：吸气时，头部随身体转动至头部向上的位置，吸气，然后头部随身体转动回头部向下的位置，整个过程都不​​能打乱划水的节奏，也不能失去姿势或平衡。如果在几组三个划水动作后，你感觉需要更多空气，可以在滑行阶段转动头部再吸一两口气（但前提是你已经评估并纠正了姿势和平衡）。

3. The final step in learning 3S&G is to take your breath on the second stroke of each set of strokes and to do the glide portion between each set of three strokes in a nose-down position. As before, assess and correct posture and balance and plan ahead during the glide before you continue with the next set of three strokes. The goal of this step is to take that breath by letting your head rotate with your body to a nose-up position, then to inhale, and then to let your head rotate with your body back to a nose-down position, all without disrupting the rhythm of strokes and without losing your posture or balance. If after a couple of sets of three strokes you find that you need more air, you may turn your head to take an additional breath or two during the glide phase (but only after you have assessed and corrected your posture and balance).

 

反馈工具

Feedback Tools

 

• 每次旋转和划水时，你都应该注意你的肚脐直接指向侧壁，就像你在侧滑姿势时一样。

• Each time you rotate and stroke, you should be aware of your navel pointing directly toward the sidewall, just as it does when you are in side-glide position.

• 每次划水时，务必将双手交替伸到身前，或许可以时不时地利用手套的焦点。

• Each time you take a stroke, be sure to swap hands out in front of your body, perhaps using the glove focus point from time to time.

• 在每组划水动作的第三桨结束时，当你到达侧滑位置时，你应该能感觉到后臂上干燥的肌肉条。如果没有感觉到，说明你可能抬起了头、松开了浮标、解开了鱼线，或者以上几种情况的组合。

• As you reach the side-glide position at the end of the third stroke of each set, you should feel the dry strip of flesh along your trailing arm. If not, you have either lifted your head up, let pressure off your buoy, lost your tight line, or some combination thereof.

• 进行必要的调整，并保持侧滑姿势足够长的时间，以便思考在接下来的三杆中需要做的任何改变。

• Make any necessary corrections and stay in the side-glide position long enough to think through any changes you will need to make on the next set of three strokes.

 

做个小实验

Experiment a Bit

 

如果你仔细遵循我制定的训练计划，在掌握每个步骤后再进行下一步，最终你会掌握一种接近完整泳姿的练习方法，这种方法既能让你评估自身动作，又能让你有机会进行调整和提前规划。随着你3S&G练习的进步，你可以在每组划水动作中增加划水次数，从而有效地将练习变成5S&G或7S&G练习，在这种练习中，你将在每组划水动作中换两次或更多次呼吸。只有当你能够在换气的同时保持姿势、平衡和节奏，并且能够在每次滑行阶段都保持完全平衡、笔直的泳姿，无需任何调整时，才能增加划水次数。

If you carefully follow the progression I’ve laid out, mastering each step before moving on to the next, you will end up with a drill that is close to full-stroke swimming but that provides opportunities to assess, correct, and plan ahead. As you improve at the 3S&G drill, you can take more strokes in each set of strokes, effectively turning the drill into a 5S&G or 7S&G drill in which you will take two or more breaths during each set of strokes. Only increase the number of strokes once you are able to maintain posture, balance, and rhythm while taking breaths and only once you are able to enter each glide phase with a fully balanced tight line that needs no correction.

微调你的击球动作

Fine-Tuning Your Stroke

 

你可能已经注意到，目前为止介绍的概念和练习都是建立在先前信息的基础上的。你正在构建技能和知识体系，而这仅仅是个开始。基本技能是基础，在此基础上才能发展出更精细、更复杂的技能。本节详细讲解了整个划水循环——划水、回水、入水和伸展——并对之前讨论的内容进行了补充和完善。后续章节还会有更多内容。为什么我不一次性讲完所有内容，然后直接让你去泳池练习呢？因为在其他复杂项目中积累的经验在这里很有启发意义——也就是说，在你能够站在地面上抛接网球之前，详细讲解如何在高空骑独轮车时同时抛接链锯是没有意义的。换句话说，信息过载反而会阻碍学习。

You have likely noticed that the concepts and drills presented so far each build on prior information. You are constructing both a skill base and a knowledge base, and you are only partially done. Fundamental skills are the foundation on which refinements and more complex skills can be built. This sections details the entire stroke cycle—stroke, recovery, and entry and extension—and offers refinements and additions to what has already been discussed. In subsequent chapters, there will be even more. Why don’t I just explain it all at once and then send you to the pool? Because experience gained in another complex endeavor is instructive here—that is, detailed instructions for juggling chain-saws while riding a unicycle on a high wire are not germane until sometime after you can juggle tennis balls while standing on terra firma. In other words, too much information too soon gets in the way of learning.

推进式手臂划水

Propulsive Arm Stroke

 

现在是时候更详细地解释一下在水下划水推进阶段，手和手臂是如何工作的了。简单来说，你的划水臂（也就是你的手和前臂）应该尽可能地伸到身体前方，并与池底保持垂直，而且在整个划水过程中都应该尽可能长时间地保持这种垂直状态。这通常被称为高肘划水。听起来很简单，但和往常一样，其中还有一些细节需要说明。

It’s time to explain more fully what the hand and arm do during the underwater propulsive part of the stroke. Simply put, your paddle (that is, your hand and forearm) should be vertical to the pool bottom as far out in front of your body as possible and should be kept vertical for as much of the stroke as possible. This is often referred to as swimming with a high-elbow stroke. It sounds simple, but as usual, there are details to clarify.

划桨动作始于所谓的“入水”——也就是你第一次抓住水面获得推进力的那一刻。为了感受入水的感觉，将一个空的啤酒桶（或类似大小的圆形容器）侧放在矮桌上。身体前倾，手臂向前伸展，略微向下倾斜，手轻轻放在桶顶上。然后向前迈一步，保持手放在桶上的相同位置，让桶向前滚动。随着桶的滚动，将手和手臂弯曲覆盖在桶上，略微抬起肘部，避免身体倚靠或以其他方式对桶施加任何向下的压力。继续滚动桶，直到你的手位于桶的另一侧，肘部内侧和上臂接触到桶顶（记住，不要倾斜身体）。要达到这个位置，你需要张开腋窝并收紧背部肌肉，这样就能在背部、肩膀和桨之间形成一条肌肉张力线。我称之为桨的连杆。你应该还记得，紧绷的姿势使你的头部、躯干和臀部紧密连接，形成类似皮划艇的形状。同样地，这种新的肌肉张力也使你的桨与紧绷的绳索紧密连接。现在你应该能体会到划桨开始时的感觉了——也就是入水的感觉。

The stroke begins with what is called the catch—the spot where you first get a propulsive grip on the water. To get a feel for the catch, place an empty beer keg (or similarly sized round container) on its side on a low table. Bend forward and extend your arm in front of you at a bit of a downward angle, placing your hand lightly on top of the keg. Now step forward, keeping your hand on the same spot on the keg so that the keg rolls forward. As the keg rolls, curve your hand and arm over it, lifting your elbow slightly to avoid leaning on or otherwise exerting any downward force on the keg. Continue rolling the keg until your hand is on the far side of the keg and the inside of your elbow and upper arm are touching the top of the keg (remember, no leaning). To reach this position, you had to flare your armpit and contract your back muscles, which engaged a line of muscular tension across your back, through your shoulder, and to your paddle. I call this your paddle linkage. You will recall that the muscular tension of your tight-line posture firmly connects your head, torso, and hips into a kayaklike shape. In the same manner, this new line of muscular tension firmly connects your paddle to your tight line. Now you have an idea of what the beginning of the stroke—that is, the catch—will feel like.

在泳池中尝试一下，想象一个水桶，水深刚好够你侧滑时，手臂向下伸展，手掌刚好搭在桶上（图 5.5a ）。向前滑行时，将手臂弯曲越过桶，向前滚动（图 5.5b）。感觉就像肘部向前越过手掌（图 5.5b和c ） ，而不是将手向后或向下拉。越过桶时，有意识地张开腋窝，感受背部肌肉将桨与绷紧的绳索连接起来——启动你的划水连线。避免向下施压——不要让你的想象中的桶沉下去。

Try it in the pool with an imaginary keg that is just deep enough in the water that as you side glide with your arm extended at a downward angle, your hand rests just on top of the keg (figure 5.5a). As you glide forward, curve your arm over the keg, rolling it forward (figure 5.5b). It should feel as though you are running your elbow forward over your hand (figures 5.5b and c), not pulling your hand back or down. As you reach over the keg, consciously flare your armpit and feel your back muscles connect your paddle to your tight line—engage your paddle linkage. Avoid applying downward pressure—don’t sink your imaginary keg.

 

图 5.5越过酒桶的划桨动作。(a)侧身向前滑行。(b, c)尽可能越过酒桶，将桨叶保持垂直，并尽可能向前伸展。(c, d)在整个划桨过程中尽可能保持桨叶垂直。(e)完成越过酒桶的动作。请注意，在整个划桨过程中，酒桶始终保持在原位，您是越过酒桶而不是向后猛拉它。

Figure 5.5 Over-the-keg stroke. (a) Glide forward on your side. (b, c) Reach over the keg as far as you can, putting your paddle in as vertical a position and as far in front of you as possible. (c, d) Continue to keep the paddle vertical for as much of the stroke as possible. (e) Finish levering past the keg. Note that the keg remains in place throughout the series of drawings, and you move past it rather than yanking it backward.

 

根据肩部的柔韧性，当你的手臂越过酒桶时，你可能正准备开始下一次旋转（肩部柔韧性较好），或者刚刚开始旋转（肩部柔韧性较差）。无论哪种情况，通常的动作是下沉肘部，并利用手臂和肩部肌肉将手向后猛拉划过水面。不要这样做。相反，保持腋窝外展，主要依靠手臂和肩部肌肉，尽可能在划桨过程中保持桨杆垂直（图 5.5 c和d），并利用桨杆连杆将核心旋转的力量传递到桨杆上（图 5.5 e）。这种感觉应该更像是利用杠杆原理越过酒桶，其中高达 75% 的力量来自背部和核心旋转，而只有不到 25% 的力量来自手臂和肩部。

Depending on your shoulder’s flexibility, when you reach your arm over the keg, you are either just about to initiate your next rotation (more flexible shoulders), or you have just begun your rotation (less flexible shoulders). In either case, the typical action is to drop the elbow and to use arm and shoulder muscles to yank the hand backward through the water. Don’t. Instead, keep your armpit flared, use mainly your arm and shoulder muscles to keep your paddle vertical through as much of the stroke as possible (figures 5.5c and d), and use your paddle linkage to transmit core rotation to your paddle (figure 5.5e). The sensation should be more like levering past the keg, with as much as 75 percent of the work coming from the back and core rotation and as little as 25 percent coming from the arms and shoulders.

 
重点➤向下角度手臂伸展（展开）
 

大多数游泳者难以做到有效的划水动作，原因在于他们手臂伸展时要么是水平的，要么是略微向上倾斜。对大多数游泳者而言，除非手臂略微向下倾斜，否则肱骨头和肩胛骨顶部之间的空间不足以实现有效的高肘划水。在这种情况下，游泳者在划水开始时几乎只是向下推水，无法有效地向前推进。手臂略微向下倾斜可以增加划水时的运动幅度，从而帮助游泳者实现有效的划水动作。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Downward Angle Arm Extension (expanded)
 

An effective catch eludes most swimmers because they extend the arm either horizontally or at a bit of an upward angle. For most swimmers, unless the arm is extended at a bit of a downward angle, there is not enough room between the ball of the upper-arm bone and the roof of the shoulder to allow for an effective high-elbow catch. Instead, the swimmer will do little more than push down on the water at the beginning of the stroke, which will not propel him forward. Extending the arm at a bit of a downward angle allows greater range of motion as the swimmer attempts to achieve an effective catch.

 
 
重点➤越桶击球
 

在划水开始时，尽可能向前伸展手臂，越过一个想象中的酒桶，使肘部高高抬起。然后利用核心肌群的旋转，通过紧绷的绳索和桨杆连接处的肌肉张力传递，从而撬动水面越过酒桶。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Over-the-Keg Stroke
 

Reach over an imaginary keg as far out in front of the body as possible to make a high-elbow catch at the beginning of your stroke. Then use your core rotation, transmitted through the muscular tension of your tight line and paddle linkage, to lever past the keg.

 
 
重点➤俏皮的臀部
 

想让你的划水更有力吗？那就试试灵活的髋部动作。用汽车来打比方，发动机曲轴转得越快，车轮转得也越快。同样地，你髋部左右转动得越快，身体向前旋转的速度就越快，越能越过那个假想的“桶”。运用你的长轴旋转技巧来加快髋部的旋转速度。你紧绷的姿势和桨的连贯性会将这额外的速度通过桨传递到水中，从而产生更有推进力的划水。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Snappy Hips
 

Want to put more power in your stroke? Think snappy hips. In the car analogy, the faster the engine turns the crankshaft, the faster the wheels turn. Similarly, the faster you rotate your hips from one side to the other, the faster your body rotates forward past that imaginary keg. Use your long-axis rotation skills to drive a faster rotation of your hips. Your tight-line posture and paddle linkage will transmit that extra speed through your paddle to the water, which will produce a more propulsive stroke.

 
 
重点➤完成你的击球动作
 

一个常见的错误是划水动作没有完成。站直后，双臂向下伸到大腿处。这大致就是你在练习划水动作或以轻松或中等速度游泳时，每次划水动作结束时应该完成的位置。游泳或练习时，在完成一次划水动作后，偶尔用拇指轻触大腿，以便观察划水动作的完成位置。两侧都要这样做，因为两侧的位置通常不同。即使只是划水动作差几英寸，纠正后也能让你每次划水游得更远，从而减少划水次数。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Finish Your Strokes
 

A common error is to not finish your strokes. While standing up straight, reach down with both arms and touch your thighs. This is roughly where you want to finish each stroke when you are practicing drills or when swimming at easy or moderate paces. When swimming or drilling, occasionally brush your thumb against your thigh as you complete a stroke in order to see where you are finishing your strokes. Do this on both sides, as it is common for them to be different. Correcting strokes that are even a few inches short will let you travel noticeably farther with each stroke and thus take fewer strokes.

 

安全高效的回收和进入

Safe and Efficient Recovery and Entry

 

在游泳中，即使是出水动作也至关重要。它们会影响你在水中的运动方式，就像皮划艇运动员在水面上的手臂动作会影响皮划艇在水中的运动一样。纠正手臂出水、向前运动和重新入水的动作可以提高你的游泳技术效率。以下重点内容将按照从恢复动作开始到入水结束的顺序进行讲解。

In swimming, even the motions you make in the air are important. They affect how you move in the water in much the same way that a kayaker’s arm motions above the water affect the kayak in the water. Correcting how your arm comes out of the water, moves forward, and reenters the water can increase the effectiveness of your technique. The following focus points are offered in order from the beginning of your recovery to the end of your entry.

 
重点➤木偶康复
 

恢复动作从划水和旋转动作结束的地方开始——你侧卧，一只手位于大腿下方（或在某些练习中，放在大腿上）。想象你是一个木偶。你的操纵者用一根线连接着你恢复手臂的肘部。操纵者向上拉动这根线，将你的手臂抬出水面。你的肘部抬起，前臂和手自然下垂，肘部放松，指尖靠近水面（甚至可以划过水面），并紧贴身体（图 5.6a ）。随着肘部向船头方向移动，手几乎沿直线向前移动，始终紧贴身体和水面（图 5.6b ）。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Marionette Recovery
 

The recovery starts from where the stroke and rotation have finished—you are on your side, with your hand just below the surface by your thigh (or, in some drills, resting on your thigh). Imagine that you are a marionette. Your puppeteer has a single string attached—to the elbow on your recovering arm. Your puppeteer lifts your arm out of the water by pulling up on that string. Your elbow rises while your forearm and hand hang down, relaxed from the elbow, with the fingertips near the water’s surface (perhaps even dragging through the surface) and close to the body (figure 5.6a). As the elbow travels toward the front end of your vessel, the hand follows a nearly straight line forward, never straying far from the body or the water’s surface (figure 5.6b).

 
 
重点➤中立肩部
 

常见的恢复错误是允许或强迫肘部移动到身体前后（肚脐侧和臀部侧）平面的后方。这会导致上臂骨头与肩关节窝的后部和上部发生摩擦——这是一种毫无益处的骨骼摩擦。经过成千上万次的重复动作，这种动作几乎肯定会造成损伤。但在木偶式恢复中，应使肩部大致保持在前后运动范围的中心位置。这样可以使肘部保持在身体平面的前方，并使肩部在整个恢复过程中保持高位和放松（图 5.6a和5.6b ）。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Neutral Shoulder
 

A common recovery mistake is to allow, or force, the elbow to move behind the plane that divides the body between the front (navel) side and back (butt) side. This causes the head of the upper-arm bone to bind against the back and top of the shoulder socket—a no-win bone-on-bone conflict. Over the course of thousands (or millions) of repetitions, this motion will almost certainly cause an injury. But in the marionette recovery, you want to keep the shoulder roughly in the center of its front-to-rear range of motion. This keeps the elbow in front of the body plane and allows the shoulder to stay high and relaxed throughout the recovery (figures 5.6a and b).

 
 
焦点➤激光束旋转触发器
 

我之前讲过如何将身体从一个侧滑姿势旋转到另一个侧滑姿势，但很少谈到何时旋转。旋转时机的秘诀在于划水动作的恢复阶段。想象一道激光束横穿你的泳道，位于你头部前方，距离水面几英寸。当你的“操纵者”向前移动你的肘部、前臂和手时，身体的其他姿势不应改变（也就是说，保持侧身姿势，另一只手臂完全伸直）。当恢复的手越过激光束时，这就是开始旋转身体的触发点（在木偶划水动作的侧视图中，恢复的手正好越过这道假想的激光束）。随着腿部带动核心旋转，恢复的手继续向前移动，朝着入水点移动。运用这种心理暗示，你就能划出近乎完美的前象限划水。

 

 

图 5.6木偶式抓取动作，指尖划过表面。(a)正面视图。注意侧滑姿势和位于身体平面前方的高肘。(b)侧面视图。抓取的手正穿过头部顶部的激光束旋转触发点。

 
 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Laser-Beam Rotation Trigger
 

I have talked about rotating the body from one side-glide position to the other, but not much about when to rotate. The secret to timing your rotation is in the recovery. Imagine a laser beam stretching across your lane at the front edge of your head, a few inches above the water’s surface. As your puppeteer moves your elbow, forearm, and hand forward, nothing else about your body position should change (i.e., you stay on your side and you keep the other arm fully extended). When the recovering hand crosses the laser beam, this is the trigger to begin rotating your body (in the side view of the marionette recovery figure, the recovering hand is just crossing this imaginary laser beam). As your legs drive your core rotation, the recovering hand continues moving forward toward the entry point. Using this mental image will result in a nearly perfect front-quadrant stroke.

 

 

Figure 5.6 Marionette recovery with fingertips dragging through the surface. (a) Head-on view. Note the side-glide position and the high elbow in front of the body plane. (b) Side view. The recovering hand is passing through the laser-beam rotation-trigger point at the top of the head.

 
 
重点➤滑动板入口
 

你的双腿并非唯一驱动核心身体旋转的力量。它们的作用是启动旋转，而另一种机制则帮助完成旋转。在划水回旋过程中，将手臂和肩膀抬出水面，会以即将再次下落的动能形式储存能量（势能）。当你的手穿过想象中的激光束，并开始用双腿进行下一次核心身体旋转时，你通过让手臂和肩膀下落来释放储存的能量。你引导着它们的下落——就像手沿着滑板快速滑行，以向下的角度刺破水面，指向你的伸展点。这种下落和伸展的动能会添加到你核心身体旋转的能量中，并通过你紧绷的绳索和桨叶连接传递到划水的手臂。你用身体这一侧的肌肉积极地进入和伸展，进一步增强了旋转的力量和爆发力。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Sliding-Board Entry
 

Your legs are not alone in driving your core body rotation. Their job is to initiate the rotation, and another mechanism helps complete the rotation. Lifting your arm and shoulder out of the water during the recovery stores energy (potential energy) in the form of a lifted mass that is poised to fall again (kinetic energy). As your hand passes through the imaginary laser beam and you begin the next core body rotation with your legs, you release that stored energy by allowing your arm and shoulder to fall toward the water. You guide its descent—as if the hand were zipping down a sliding board so that it pierces the surface of the water at a downward angle toward your extension point. The kinetic energy of this falling and extending mass adds to the energy of your core body rotation and is thus transmitted to the stroking arm through your tight line and paddle linkage. The muscles that you use along that side of your body to aggressively enter and extend further add to the power and snappiness of your rotation.

 

转弯

Turning

 

无论是游泳还是划水，到达池壁后，你需要做两件事之一：（1）转身或（2）上岸。假设你选择前者，那么需要考虑以下几点。任何转身的目标都是在最短的时间内快速改变方向，同时保持速度并节省体力。

Whether swimming or drilling, once you get to the wall, you need to do one of two things: (1) turn or (2) get out. Assuming that you opt for the former, there are a few considerations. What you want with any turn is a rapid change of direction in a minimum amount of time, without losing speed, and while conserving energy.

你可以选择做翻转转身——就是自由泳快速选手常用的那种类似翻筋斗的动作——或者你可以做开放式转身，这种转身通常用于蛙泳和蝶泳。开放式转身允许你在触壁时换气，而翻转转身则不行。如果只是游一两圈，这无关紧要。但如果游200码或更长的距离，这种差别就会累积起来。翻转转身比开放式转身更复杂，学习时间也更长。然而，几乎所有游泳爱好者都希望掌握高质量的翻转转身技巧。以下将介绍这两种快速、低成本的转身方法，以及每种转身后应该采取的措施。

You can choose to do a flip turn—that somersault-looking thing that fast swimmers do when they swim freestyle—or you can do an open turn, the turn commonly used for breaststroke and butterfly. The open turn allows you to take a breath at the wall but the flip turn does not. For just a lap or two, this is not a big deal. But for distances of 200 yards or more, this difference adds up. Flip turns are more complex and take much longer to learn than open turns. Virtually everyone who swims laps, however, wants a high-quality flip turn as part of their swimming arsenal. Following are descriptions of lightning-fast, low-cost turns of both varieties and of what should happen following either.

开放转弯

Open Turns

 

要完成一个开放式转身，在接近泳池末端时，用力划水最后一次，进入平衡的侧滑姿势，一只手臂向前伸展，另一只手臂刚好贴近水面，肚脐朝向池壁。（在整个转身和蹬壁过程中，肚脐都应该朝向池壁。）完成最后一次划水后继续踢腿，直到伸出的手触到池壁。随着身体的惯性向池壁移动，让贴池壁的手臂自然弯曲（图 5.7a ）。避免抓住池沿，因为向上拉会破坏转身的惯性并浪费能量。将双腿紧紧地收回到身下，利用身体的惯性将臀部向池壁摆动，同时用手臂将上半身推离池壁（图 5.7b ）。保持贴近水面的手臂不动，不要让它随着臀部一起移动。你的身体将以躯干中部的一个点为轴心旋转。

To execute an open turn, as you near the end of the pool, take your last stroke aggressively into your balanced side-glide position, with one arm extended in front of you, your trailing arm just at the surface of the water, and your navel facing the sidewall. (Throughout the turn and push-off, your navel should face the sidewall.) Continue kicking as you finish this last stroke and until your extended hand touches the wall. Allow the wall arm to bend as your momentum moves your body toward the wall (figure 5.7a). Avoid grabbing the gutter, since pulling yourself up breaks the momentum of the turn and wastes energy. Draw your legs up tightly under you and let the momentum of your body swing your hips toward the wall as you push your upper torso away from the wall with your arm (figure 5.7b). Leave your trailing arm near the surface rather than moving it with your hips. Your body will pivot around a point in your midsection.

当手臂蹬墙时，你的躯干保持笔直，双腿紧贴身体下方，并向墙面摆动。随着身体继续以腰部中心点为轴旋转，手臂会越过头顶。此时，身体的任何部位都不会接触墙面（图 5.7 c）。上半身向下旋转入水的同时，你希望上方的手臂与下方的手臂在水面下相遇，此时你的双脚——只需脚趾和前脚掌，不要完全着地——与肩同宽接触墙面，并跃入完全流线型的滑行姿势（图 5.7 d）。在跃离墙面之前，不要将双脚踩实或进一步下蹲。你的目标是双脚与墙面接触的时间不要超过高尔夫球在地面上弹跳的时间（图 5.7 e）。

As the wall arm pushes off the wall, your torso is straight and your legs are tucked in tight under you as you swing them toward the wall. Your wall arm swings over your head as your body continues to pivot around a point in your midsection. At this instant, no part of your body is touching the wall (figure 5.7c). While your upper torso pivots down into the water, you want the top arm to meet the trailing arm below the surface of the water at the instant your feet—just the toes and balls, you should not be flat footed—contact the wall at shoulder’s width as you are leaping into a fully streamlined glide position (figure 5.7d). Don’t plant your feet or crouch any more deeply before leaping off the wall. Your goal is to have your feet in contact with the wall for no longer than a bouncing golf ball would stay on the ground (figure 5.7e).

 

图 5.7一个好的开放式转身可以让你在快速转身的同时换气。(a)加速最后一次划水，进入侧滑姿势。当你伸出的手触到墙面时，让手臂弯曲，但不要抓住墙沟。(b)双腿紧紧地收拢在身下。惯性使你的臀部向墙面摆动，同时你蹬墙离开，身体以躯干中点为轴旋转。(c)随着旋转继续，手臂笔直地挥过头顶。身体的任何部位都不要触碰墙面。(d)当你的双脚触墙并开始跳离时，上方的手臂与下方的手臂在水面下相遇。(e)离开墙面时，迅速进入标枪姿势。

Figure 5.7 A good open turn allows you to take a breath while still turning lightning fast. (a) Accelerate your last stroke into the side-glide position. As your extended hand touches the wall, allow the arm to bend without grabbing the gutter. (b) Draw your legs up tightly under you. Momentum swings your hips toward the wall as you push away from it, while your body pivots around a point at your midsection. (c) Swing your arm straight over your head as your pivot continues. No part of your body is touching the wall. (d) Your top arm meets the trailing arm below the surface as your feet make contact with the wall and you begin leaping away. (e) Snap into javelin position as you leave the wall on your side.

 

翻转转弯

Flip Turns

 

只有当你掌握了开放式转身之后，才能尝试翻转转身。接近池壁时，加速最后两下划水，使每次划水都以大腿为终点（图 5.8 a）。接近池壁时速度越快，转身就越容易。快速有力地屈体，就像做仰卧起坐一样（图 5.8 b和c）。不要让你的手或肘部向两侧移动。在整个转身过程中，保持它们靠近你的行进路线。当臀部和腿部继续滑向水面的池壁时，你的上半身应该已经完成​​了四分之三的转身（图 5.8 c）。快速弯曲膝盖抬起脚后跟（图 5.8 d和e）。这是将双腿抬出水面所需的唯一大幅度肌肉动作——剩下的就靠惯性了（图 5.8 e和f）。试图将双腿甩出水面只会让上半身更深地沉入水中。利用惯性将双腿摆动过水面，你的上半身就能保持与水面平行。

Once you have mastered the open turn, and only then, you might want to try the flip turn. Approach the wall by accelerating your last two strokes, finishing each at your thighs (figure 5.8a). More speed going into the wall makes for an easier turn. Execute a strong, quick pike, as if doing a toe-touch sit-up (figures 5.8b and c). Don’t let your hands or elbows move out to the sides. Keep them in close to your line of travel throughout the turn. Your upper body should be three-quarters of the way through the turn as the hips and legs continue gliding toward the wall at the surface (figure 5.8c). Pick up your heels by quickly bending at the knees (figures 5.8d and e). This is the only large muscular movement needed to get your legs over the top of the water—momentum does the rest (figures 5.8e and f). Trying to throw your legs over the surface just pushes the upper body deep into the water. By allowing momentum to swing your legs over, your upper body will remain parallel with the surface of the water.

触壁时，双脚应与肩同宽或更宽，膝盖弯曲近90度。蹬壁动作开始时，双脚应触壁（图5.8 f和g ）。蹬壁前不要双脚着地，更不要蹲得过深。蹬壁时双脚应触壁，是因为你要向后跳跃，而不是在跳跃之前。记住“翻转-蹬壁”的要领，而不是“翻转-着地-蹬壁”。

As you make contact with the wall, your feet should be at shoulder width or wider and your knees should be bent almost to 90 degrees. Your feet should hit the wall as your push-off begins (figures 5.8f and g). Do not plant your feet or, worse, crouch deeper before your push-off. Your feet should hit the wall because you are leaping away from it, not before you leap. Think flip-push instead of flip-plant-push.

 

图 5.8快速、紧凑的转身被许多人认为是真正游泳者的必备技能。(a)在触壁前加速最后两下划水，每次划水都以大腿为结束点。你的鼻子应垂直向下。(b)开始有力、快速的屈体动作，保持双手和肘部靠近行进路线。(b, c)转身过程中，你的上半身大部分都在移动，而你的臀部和腿部则在水面滑向池壁。(d, e)快速弯曲膝盖，抬起脚后跟，就像要踢自己的屁股一样。(e, f)惯性使你的双腿在水面上滑行，你的上半身几乎与水面平行。(g)双脚触壁，膝盖弯曲，开始蹬壁。双脚应与肩同宽或更宽。(h)离开池壁时，迅速摆出标枪姿势，仰卧在水面上。

Figure 5.8 A quick, compact flip turn is considered by many to be the defining skill of a real swimmer. (a) Accelerate the last two strokes before the wall, finishing each at your thighs. Your nose is pointed straight down. (b) Begin a strong, quick pike, keeping your hands and elbows in close to your line of travel. (b, c) Your upper body moves most of the way through the turn while your hips and legs glide toward the wall at the water’s surface. (d, e) Pick up your heels by quickly bending at the knees, as if trying to kick yourself in the butt. (e, f) Momentum carries your legs over the surface of the water and your upper body remains nearly parallel with it. (g) Feet touch the wall with knees bent as your push-off begins. Your feet should be shoulder width apart or wider. (h) Snap into javelin position as you leave the wall on your back.

 
 

从图示中可以看出，你应该以俯卧姿势进入转身，并以仰卧姿势离开（图 5.8 h）。在蹬壁前扭转成侧卧或扭转回俯卧都会减慢转身速度。从水面下的墙壁上仰卧跳下，然后稍微扭转身体，使身体在水中呈螺旋状旋转，最终侧卧，滑离墙壁。

Note from the diagrams that you should enter the turn on your belly and leave on your back (figure 5.8h). Twisting onto your side or twisting back to your belly before pushing off slows the turn. Leap off the wall on your back under the water’s surface, then twist your body slightly so that you corkscrew through the water and end up on your side, gliding away from the wall.

回合结束后

After the Turn

 

无论你采用哪种转向方式，当你离开池壁时，你的水下滑行速度都会比你在水面上游泳的速度更快。由于水下阻力比水面阻力小，每个长度的前5到9码（4.6到8.2米）（短池的20%到30%）就成了利用比游泳速度更快的滑行速度而几乎不消耗能量的机会——这就是所谓的“自由速度”。

Regardless of which turn you use, when you leave the wall, you will be traveling underwater faster than you can swim on the surface. Because there is less resistance below the surface than at the surface, this first 5 to 9 yards (4.6 to 8.2 meters) of each length (20 to 30 percent of a short-course swimming pool) becomes an opportunity to capitalize on faster-than-swimming glide speed with little or no energy expense—free speed.

蹬壁时，迅速进入完全流线型姿势——双手紧贴，上手叠放，上方拇指勾住另一只手的边缘，一只手腕紧贴另一只手腕，双耳紧紧夹在双臂之间，双腿并拢，脚尖绷直。想象一下标枪的姿势。当你的脚趾离开池壁时，你应该已经处于标枪姿势（只是双腿会在脚趾离开池壁后立即并拢）。哪怕多花零点几秒，也会浪费你比游泳更快的滑行速度的很大一部分。蹬壁的深度应该在水面以下 30 到 45 厘米（12 到 18 英寸）处，以避免滑行时受到跟随你来到池壁的波浪和水面湍流的影响。

During your push-off, snap into a fully streamlined position—tight-line posture, hand on top of hand, top thumb locked around the edge of the other hand, one wrist directly on top of the other wrist, ears squeezed firmly between your upper arms, legs together, and toes pointed. Think javelin. As your toes leave the wall, you should already be in javelin position (except that your legs will come together just after the toes leave the wall). An extra fraction of a second to get there will squander a large percentage of your faster-than-swimming glide speed. The push-off should happen 12 to 18 inches (about 30 to 45 cm) below the surface in order to avoid gliding through the waves and surface turbulence that have followed you to the wall.

用力过猛会导致投掷姿势偏离流线，背部过度后仰。一开始要缓慢起跳，专注于在双脚离开墙面时保持身体紧绷、姿势流畅。随着你逐渐掌握快速进入标枪姿势的能力，再逐步加大起跳力度，以提高速度和投掷距离。

Pushing off too hard can result in overshooting a streamlined javelin position, arching the back at full extension instead. Start with slow push-offs and focus on hitting a tight-line posture and a streamlined position as your feet leave the wall. As you hone your ability to snap into the javelin position, gradually increase your push-off oomph for more speed and distance.

在滑行过程中，浮力会将你带到水面。试图控制自己上浮会迅速降低你的速度。踢水或爬水都会消耗肌肉能量。而利用浮力将你带到水面则是免费的。根据个人的浮力，你的蹬水动作可能需要水平或略微向下倾斜。调整肺内空气量会影响你的上升速度（空气越少，上升速度越慢）。你的目标是在第一只划水臂刚好露出水面、开始恢复划水动作时到达水面。目标是在滑行速度从快于游泳的速度减慢到游泳速度时，立即开始第一次划水。过早开始第一次划水会导致速度过早降低。滑行时间过长，则需要通过第一次划水来加速，才能恢复到游泳速度。

During your glide, buoyancy should bring you to the surface. Trying to steer yourself to the surface will cause you to lose momentum quickly. Kicking or climbing to the surface costs muscle energy. Allowing buoyancy to lift you to the surface is free. Depending on personal buoyancy, your push-off may need to be either horizontal or angled slightly downward. Adjusting the amount of air in your lungs will alter your ascent rate (less air = slower rise toward the surface). You want to reach the surface just as the first stroking arm breaks the surface as recovery begins. The goal is to begin your first stroke just as your faster-than-swimming glide slows to swimming speed. Taking your first stroke too soon will slow you prematurely. Glide too long and your first strokes will have to accelerate you back to swimming speed.

在划水前，先快速有力地踢腿。踢腿开始的时间取决于你的踢腿质量。如果你的踢腿快速有力，能显著提升你的滑行距离，甚至超过游泳速度，那么在双脚离开池壁后立即开始踢腿可能很有帮助（但要注意，即使是优秀的踢腿也会消耗大量能量）。如果你的踢腿力量不足，反而会减慢你的速度。这时，保持脚尖绷直滑行，直到即将划水前，或许是最佳选择。两种方法都可以尝试一下。

Begin a compact, rapid kick before you take your first stroke. How early in your streamlined glide you begin that kick depends on the quality of your kick. If you have a fast, compact kick that adds substantially to the distance you travel at faster-than-swimming speed, then it may be useful to start it as soon as your feet leave the wall (realizing that there is a tradeoff here, because even an excellent kick costs a lot of energy). If your kick is weak, it may actually slow you down. Simply gliding with your toes pointed until just before your first stroke may be your best choice. Experiment with both options.

随着你在水下停留时间的延长，你的身体会发出呼吸的渴望，促使你缩短滑行速度（比游泳速度快）。你可能会不自觉地抬起头，或者扭曲身体，改变流线型姿势，以便吸入第一口空气。在游泳时，每隔一次划水呼吸（而不是每三次或四次划水呼吸一次），可以让你在转身时屏住呼吸足够长的时间，从而充分利用滑行速度（比游泳速度快）。持续练习长距离滑行，可以帮助你抑制过早浮出水面的冲动，同时还能让你在开始游泳时获得充足的第一口空气。

As you learn to stay under the water longer, your body will cry out for air, urging you to cut short your faster-than-swimming glide. You may tend to lift your head or otherwise contort yourself out of streamline to get that first breath of air. Breathing every other stroke (instead of every third or fourth stroke) while swimming will allow you to hold your breath on turns long enough to capitalize on your faster-than-swimming glide. Practicing long glides consistently will help you resist the urge to surface early yet still allow you to get an adequate first breath as you begin to swim.

第三部分
 
游泳训练
 

游泳训练并非只是跳进水里拼命搅动水流直到泳池关闭（尽管有些人确实这么认为）。在我们看来，训练以及由此带来的体能提升，是学习和练习高效游泳技巧的副产品（因此我交替使用“训练”和“练习”这两个词）。精心设计的训练计划包含旨在教授或提升各种技能，并以不同强度进行练习的活动。本部分将帮助您规划训练。第六章解释了各种运动强度，以及一些测量和控制运动强度的方法。它还解释了训练区间及其与后续六个训练级别的关系。此外，本章还讨论了有效的热身和放松运动。第七章至第十二章包含六个训练级别，每个级别都包含十个技能提升和体能训练项目。

A swimming workout is not just about diving in and churning the water as hard as possible until they close the pool (though some people approach it that way). In our paradigm, a workout, and the conditioning that results from it, is a by-product of learning and practicing the skills of highly effective swimming (hence I use the words workout and practice interchangeably). A well-planned workout involves activities intended to teach or refine a variety of skills and to practice those skills at a variety of planned intensities. This part will help you plan your workouts. Chapter 6 explains various exercise intensities as well as some ways to measure and control your exertion level. It also explains workout training zones and how they relate to the six levels of workouts that follow. In addition, the chapter discusses effective warm-ups and cool-downs. Chapters 7 through 12 include the six workout levels, each of which contains 10 skill-building and conditioning workouts.

训练形式

Workout Format

 

为了将每项训练内容都浓缩到一张易于复印的纸上，我们对大部分训练说明都使用了简写符号。每个训练级别章节都包含如何解读这些简写符号的详细说明。随着级别的提升，我们会添加新的、有时也更复杂的符号。

In order to fit each workout onto a single, easy-to-photocopy page, we use shorthand notation for most of the workout instructions. Each workout-level chapter includes detailed instructions on how to read the workout notation. As you move from level to level, new and sometimes more complex notation is added.

由于美国大多数训练泳池都是短池（25码或25米长），所有训练计划都是针对短池设计的，也可以用于20码泳池。稍作调整，这些计划也适用于50米泳池。

Because most workout pools in the United States are short-course pools (25 yards or 25 meters long), all workouts are written for short-course pools and can be used in 20-yard pools. With some commonsense adaptations, they can also be used in 50-meter pools.

开始训练前，请通读整个训练计划及其注释，确保您理解所有要求——您肯定不想在水里泡到胸口时才发现某个动作的说明或训练符号。每次训练都以热身开始，并立即进行下一个动作。完成一行训练后，请间隔不超过15到20秒再开始下一行。跳过任何一部分练习都可能极大地影响整个训练的效果。

Before starting a workout, read through the entire workout, as well as the notes, in order to make sure you understand what the instructions call for—you don’t want to be chest-deep in the water and need to look up a drill description or a workout notation in the book. Begin each workout with the warm-up and move immediately from one activity to the next. Take no more than 15 to 20 seconds after completing one line of the workout to begin the next line. Skipping any portion of the practice can greatly alter the training effect of the entire workout.

第223页有一个图例，列出了书中每项练习的缩写和全称，以及练习说明所在的页码。此外，从第220页开始，每个重点内容都有相应的总结。您可以将这些资料复印后放入密封袋中，放在泳池边方便查阅。

On page 223, you will find a legend showing the abbreviation and full name of each drill used in the book, as well as the page where the drill description appears. You’ll also find each of the focus points summarized beginning on page 220. You may want to put photocopies of these in water-tight sandwich bags to keep at the poolside for easy reference.

选择培训级别

Choosing a Training Level

 

由于一级训练主要包括姿势、平衡和游泳技巧练习，这些练习非常适合集中练习各项技能、精进技术，或者作为高强度训练前的热身。无论您的游泳基础如何，我都建议您从一级开始，并按顺序完成所有练习。熟练的游泳者可能会发现，他们可以在一次泳池训练中轻松完成不止一项练习。而水平较低的游泳者可能每次泳池训练只能完成一项练习，甚至可能需要重复练习几次才能进行下一项。

Because level 1workouts consist primarily of posture, balance, and swimming-skill drills, these practices are excellent for isolating skills and refining technique, or for a warm-up before intense workouts. Regardless of your swimming background, I encourage you to start with level 1 and to work through all the practices in the order presented. Skilled swimmers may find that they can breeze through more than one of these practices in a single pool session. Less-skilled swimmers might do just one practice per pool session and, in fact, may need to repeat a practice a couple of times before moving to the next one.

在任何锻炼计划中，人们都会对进入下一个阶段感到兴奋、期待和渴望。然而，为了取得长期的成功，必须为每一个阶段的提升做好充分的准备。在1到4级中，务必在进入下一级别之前完成所有练习。我建议您至少完整地完成当前级别的两遍练习后再进入下一级别。您应该能够在不偏离目标心率范围的情况下完成每个级别的所有练习，即使偏离的时间很短。在进入下一级别之前，您还应该对当前级别的技能练习和重点内容感到自信。如果没有，您可能需要复习并练习那些您不自信的部分。当您无法掌握某个技能时，通常是因为您还没有掌握之前的技能。如果您发现自己在进阶过程中难以完成训练，那么请回溯，回到该级别的开头，甚至可以回到更早的级别。

In any exercise regimen, there is a certain excitement, anticipation, and eagerness over moving to the next level. For long-term success, however, it is necessary to be fully prepared for each step up. In each of the levels 1 through 4, be sure to complete every practice before moving up to the next level. I encourage you to make at least two full passes through the level before moving on to the next one. You should be able to complete all the practices in a level without straying out of the target heart-rate range any longer than brief periods. You should also feel confident with the skill drills and focus points presented in your current level before moving up to the next level. If not, you may want to review and practice the areas you are not confident with. When a skill eludes you, often the problem is that you have not mastered an earlier skill. If you find that you are struggling to complete workouts as you progress through a level, then backtrack, either returning to the beginning of the level or even, perhaps, to an earlier level.

如果你是一位游泳水平不错的选手，并且渴望投入高强度训练，我强烈建议你按照顺序完成1到4级的所有训练。如果你决定跳过某些级别，也务必至少通读一遍，以便熟悉每个部分中出现的术语和训练理念。

If you are an accomplished swimmer who is chomping at the bit to get to the hard work, I strongly suggest that you still progress through the workouts in levels 1 through 4 in the order in which they are presented. If you decide to skip over any levels, however, be sure to at least read through them in order to familiarize yourself with the terminology and training concepts presented in each section.

每个训练级别都会反复练习最基本的技能。随着练习级别的提升，你会发现技能难度逐渐增加，呈现出一种逻辑规律。这种反复循环练习各个技能级别是长期提升泳姿水平的基石。

Every workout level will repeatedly revisit the most fundamental skills. As the practices progress through a level, you will notice a logical pattern of increasingly difficult skills. This repeated cycling through all the skill levels is a cornerstone of long-term stroke development.

进度图表

Charting Progress

 

在开始你的训练计划之前，你已经完成了T-20游泳测试（第21页），并记录了你的成绩。每次你完成一个级别的训练组后，都要重复进行T-20游泳测试，并将你的新成绩与之前的成绩进行比较。

Before you began your exercise program, you completed the T-20 swim (page 21) and kept records of your performance. Each time you cycle through a set of practices in a level, repeat the T-20 swim and compare your new results with previous ones.

每完成一个级别，你的游泳距离、速度、IHR（或游泳后半程的平均心率）、平均划水次数、RPE（主观疲劳程度）或这些指标的组合都应该有所提高。最终，你会更有信心挑战T-30游泳。完成4级后，你应该可以进行T-30游泳，而不是T-20游泳了。

As you complete each level, you should see improvement in distance, speed, IHR (or average heart rate for the last half of the swim), average stroke count, RPE, or a combination of these. Eventually you will feel confident about moving up to T-30 swims. By the time you have completed level 4, you should be doing T-30s instead of T-20 swims.

能力 vs. 体能

Ability vs. Conditioning

 

游泳和其他任何运动一样，能力是技术和体能的结合。一般来说，我们可以将能力定义为三个可衡量因素的交集：你游得有多快？你能游多久？你在游泳时消耗多少能量？

In swimming, as with any sport, ability is a combination of technique and conditioning. In general terms, we can define ability as the intersection of three measureable factors: How fast do you swim? For how long can you swim? How much energy do you use while you swim?

人们常常将体能与能力混淆，或者忽视技术的重要性，以至于在许多运动员眼中，能力和体能几乎成了同义词。对于跑步这类我们天生擅长的运动，或者像自行车这类容易控制的运动，体能和能力之间的界限很容易模糊。在这些运动中，技术在整体能力中所占的比重远小于体能。然而，在高尔夫、网球或武术等运动中，技术在能力中所占的比重则远大于体能。

It is common to confuse conditioning with ability or to discount the importance of technique, so ability and conditioning become synonymous in many athletes’ eyes. For sports that use motions we are naturally suited for, such as running, or for motions that are easily constrained or controlled, such as those in cycling, it is easy to blur the distinction between conditioning and ability. Technique in these sports is a much smaller component of overall ability than is conditioning. In sports such as golf, tennis, or the martial arts, however, technique is a much larger component of ability than conditioning.

游泳属于后一类。游泳能力70%到90%取决于技术，只有10%到30%取决于体能。本书中的练习不仅能为你提供有效的体能训练，更着重提升你的技术能力。在1级和2级中，每次练习60%到90%是技巧训练，旨在突出自由泳的关键要素。剩余的10%到40%是短距离游泳（一到两个泳道长度），重点练习某个特定的概念或技巧。随着级别的提升，练习中游泳技巧的占比会越来越高。3级和4级包含40%到70%的技巧训练，而5级和6级则包含20%到50%的技巧训练。

Swimming falls into this latter category. Ability in swimming is 70 to 90 percent technique and only 10 to 30 percent conditioning. In addition to providing you a great conditioning workout, the practices in this book strongly emphasize improving your technical ability. In levels 1 and 2, 60 to 90 percent of each practice is skill drills that isolate specific, critical aspects of freestyle swimming. The remaining 10 to 40 percent are short swims (one or two lengths) with a specific concept or skill to focus on. As you move through the levels, there will be more emphasis on swimming. Levels 3 and 4 include 40 to 70 percent drills, and levels 5 and 6 include 20 to 50 percent drills.

继续技术教育

Continuing Technique Education

 

随着级别的提升，您将不断学习、积累和完善您的技术。随着经验、信心和能力的增长，新的技能、练习、概念和重点也会逐步引入。但即便您掌握了新的内容，也不要认为可以忽略已经学习过的基础练习。这些练习会在后续章节的各个级别练习中出现。事实上，在您的整个游泳生涯中，本书中的练习将持续帮助您拓展和提升技能。

As you move through the levels, you will continue to learn, build, and refine your technique. New skills, drills, concepts, and focus points are introduced along the way as your experience, confidence, and competence grow. But even as you encounter and master new material, don’t assume that you can dispense with the foundational drills you’ve already learned. These drills show up in practices at every level in the following chapters. In fact, throughout your swimming career, the drills in this book will continue to be beneficial for expanding and refining your skill base.

嬉戏

Cavorting

 

2级及以上级别的一大特色是“嬉戏玩耍”，即将趣味活动融入到锻炼中。你有没有注意到，孩子们在游泳池里的行为与成年人截然不同？他们跳跃、漂浮、翻跟头、跳水、坐在池底，还会自创各种滑稽的游戏。换句话说，他们在玩耍。他们不断地了解周围的环境，并不断拓展自己在环境中的舒适区。正是由于这种持续不断的无意识的身体学习，孩子们在机会出现时，能够更自觉地掌握和运用新技能。而成年人每次去游泳池，往往都会重复同样的模式——同样的圈数、同样的泳姿、同样的速度、同样的装备、同样的泳道、同样的想法，一切都一成不变。成年人找到自己的舒适区，并安于现状。如果一个人从不尝试任何新鲜事物，就很难有所收获。

A special feature of levels 2 and up is cavorting, where playful activities are incorporated into the workouts. Ever notice that kids in a swimming pool behave differently than adults do? They jump, they bob, they do flips, they do cannonballs, they sit on the bottom, and they make up silly games. In other words, they play. They are always learning about their environment and are always expanding their comfort zone within that environment. Because of this constant unintentional physical learning, kids are more capable of intentionally grasping and executing new skills when the opportunity presents itself. Adults tend to repeat patterns of behavior during every visit to the pool—same number of laps, same strokes, same pace, same equipment, same lane, same thoughts, same, same, same. Adults find a comfort zone and stay well within it. Very little learning takes place when one never does anything new or different.

我鼓励你每天在水里尝试一些不同的活动——也许是你从未做过的，也许是一些傻乎乎的。尽情玩耍！尽情嬉戏！你会变得更加自在放松，更加适应水。你会更有信心学习和运用新技能，并且进步更快。长此以往，你会成为一名更优秀的游泳者，也会获得更多乐趣。

I challenge you to do something different in the water every day—perhaps something that you’ve never done before, perhaps something silly. Play! Cavort! You will become more comfortable and relaxed in the water. You will have more confidence in your ability to learn and execute new skills. You will learn these skills more rapidly. In the long run, you will be a better swimmer and you’ll have more fun.

为此，我在训练中加入了一些嬉戏动作。有些动作可能看起来与游泳完全无关；有些动作可能与高效游泳背道而驰；还有一些动作可能只是你一直在练习的某个技巧或技能的有趣变式。不要被我的建议或频率所限制。如果我建议的嬉戏动作不适合你的情况，那就自己想一些别的。嬉戏也是很好的热身或放松方式。如果你过于拘谨和成熟，实在提不起劲儿来玩耍或嬉戏，那就把它当作练习即兴水上技能。你完全可以假装自己觉得没意思。

Toward this end, I have included a number of cavorts in the workouts. Some may seem entirely unrelated to swimming; some may seem antithetical to effective swimming; others may simply be an interesting variation on a drill or skill that you have been working on. Don’t feel limited by what I suggest or how often I suggest it. If the cavort I suggest is not workable in your situation, make up something different. Cavorting is also a great way to warm up or cool down. If you are so stodgy and grown up that you simply can’t bring yourself to play or cavort, then think of it as practicing improvised aquatic skills instead. You can always pretend that you aren’t having any fun doing it.

第六章
 
训练强度
 

本书中的大部分体能训练方法都涉及定期监测运动强度并调整训练强度，以使整体运动强度保持在特定范围内。运动时有很多方法可以判断训练强度，但并非所有方法都适用于游泳。本章介绍两种可以单独或结合使用来评估和控制运动强度的方法：主观疲劳程度评级和心率测量。我还解释了如何将这些数据应用到本书的训练计划中，以获得最佳效果。最后，我将解释如何为运动做好准备以及如何进行运动后的放松。

Much of the conditioning methodology in this book involves regularly monitoring your exercise intensity and adjusting your effort level in order to keep your overall exercise intensities within specified ranges. There are a number of ways to judge training intensity while exercising, but not all are easily applicable to swimming. This chapter presents two methods that you can use separately or in tandem in order to gauge and control your exercise intensity: ratings of perceived exertion and measured heart rate. I also explain how to apply those numbers to the workouts in this book for maximum benefit. Finally, I explain how to prepare for your exertions and how to cool down afterward.

感知用力程度

Perceived Exertion

 

由冈纳·博格博士开发并更新的感知运动强度（RPE）量表，可以帮助您用数字来描述运动过程中的感受。通过监测运动强度，您可以将运动强度调整到量表上的指定级别。通过练习监测身体感受，您将更容易掌握何时调整运动强度。例如，一位计划进行中等强度运动的游泳运动员，其目标强度应为博格量表上的“略微吃力”（12 至 14）。如果在游泳过程中，她感到肌肉疲劳和呼吸都很轻松（博格量表 9），那么她应该游得更快。但如果她感到非常吃力（博格量表 19），则应该放慢速度，以保持在中等强度范围内。

Developed and updated by Dr. Gunnar Borg, the rating of perceived exertion (RPE) scale allows you to assign numbers to how you feel during exercise. By monitoring how hard you are working, you can adjust the intensity of the activity to a prescribed level on the scale. Through the practice of monitoring how your body feels, it will become easier to know when to adjust your intensity. For example, a swimmer who intends to exercise at a moderate intensity would aim for a Borg scale level of somewhat hard (12 to 14). If partway into the swim her muscle fatigue and breathing are very light (9 on the Borg scale), then she should swim faster. But if she finds that her exertion is extremely hard (19 on the Borg scale), she should slow down in order to move into the moderate-intensity range.

在以下章节描述的练习中，您会经常看到RPE这个缩写。每项练习都会包含一个目标RPE范围。在每次练习过程中，您会被多次要求评估自己的运动强度。您应该在运动过程中使用博格RPE量表来评估您的运动强度，而不是在运动结束后再进行评估。

You will often see the acronym RPE in the practices described in the following chapters. Each practice will include a target RPE range for the workout. During each practice, you will be asked several times to rate your exertion level. You should use the Borg RPE scale to assess your exertion level while you are still exercising rather than after you stop.

博格RPE量表使用说明
 

在运动过程中，我们希望您评估自己的运动强度感知，即您感觉运动的强度和费力程度。运动强度感知主要取决于肌肉的紧张和疲劳程度，以及您是否感到呼吸困难或胸闷。

请看这个评分标准；我们希望您使用 6 到 20 的评分标准，其中 6 表示“完全没有用力”，20 表示“最大程度的用力”。

6. 完全不用费力

7

8 非常轻

9 非常轻

10

11 灯

12

13 有点难

14

15 硬（重）

16

17 非常难

18

19 极其困难

20 最大努力

 

9 代表“非常轻度”的运动。对于一个正常、健康的人来说，这相当于以自己的节奏慢慢走几分钟。

13 分代表“有点难”的运动，但感觉还可以继续。

17. “非常”困难是指非常费力。健康的人或许还能继续，但必须竭尽全力。感觉非常沉重，人也会非常疲惫。

该量表上的19级代表着极其剧烈的运动。对大多数人来说，这是他们经历过的最剧烈的运动。

尽量诚实地评估你的运动强度，不要考虑实际的体力消耗。不要低估，也不要高估。重要的是你自身的运动强度感受，而不是与他人的感受进行比较。别人的看法也无关紧要。看看量表和上面的描述，然后给出一个数值。

经许可转载自 G. Borg，1998 年出版的《博格感知劳累和疼痛量表》（伊利诺伊州香槟市：Human Kinetics 出版社），第 47 页。© Gunnar Borg，1970、1985、1994、1998 年

 
Borg’s RPE Scale Instructions
 

While exercising, we want you to rate your perception of exertion, i.e. how heavy and strenuous the exercise feels to you. The perception of exertion depends mainly on the strain and fatigue in your muscles and on your feeling of breathlessness or aches in the chest.

Look at this rating scale; we want you to use this scale from 6 to 20, where 6 means “no exertion at all” and 20 means “maximal exertion.”

6 No exertion at all

7

8 Extremely light

9 Very light

10

11 Light

12

13 Somewhat hard

14

15 Hard (heavy)

16

17 Very hard

18

19 Extremely hard

20 Maximal exertion

 

9 corresponds to “very light” exercise. For a normal, healthy person it is like walking slowly at his or her own pace for some minutes.

13 on the scale is “somewhat hard” exercise, but it still feels OK to continue.

17 “very” hard is very strenuous. A healthy person can still go on, but he or she must really push him- or herself. It feels very heavy and the person is very tired.

19 on the scale is an extremely strenuous exercise level. For most people this is the most strenuous exercise they have ever experienced.

Try to appraise your feeling of exertion as honestly as possible, without thinking about what the actual physical load is. Don’t underestimate it, but don’t overestimate it either. It’s your own feeling of effort and exertion that’s important, not how it compares to other people’s. What other people think is not important either. Look at the scale and the expressions and then give a number.

Reprinted, by permission, from G. Borg, 1998, Borg’s perceived exertion and pain scales (Champaign, IL: Human Kinetics), 47. © Gunnar Borg, 1970, 1985, 1994, 1998

 
 

测量心率

Measured Heart Rates

 

心率通常以每分钟心跳次数 (bpm) 表示，如果测量准确，可以精确评估运动强度。您可以手动或使用电子设备监测心率。一般来说，您会在完成一圈运动后立即测量心率。一旦停止运动，心率就会开始下降。有氧运动能力越强，心率下降得越快。您需要在心率显著下降之前测量心率。电子心率监测器 (HRM) 是测量心率的首选方法。它即时、非常准确，而且几乎不需要思考，也不需要任何专业技能。

Heart rates are generally expressed as a number of beats per minute (bpm) and, if accurately taken, can precisely assess exercise intensity. You can monitor your heart rate either manually or electronically. In general, you will take your heart rate immediately upon completion of a lap. As soon as exertion ceases, your heart rate begins to drop. The better your aerobic conditioning, the faster it drops. You want to take your heart rate before it drops significantly. An electronic heart-rate monitor (HRM) is the much-preferred method of taking your heart rate. It is immediate and very accurate, and it requires little conscious thought and no refined skill.

手动（或触诊）心率测量（将手指放在颈部或手腕的动脉上，然后数脉搏）远不如电子心率测量准确，原因有二：首先，由于脉搏跳动快、疲劳且呼吸困难，数脉搏很困难；其次，在寻找和数脉搏的过程中，心率会下降，即使数得准确，也会低于实际的瞬时心率。只有细心和反复练习才能改善前者。我们试图通过缩短计数时间（0.10 分钟，即 6 秒）来尽量减少后者的误差，然后乘以 10。但即使是较短的计数时间，计算出的心率也会比实际心率低 10 到 30 次/分钟。为了弥补这种误差，可以在乘以 10 之前将计数结果加 2。即使这样调整，结果充其量也只是一个运动心率的估计值，而不是一个精确的测量值。

A manual (or palpated) heart rate (taken by placing your fingers on an artery in your neck or wrist and then counting the beats) is much less accurate than an electronic reading for two reasons: Counting is difficult because the beats are rapid, you are tired, and your breathing is labored; and because your heart rate is dropping while you find and count your pulse, even an accurate count will be lower than the actual immediate heart rate. Only care and repetition can help with the former. We try to minimize the latter error by keeping the counting period short—0.10 of a minute, or 6 seconds—then multiplying by 10. But even a short count results in a calculated heart rate that is anywhere from 10 to 30 beats per minute lower than your actual heart rate. To offset this phenomenon, you can add 2 to the count before multiplying by 10. Even with this adjustment, the result is, at best, an estimate of your exercise heart rate rather than an accurate measurement.

如何手动测量心率
 

用两根手指找到你的颈动脉，它位于下颌关节下方——大约在耳垂下方一英寸左右——然后感受脉搏。用你能感觉到脉搏跳动的最小力度按压。有些人更容易在手腕内侧找到脉搏，位置比小指更靠近拇指。持续6秒钟，数出你感觉到的脉搏跳动次数。看着时钟，在时钟上任意一个合适的刻度线之后，第一个脉搏跳动时数到1，然后继续数到第六秒。如果在6秒刻度线处有一个脉搏跳动，也算在内。 （例如，你游完一段距离后，抬头看时秒针指向37秒。你在39秒处找到脉搏。从40秒后感觉到​​的第一下脉搏开始计数。从1开始。一直数到46秒。）假设你数到14下，加上调整值2得到16下。将这个数字乘以10，你就得到了估计的心率160。如果你是第一次用这种方法测量心率，需要一些练习才能熟练掌握。运动后比休息时更容易找到脉搏，因为脉搏更强，更容易感觉到。

How to Take a Manual Heart Rate
 

Use two fingers to locate your carotid artery, which is just below the hinge point of your jaw—an inch or so below your earlobe—and feel your pulse. Use the smallest amount of pressure that allows you to feel the beats. Some people can more easily find their pulse on the inside surface of their wrist, closer to the thumb than the pinkie. For 6 seconds, count the number of beats you feel. As you watch a clock, count one on the first beat after any convenient mark on the clock, then continue counting beats until the sixth second ticks by. If a beat falls on the 6-second mark, include it in your count. (For example, you finish swimming a particular distance, and when you look up, the second hand is on the 37-second mark. You locate your pulse by the 39-second mark. You begin counting on the first beat you feel after the 40-second mark. Start with one. Count all beats up to and including the 46-second mark.) Let’s say you count 14 beats and you add your adjustment of 2 to get 16. Multiply that number by 10, and you have your estimated IHR of 160. If you are new to taking your heart rate in this manner, it will take some trial and error to get good at it. It is easier to find your pulse after physical exertion than when you are at rest, because the beats are stronger and are thus easier to feel.

 

你可以借用一个心率监测器并进行一些测试，从而更准确地手动测量心率。你需要一个伙伴来帮忙。佩戴监测器后，以不同的强度游几段不同的距离。每次游完后，你的伙伴立即读取你监测器上的读数（但暂时不要告诉你结果），同时你手动测量心率。将你的读数与伙伴的读数进行比较。像这样反复试验可以帮助你确定2是否是适合你的正确调整值。你可能会发现调整1或3（或更多）会让你更接近电子读数。最好每隔几个月就重复这个练习，因为随着你体能的提高，你的调整值可能会发生变化。

You can become more accurate at manually taking your heart rates by borrowing a heart-rate monitor and doing some testing. You’ll need a buddy to help you. While wearing the monitor, swim several different distances at various intensities. Immediately upon completing each swim, your buddy reads your monitor (but does not tell you the result just yet) as you take your heart rate manually. Compare your reading with the reading your buddy took. Repeated experimentation like this can help you determine whether 2 is the correct adjustment for you. You may find that an adjustment of 1 or 3 (or more) gets you closer to the electronic readings. It is good to revisit this exercise every few months, because as your conditioning improves, your adjustment may change.

如果您没有心率监测器，或者无法始终将手动测量的心率与电子读数保持一致，则不应手动测量心率来评估运动强度。您可以购买并使用自己的心率监测器，或者使用本章前面介绍的RPE（主观运动强度）方法。对于服用影响心率或脉搏药物的人来说，RPE也是评估运动强度的首选方法。将运动过程中手动测量的心率与根据电子读数计算出的基准值进行比较，很可能会得出不可靠的结果。如果您选择手动测量，则应在运动过程中以及即将进行的计算中使用手动测量的心率。

If you do not have access to a heart-rate monitor or if you are unable to consistently match your manual readings to electronic readings, then you should not take your heart rate manually to gauge exercise intensity. Either buy and use your own monitor or else use the RPE method described earlier in this chapter. RPE is also the preferred method to assess intensity among people who take medications that affect heart rate or pulse. Comparing heart rates taken manually during workouts to benchmarks calculated from electronic readings will likely yield unreliable results. If you choose to go the manual route, you should use manual heart rates both during workouts and for the calculations you’ll be doing soon.

在接下来的章节中，您会经常看到缩写 IHR。IHR 指的是运动结束后立即测量的心率。使用心率监测器时，只需在触壁后尽快查看即可。您看到的第一个数字就是您的 IHR。如果您是手动测量心率，请使用“如何手动测量心率”侧边栏中详细介绍的方法。

You will often see the acronym IHR in the following chapters. IHR is your heart rate taken immediately after completing a period of exertion. When you use an HRM, simply glance at it as soon as possible after touching the wall. The first number you see is your IHR. If you are taking your heart rate manually, use the method detailed in the How to Take a Manual Heart Rate sidebar.

SLTHR：游泳 乳酸阈值心率

SLTHR: Swimming Lactate-Threshold Heart Rate

 

几乎所有运动过程中，都会消耗碳水化合物和脂肪的组合作为能量来源。乳酸（乳酸盐）是运动肌肉中碳水化合物代谢的副产物。如果肌肉或血液中乳酸积累过多，就会引起不适或疼痛，并限制运动表现。运动时，有氧系统会清除肌肉和血液中的乳酸。在休息以及低强度和中等强度运动时，乳酸的产生和清除处于平衡状态。然而，随着运动强度的增加，会达到一个临界点，此时身体产生乳酸的速度超过了清除速度。这会导致乳酸在肌肉和血液中积累，很快就会限制运动表现。这个临界点被称为无氧阈值或乳酸阈值。乳酸阈值训练是指你能长时间持续进行的最高运动强度，也是提高有氧运动能力的有效训练范围。训练计划中详细介绍的大部分训练强度都刚好达到或略高于你的游泳乳酸阈值。训练中要求的其他训练强度也以你的 SLTHR 的百分比表示。

During nearly all exercise, some combination of carbohydrate and fat is used for fuel. Lactate (lactic acid) is a by-product of carbohydrate metabolism in working muscles. If too much lactate accumulates in your muscles or blood, it begins to cause discomfort or pain and to limit performance. During exercise, your aerobic system clears lactic acid from your muscles and blood. At rest and at low and moderate levels of exertion, there is a balance between lactate production and lactate removal. As exercise intensity increases, however, there is a tipping point at which the body produces lactate faster than it can be removed. This causes an accumulation of lactate in the muscles and blood, which soon limits performance. This tipping point is called the anaerobic threshold or lactate threshold. Lactate-threshold work is the highest intensity of exercise that you can continue for an extended time, and it is a very effective work range for improving your aerobic fitness. A good portion of the training detailed in the practices is performed just at and just above your swimming lactate threshold. Other training intensities called for in the practices are also expressed as a percentage of your SLTHR.

在第三章中，您学习了T-20游泳测试。如果您全力以赴，全程不停歇（或仅有短暂的停顿），且在最后两分钟没有加速，那么您在测试结束时测得的心率（IHR）就是您的游泳乳酸阈值心率。事实上，在您的整个游泳生涯中，您全力游完的T-20（或T-30）心率将是您当前游泳乳酸阈值心率的最佳指标。但是，对于那些体能较差、缺乏持续运动经验或缺乏持续游泳经验的人来说，您认为自己尽力游完的程度可能远低于您的实际体能水平。因此，您的T-20游泳心率将低于您的真实游泳乳酸阈值心率。不过没关系，因为您将有很多机会重新测试并获得更准确的结果。随着训练的进行，课程将要求您定期进行T-20游泳测试。每次进行T型游泳训练，目标都是超越之前的成绩。如果你每次都抱着这样的心态进行训练，并且随着时间的推移，你的体能和表现不断提高，那么你的SLTHR（单次心率）就会上升。

In chapter 3, you were exposed to the T-20 swim. If you gave this swim your best effort, without stopping (or with only very short pauses) and without speeding up in the last two minutes, then the IHR you took at the end of this swim is your lactate-threshold heart rate for swimming. In fact, throughout your swimming career, your best-effort T-20 (or T-30) IHR will be your best indicator of your current SLTHR. But for those of you who are in poor condition, are new to sustained exercise, or are new to sustained swimming, your perception of a best effort may be well short of your true physical ability. Your T-swim IHR will thus fall short of your true swimming lactate-threshold heart rate. That’s okay, though, because you’ll have lots of opportunity to retest yourself and to get more accurate results. As you move through the workouts, the program will call for you to do T-swims on a regular basis. Each time you do a T-swim, the goal is to improve upon previous performances. If you approach each T-swim in that manner and if your conditioning and performances improve over time, your SLTHR will increase.

训练强度区间

Training-Intensity Zones

 

以乳酸阈值强度游泳可以带来有益的训练适应，但无论强度高低，训练同样有益。事实上，只要你的心率超过乳酸阈值心率的70%，并持续至少10分钟，你就能确保从训练中获益。低于乳酸阈值心率的70%，任何益处都微乎其微。

Beneficial training adaptations will result from swimming at your lactate threshold, but beneficial adaptations will result from training at both lower and higher intensities as well. In fact, whenever you exercise at a heart rate greater than 70 percent of your SLTHR for at least 10 minutes, you can be sure that you will benefit from your efforts. Below 70 pecent of your SLTHR, any benefits will be negligible.

当心率达到理想心率的70%以上时，不同的训练强度会产生不同的效果。训练强度决定了训练的适应性以及训练过程中的感受。通常认为，训练强度可以分为五个区间，每个区间对应不同的理想心率百分比。本书中的训练计划涵盖了每个训练区间。

Above 70 percent of SLTHR, different training intensities produce different effects. Exercise intensity determines the training adaptation as well as the sensations you can expect during that training. There are five generally accepted training zones that are delineated by the different percentages of SLTHR. The workout levels in this book include work in each training zone.

轻松恢复区或主动恢复区：间歇心率 (IHR) 为标准心率 (SLTHR) 的 70% 至 80%，主观疲劳程度 (RPE) 为 9 至 11。

Easy- or Active-Recovery Zone: IHR 70 to 80 Percent of SLTHR, RPE 9 to 11

 

这是对健身有益的最低强度运动。初学者和长时间未锻炼的人应该从这个强度区间开始。对于需要从高强度训练中休息的人来说，这是一个很好的恢复区间。它也是高强度训练间隙进行恢复性游泳以及训练结束后进行放松运动的理想强度。轻松的运动比完全休息更能帮助你从高强度训练中恢复过来。轻松的有氧训练可以促进血液循环和生长激素的分泌，从而加速修复因高强度训练而受损的组织。在这个强度下，肌肉的主要能量来源是体脂。在这个强度区间内的运动感觉非常轻松，可以长时间保持舒适。

This is the lowest intensity of exercise that has some fitness benefit. Beginners and people who have not exercised for a long time should start in this zone. It is a good recovery zone for people who need a break from hard training. It is also the correct intensity for recovery swims between intense exercise bouts and for cool-downs at the end of practice sessions. Easy work allows you to recover from hard work more rapidly than total rest does. Easy aerobic training stimulates circulation and growth-hormone release, which speeds the healing of tissues that have been damaged by hard training. The main source of fuel used by the muscles at this intensity is body fat. Work in this zone is perceived as very light to light and is comfortable for long durations.

低需氧区：间歇心率 (IHR) 为标准心率 (SLTHR) 的 80% 至 90%，主观疲劳程度 (RPE) 为 11 至 13。

Low-Aerobic Zone: IHR 80 to 90 Percent of SLTHR, RPE 11 to 13

 

这个强度区间非常适合进行长距离慢速游泳。在这个强度区间进行锻炼可以提高心脏泵血能力和肌肉利用氧气的能力。身体能够更有效地代谢储存的脂肪，而脂肪仍然是肌肉的主要能量来源。在这个强度区间进行训练是有效增强耐力肌纤维负荷的方法，而强度过高的训练在这方面效果不佳。

This is a good zone for long, slow distance swimming. Exercise done in this zone improves the ability of your heart to pump blood and of your muscles to utilize oxygen. The body becomes more efficient at metabolizing stored body fat, still the main source of fuel for your muscles. Training in this zone is an effective way to overload endurance muscle fibers, and training above this intensity is less beneficial for this purpose.

这种强度根据您的体能水平而言，感觉轻松到中等——舒适到您可能感觉不到自己在真正训练。正因如此，心率训练计划中最难的部分在于如何在轻松日和长时间训练中保持较低的强度。以过高的强度进行基础有氧运动会降低后续高强度训练的效果。在轻松日过度训练是导致过度训练的主要原因。

This intensity is perceived as easy to moderate, depending on your fitness level—comfortable enough that you may not feel like you are actually training. Because of this, the most difficult part of following a heart-rate training program is keeping the intensity low on easy days and in long workouts. Performing basic aerobic workouts at too high of an intensity reduces the effectiveness of harder workouts on subsequent days. Working too hard on easy days is a primary cause of overtraining.

高强度有氧区：间歇心率达到标准心率的 90% 至 95%，主观疲劳程度为 13 至 14。

High-Aerobic Zone: IHR 90 to 95 Percent of SLTHR, RPE 13 to 14

 

这个训练区间能有效提升整体心肺功能。在此区间进行训练可以提高身体将含氧血液输送到肌肉细胞并将二氧化碳排出细胞的能力。糖原（葡萄糖）和脂肪都会被用作能量来源，但随着训练量的增加，身体会消耗更少的葡萄糖，而更多地消耗储存的脂肪。由于乳酸是运动肌肉中糖原代谢的副产物，因此你会感受到一些乳酸的影响。但由于这种训练强度并不高，你的有氧系统能够在乳酸积累到足以引起疼痛或影响运动表现之前将其从肌肉中清除。这个训练区间对增强肌肉力量也有一定的效果。根据个人体能水平的不同，在这个区间进行训练的感受可能从适中舒适到略微吃力略感不适不等。

This zone is effective for improving overall cardiorespiratory fitness. Working here improves your ability to transport oxygenated blood to the muscle cells and carbon dioxide out of the cells. Glycogen (glucose) and fat are both utilized for fuel here, but as you do more training at this level, your body will burn less glucose and more stored fat. Since lactic acid is a by-product of glycogen metabolism in working muscles, you will experience some effects of lactic acid. But because this work is not very intense, your aerobic system is able to clear the lactic acid from the muscles before enough accumulates to cause pain or limit performance. This zone is also somewhat effective for increasing muscle strength. Training in this zone can be perceived as moderate and comfortable to somewhat hard and somewhat uncomfortable, depending on your fitness level.

 

有效的游泳体能训练需要在保持良好技术的同时，进行各种强度的训练。

Effective conditioning for swimming requires work at a variety of intensities while maintaining excellent technique.

© Icon Sports Media

© Icon Sports Media

 

乳酸阈值区：IHR 为 SLTHR 的 95% 至 100%，RPE 为 14 至 15

Lactate-Threshold Zone: IHR 95 to 100 Percent of SLTHR, RPE 14 to 15

 

乳酸阈值训练是指你能长时间持续进行的最高运动强度。在接近乳酸阈值的强度下进行训练可以提高你的乳酸阈值，这意味着你能以更快的速度游泳更长时间。训练时的心率越接近你的实际乳酸阈值心率，这种训练效果就越显著。在这个强度范围内训练会感觉比较吃力但可以忍受：你会感到肌肉疲劳、呼吸急促，并且身体会有些不适。

Lactate-threshold exercise is the highest intensity of exercise that you can continue for an extended time. Training near your lactate threshold increases your lactate threshold, which means that you’ll be able to maintain a faster swimming pace for a longer time. The closer to your actual lactate-threshold heart rate you train, the greater this training effect. Training in this zone is perceived as difficult but tolerable: your muscles will feel tired, your breathing will be heavy, and you will be uncomfortable.

红线区域：IHR 高于 SLTHR，RPE 16 及以上

Red-Line Zone: IHR Above SLTHR, RPE 16 and Up

 

在这个区间，你的身体将承受极限负荷。只有身体素质极佳且获得医生许可的人才能进行此类训练。由于乳酸堆积迅速，会限制运动表现，因此只能在这个区间停留很短时间。在此区间训练可以提高身体缓冲和清除乳酸的能力，并增强快肌纤维的收缩力，从而提升速度。身体可以承受相对较少的此类训练量，但积少成多，效果显著。这种训练强度被认为是极端的：肌肉会感到灼烧，呼吸会变得非常急促，身体会感到疼痛，甚至可能出现呕吐的冲动。

In this zone, you push your body to its limit. Only train in this zone if you are very fit and have your physician’s blessing. It is possible to stay in this zone only for a short time since lactic acid accumulates rapidly, limiting performance. Training in this zone improves your body’s ability to buffer and clear lactic acid. It also improves the contractility of your fast-twitch muscle fibers, which increases speed. Your body can tolerate a relatively small amount of this type of work, but a little goes a long way. This intensity of training is perceived as extreme: your muscles will burn, your breathing will be very heavy, you will be in pain, and you may feel like you are going to vomit.

将RPE、IHR和 心率训练区间结合起来

Putting RPE, IHR, and Heart-Rate Training Zones Together

 

对大多数人来说，主观运动强度（RPE）与运动心率之间存在良好的相关性。您可以利用T-20游泳测试中获得的SLTHR值，填写个人训练区间表，轻松计算出不同RPE和训练区间对应的心率。

For most people, there is a good correlation between RPEs and exercise heart rates. You can easily calculate your heart rates for each of the different RPEs and training zones by filling in the Personal Training-Zone Chart using your SLTHR from your T-20 swim.

随着训练强度和训练量的变化，你的游泳乳酸阈值心率（SLTHR）也会随之改变。每次进行T-swim测试时，实际上都是在重新测试你的SLTHR（假设你按照说明进行游泳，并尽了全力——你应该在完成测试后感到自己已经竭尽所能）。然而，重要的是，在T-swim测试的最后几分钟内，不要加速或减速。这将确保你在测试结束时测得的间歇心率（IHR）能够代表你在整个游泳过程中的平均努力程度。如果你有心率监测器（HRM）可以测量特定时间段内的平均心率，你可以在T-swim测试进行到大约一半时停止游泳几秒钟，以此作为该时间段的开始。这样，你就可以在剩余的游泳过程中全力以赴，而不必担心“临近结束时不要加速”的限制（只需确保在完成游泳后立即停止该时间段的测量即可）。在这种情况下，使用该时间段的HRM平均值作为你的SLTHR。

Over time, your swimming lactate-threshold heart rate will change in response to your level and volume of training. Each time you do a T-swim, you are, in effect, retesting for your SLTHR (assuming that you do the swim according to the instructions and truly give your best effort—you should finish knowing you gave it everything you had). It is important, though, that you do not speed up or slow down during the last few minutes of your T-swim. This will ensure that your IHR at the end of the swim represents your average level of effort during the swim. If you have an HRM that will give you an average heart rate across a given interval, you can stop swimming for a few seconds at about the halfway point of the T-swim to start that interval.
