This will allow you to simply go for it through the rest of the swim and not have to worry about the “don’t speed up near the end” restriction (just be sure to stop the interval as soon as you finish the swim). In this case, use the HRM average for that interval as your SLTHR.

当你在T型游泳测试中发现SLTHR值升高时，你应该重新计算你的心率训练区间。同样地，如果在一段时间的训练量减少后，你在T型游泳测试中发现SLTHR值降低，你也应该重新计算你的训练区间数据。但如果你只是状态不佳，或者在T型游泳测试中没有尽全力，则无需重新计算你的训练区间数据。

As you experience higher SLTHRs in your T-swims, you should recalculate your heart-rate training zones. Similarly, if after a period of reduced training you experience lower SLTHRs in your T-swims, you should recalculate your chart entries. But if you simply have an off day or if you give your T-swim something less than your best effort, do not recalculate your chart entries.

 

个人训练区域图

Personal Training-Zone Chart

 

训练级别

Workout Levels

 

以下章节的训练计划根据持续时间和强度分为六个级别。前四个级别的训练计划都建议了运动强度范围，以SLTHR和RPE的百分比范围表示。这是您大部分训练的目标心率和RPE范围。在每次训练中，您需要多次测量IHR或RPE。一般来说，您的目标应该是监测运动强度和休息时间，使心率或RPE保持在建议的目标范围内。许多训练计划中的组数会导致心率和RPE略高于此范围。这些峰值持续时间较短，通常会伴随训练计划中安排的休息或轻松活动，使您的心率或RPE恢复到指定的目标范围内。在第五和第六级别中，IHR和RPE的使用方式会略有不同。我们稍后会详细讨论。

The workouts in the following chapters are arranged into six workout levels according to duration and intensity. Workouts in the first four levels have a suggested range of effort, which is expressed as a percentage range of SLTHR and RPE. This is your target heart rate and RPE range for most of the practice. You will take an IHR or RPE several times during each practice. In general, your goal should be to monitor your exertion level and rest periods so that your heart rate or RPE stays in the recommended target range. Sets in many practices will produce heart rates and RPEs that are somewhat higher than this range. These peaks will last for short periods and will usually be accompanied by rest or easy activity that is built into the practice, allowing your heart rate or RPE to return to within the specified target range. In levels 5 and 6, use of IHRs and RPEs will be a bit different. We’ll talk more about that later.

从一个训练级别过渡到下一个级别，要么会增加训练的平均强度，要么会增加训练的持续时间。每个级别包含 10 个练习，大致按难度递增的顺序排列。每个练习的难度各不相同，并受技能和训练动作的复杂程度、游泳的长度、次数和强度、休息时间以及目标心率范围的影响。下表概述了每个训练级别。

Moving from one exercise level to the next either increases the average intensity of the workout or increases the duration of the workout. Within each level, there are 10 practices that are arranged roughly in order of increasing difficulty. The degree of difficulty varies from practice to practice and is affected by skill and drill complexity; by length, number, and intensity of swims; by amount of rest; and by target-heart-rate range. A summary of each workout level is given in the following table.

 

热身和放松

Warming Up and Cooling Down

 

热身是每次训练课的第一个水上活动。热身的三大要点是：克服水的冰冷感、让身体做好运动准备以及调整心态。最佳的热身方式是直接下水，然后慢游几圈。但你会立刻遇到一个问题——运动时舒适的水温，在你刚下水时通常会感觉很冷。你可能会很想立刻冲刺，这种感觉会让你心跳加速、呼吸困难，只有游了几圈之后才会逐渐恢复舒适。但这很容易导致受伤。更好的做法是先进行陆上热身——比如徒手体操、普拉提、快跑或其他类似的运动，以提高体温并适度出汗——然后再跳入水中，以免体温下降。

The warm-up is your first in-water activity of each training session. The three important aspects of the warm-up are overcoming the chill of the water, getting your body ready for the workout, and tuning your mind in to the task. The best way to warm up is to get into the water and to start swimming slowly for several laps. Immediately, you are presented with a problem—water temperature that is comfortable during a workout is usually uncomfortably cool when you first get in. The urge to start sprinting can be strong, with heart-stopping, lung-gripping semipanic that only gives way to relative comfort after a few laps or more. But this can be a short path to injury. Better to do a dryland warm-up—calisthenics, Pilates, a brisk jog, or something similar to raise your body temperature and get you moderately sweaty—and then to jump into the water before you have a chance to cool down.

适应水温后，集中注意力，调整神经肌肉系统。进行一系列游泳技巧练习，可以迫使你的游泳肌肉完成完整划水动作所需的所有运动范围。这些练习还能帮助你专注于动作的正确执行。这是练习那些在疲劳时难以正确完成的动作的绝佳时机。你的大脑需要一些时间才能完全投入，而技巧练习可以有效地集中注意力。交替进行一段练习和一段游泳（也就是说，将你在练习中正确完成的动作运用到你的划水动作中），是过渡到正式训练的理想方式。避免在热身时只是游一些无关紧要的距离。本书中的热身练习都要求技巧练习和游泳相结合。

After adjusting to the water temperature, focus your mind and neuromuscular system. Going through a progression of swimming-skill drills will force your swimming muscles to move through all the ranges of motion that are required for full-stroke swimming. The drills also allow you to focus on proper execution. This is an excellent time to work on drills that are difficult to execute properly when you are tired. Your brain also takes a while to get fully involved, and skill drills focus it effectively. Adding full-stroke swimming by alternating a length of drilling with a length of swimming (that is, making what you correctly executed in the drill show up in your stroke) is an ideal way to transition into the main part of the workout. Avoid the tendency to just swim garbage yardage as your warm-up. The warm-ups throughout this book call for a mix of skill drills and swimming.

训练结束后进行积极的放松运动，就像反向的热身——通过轻松的游泳或划船等运动，使身体及其各项机能恢复到接近静息状态。剧烈运动后，肌肉会持续将乳酸释放到血液中一段时间​​。轻松的运动有助于保持含氧血液快速流动，从而将乳酸从肌肉中排出。否则，即使停止运动，乳酸也会继续积累。想想看，长途驾驶后熄火，汽车引擎的滴答声和尾气排放的声音会持续几分钟。同样，当你剧烈游泳后突然停止时，身体也会发出抗议。积极的放松运动可以避免心脏承受额外的压力，并减轻运动后的肌肉痉挛和酸痛。

Actively cooling down at the end of a training session is like warming up in reverse—returning the body and all its functions to near-resting levels by doing some easy swimming or drilling. For a while after a strong exercise effort, your muscles continue to clear lactic acid into your bloodstream. Easy activity helps keep oxygenated blood flowing rapidly, thereby transporting lactic acid away from the muscles. Otherwise, lactic acid continues to accumulate even after you stop exercising. Listen to your car after you’ve turned it off following a long, hard drive; those sounds of ticking metal and passing vapors go on for minutes. In the same way, your body protests when you swim it hard and then come to a sudden stop. An active cool-down avoids extra strain on the heart and lessens postexercise cramping and soreness.

由于普遍存在一种误解，认为低强度运动没有训练效果，因此放松环节常常被视为浪费时间。然而，无知是福。游泳训练中最重要的部分是神经肌肉系统的训练（重要的是动作要正确，而不仅仅是做动作）。放松环节是进行高质量专项练习的绝佳时机。事实上，在肌肉疲劳时引导它们进行特定的技能练习，能够有效地促进肌肉的运动学习。放松环节应该选择你已经掌握的练习和技能，而不是那些休息后难以完成的练习。

The cool-down is often treated as a waste due to the common misconception that moving at a low intensity offers no training effect. Ignorance is bliss. The most important training you do in swimming is the training of your neuromuscular system (doing it right rather than just doing it). The cool-down is an excellent time to do some high-quality drill work. In fact, coaxing your muscles to go through specific skill drills when they are fatigued presents an effective motor-learning opportunity. Choose drills and skills you have mastered for cool-downs rather than ones you have difficulty executing when rested.

第七章
 
一级：基础技能训练
 

一级训练主要包括姿势、平衡和游泳技巧练习，以及少量全泳姿练习。本章的训练大约需要20到30分钟完成。你将在其他级别中使用一级的所有练习。如果你在某个练习中遇到困难，请花更多时间练习，直到掌握为止。通常，真正的问题在于你还没有完全掌握之前的练习。无论你的水平如何，本书中即使是最简单的练习也能增强你的神经肌肉控制能力。在你熟悉每个练习之前，建议你复印练习说明，并将其放入密封的保鲜袋中，以便在泳池边练习时快速查阅。

Level 1 workouts consist primarily of posture, balance, and swimming-skill drills with a small amount of full-stroke swimming. The workouts in this chapter will take approximately 20 to30 minutes to complete. You will use each of the level 1 drills in the other levels. If you have trouble with a specific drill, spend extra time on it to get it right. Often the real problem is that you haven’t mastered an earlier drill. Regardless of your ability, even the simplest drills in this book will enhance your neuromuscular knowledge. Until you are familiar with each drill, you might want to photocopy the drill descriptions and put them in watertight sandwich bags so that you can have them for quick reference at poolside while you practice.

本章中的训练可以使用全尺寸或短鳍训练脚蹼。如果您在不穿脚蹼的情况下踢水进步显著，也可以赤脚进行这些训练。假设您一开始使用全尺寸脚蹼，随着您对各种练习和动作越来越熟练，您可以逐渐过渡到短鳍脚蹼，最终赤脚进行训练。

You may do the workouts in this chapter with full-size or short-blade training fins. If you make good forward progress when kicking without fins, you can also do these workouts with bare feet. Assuming that you start with full-size fins, you will want to switch to short-blade fins and eventually to bare feet as you become more comfortable with various drills and exercises.

你应该尽可能多地利用游泳时间来巩固所学的基本技巧。在游泳过程中，要时刻牢记重点，保持专注。你可以把重点清单（第220页）的复印件装进塑料袋里，以备不时之需。

You will want to spend as much of your swimming time as possible emphasizing the fundamentals you have been learning. Use the focus points throughout the swim to keep your mind engaged. A photocopy of the focus-point list (page 220) in a plastic bag can come in handy.

完成本章所有练习后，请重复第三章的T-20游泳练习。目标是在规定的20分钟内游得比之前更远。进行T-20练习时请勿使用脚蹼，以便进行公平的比较。如果您之前无法不间断地完成T-20游泳，那么缩短休息时间或许能显著提高您的成绩。完成T-20后，请记录您的成绩并与之前的成绩进行比较。如果您的SLTHR（标准肺活量心率）有所提高，请务必重新计算您的训练区间心率。

After you have completed all of the practices in this chapter once, repeat the T-20 swim from chapter 3. The goal is to swim farther in the allotted 20-minute period than you did originally. Do the T-20 without fins so that you’ll be comparing apples to apples. If you were unable to complete the initial T-20 swim without stopping, then you may improve significantly simply by taking shorter rests. After you complete the T-20, record your results with your original results, and be sure to recalculate your training-zone heart rates if your SLTHR has increased.

在进入下一级别之前，您应该至少完成两遍第一级练习。第一次完成第一级练习后，请重新阅读练习中每个训练动作和重点的描述。您很可能会吸收一些第一次阅读时没有注意到的新概念和细微差别。第二次完成第一级练习后，请重复T-20练习并记录结果，然后再进入第二级练习。

You should plan on going through the level 1 practices at least twice before moving to the next level. After your first pass through level 1, reread the descriptions of each drill and focus point that appear in the practices. Chances are you’ll absorb new concepts and nuances that you may not have noticed when you first read them. After completing your second pass through level 1, repeat the T-20 and record the results before going on to level 2.

阅读训练计划

Reading the Workouts

 

本书练习部分中，我使用了一些符号速记方法。

I use some notation shortcuts throughout the practice sections of this book.

乍一看它们可能令人困惑，但读完下面的几个例子后，你就会明白了。

At first glance they may be confusing, but after you’ve read through a couple of the examples that follow, you’ll catch on.

 

6 × 25 游泳TS :15R

6 × 25 swim TS on :15R

 

这意味着使用训练呼吸管（ TS ）游六个泳池长度（每个长度为25码或米），在泳池两端各休息15秒。一般来说，休息时间只是一个建议，而非硬性规定。目的是让你有足够的时间重新整理思路，并充分恢复体力，以便能够继续顺利完成训练。如果你需要更多休息时间，那就休息。如果你的技能和体能允许你减少休息时间，那也没问题。

This means to swim six lengths (each length is 25 yards or meters) of the pool with your training snorkel (TS), taking 15 seconds rest at each end of the pool. In general, the rest duration is a suggestion rather than a requirement. The idea is to allow yourself enough time to regroup your thinking and to recover enough physically that you can continue with success. If you need more rest, take it. If your skills and conditioning allow you to take less rest, that’s fine too.

 

1 × 100—替代 25 FB、25 BB、25 SGB、25 SGSS

1 × 100—alt 25 FB, 25 BB, 25 SGB, 25 SGSS

 

这意味着要不停歇地跑完四个来回，每个来回都要从一个练习过渡到下一个练习。

This means to do four lengths without stopping, moving from one drill to the next with each length.

 

6 × 25 on :15R—alt 25 FB, 25 BB

6 × 25 on :15R—alt 25 FB, 25 BB

 

这意味着要游六个来回，每个来回休息15秒。交替进行一个来回的前平衡练习和一个来回的后平衡练习。

This means to swim six lengths of the pool, taking 15 seconds rest after each length. Alternate one length of front-balance drill and one length of back-balance drill.

 

4 × 50 SGNU 在 :15R 作为 25 rt，25 lft

4 × 50 SGNU on :15R as 25 rt, 25 lft

 

这意味着要进行50米的SGNU（侧滑抬头）练习——即游完泳池的两个来回，到达远端后不要休息——然后休息15秒。重复三次，总共游四个50米。每次游完50米后，交替进行，第一来回用右侧身体，第二来回用左侧身体。

This means to do the SGNU (side-glide nose-up) drill for 50—two lengths of the pool with no rest at the far end—and then to rest for 15 seconds. Repeat three more times for a total of four 50s. On each 50, alternate doing the first length on your right side with doing the second length on your left side.

 

6 × :15 VK on :10R—奇数：双手放在胸前；偶数：双手离开水面

6 × :15 VK on :10R—odd: hands on your chest; even: hands out of the water

 

这种训练方法要求进行六组15秒的垂直踢腿动作，奇数次和偶数次重复时手部位置不同。每组15秒的垂直踢腿动作之间休息10秒。

This notation asks for six 15-second periods of vertical kicking with different hand positions on odd and even repeats. There are 10-second rests between each 15-second VK period.

 

IHR 或 RPE

IHR or RPE

 

立即测量心率或主观疲劳程度。看到此提示时，请在活动结束后尽快测量心率。如果您使用的是博格主观疲劳程度量表 (Borg RPE scale)，请在活动过程中评估您的疲劳程度。

Immediate heart rate or rating of perceived exertion. When you see this, take your heart rate as quickly as possible after completing the activity. If you are using the Borg RPE scale instead, assess your level of exertion as you are completing the activity.

 

1 × 100 SGB-alt 25 个良好，25 个不良

1 × 100 SGB-alt 25 good, 25 weak

 

许多技能都需要先在一侧完成某个动作，然后再在另一侧重复该动作（例如侧滑平衡、呼吸练习等等）。你通常会发现，你更容易在一侧完成某个技能。在感觉更放松的一侧，你会更迅速地找到正确的姿势。你也可能能够更长时间、更轻松地保持这个姿势。这就是你的强侧。而你感觉比较吃力的一侧，就是你的弱侧。

Many skills involve doing something on one side, then repeating the action on the other side (e.g., side-glide balance, breathing, and the like). You will usually find that you are better at performing a skill on one side than on the other. On that side, you’ll be more relaxed and better able to get into a proper position quickly. You may also be able to hold that position longer and with less effort. This is your good side. The side on which you experience more problems is your weak side.

继续技术教育

Continuing Technique Education

 

在最初的训练说明中，我加入了一些重点，每个重点都将两项或多项技能和反馈工具整合到一个简短易记的短语中。这些重点旨在引导你在游泳或训练时将注意力集中在重要方面。你会在训练中经常看到它们。随着你级别的提升和技能的提高，我会引入更多重点。以下是一些你现在可能已经准备好学习的重点。

In the original drill descriptions I included a number of focus points, each of which bring together two or more skills and feedback tools in a short, easy-to-remember phrase. These are intended to direct your thinking to important areas while swimming or drilling. You’ll see them mentioned often in the workouts. As you progress through the levels and as your skills improve, I will introduce more focus points. Following are a few you are likely ready for now.

 
重点➤下坡游泳
 

当你摆出紧绷的绳索姿势时，要保持足够的浮力，使你的臀部和腿部保持在水面。你应该感觉整个身体略微向下倾斜。你真正想要的是保持水平姿势，但如果你习惯于略微上翘的姿势——头部和肩膀比臀部和腿部略高——那么当你真正保持水平姿势时，就会感觉身体略微向下倾斜。

 
重点➤侧滑
 

划水时，每次身体旋转时，都要完全侧身，或者几乎侧身，使肚脐朝向侧壁。尝试用侧身“滑行”，下侧手臂略微向下伸展。保持这个姿势继续滑行，同时另一只手臂向前越过头部，到达激光束旋转触发点。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Downhill Swimming
 

When you are organized in a tight-line posture, maintain enough buoy pressure to keep your hips and legs at the surface. It should feel as if your entire body is tilted slightly downhill. You really want to be horizontal, but if your habit is to be in a somewhat uphill position—head and shoulders a bit higher than your hips and legs—then when you are in a horizontal position, it will feel like you are tilted slightly downhill.

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Side Skating
 

As you take strokes, you should turn all the way onto your side, or nearly so, with each rotation of your body, so that your navel is pointed toward the side wall. Try to “skate” on that side with your bottom arm extended at a slightly downward angle. Continue skating in that position while the recovering arm moves forward past your head to the laser-beam rotation-trigger point.

 
 
重点➤换手
 

这比手套的重点少一步。关键在于保持伸直的手臂在身体前方，直到准备接替或入水的手臂准备好为止。始终用一只手作为移动船只的前方；切勿用头部作为前方。这是理解前象限游泳的另一种方式。更完整的描述请参见第五章第50页。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Hand Swapping
 

This is one step short of the glove focus point. The idea is to keep your extended arm in front of your body until your recovering, or entering, hand is ready to take its place. Always use one of your hands as the front of your moving vessel; never use your head as the front. This is another way to think of front-quadrant swimming. See chapter 5, page 50 for a more complete description.

 
 
重点➤笔画数
 

衡量游泳技术水平和效率的一个指标是每次划水的距离。计算游完泳池每个来回所需的划水次数，可以让你很好地了解每次划水的距离——划水次数越少，每次划水的距离就越远。每次手入水都算一次。即使最后一次手入水时触到了池壁而不是继续划水，也算在内。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Stroke Count
 

One indicator of technical proficiency and swimming efficiency is the distance you travel with each stroke. Counting the number of strokes it takes to swim each length of the pool gives you excellent feedback about the distance you are traveling with each stroke—the fewer you take, the further you travel with each one. Count one for each hand as it enters the water. The last hand entry at the end of the pool counts as well, even though you touch the wall instead of taking another stroke.

Posture and Static Balance

 

Training zone: Recovery and low aerobic

Target RPE range: 9 to 11

Target heart-rate range: 70 to 85% of SLTHR

Our goal is still flawless execution, though, so if you feel that you need more rest in order to execute well, then take extra time between repeats at the walls.

第八章
 
二级：技能发展训练
 

假设您已经完整地练习过几遍一级练习，并且能够轻松完成，心率也保持在目标范围内，那么现在就可以开始二级练习了。到目前为止，您应该对一级练习中讲解的所有技能和重点内容都感到自信。如果没有，建议您复习并练习任何需要加强的地方。您需要熟练掌握目前为止讲解的所有技能和练习，才能进行下一步，将核心旋转与划水动作结合起来。

Assuming that you have worked through the complete set of level 1 practices a couple of times and that you have been completing them easily and within your target heart-rate range, it is probably time to move to level 2 practices. By now you should feel confident with all of the skill drills and focus points presented in level 1. If not, you may want to review and practice any areas of concern. You will need to be proficient in all of the skills and drills presented so far in order to take the next step of connecting your core rotations to your strokes.

二级训练与一级训练类似，主要包括姿势、平衡和游泳技巧练习，但也包含少量完整泳姿练习。二级训练时间稍长（30-40分钟，而一级训练为20-30分钟）。二级训练与一级训练非常相似，但各项练习的重复次数更多，并且增加了一些重点练习。

Level 2 practices, like level 1 practices, are primarily posture, balance, and swimming drills, but they also have a small amount of full-stroke swimming. These practices will be a bit longer (30-40 minutes rather than 20-30 minutes for level 1 practices). They are very similar to level 1 practices, but there are more repetitions of the various drills and some added focus points.

在训练符号中，我会在多个地方标明多个重点（例如，重点：紧线和木偶式恢复）。最初，这意味着你应该在这些重点之间交替练习。你应该专注于一个重点几个划水动作，然后切换到另一个重点几个划水动作，以此类推。或者，如果练习时间足够长，你可以先专注于一个重点完成一个划水动作，然后再专注于另一个重点完成另一个划水动作，以此类推。随着你技能的不断提升和精进，你将能够同时专注于多个重点。

At various places in the workout notation, I indicate multiple focus points (e.g., focus: tight line and marionette recovery). Initially, this means that you should alternate between the focus points indicated. You should focus on one point for several strokes, then shift your focus to another point for several strokes, and so on. Alternatively, if the length of the activity is sufficient, you could complete a length with one focus, then a length with another, and so on. As you acquire and refine more skills, it will be possible for you to focus on multiple points at the same time.

虽然我们仍然鼓励您在尚未完全适应的练习中使用训练脚蹼，但我们的长期目标是逐步过渡到从长鳍脚蹼到短鳍脚蹼，最终在尽可能多的练习中赤脚游泳。在进行这些练习的过程中，请寻找机会减少对脚蹼的依赖，尤其是在游泳而非进行专项训练时。

While training fins are still encouraged for any drills that you have not yet become comfortable with, our long-term goal is to move from long-blade fins to short-blade fins and finally to bare feet in as many of the drills as possible. As you work through these practices, look for opportunities to rely less on fins, especially when you are just swimming as opposed to drilling.

阅读训练计划

Reading the Workouts

 

本节介绍一些新的符号快捷方式。

This section introduces a few new notation shortcuts.

 

1 × 50 米游泳，其中 25 米按 NSPL 标准游，25 米按 -1SPL 标准游

1 × 50 swim as 25 @ NSPL, 25 @ -1SPL

 

SPL 指的是“每长度划水次数”。在二级水平，你需要了解并控制每长度的划水次数。25 @ NSPL 指的是以正常的 SPL 游完前 25 码——也就是你现在感觉正常的每长度划水次数，无需刻意增加划水幅度。25 @ -1SPL 指的是在接下来的 25 码或米中，比你通常游完该长度少划一次。

SPL means “strokes per length.” In level 2 you will need to be aware of and control how many strokes per length you are taking. By 25 @ NSPL, I mean to swim the first 25 at normal SPL—that is, the number of strokes per length that feels normal to you right now without trying to do anything special to lengthen the strokes themselves. 25 @ -1SPL means to swim the next 25 yards or meters taking one fewer stroke than you normally would take at that length.

 

4 × 25 米游泳 @ N, -1, -1, -2SPL

4 × 25 swim @ N, -1, -1, -2SPL

 

先以正常划水频率游完一个25米，接下来的两个25米每次少划一次，最后一个25米少划两次。例如，如果你第一个25米用了18次划水，那么第二个和第三个25米应该各用17次划水，第四个25米用16次划水。

Swim one 25 at normal SPL, the next two 25s taking one fewer stroke than normal, and the last 25 taking two fewer strokes than normal. In this example, if you swim the first 25 using 18 strokes, then the second and third lengths should be swum using 17 strokes each, and the fourth using 16.

 

4 × 25 游泳—下降 1-4（或下降 1-4）

4 × 25 swim—descend 1-4 (or desc 1-4)

 

第二级引入了一系列速度变化的游泳练习。“递减 1-4”表示在 4 次游泳练习中，每次游泳的完成时间都要比前一次更短。第一次以轻松的速度游，第二次稍快一些，第三次更快，第四次更快。尽量使每次游泳的速度提升幅度大致相同。例如，如果您第一次游 25 米用了 22 秒，那么接下来的三次游泳，尝试分别用 21 秒、20 秒和 19 秒完成。

Level 2 introduces a series of swims in which you vary your speed. Descend 1-4 means that in a set of 4 swims, each swim is to be completed in less time than the previous one. The first one is swum at an easy pace, the second one a bit faster, the third one even faster, and the fourth one faster still. Try to make roughly the same increase in speed from one swim to the next. In this example, if you swim the first 25 in 22 seconds, try to swim the next three in 21, 20, and 19 seconds, respectively.

 

4 × 25 米游泳（奇数：快；偶数：慢）

4 × 25 swim (odd: fast; even: easy)

 

奇数和偶数：奇数次重复动作使用一个指令或重点；偶数次重复动作使用不同的指令或重点。在这个例子中，奇数次重复动作要游得快，偶数次重复动作要游得慢。

Odds and evens: Odd-numbered repeats are done with one instruction or focus point; even-numbered repeats are done with a different instruction or focus point. In this example, you would swim the odd repeats fast and swim the even repeats easy.

 

男孩们

BOYLFS

 

练习用你不太擅长的一侧呼吸：当你看到“BOYLFS”（双侧呼吸法）时，只用这一侧呼吸，并着眼于改进——想象你头顶上的红点，保持头部不动，尽量让身体抬高，保持手臂向前伸直等等。仅仅能够两侧呼吸是不够的，更重要的是两侧都能有效呼吸。BOYLFS 指导让你练习呼吸经验较少的那一侧，这样你的习惯（无论好坏）就不会那么根深蒂固。你的弱侧更容易学习新的、更有效的技巧，也更容易提高你对呼吸如何影响其他游泳技术的认识。随着你在这一侧的技巧和意识不断提高，你可能会发现它逐渐成为你最擅长的呼吸侧，这意味着是时候将你所学到的东西应用到你不太擅长的那一侧了！

Breathe on Your Less Favorite Side: When you see BOYLFS, breathe only on this side, with an eye toward making improvements—imagine the red dot on your head, maintain zero head lift, go more toward nose-up, keep your weightless arm out front, etc. It is not sufficient to simply be able to breathe on both sides but, rather, to breathe well on both sides. The BOYLFS instruction makes you work on the side on which you have less experience breathing, and thus your habits, good or bad, are not as ingrained. Your weak side is the easier side for learning new, more effective skills and for improving your awareness of how your breathing affects the rest of your swimming technique. As your skills and awareness improve on this side, you will likely find that it becomes your favorite breathing side, indicating that it is time to apply what you have learned to your new less favorite side!

我之前提到过左右交替呼吸法，也就是在练习时左右两侧各呼吸一半，这种方法也适用于全程划水。左右两侧呼吸对于确保你的游泳技术不失衡至关重要。游泳者通常会选择每三次划水就换一次气——也就是所谓的双侧呼吸。但对于大多数成年游泳者来说，双侧呼吸无法提供足够的氧气来应对超过50码（约45米）的游泳距离。面对氧气不足，人们的本能反应是增加每次划水的次数，以便能多呼吸几次——我希望我已经让你意识到，这种不必要地增加划水次数的做法是不可取的。因此，我建议你练习左右交替呼吸法，先用右侧呼吸游25码（或50码、100码），再用左侧呼吸游25码（或50码、100码）。这样，你就可以在不缩短呼吸次数的情况下，比传统的双侧呼吸多呼吸 33%。

Earlier I mentioned half-and-half breathing, or the idea of taking roughly half your breaths on one side and half your breaths on the other side during drills, and that this idea applies to full-stroke swimming as well. Breathing on both sides is important for ensuring that you do not develop lopsided technique. Swimmers often choose to breathe on both sides by taking a breath every third stroke—often called bilateral breathing. But for most adult swimmers, bilateral breathing does not supply enough oxygen for swims over 50 yards or so. The instinctive response to this lack of oxygen is to take more strokes in each length so that more breaths can be taken—and I hope I’ve conditioned you to recoil at the thought of needlessly adding strokes to your swim. Instead, I encourage you to practice half-and-half breathing by breathing to your right for a 25 (or 50 or 100) and then breathing to your left for a 25 (or 50 or 100). This allows you to take 33 percent more breaths than traditional bilateral breathing without having to shorten your strokes.

继续技术教育

Continuing Technique Education

 

到目前为止，通过VKR和LAR练习中的核心旋转训练，你已经能够更好地利用身体最大的肌肉群来旋转核心肌群，并通过保持紧绷的姿势将这种旋转传递到肩部。接下来的旋转连接练习和重点练习将帮助你把手臂及其运动与这个强大的核心肌群连接起来。

By now, through your core-rotation work in the VKR and LAR drills, you have improved at rotating your core with the largest muscles in the body and transmitting that rotation to your shoulders via tight-line posture. The rotation-connection drills and focus points that follow will help you connect your arms and their motions to this large core engine.

多次旋转，三次冲程 (MR3S)

Many Rotations, Three Strokes (MR3S)

 

这个练习是LAR练习和3S&G练习的混合体。最好在熟练掌握LAR和3S&G练习之后再尝试这个练习。以下是逐步完成MR3S练习的步骤。建议使用训练呼吸管循序渐进地练习这些步骤，直到熟练掌握后再尝试用真呼吸进行练习。

This drill is a hybrid of the LAR drill and the 3S&G drill. It is best not to attempt it until you have mastered both the LAR and 3S&G. The following are drill steps for building up to the complete MR3S drill. You’ll want to progress through the steps using your training snorkel until you’ve mastered them before trying them with real breathing.

第一步：多次旋转，一次划水 (MR1S)这是熟悉的 LAR 练习，偶尔会穿插单臂自由泳划水循环。练习时，保持流线型的头朝下 LAR 姿势，在泳池中游动，每次划水都用一次旋转（由旋转打腿启动）来驱动。旋转开始时，用靠近池底的那只手臂划水。划水与旋转同时开始。尽量在旋转结束的同时完成划水。在旋转打腿后的两次打腿过程中，进行木偶式手臂的恢复动作。调整恢复手臂的时机，使你的手刚好经过头部（激光束旋转触发点），同时下一次旋转打腿启动身体旋转。记住你在 SGSS 和 3S&G 练习中建立的手部入水到打腿的协调性。旋转时，那只手臂应该刺破水面并向前伸展——而且应该略微向下倾斜，以便与之前一直保持在同一位置的手臂重新连接。继续进行长轴旋转一段时间，同时评估划水、回桨和入水动作，然后为下一个循环做好准备。再旋转几次后，用另一只手臂重复上述步骤，进行单臂划水循环。你的目标是保持稳定的长轴旋转节奏，并在每个划水循环中保持不变。

Step 1: Many Rotations, One Stroke (MR1S) This is the familiar LAR drill with an occasional single-arm freestyle-stroke cycle thrown in. As you work your way down the pool practicing a fully streamlined nose-down LAR drill, use one rotation, initiated by a rotation kick, to power each stroke. Stroke with the arm that is closer to the bottom of the pool at the beginning of the rotation. Start the stroke at the same time you start the rotation. Try to finish the stroke at the same time you finish the rotation. Do your marionette arm recovery during the two flutter kicks that follow the rotation kick. Time your recovering arm so that your hand is just passing your head (laser-beam rotation-trigger point) as the next rotation kick initiates body rotation. Remember your hand-entry-to-kick coordination that you established in the SGSS and 3S&G drills. That arm should pierce the surface and extend forward as you rotate—and it should extend at a bit of a downward angle in order to rejoin the arm that remained there throughout the cycle. Continue your long-axis rotations for a while as you assess the stroke, recovery, and entry, and then plan ahead for the next cycle. After some more rotations, repeat the step with a single-arm stroke cycle of the other arm. Your goal is to have a consistent LAR rhythm that continues unchanged through each stroke cycle.

步骤 2 ：多次旋转，两次划水 (MR2S)现在，我们在 MR1S 的基础上，在每个练习周期中加入另一只手臂的划水动作，而不是像 MR1S 那样将手臂放在身前。请注意，MR1S 练习中，每个单臂划水周期需要旋转两次。MR2S 练习则需要旋转三次才能完成一个包含两次划水的周期，具体步骤如下：起始动作与 MR1S 相同，旋转一次以驱动划水，并在手臂收回至头部前方时进行两次打腿。

Step 2: Many Rotations, Two Strokes (MR2S) We now expand MR1S to add in a stroke with the other arm in each cycle of the drill, instead of just leaving that arm out front. Note that the MR1S drill required two rotations for each single-arm stroke cycle. The MR2S drill requires three rotations to complete a cycle of two strokes as follows: Start as you did in MR1S, using one rotation to power a stroke and using two flutter kicks as you recover that arm to the front of your head.

以下是补充说明：在开始第二次旋转时，用另一只手臂开始划水，这样，当第二次旋转带动收回的手臂刺破水面时，也能为第二次划水提供动力。在第二次旋转结束时，我们希望第二次划水结束于大腿附近，同时，入水的手臂在身体前方完全伸展。在收回第二只手臂的同时，再做两次打水动作。当这只手经过激光束旋转触发点时，开始第三次旋转，这将带动手刺破水面并向前与仍然伸展在身体前方的第一只手臂汇合。继续进行长轴旋转，同时评估两次划水的周期，并为下一个周期做好准备。再旋转几次后，重复另一个两次划水的周期。你应该交替使用两只手臂进行第一次划水。同样，我们希望你的长轴旋转能够带动划水，同时保持旋转节奏不变。

Here is the addition: as you begin the second rotation, start to stroke with the other arm, so as the second rotation drives the recovering arm to pierce the surface, it also powers the second stroke. As this second rotation is finishing, we want the second stroke to finish by your thigh and, at the same time, to have the entering arm reach full extension in front of the body. Take two more flutter kicks as you recover that second arm forward. As that hand passes the laser-beam rotation-trigger point, initiate the third rotation, which drives the hand through the surface and forward to meet the first arm, which is still extended in front of the body. Continue your long-axis rotations as you assess the cycle of two strokes, and plan ahead for the next cycle. After a few more rotations, repeat with another two-stroke cycle. You should alternate which arm takes the first stroke. Again, we’re looking for your long-axis rotations to drive the strokes without changing the rotation rhythm.

步骤 3 ：多次旋转，三次划水 (MR3S)现在，我们像在 MR1S 中加入一次旋转和一次划水，得到 MR2S 一样，在循环中加入第四次旋转和第三次划水。和之前一样，在分隔划水循环的旋转阶段保持呼吸。每组划水包含三次划水，你会开始感受到划水的节奏。不要让你的手臂控制远离腿部的长轴旋转的节奏。相反，要专注于你的上半身和手臂，让它们由构成循环的四个核心旋转驱动。保持紧绷的姿势，并利用手套和激光束旋转触发点来集中注意力，会有所帮助。此外，在每组划水之间留出足够的旋转时间，以便你有时间评估每组划水的效果，并为下一个循环做好准备。在练习过程中，你应该交替使用不同的手臂在每个循环中的第一划。

Step 3: Many Rotations, Three Strokes (MR3S) Now we add a fourth rotation and a third stroke to the cycle in the same way that we added a rotation and a stroke to MR1S to arrive at MR2S. As before, breathe during the segments of rotations that separate stroke cycles. With three strokes in each set of strokes, you will begin to sense a stroking rhythm. Don’t let your arms take control of the rhythm of the long-axis rotations away from your legs. Instead, focus on your upper body and arms being driven by the four core rotations that underlie the cycle. Keeping your tight-line posture and using the glove and laser-beam rotation-trigger focus points will help. Also include enough rotations between each set of strokes to give you time to assess each set and to plan ahead for the next cycle. You should alternate which arm takes the first stroke of each cycle as you do this drill.

第四步：加入真实呼吸暂时把呼吸管放在一边。就像你在3S&G练习中那样，你可以在每个循环的最后一次划水时加入一次呼吸，不过在侧滑姿势下你无法停下来。然后按照你在3S&G练习中使用的模式，将呼吸移到第一次或第二次划水时。

Step 4: Add Real Breathing Set the snorkel aside for this. As you did with the 3S&G drill, you can add a breath on the last stroke of each cycle, though you won’t have the luxury of stopping while in a side-glide position. Then follow the pattern you used in the 3S&G drill, moving the breath to the first or second stroke.

通往MR3S的垫脚石

Stepping-Stone to MR3S

 

当你开始进行这项训练时，我建议你先用普通脚蹼完成每个步骤，直到你能很好地完成该步骤，然后逐渐过渡到短脚蹼，最后过渡到赤脚。

When you start this progression, I suggest you do each step with regular fins until you can perform that step well, then wean yourself first to short fins and then to bare feet.

反馈工具

Feedback Tools

 

• 将你的旋转节奏与节奏提示器（或脑海中一段节奏鲜明的熟悉旋律）相匹配，可以帮助你判断在从单纯旋转切换到带击打的旋转，以及切换回单纯旋转时，你的节奏是否发生了变化。目标是在整个过程中保持不间断的旋转节奏（即使在转头呼吸时也是如此）。

• Matching your rotation tempo to a tempo beeper (or to a familiar tune with a distinctive beat in your head) can help you determine whether you are changing tempo as you switch from just rotations to rotations with strokes and back. The goal is to have an uninterrupted rotation tempo throughout (even when turning your head to breathe).

• 使用脸颊和脸颊的焦点来判断你的肤色是否平衡。

• Use the patches-and-cheeks focus point to determine whether you are balanced.

 

做个小实验

Experiment a Bit

 

到目前为止，这些练习都是以非常轻松的节奏进行的，重点在于保持稳定的节奏和时机。在你掌握了轻松节奏下的这些练习之后，可以尝试加快长轴旋转的节奏，并将你的划水动作与这种更快的核心旋转结合起来。这意味着你的手臂动作也会更快。和之前一样，挑战在于避免让手臂主导节奏。这应该是腿部驱动的核心旋转的任务。只有当你能够在划水的同时保持姿势、平衡和稳定的旋转节奏，并且能够在每组划水动作结束后都保持平衡、紧凑的线条，无需任何调整时，才能加快节奏。

So far, these drills have been performed at very relaxed tempos with an emphasis on maintaining even rhythm and timing. After you have mastered these drills at relaxed tempos, experiment with setting a faster long-axis rotation rhythm and with connecting your strokes to that faster core rotation. This means that your arm motions will be faster as well. The challenge, as before, is to avoid letting your arms take over and set the rhythm. That is the job of your leg-driven core rotations. Increase the tempo only when you are able to maintain your posture, balance, and consistent rotation tempo while taking strokes and only when you are able to finish each set of strokes with a balanced tight line that needs no correcting.

 
焦点➤地铁
 

这个“管道”是一种心理意象，可以帮助你感知自己游泳或练习时所处的空间。目标是尽可能缩小身体在水中滑行的“管道”范围。当你以紧绷的姿势和完美的平衡进行LAR练习时，随着身体沿泳道旋转，你的肩膀会划出一个“管道”。你的头部、臀部和腿部都应该保持在这个“管道”内。如果你在进行完整划水动作时运用这种心理意象，那么只有你的手臂应该超出这个“管道”。如果腿部在踢腿时超出“管道”，虽然这会在一定程度上增加踢腿的推进力，但通常会增加阻力而不是推进力——这是一种效率低下的权衡。在某些练习中使用快速踢腿可以帮助你保持踢腿幅度更小，并始终保持在“管道”内。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ The Tube
 

The tube is a mental image that helps you become aware of the space through which you are swimming or drilling. The goal is to minimize the size of the tube your body slides through in the water. When you are doing the LAR drill with tight-line posture and perfect balance, your shoulders carve out a tube as you rotate down the lane. Your head, hips, and legs should all stay inside this tube. If you use this mental image when you are swimming full strokes, only your arms should stray outside this tube. If your legs move outside of the tube as they kick, although they somewhat increase the propulsive force of the kick, they generally add more drag than propulsion—an inefficient tradeoff. Using a fast kick during certain drills will help you keep your kicks smaller and inside the tube.

 
 
重点➤髋部踢腿
 

我们不仅关注你踢腿的幅度——也就是是否在泳圈内。我们还希望你使用正确的肌肉进行踢腿。人们在学习游泳时，往往会本能地用膝盖踢腿——通常是为了支撑下沉的臀部。但正确的做法是，每次踢腿都应该主要由臀部发力，膝盖在腿部向前踢出时略微弯曲以应对水的阻力。腿部回撤时，膝盖完全不能弯曲。你在垂直踢腿练习中已经练习过这一点，这些练习旨在培养正确的踢腿动作。你可能已经发现，如果用膝盖踢腿，在垂直踢腿练习中几乎不可能完成旋转动作。将这一点运用到你的游泳练习中非常重要。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Kick From Hips
 

We are not just interested in the size of your kick—i.e., keeping it inside the tube. We also want to use the correct muscles for kicking. People instinctively kick from their knees as they learn to swim—generally as an attempt to support sinking hips. Instead, each kick should originate predominantly from your hip, allowing the knee to yield slightly to the resistance of the water as the leg kicks forward. There should be no knee bend at all on the leg recovery. You’ve been practicing this in your vertical kicking drills, which encourage proper kicking motions. You’ve likely discovered that it is nearly impossible to drive rotation in the VKR drills if you kick from your knees. It is important to carry this focus point into your swimming.

提示：随着你对这些练习越来越熟练，你需要的休息时间也会减少。看看你能做到多短的休息时间——不一定非要在每次重复练习之间完全恢复。不过，重点仍然是动作的完美执行，所以如果你觉得需要更多休息才能发挥最佳水平，那就给自己额外的休息时间。始终尝试将你已掌握的练习技巧运用到你的完整泳姿中。

 
4
 
Beginning Stroke Integration
 

Training zone: Recovery and low aerobic

Target RPE range: 9 to 11

Target heart-rate range: 70 to 85% of SLTHR

Warm-Up
 

8 × 25 on :10R TS—alt 25 LAR, 25 SGND rt, 25 LAR, 25 SGND lft

4 × 25 on :15R—alt 25 SGB, 25 swim (focus: side skating and stroke count)

IHR or RPE

Main Set
 

4 × 75 on :20R—alt 25 SGNU good, 25 SGNU weak, 25 SGSS (focus: laser-beam rotation trigger)

4 × 25 SGSS on :15R—desc 1-4 (focus: downward angle arm extension)

2 × 25 cavort on :15R—body dolphin. Lying on your belly in the pool, arms extended in front of you, alternate pressing your chest, and then your hips, toward the bottom of the pool. Let your legs transmit that pulse to the water. This is a full-body undulation; it is not kicking with your legs. (Hint: A dolphin is one big swimming muscle with no legs.) Keep your head in tight-line position, and lift it as little as possible when you breathe. Take no strokes. Use fins for this cavort.

2 × 25 swim on :15R BOYLFS—second one faster (focus: over the keg and stroke count)

IHR or RPE

6 × :20 VKR on :15R—odd: hands on your chest; even: hands out of the water (focus: kick from hips)

Cool-Down
 

6 × 25 on :15R TS—alt 25 SGSS, 25 swim (focus: over the keg and the tube) IHR or RPE

Total distance: 1,100 (includes estimated equivalent for VKR)

Comments: As you become more skilled at these drills, you should need less rest. See how little rest you can get away with—not necessarily recovering completely between repeats. The focus is still on flawless execution, though, so if you feel that you need more rest for proper performance, then take the extra time to get it. Always try to apply an aspect of a drill you have mastered to your full-stroke swimming.

2 × 25 米游泳，每分钟 10 次划水，1 次以 NSPL 强度游，1 次以 -2SPL 强度游（重点：换手和划水次数）

IHR 或 RPE

总距离：1,150（包括VKR的估计等效距离）

备注：如果您感到呼吸困难或觉得需要更多休息才能更好地完成动作，请比建议的休息时间更长一些。您在哪些练习中使用了短鳍或赤脚？在快速LAR（快速反脚划水）环节，您需要比进行慢速LAR时拉紧绳索。

笔画整合与旋转连接

 

训练区：恢复期和低强度有氧运动

目标RPE范围：9至11

目标心率范围：SLTHR 的 70% 至 85%。

热身
 

4 × 25 组，每组 10 分钟交替进行：25 次右脚蹬地，25 次左脚蹬地，25 次 3 脚蹬，25 次游泳（重点：下坡游泳）

4 × 25 on :10R TS —alt 25 SGND weak, 25 SGSS, 25 MR1S, 25 swim (focus: tight line)

4 × 25 :10R TS —交替 25 3S&G、25 5S&G、25 MR1S、25 游泳（重点：完成你的划水动作）

IHR 或 RPE

主套装
 

2 × 25 游泳 :10R（重点：木偶恢复和激光束旋转触发）

2 × 50 on :15R—alt 25 3S&G, 25 MR1S (focus: red dom)

2 × 25 组，每组 15 分钟——交替进行 25 分钟 MR1S 和 25 分钟 MR2S（重点：利用臀部的浮力和踢腿）

4 × 75 上：15R TS —交替 25 MR1S、25 MR2S、25 游泳（重点：中立肩部）

IHR 或 RPE

2 × 25 游泳 :10R BOYLFS（重点：换手和绷紧鱼线）

2 × 25 卡波特泳姿：10R——双臂伸展式慢速海豚式。仰卧，双臂伸向泳池远端，进行慢速海豚式划水。双臂同时划水，然后向上伸直，越过头顶，回到水中。第一个来回尝试每次划水循环做一次海豚式脉冲，第二个来回尝试每次划水循环做两次海豚式脉冲。使用脚蹼会有很大帮助。

4 × :20 VKR，每组间隔 :20R——双手放在胸前。踢腿速度要足够快，以抬起并保持肩膀离开水面。

IHR 或 RPE

1 × 50 TS —alt 25 LAR, 25 MR3S（重点：绷紧钓线和浮标压力）

冷却
 

6 × 25 :10R TS —交替 25 MR1S、25 3S&G、25 游泳（重点：快速扭动臀部并完成划水动作）

备注：练习时，要像认真对待正式训练一样，认真对待每一个花式动作。你是否重新阅读过训练动作和重点的说明？这样做有助于你更好地理解它们。在高强度垂直膝关节旋转（VKR）训练中，注意不要试图通过耸肩来辅助旋转。保持身体紧绷，让肩膀自然地跟随下半身的动作。

Stroke Integration and Rotation Connection

 

Training zone: Recovery and low aerobic

Target RPE range: 9 to 11

Target heart-rate range: 70 to 85% of SLTHR

Warm-Up
 

4 × 25 on :10R—alt 25 SGB rt, 25 SGB lft, 25 3S&G, 25 swim (focus: downhill swimming)

4 × 25 on :10R TS—alt 25 SGND weak, 25 SGSS, 25 MR1S, 25 swim (focus: tight line)

4 × 25 on :10R TS—alt 25 3S&G, 25 5S&G, 25 MR1S, 25 swim (focus: finish your strokes)

IHR or RPE

Main Set
 

2 × 25 swim on :10R (focus: marionette recovery and laser-beam rotation trigger)

2 × 50 on :15R—alt 25 3S&G, 25 MR1S (focus: red dot)

2 × 25 on :15R—alt 25 MR1S, 25 MR2S (focus: buoy pressure and kick from hips)

4 × 75 on :15R TS—alt 25 MR1S, 25 MR2S, 25 swim (focus: neutral shoulder)

IHR or RPE

2 × 25 swim on :10R BOYLFS (focus: hand swapping and tight line)

2 × 25 cavort on :10R—double-overarm lollygag. A slow-body dolphin, performed on your back, with your arms extended toward the far end of the pool. Take a stroke with both arms at the same time, and then recover them straight up, over your head, and back into the water. Try it with one dolphin pulse per stroke cycle on the first length, then two dolphin pulses per stroke cycle on the second length. Fins help greatly.

4 × :20 VKR on :20R—hands on your chest. Kick fast enough to raise and keep your shoulders out of the water.

IHR or RPE

1 × 50 TS—alt 25 LAR, 25 MR3S (focus: tight line and buoy pressure)

Cool-Down
 

6 × 25 on :10R TS—alt 25 MR1S, 25 3S&G, 25 swim (focus: snappy hips and finish your strokes)

IHR or RPE

Total distance: 1,200 (includes estimated equivalent for VKR)

Comments: Put as much focus into smoothly executing cavorts as you put into doing the serious stuff. Have you reread the descriptions of the drills and focus points? Doing so will improve your understanding of them. On the higher-intensity VKR drill, be careful not to try to help the rotation by throwing your shoulders. Your tight line should simply allow them to go along with what the lower body is doing.

钻探回顾

 

训练区：恢复期和低强度有氧运动

主套装
 

2 × 75 on :15R TS —alt 25 SGND, 25 BBR, 25 SGSS (focus: red dot)

2 × 75 分钟，每组 30分钟，交替进行 25 分钟 3 次划船和划船练习，25 分钟 5 次划船和划船练习，25 分钟游泳（重点：换手）。心率或主观疲劳程度 (RPE) 测量。

4 × 25 分钟，每组 10 分钟——交替进行 25 分钟 MR1S、25 分钟 MR2S、25 分钟 MR3S、25 分钟游泳（重点：用臀部踢腿）

Drill Review

 

Training zone: Recovery and low aerobic

Target RPE range: 9 to 11

Target heart-rate range: 70 to 85% of SLTHR

Warm-Up
 

4 × 25 on :10R—alt 25 FB, 25 BB, 25 SGNU rt, 25 SGNU lft

4 × 50 on :15R—alt 25 SGB weak, 25 SGB good (focus: buoy pressure)

IHR or RPE

Main Set
 

2 × 75 on :15R TS—alt 25 SGND, 25 BBR, 25 SGSS (focus: red dot)

2 × 75 on :30R TS—alt 25 3S&G, 25 5S&G, 25 swim (focus: hand swapping) IHR or RPE

4 × 25 on :10R—alt 25 MR1S, 25 MR2S, 25 MR3S, 25 swim (focus: kick from your hips)

2 × 25 swim on :05R as 25 @ NSPL, 25 @ -2SPL (focus: downhill swimming and the tube)

加快速度

 

训练区：恢复期和低强度有氧运动

目标RPE范围：9至11

目标心率范围：SLTHR 的 70% 至 85%。

热身
 

6 × 25，每组 10 次循环——交替进行 25 次 LAR，25 次 SGSS。在完成整组动作的过程中逐渐加快速度。

1 × 100 米，其中 50 米以 NSPL 强度游泳，25 米以较弱的 SGB 强度游泳，25 米以与前 50 米相同的 SPL 强度快速游泳。

IHR 或 RPE

主套装
 

4 × 25 游泳，每分钟 15 分钟，TS—描述 1-4（重点：臀部灵活，泳姿紧绷）

2 × 75 on :15R TS —alt 25 MR1S, 25 MR2S, 25 MR3S (重点：从髋部踢腿)

2 × 75 on :15R TS —alt 25 SGSS, 25 3S&G, 25 swim fast (focus: hand swapping)

3 × 50 SGB 于 :10R 描述 1-3—交替 25 弱，25 好

IHR 或 RPE

6 × 25 :15R—奇数：SGB 或 SGSS；偶数：快速游泳（重点：绷紧鱼线）

4 × :30 VKR :15R—1：双手放在胸前；2：双手离开水面；3：双手放在胸前；4：双手放在头顶

1 × 50 米旋转练习——1/1 长轴组合（重点：紧贴泳道线和红点）。先划一次自由泳，再划一次仰泳，再划一次自由泳，最后再划一次仰泳。重复此循环，游完泳池长度。如果练习正确，你会沿着泳道呈螺旋状游动。游到第二个长度时，改变旋转方向。

1 × :30 VKR 处于完全流线型位置（焦点：紧绷的线条和管子）

IHR 或 RPE

2 × 50 米游泳，速度较快：20R BOYLFS，25 米 @ NSPL，25 米 @ -1SPL（焦点：管子）

IHR 或 RPE

冷却
 

3 × 50，每组 10 分钟——交替进行 25 分钟 SGB 轻柔划水，25 分钟游泳（重点：浮力压力和手臂向下伸展的角度）

IHR 或 RPE

总距离：1300（包括VKR的估计等效距离）

评论：你应该注意到，一些技巧在你游得更快的时候开始显现出来。如果需要，在快速游完后多休息一会儿。试着找出你在弱侧练习中与强侧练习不同的地方，看看是什么导致你无法像在强侧那样出色地完成练习。通常是姿势、头部位置、浮力压力或这几方面因素的组合出了问题。

中风计数意识

第九章
 
第三级：全泳姿游泳训练
 

在第二阶段，您继续专注于学习和精进技能训练，并以训练的形式进行。游泳距离限制在每次训练总距离的30%以内。如果您已经完成第二阶段的训练几次，并且大部分时间都能将心率保持在目标范围内（快速游泳或垂直踢腿时除外），那么就可以进入第三阶段了。

In level 2, you continued to focus on learning and refining skill drills in a workout format. The amount of swimming was restricted to no more than 30 percent of the distance of any practice. If you have cycled through the level 2 practices a couple of times and can stay within your target heart-rate range most of the time (except during a fast swim or during vertical kicking), it is time to move on to level 3.

训练将增加全泳姿练习，但仍会包含30%至50%的技巧练习。每次训练时长仍保持在30至40分钟，但水平更高的游泳者可以在更短的时间内完成。训练强度将会增加，具体方式包括减少休息时间、提高速度或两者兼而有之。因此，您的总游泳距离将比二级训练更长。您会注意到，目标心率范围已提高至标准低强度心率（SLTHR）的80%至95%，目标主观运动强度（RPE）范围已提高至11至14（轻度至略微吃力）。通常情况下，在三级训练的每次主要训练组中，您应始终保持这些目标心率范围——但与之前一样，训练过程中偶尔会出现心率短暂高于这些范围的情况。如果您需要延长或缩短建议的休息时间，请自行调整。

Practices will involve more full-stroke swimming but will still include anywhere from 30 to 50 percent skill drills. The duration of these practices will remain in the 30- to 40-minute range, though more accomplished swimmers will complete them in less time. The intensity will increase, either by reducing rest, increasing speed, or both. Therefore, the total distance you cover will be greater than in level 2. You will note that the target heart-rate range has increased to 80 to 95 percent of SLTHR and that the target-RPE range has moved up to 11 to 14 (light to somewhat hard). In general, you should stay within those target ranges throughout the main set of each of the level 3 workouts—though, as before, there will be instances when the activity will get your heart rate above those ranges for short periods. If you need to lengthen or shorten the amount of rest that is suggested, do so.

虽然我鼓励你在练习中用训练脚蹼练习一些你还不熟练的动作，但你至少应该已经开始在大部分练习中使用短鳍脚蹼了。接下来的练习规则会告诉你何时需要使用脚蹼。除非必要，否则不要使用脚蹼，除非练习规则明确要求使用。

Although I encourage you to use training fins for drills that you are not yet comfortable with, you should have at least moved on to using short-blade fins for most of them. The upcoming practice notation will tell you when to use fins. Unless you need them, do not use fins unless the practice notation calls for them.

阅读训练计划

Reading the Workouts

 

本节介绍一些新的符号快捷方式。我们提供器材、练习和重点训练选项，旨在丰富您的训练内容。这些选项并非旨在帮助您逃避不喜欢的技能、练习和重点训练。恰恰相反，您应该多练习那些让您感到吃力的技能和练习，因为它们通常能帮助您发现游泳方面的不足。

This section introduces some new notation shortcuts. Equipment, drill, and focus options and choices are offered in order to increase variety in your training. They are not intended to help you avoid the skills, drills, and foci you don’t like. If anything, you should do more of the skills and drills that give you trouble, since they usually alert you to something that is lacking in your swimming.

 

鳍片，SBFins

Fins, SBFins

 

“Fins”表示您可以使用任何类型的脚蹼。“SBFins”表示您应该使用短叶脚蹼。

Fins means that you should use fins of any type. SBFins means that you should use short-blade fins.

 

FinsOpt、SBFinsOpt、TSOpt

Opt means that you should feel free to use the specified piece of equipment, or not, as you choose.

You choose the rotation-connection drill (MR3S and its lead-up drills, or 3R3S, which you’ll read about shortly).

 

Dchoice，Dmix

Dchoice, Dmix

 

Dchoice指的是训练选择。这意味着你可以替换我展示的任何技能训练。Dmix指的是你可以选择并混合多种训练（例如：完成一次 FB 训练、一次 SGB 训练和两次 3S&G 训练）。

Dchoice means drill choice. This means that you may substitute any skill drill I have presented. Dmix means that you may choose and mix more than one drill (example: completing one length of FB, one length of SGB, and two lengths of 3S&G).

 

焦点：选择

Focus: choice

 

这意味着您可以替换我提出的任何重点。

This means that you may substitute any of the focus points I have presented.

 

SLSSS

SLSSS

 

这意味着超低频慢速隐蔽游泳。其目标是以极低的划水次数游泳，每次划水动作都极其缓慢，尽可能减少噪音，并尽可能减少对水面的扰动。超低频慢速隐蔽游泳会暴露你在姿势、平衡和动作技巧方面的不足。如果你无法在以极慢的节奏完成完整划水动作的同时保持完美的平衡和协调，那么你需要努力弥补这些不足。较慢的节奏能够精准地揭示这些不足之处。如果你在划水过程中感到需要加快速度，那么要么你失去了平衡，要么你只是在忽略了划水过程中姿势、平衡和/或位置存在问题的环节。噪音、水花和水面扰动都表明你正在将宝贵的动能浪费在水中。

This means super-low-and-slow stealth swimming. The objectives are to swim at a super-low stroke count, to use super-slow movement through each stroke cycle, to make as little noise as possible, and to disturb the surface as little as possible. SLSSS exposes the gaps in your posture, balance, and motion skills. If you are unable to maintain perfect balance and coordination while taking full strokes at very slow tempos, then you need to work to bridge those gaps. Slower tempos expose precisely where the gaps are. If you feel the need to hurry up during any part of the stroke, you are either losing balance or are simply glossing past a portion of the stroke in which posture, balance, and/ or position are iffy. Noise, chop, and wake signal that you are losing precious kinetic energy to the water.

 

8分钟内完成50秒的IHR或RPE训练（保持在目标范围内）

8-minute set of 50s on IHR or RPE (stay in target range)

 

游50米，然后测量心率（IHR）或主观疲劳程度（RPE）。一旦确定了心率或主观疲劳程度，立即再游50米，然后再次测量心率或主观疲劳程度。重复此过程8分钟。如果在时间结束前还有时间再游50米，那就游完这50米。这组练习的最后一步是，以保持心率或主观疲劳程度在练习目标范围内的速度游泳。

Swim a 50, then take an IHR or RPE. As soon as you determine the IHR or RPE, swim another 50, and then take another IHR or RPE. Repeat this pattern for 8 minutes. If you have time to start another 50 before time expires, then do the whole 50. On this set, the final instruction is to swim at a pace that keeps your IHR or RPE in the target range indicated for the practice.

 

2 × 75米游泳——交替进行25次握拳、25次握手指、25次握手。

2 × 75 swim—alt 25 fists, 25 fingers, 25 hands

 

握拳游泳是指将双手握成拳头游泳。握拳游泳通过大幅降低手部无数神经末梢的感知冲动，帮助你学会如何用手臂而不是你那微弱的双手来划水。你会更加敏锐地感知手臂（尤其是前臂）所感受到的压力和水流。随着前臂敏感度的提高，你可以更精准地控制手臂，使其在水中发挥最佳抓水效果。

Fists means to ball your hands into fists and swim. Fist swimming, by dramatically decreasing the sensory impulses from the bazillions of nerve endings in your hands, helps you figure out how to use your arms, rather than your puny hands, as your paddles. You become much more aware of the pressure and flow that your arms—especially your forearms—experience. As the sensitivity in your forearms increases, you can more accurately move them to where they most effectively hold onto the water.

“手指”指的是半握拳。张开小指一侧的三根手指（你的手大致呈“OK”字形）。这是练习张开手掌游泳的基础。游泳时，记住你的前臂是划水动作中最主要、最有力的部分。

Fingers simply refers to a partial fist. Open the three fingers on the pinkie side of the hand (you’ll be holding your hand roughly in the “OK” position). This is a stepping-stone to swimming with open hands. As you swim, remember that your forearms are the largest, most predominant part of your paddle.

最重要的是，当你松开手指，恢复正常张开手掌游泳时会发生什么。你可能会发现，经过大量的握拳游泳练习后，最初几趟张开手掌游泳的划水次数会比平时张开手掌游泳时显著减少。握拳游泳的意识、敏感度和技巧会保留下来，因为你自由的双手就像是你新发现并变得更加敏感的前臂的延伸。你会感觉划水幅度更大，每次划水都能游得更远，这当然是游得更快的关键（更不用说看起来更像个游泳高手了）。但你很快就会恢复到只用双手和旧动作的习惯——除非你定期进行足够的握拳游泳练习，从而养成新的、更有效的习惯。

What matters most is what happens once you release your fingers and return to normal swimming with your hands open. You will probably find that after a lot of fist swimming, the first few lengths you swim with open hands will be at significantly lower stroke counts than you normally swim with open hands. The awareness, sensitivity, and technique of fist swimming will remain with you as your unfettered hands act as an extension of your newly discovered and sensitized forearms. Your paddles will feel big and you will swim farther with every stroke, which, of course, is the primary ingredient of faster swimming (not to mention of simply looking more like an accomplished swimmer). But you will soon return to the habit of using only your hands and your old motions—unless, of course, you do enough fist swimming on a regular basis to create new, more effective habits.

 

4 × 50 米，每组游 2 分钟，快速游完。

4 × 50 swim fast on 2:00

 

你可能经常看到这样的训练计划表，例如“4 × 50 米游泳，每组 20 分钟休息”，其中每组 50 米游泳后都有指定的休息时间。从这个级别开始，你会看到一种叫做间歇训练法的训练计划表。训练间歇是指你进行一项训练活动，然后休息一段时间，之后再重复这项训练活动的特定时间。

You are used to seeing exercises listed in the form of, for example, “4 × 50 swim on :20R,” where a specified amount of rest follows each repeat. Beginning in this level, you will see exercises listed in a format called interval notation. A training interval is a specified time during which you perform an activity and get some rest before repeating the activity.

“4 × 50 米快速游泳，每 2 分钟一组”是指快速游完四个 50 米，每个 50 米之间间隔两分钟。这被称为两分钟间隔游泳。如果你游完一个 50 米用时 1 分 15 秒，那么你需要休息 45 秒再开始下一个 50 米。如果你游完一个 50 米只用了 55 秒，那么你需要休息 1 分 5 秒。整组训练需要 8 分钟。需要说明的是，像这样长时间的休息，指的是积极休息——轻松游泳或进行一些练习、踩水、漂浮或其他低强度水中运动。保持运动有助于加快恢复。

4 × 50 swim fast on 2:00means to swim four 50s fast with two minutes between the beginning of one 50 and the beginning of the next. This is referred to as swimming on a 2-minute interval. If it takes you 1:15 to swim a 50, then you would rest for 45 seconds before beginning the next 50. If it takes you only 55 seconds to swim a 50, then you’d rest for 1 minute and 5 seconds. The whole set would take 8 minutes. I should specify that with long rests like this, I mean active rest—easy swimming or drilling, treading water, bobbing, or other low-intensity water exercises. Keep moving and you’ll speed recovery.

 

4 × 50 SGolf 于 1:45

4 × 50 SGolf on 1:45

 

以1分45秒的间隔进行四次50米游泳高尔夫练习。每次50米，记录划水次数，并在计时器上记录游泳时间，然后利用休息时间的一部分来计算本次游泳高尔夫的得分。每次游泳高尔夫练习的目标都是尽可能降低得分。（有关游泳高尔夫的详细说明，请参见第三章第23页。）

Swim four 50s SGolf on a 1:45 interval. For each 50, count the total number of strokes you take, note your elapsed swim time on the clock, and use part of the rest period to compute your swimming golf score for the swim. The goal of any SGolf set is to lower your score. (See chapter 3, p. 23 for a detailed description of swimming golf.)

 

4 × 50 SGolf，每分钟 1:45（或 :45RMin）

4 × 50 SGolf on 1:45 (or :45RMin)

 

以 1 分 45 秒的间隔游四圈 50 米标准高尔夫泳。括号内为速度较慢的游泳者的替代方案。45秒 RMin表示休息时间至少应为45 秒。如果 1 分 45 秒的间隔无法保证至少 45 秒的休息时间，则应使用更长的间隔。再次强调，较长的休息时间应为积极休息。

Swim four 50s SGolf on a 1:45 interval. In parenthesis is an alternative for slower swimmers. :45RMin means that you should rest for at least 45 seconds. If a 1:45 interval doesn’t allow for at least 45 seconds of rest, then use a longer interval that does. Again, long rest periods should be active rest.

继续技术教育

Continuing Technique Education

 

在上一阶段，MR3S训练方法教你如何在一系列核心旋转动作中穿插一些划水和呼吸。这一阶段，我们将进一步优化这一过程，让你在练习的同时尽可能接近完整的划水动作。我还会加入一些更高级的训练要点，并探讨如何才能游得更快。

In the previous level, the MR3S drill progression taught you to occasionally mix a few strokes and breaths into a long series of core rotations. Here we will refine that process in order to bring you as close as possible to full-stroke swimming while still drilling. I also will add some more advanced focus points, and I will discuss how you should think about swimming faster.

三圈三划（3R3S）

Three Rotations, Three Strokes (3R3S)

 
这第二套旋转连接练习是 MR3S 练习的延伸。每组击球之间只需进行三次旋转。即使您已在二级练习中练习过 MR3S 练习，在继续学习这套练习之前，建议您重新阅读 MR3S 练习的学习步骤。以下是 3R3S 的学习步骤：

1. 首先进行MR3S练习，在每个三划循环的第二次划桨时吸气，并在划桨组间进行多次旋转。记住，转身吸气时，头部保持的深度要适中。目标是头部完全不抬（记住红点瞄准点），避免打乱旋转的节奏，并保持姿势和平衡。如果感觉需要更多空气，可以在每次划桨组间的旋转过程中额外吸气一次。

1. Start by doing the MR3S drill, taking a breath on the second stroke of each three-stroke cycle and making many rotations between sets of strokes. Remember to be risky as to how deep you keep your head when you turn for a breath. The goals are to have zero head lift (remember the red-dot focus point), to avoid introducing a hitch into the rhythm of rotations, and to maintain your posture and balance. If you find that you need more air, you may add an additional breath during the rotations that occur between each set of strokes.

2. 当你熟练掌握第一步后，就可以尝试在每个划水周期中吸两口气，即在第一和第三次划水时吸气。根据你所需的空气量，你应该能够轻松地在仅在第二次划水时吸气和在第一和第三次划水时吸气之间切换，然后再切换回仅在第二次划水时吸气。

2. Once you are comfortable with step 1, you can switch to taking two breaths in each cycle by breathing on the first and third strokes. Depending on how much air you need, you will want to be able to switch easily from breathing on the second stroke only to breathing on the first and third strokes and then back to breathing on the second stroke only.

3. 当你逐渐适应在每组三次划水之间呼吸后，减少每组划水之间的旋转次数。在最终的练习中，我们希望每组划水之间只进行三次长轴旋转，并且只在划水期间呼吸。

3. As you become comfortable with breathing during each set of three strokes, make fewer rotations between each set. In the finished form of the drill, we want to make only three long-axis rotations between each set of strokes, and we want to breathe only during the sets of strokes.

 

3R3S练习方法如下：以流线型姿势蹬墙，保持身体紧绷。先做三次不划水的长轴旋转，然后划水旋转三次，再做三次不划水的旋转，再划水旋转三次，以此类推，所有呼吸都在划水过程中完成。由于每组三划水需要四次旋转，且在下一组划水之前还有三次旋转，因此整个模式每七次旋转重复一次。这意味着每组划水都从与上一组相反的手臂开始。和之前一样，目标是将划水（和呼吸）无缝地融入到长轴旋转中。如果我只观察你的腿、臀部和躯干，我应该无法分辨你是在单纯旋转还是在划水旋转。

So the 3R3S drill goes as follows: Push off the wall in a streamline position with tight-line posture. Do three long-axis rotations without strokes, take three strokes with rotations, do three more rotations without strokes, take three more strokes with rotations, and so on, with all your breaths coming during the strokes. Since each cycle of three strokes requires four rotations and since there are three more rotations before the next set of strokes, the entire pattern repeats every seven rotations. This means that each set of strokes begins with the opposite arm from the previous set. As before, the goal is to seamlessly add strokes (and breaths) to your long-axis rotations. If I were to watch just your legs, hips, and torso as you do this drill, I should not be able to tell when you are just rotating and when you are rotating with strokes.

在训练说明中，当 3R3S 与TS一起出现时，由于无需转头呼吸，练习会更简单。在进行 3R3S 的进阶训练时，我建议您先用普通脚蹼练习每个步骤，直到能够熟练完成为止。然后逐渐过渡到短脚蹼，最后再赤脚。

In the workout descriptions, when 3R3S appears with TS, the drill is simpler since you don’t have to turn your head to breathe. When you move through this progression to 3R3S, I suggest that you do each step with regular fins until you can do the step well. Then wean yourself first to short fins and then to bare feet.

反馈工具

Feedback Tools

 

• 将你的旋转节奏与节奏提示器（或脑海中一段节奏鲜明的熟悉旋律）相匹配，可以帮助你判断在仅旋转和旋转加击打之间切换时，你的节奏是否发生了变化。目标是在整个过程中保持不间断的旋转节奏（即使在呼吸时头部随身体转动）。

• Matching your rotation tempo to a tempo beeper (or to a familiar tune with a distinctive beat in your head) can help you determine whether you are changing tempo as you switch back and forth between rotations only and rotations with strokes. The goal is to have an uninterrupted rotation tempo throughout (even while letting your head turn with your body to breathe).

• 使用脸颊和脸颊的焦点来判断你的肤色是否平衡。

• Use the patches-and-cheeks focus point to determine whether you are balanced.

 

做个小实验

Experiment a Bit

 

当你能够以轻松的节奏掌握3R3S练习后，可以尝试加快长轴旋转的节奏。然后将你的划水动作与这种更快的核心旋转节奏结合起来。由于核心旋转节奏加快，你的手臂动作也会随之加快。但如果你发现是手臂而不是腿部驱动的核心旋转带动了节奏，那么就放慢速度，找到一个你能用旋转控制的节奏。此外，随着你3R3S练习的进步，你可以增加每组划水的次数，从而有效地将其转化为3R5S或3R7S练习，这样你就可以在每组划水期间进行更多次的呼吸。只有当你能够在划水和呼吸的同时保持姿势、平衡和旋转节奏，并且能够在每组划水结束后保持完全平衡、紧凑的姿势，无需任何调整时，才能增加划水次数。

After you have mastered 3R3S at an easy tempo, experiment with setting a faster long-axis rotation rhythm. Then connect your strokes to that faster core rotation. Your arm motions will be faster as a result of the faster core-rotation tempo. But if you find your arms setting the rhythm instead of your leg-driven core rotations, then slow down to a tempo that you can control with your rotations. Also, as you improve at the 3R3S drill, you can take more strokes in each set of strokes, effectively turning this into a 3R5S or 3R7S drill in which you can take more breaths during each set of strokes. Increase the number of strokes only if you are able to maintain your posture, balance, and rotation tempo as you take strokes and breaths and only if you can finish each set of strokes in a fully balanced tight line that needs no correction.

 
重点➤手与髋的连接
 

你可能还记得第五章（你的游泳机器，第48至50页）中提到，真正高效游泳的动力源泉在于腿部和核心肌群，而非手臂。高水平游泳者主要用手臂将核心肌群旋转产生的能量传递到水中。一个有效的想象是，你的手和髋部之间存在着内在的联系。实际上，你的右手通过紧绷的姿势和划水动作与右髋部紧密相连。你的左髋部和左手也以类似的方式连接在一起。我们希望利用这些连接，为身体一侧的划水提供动力，同时驱动另一侧的入水和伸展动作。

划水与髋部连接：如果您练习的是前向划水，当另一只手臂向前划水入水时，您的一只手臂会略微向下伸入水中。就在划水手越过头部并完成旋转动作的瞬间，双腿开始带动身体旋转。随着髋部和核心开始旋转，您应该能感觉到肌肉的张力将伸入水中的手臂向后拉，就像您伸过桶身完成划水动作一样。只有当您的引导臂完全越过桶身，肘部接近水面，前臂几乎垂直时，这只手臂和肩膀才应该施加一些向后的划水力量。手臂和肩膀应该只对桨施加足够的压力，以便在髋部和身体旋转完成的瞬间完成划水动作。

你应该能感受到旋转的髋部带动划水手在整个划水过程中保持内在的连接。如果过早开始划水，你将感受不到这种连接——最终大部分力量会落在你的肩膀上（这类似于棒球投手先挥动手臂，然后转动髋部）。如果你游泳时身体僵硬，而不是保持核心肌群的紧绷，你就无法有效地控制划水。如果你用手臂和肩膀肌肉对桨施加过大的压力，划水动作就会先于核心旋转完成，导致你无法有效地控制划水。然而，保持内在的连接感，可以让大部分作用于桨的力量来自你的核心旋转。

入水手臂与髋部的连接你还需要保持入水手臂与其髋部之间的连接。从恢复的手臂越过头部并开始向即将刺入水面的位置移动的那一刻起，你应该感觉到手臂的伸展是由于核心的旋转，而不是仅仅从肩膀向前刺出。手臂的前伸始于核心旋转开始之时，也止于核心旋转结束之时。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Hand and Hip Connection
 

You might recall from chapter 5 (Your Swimming Machine, pages 48 to 50) that the engine that drives truly effective swimming is in the legs and the core, not the arms. Highly effective swimmers use their arms primarily to transmit energy, which is generated by core rotation, to the water. An effective mental image is that of an internal connection between your hand and your hip. In reality, your right hand is firmly connected to your right hip via the tension of your tight-line posture and paddle linkage. Your left hip and hand are similarly connected. We want to exploit those connections in order to power the stroke on one side of your body and, at the same time, to drive the entry and extension on the other side.

Stroke and Hip Connection If you are practicing front-quadrant swimming, you have one arm extended underwater at a slightly downward angle as your recovering arm moves forward to enter the water. Just after the recovering hand passes your head and then passes through the laser-beam rotation trigger, the legs initiate body rotation. As your hips and core begin to rotate, you should feel your tight-line tension tugging your extended arm back just as you reach over the keg to make your catch. Only once your lead arm is fully over the barrel, with your elbow close to the surface of the water and your forearm nearly vertical, should that arm and shoulder add some backward stroking force of their own. The arm and shoulder should put only enough pressure on your paddle to complete the stroke at the same instant that the hip-and-body rotation finishes.

You should feel the internal connection of the rotating hip pulling the stroking hand throughout the stroke. Start stroking too early and you will feel no connection—and your shoulders will end up doing most of the work (an analogous scenario would be of a baseball pitcher making his arm motion first and then turning his hips). If you swim schlumpy instead of using a tight internal-core line, you will have no effective connection. If you put too much pressure on the paddle with your arm and shoulder muscles, the stroke will get ahead of and finish before the core rotation, and you will not have a working connection. Maintaining a feeling of internal connection, however, allows most of the force that you apply to the paddle to come from your core-rotation engine.

Entering Arm and Hip Connection You also want to maintain a connection between the entering arm and its hip. From the moment the recovering arm passes the head and begins to move toward the spot where it will pierce the surface, you should feel as though the arm is extending as a result of the core’s rotation, rather than just stabbing the hand forward from the shoulder. The forward extension of the arm begins as the core’s rotation begins, and it ends as the rotation ends.

 
 
重点➤无重力手臂
 

侧身呼吸时，另一侧的手臂应保持向前伸展，略微向下倾斜。除非养成良好的习惯，否则很容易出现以下两种情况：要么用伸展的手臂向下推水，要么过早地开始下一次划水。正确的做法是，在整个吸气过程中，伸展的手臂应保持自然伸展的状态。这样，当你开始下一个旋转动作（即吸完一口气后）时，手臂就能处于合适的位置，从而开始下一次划水。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Weightless Arm
 

When breathing to one side, you want the arm on your other side to remain extended in front of you at a slightly downward angle. The tendency, unless you have ingrained good habits, is either to push down on the water with the extended arm or to start the next stroke too early. Instead, throughout your inhalation, the extended arm should remain weightlessly extended. This way, it will be in the right place to start the next stroke as you begin the next rotation (which comes after you’ve taken a full breath of air).

 
 
重点➤隐身
 

游泳时，你能做到多安静，对水面的扰动能做到多小？一位技术娴熟的游泳者以轻松的速度游动时，应该能将水面产生的尾流控制在极小的范围内，使其不会越过泳道线进入相邻泳道。噪音、波浪和尾流都会将宝贵的动能传递给水。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Stealth
 

How quiet can you be and how little can you disturb the water as you swim? A highly skilled swimmer swimming at an easy pace should be able to make a wake so small that it does not move past the wave-eating lane lines into adjacent lanes. Noise, chop, and wake give up precious kinetic energy to the water.

 
 
重点➤双拍踢腿
 

到目前为止，我们关于游泳踢腿的讨论都集中在六拍踢腿上——每次划水三次踢腿，其中一次踢腿带动身体旋转，紧接着两次打水踢腿；另一次踢腿带动身体旋转，完成下一次划水；最后两次打水踢腿完成一个完整的两划水循环。旋转踢腿之间的打水踢腿有两个可能的作用。对于平衡感较差的游泳者来说，打水踢腿可以防止臀部和腿部下沉。对于平衡感良好的游泳者来说，打水踢腿可以提供类似快艇的直接推进力。

到了现在，作为一名姿势良好、平衡感强的游泳者，前一点对你来说应该已经无关紧要了。然而，第二点值得进一步探讨。即使是最优秀的游泳者，通过踢腿来产生这种直接推进力也需要消耗大量能量，而速度提升却微乎其微（甚至没有）。

以旋转为主的踢腿方式并不能像自由泳踢腿那样有效地推进身体前进。如果运用得当，低强度的旋转踢腿配合手臂划水节奏，其产生的推进力将远超任何形式的自由泳踢腿，而且能量消耗也更少。因此，大多数长距离游泳运动员选择两拍踢腿——每次旋转和手臂划水配合一次踢腿。这种踢腿方式的唯一目的在于带动核心和身体的节奏性旋转。良好的两拍踢腿可能感觉不像普通的踢腿。许多游泳运动员表示，他们感觉自己是在用腿部力量交替地移动臀部，而不是在进行有意识的踢腿动作。

对一些人来说，从六拍打腿切换到两拍打腿很简单，只需在每次旋转打腿之间放弃额外的打水动作即可。而对另一些人来说，最好的方法是先完全不打腿，然后再逐渐增加驱动旋转所需的单拍打腿。无论哪种情况，专注于之前练习中培养的手部入水到打腿的协调性，都是学习和充分利用两拍打腿的关键。一旦你能够熟练地使用两拍的、仅用于旋转的打腿方式而不失去平衡，你可能会发现自己再也不需要回到六拍打腿了。

 
FOCUS POINT ➤ Two-Beat Kick
 

Until now, all of our discussion on kicking while swimming has been about six-beat kicking—three kicks per stroke, in which one kick rotates your body as you take a stroke and two flutter-kick beats follow; another kick rotates you back as you take the next stroke; and two more flutter-kick beats complete a cycle of two strokes. There are two possible purposes for those flutter kicks between the rotation kicks. For poorly balanced swimmers, flutter kicks prevent the hips and legs from sinking. For well-balanced swimmers, they provide direct motorboat, push-you-forward-style propulsion.

By now, as a well-postured, well-balanced swimmer, the former point should be moot for you. The second point, however, warrants further inspection. Kicking in order to produce this type of direct propulsion, even when done by the most accomplished swimmers, requires a lot of energy for a small (or zero) return in extra speed.

Kicks that primarily rotate you do not propel you forward in the same way that flutter kicks do. Used correctly, low-intensity rotation kicks properly timed with your arm strokes will indirectly net you far more propulsion than any amount of motorboat flutter kicking will—and with a much smaller energy expenditure. For this reason, most distance swimmers opt for a two-beat kick—one kick beat for each rotation and arm stroke. The only purpose of these kicks is to drive the rhythmic core-body rotation. A good two-beat kick may not feel like normal kicking. Many swimmers say they feel like they are using the legs to alternately shift the hips around the core as opposed to making deliberate kicking motions.

Switching from six-beat to two-beat timing is, for some, as simple as just saying no to the extra flutter kicks between each rotation kick. For others, switching is best accomplished by swimming at first with no kick whatsoever, then adding only the single-kick beats needed to drive the rotations. In either case, focusing on the hand-entry-to-kick coordination that you developed in earlier drills will be a key to learning and getting the most from a two-beat kick. Once you become comfortable with using two-beat, rotation-only kicking without losing your balance, you may find that you never need to go back to six-beat kicking.

 

以更快的速度移动

Moving at Faster Speeds

 

轻松的游泳和练习可以让你以较慢的速度练习技巧。然而，以更快的速度练习这些技巧则更具挑战性。想象一下学习弹奏一首复杂、节奏快速的钢琴曲。首先，你要学习弹奏哪些音符。然后，你需要进行大量的学习和练习，才能以正确的速度、力度和细微差别演奏这些音符。既然你已经尝试过以更快的速度游泳，我想谈谈几个问题。

Easy-paced swimming and drilling allow you to practice skills at a fairly slow speed. Practicing these skills at faster paces, though, is more challenging. Think of learning to play a complicated, fast-paced piece of music on the piano. First, you learn which notes to play. Then you have a lot more learning and practicing to do in order to play the notes at the right speed and with the right emphasis and nuance. Now that you’ve made some attempts to swim at faster speeds, I want to address a couple of concerns.

完全侧身吗？在练习和慢速游泳时，你有充足的时间完全侧身，而且很容易做到。但随着游泳速度的加快，你会发现侧身变得更加困难。在更高的划水频率下，根本没有足够的时间在下一次划水（以及下一次侧身）开始之前完成一次侧身。这没关系。侧身幅度略微减小会产生一些阻力，但这并不会减少你核心力量的发挥。

Rotate all the way onto your side? During drills and when you are swimming at slow speeds, there is plenty of time to rotate entirely onto your side—and it is easy to do. But as you start swimming faster, you will find that rotating onto your sides is more difficult to do. At higher stroke tempos, there simply isn’t enough time to complete one rotation before the next stroke (and hence the next rotation) begins. This is okay. A little less rotation will produce a little more resistance, but that resistance won’t decrease the amount of power available from your core engine.

你的身体线条有多紧？核心力量能否完全传递到手臂，取决于你的身体线条是否紧绷。随着旋转节奏（以及划水节奏）的加快，核心旋转速度也会加快。这就需要更大的核心张力（更紧的线条）才能瞬间且完全地传递旋转能量——节奏越快，保持紧绷的身体线条所需的核心张力就越大。因此，关键在于通过实验来确定每种游泳速度所需的张力——既要保证头部、躯干和臀部紧密连接，又不能过紧而浪费能量。

How tight is your line? Whether your power is fully transmitted from your core engine to your arms depends on your tight-line posture. As you increase your rotation tempo (and thus your stroke tempo), your core rotates faster. This requires more core tension (a tighter line) to instantly and completely transmit that rotation energy—the higher the tempo, the greater the core tension necessary to keep a tight line. The challenge, then, is to experiment in order to determine the amount of tension required for each swimming speed—enough to keep your head, torso, and hips all firmly connected, but not so much that you waste energy.

那么划水次数呢？所有游泳者在高速游动时划水次数都会比低速游动时多。但最高效的游泳者在最快速度下划水次数往往比效率较低的游泳者少。你的任务是，在每种游泳速度下，都要想办法减少划水次数。当你学会如何在不减慢速度的情况下减少划水次数时，你就会成为一名更高效的游泳者。

What about stroke count? All swimmers take more strokes at faster speeds than at slower speeds. But the most effective swimmers tend to take fewer strokes at their fastest speeds than less effective swimmers take at their fastest speeds. Your job, at each of your swimming speeds, is to figure out how to take fewer strokes. When you learn to take fewer strokes without slowing down, you become a more effective swimmer.

如何把握节奏？游泳者想要提高速度时，本能反应是加快手臂摆动。但你应该尝试加快长轴旋转的节奏，然后将划水动作与这种更快的核心旋转连接起来。这样做，你的手臂自然也会摆动得更快。关键在于，如何避免让手臂主导节奏，而是让腿部驱动的核心旋转来决定节奏。稍后会详细讲解这一点。

Where do you set the tempo? The instinct when swimmers try to increase their speed is to move the arms faster. Instead, you should try to set a faster long-axis rotation tempo, and then connect your strokes to that faster core rotation. When you do this, your arms will move faster. The challenge is to prevent them from setting the tempo instead of your leg-driven core rotations setting it. More about this later.

1
 

回归基本原理

 

训练区间：高强度有氧

目标RPE范围：11至14

目标心率范围：SLTHR 的 80% 至 95%。

热身
 

4 × 50 on :10R TS FinsOpt —alt 25 MR3S, 25 3R3S (focus: over the keg)

1 × 100 Dmix TS

IHR 或 RPE

主套装
 

4 × 25 游泳：10R 握拳—描述 1-4（重点：绷紧绳索）

6 × 50 秒，15 秒倒计时—交替 25 秒 Dchoice，25 秒游泳（奇数：拳头；偶数：手）（焦点：酒桶上方）

3 × 100 on :20R TS —alt 25 SGND, 25 swim SLSSS, 25 SGSS good, 25 swim fast (focus: stealth)

4 × 25 cavort on :15R desc 1-4 FinsOpt —在泳池中央进行 360 度空翻。每次游完一个来回，在泳池中央附近完成一个向前空翻。尽量利用惯性完成空翻，而不是用手臂辅助转身。尽可能平稳地游出空翻。

IHR 或 RPE

冷却
 

2 × 75 次游泳，每组 15 分钟——交替进行 25 次握拳、25 次用手指、25 次用手（重点：手臂无重力）

4 × 25 on :15R TSFinsOpt —alt 25 FB, 25 SGND, 25 BBR, 25 swim (focus: stealth)

2 × 25 米游泳，每组15 米（重点：手部和髋部的连接）

IHR 或 RPE

总距离：1400

备注：此练习比任何一级或二级练习都更需要完整的划水动作。重点应放在游得好而不是游得快上。随着一些游泳和练习组合的距离增加，在触壁时快速转身以及做出流畅、有力的蹬伸动作至关重要。SLSSS 是完整的划水动作，但其节奏与通常游泳的节奏截然不同——就像用慢镜头观看自己游泳一样。高水平游泳者能够在不额外踢腿且不失去平衡的情况下，将 SLSSS 的划水节奏控制在每划 4 到 5 秒的范围内。

Back to Fundamentals

 

Training zone: High aerobic

Target RPE range: 11 to 14

Target heart-rate range: 80 to 95% of SLTHR

Warm-Up
 

4 × 50 on :10R TS FinsOpt—alt 25 MR3S, 25 3R3S (focus: over the keg)

1 × 100 Dmix TS

IHR or RPE

Main Set
 

4 × 25 swim on :10R fists—desc 1-4 (focus: tight line)

6 × 50 on :15R—alt 25 Dchoice, 25 swim (odd: fists; even: hands) (focus: over the keg)

3 × 100 on :20R TS—alt 25 SGND, 25 swim SLSSS, 25 SGSS good, 25 swim fast (focus: stealth)

4 × 25 cavort on :15R desc 1-4 FinsOpt—360-degree somersault at midpool. On each length, execute a forward somersault approximately at midpool. Try to use your momentum to turn yourself through the somersault rather than using your arms to help turn you. Swim out of the somersault as smoothly as possible.

IHR or RPE

Cool-Down
 

2 × 75 swim on :15R—alt 25 fists, 25 fingers, 25 hands (focus: weightless arm)

4 × 25 on :15R TSFinsOpt—alt 25 FB, 25 SGND, 25 BBR, 25 swim (focus: stealth)

2 × 25 swim on :15R TS(focus: hand and hip connection)

IHR or RPE

Total distance: 1,400

Comments: This practice requires more full-stroke swimming than any of the level 1 or level 2 practices. The emphasis should be on swimming well rather than on swimming fast. As some of the swim and drill combinations get longer, it is important to turn quickly at the walls and to make good, long, streamlined push-offs. The SLSSS is full-stroke swimming, but it is done at a tempo that one doesn’t normally equate with swimming—as if you were watching yourself swim in slow motion on a video camcorder. Highly skilled swimmers are able to take SLSSS tempos into the 4- to 5-seconds-per-stroke range without additional kicking and without losing their balance.

旋转踢腿重点

 

训练区间：高强度有氧

目标RPE范围：11至14

目标心率范围：SLTHR 的 80% 至 95%。

热身
 

4 × 25 on :10R FinsOpt —alt 25 FB, 25 LAR (focus: tight line)

4 × 25 在 :10R SBFins —alt 25 LAR，25 游泳（重点：管子）

4 × 25 :10R 游泳 BOYLFS（重点：手和髋部的连接）

IHR 或 RPE

主套装：
 

4 × 25 分钟，每组 10 分钟——交替进行 25 分钟 FB、25 分钟 SGSS、25 分钟 LAR、25 分钟游泳（重点：划水次数和隐蔽性）

4 × :20 VKR on :10R—双手放在胸前

IHR 或 RPE

4 × 75 上 :10R FinsOpt —交替 25 LAR，25 MR3S，25 游泳（重点：两拍踢腿）

4 × :20 VKR on :10R SBFins —双手离开水面

IHR 或 RPE

2 × 50 米游泳 SLSSS :10R（焦点：25 次两拍踢腿，25 次激光束旋转触发）

4 × :20 VKR on :10R Fins —双手放在头顶

1 × 100 米交叉游——游泳时在泳道绳下方来回穿梭。在泳道绳一侧游几下后，从绳子下方穿过，在另一侧游三到五下，然后再穿回来，完成本泳道的剩余距离。尽量平稳地切换泳道，不要触碰泳道绳，并尽可能保持节奏的稳定。注意周围其他泳者。

IHR 或 RPE

冷却
 

2 × 100 米，每组 15 分钟——交替进行 25 米 SGB 轻柔划水，25 米游泳（重点：无重力手臂和划水次数）

总距离：1400（包括VKR的估计等效距离）

提示：尝试调整踢腿的幅度和速度，以防止在垂直膝关节旋转（VKR）训练组中心率过高。随着你逐步完成3级训练，尽量快速地从一组训练或活动切换到下一组。理想情况下，你应该进行足够短的休息，以确保在整个主要训练组中心率不会低于目标心率范围的下限。休息时间过长会降低训练的有氧效果。

Rotation Kick Emphasis

 

Training zone: High aerobic

Target RPE range: 11 to 14

Target heart-rate range: 80 to 95% of SLTHR

Warm-Up
 

4 × 25 on :10R FinsOpt—alt 25 FB, 25 LAR (focus: tight line)

4 × 25 on :10R SBFins—alt 25 LAR, 25 swim (focus: the tube)

4 × 25 on :10R swim BOYLFS (focus: hand and hip connection)

IHR or RPE

Main Set:
 

4 × 25 on :10R—alt 25 FB, 25 SGSS, 25 LAR, 25 swim (focus: stroke count and stealth)

4 × :20 VKR on :10R—hands on your chest

IHR or RPE

4 × 75 on :10R FinsOpt—alt 25 LAR, 25 MR3S, 25 swim (focus: two-beat kick)

4 × :20 VKR on :10R SBFins—hands out of the water

IHR or RPE

2 × 50 swim SLSSS on :10R (focus: 25 two-beat kick, 25 laser-beam rotation trigger)

4 × :20 VKR on :10R Fins—hands on top of your head

1 × 100 cavort—Cross back and forth under the lane rope as you swim. After taking a few strokes on one side of the lane rope, cross under the rope and take three to five strokes on the other side, then cross back and finish each length in your lane. Try to switch from lane to lane smoothly, without touching the lane rope, and with as little break in your rhythm as possible. Be careful of traffic.

IHR or RPE

Cool-Down
 

2 × 100 on :15R—alt 25 SGB weak, 25 swim (focus: weightless arm and stroke count)

Total distance: 1,400 (includes estimated equivalent for VKR)

Comments: Experiment with the size and speed of your kick as a way to prevent your heart rate from rising during the VKR sets. As you progress through the level 3 practices, try to switch from one set or activity to the next as quickly as possible. Ideally, you should take short enough breaks that your heart rate does not drop below the bottom of the target heart-rate range during the entire main set. Taking too much rest decreases the aerobic benefit of the workout.

IHR 或 RPE

主套装
 

10组×25米游泳，每组间隔10分钟（重点：划水次数。不要让划水幅度随着组数的增加而增加。）

IHR 或 RPE

6组50米，每组15分钟划水；交替进行25米划水，每组3次划水，每次3次游泳，最后25米游泳（重点：划水次数。不要让划水幅度随着组数的增加而增加。）

IHR 或 RPE

8 × :15 VKR on :10R SBFins —奇数：双手放在胸前；偶数：双手放在头顶（焦点：紧绷的线条）

IHR 或 RPE

4 × 25 Dchoice on :10R SBFins

IHR 或 RPE

总距离：1,500（包括VKR的估计等效距离）

备注：本次练习中出现了迄今为止最长的组数。VKR练习可能会让人感到疲劳——即使疲惫，你还能保持紧绷的泳姿吗？使用SLSSS时，你的目标是在不进行额外踢腿或重复练习的情况下，尽可能减少划水次数。一位身高六英尺（约1.83米）、技术娴熟的游泳运动员，随着时间的推移，在25码或1/2米泳池中使用SLSSS时，划水次数应该能够达到个位数，而在50米泳池中则应该能够达到20次左右。

Consistent Stroke Counting

 

Training zone: High aerobic

Target RPE range: 11 to 14

Target heart-rate range: 80 to 95% of SLTHR

Warm-Up

4 × 50 swim on :10R TS—desc 1-4 (focus: 25 patches and cheeks, 25 two-beat kick)

IHR or RPE

Main Set
 

10 × 25 swim on :10R (focus: stroke count. Don’t let SPL increase as set progresses.)

IHR or RPE

6 × 50 on :15R—alt 25 3R3S, 25 swim (focus: stroke count. Don’t let SPL increase as set progresses.)

IHR or RPE

8 × :15 VKR on :10R SBFins—odd: hands on your chest; even: hands on top of your head (focus: tight line)

IHR or RPE

1 × 100 swim (focus: stroke count. Don’t let it increase from length to length.)

IHR or RPE

Cool-Down
 

3 × 50 swim SLSSS on :10R (focus: tight line and weightless arm)

4 × 25 Dchoice on :10R SBFins

IHR or RPE

Total distance: 1,500 (includes estimated equivalent for VKR)

Comments: Longest sets yet appear in this practice. The VKR activity will likely be fatiguing—can you keep your tight line despite your fatigue? WIth SLSSS, you want to have the lowest stroke count possible without resorting to drilling or extra kicking. A six-foot-tall, highly skilled swimmer should expect, over time, to venture into the single-digit SPL range with SLSSS in 25-yard or -meter pools and into the low-20s SPL range in 50-meter pools.

IHR 或 RPE 套装

 

训练区间：高强度有氧

热身
 

1 × 100 米游泳 SLSSS（重点：50 米无重力手臂划水，50 米两拍打腿）

1 × 100 米游泳——交替进行 25 次握拳、25 次用手指、25 次用手、25 次用手（但降低 SPL）

1 × 100 Dmix

主套装
 

1 × 100—交替 25 SPBDchoice，25 游泳（重点：两拍打腿和划水次数）

8 分钟一组 50 米游泳，根据 IHR 或 RPE 进行（重点：奇数：手和臀部的连接；偶数：隐蔽）

4 × 25 米，以 IHR 或 RPE 为基准进行潜水式训练。使用脚蹼进行 LAR 训练。每次训练开始时，先在水面滑行一段距离，然后潜入水下，以一定角度向池底游去，距离池底约一两英寸，再以一定角度返回水面，正常完成剩余的泳程。目标是优雅地完成这一系列动作，保持泳姿笔直，不破坏旋转节奏。

IHR 或 RPE

以心率或主观疲劳程度快速游2组50米（重点：保持泳姿紧绷，并交替使用双手）。待心率或主观疲劳程度回到目标范围的下限后，再进行第二组50米。

6 × 50 LAR 在 IHR 或 RPE SBFinsOpt

IHR 或 RPE

冷却
 

4 × 75 上 :15R SBFins —交替 25 游泳 SLSSS，25 SIDchoice，25 游泳 SLSSS（重点：无重力手臂）

IHR 或 RPE

总距离：约1500公里

备注：请注意，25米短距离的训练次数较少，而一些练习和游泳时间则较长。随着技能的提高，您需要的休息时间也会减少。始终尝试将您已掌握的练习技巧运用到完整的划水动作中。请记住，在根据个人心率 (IHR) 或主观用力程度 (RPE) 进行训练时，目标是保持在训练目标范围内。

 
4
 

IHR or RPE Set

 

Training zone: High aerobic

Target RPE range: 11 to 14

Target heart-rate range: 80 to 95% of SLTHR

Warm-Up
 

1 × 100 swim SLSSS (focus: 50 weightless arm, 50 two-beat kick)

1 × 100 swim—alt 25 fists, 25 fingers, 25 hands, 25 hands (but lower SPL)

1 × 100 Dmix

IHR or RPE

Main Set
 

1 × 100—alt 25 SPBDchoice, 25 swim (focus: two-beat kick and stroke count)

8-minute set of 50s swim on IHR or RPE (focus: odd: hand and hip connection; even: stealth)

4 × 25 cavort on IHR or RPE—submarine. Do this as LAR with fins. Start each length on the surface, slide under the surface partway down the lane and head toward the bottom of the pool at an angle, come within an inch or two of the bottom, and then return to the surface at an angle and finish the length normally. The goal is to perform this sequence gracefully, without breaking your tight line or interrupting the rhythm of rotations.

IHR or RPE

2 × 50 swim fast on IHR or RPE (focus: tight line and hand swapping). Wait until HR or RPE returns to the low end of your target range before doing the second 50.

6 × 50 LAR on IHR or RPE SBFinsOpt

IHR or RPE

Cool-Down
 

4 × 75 on :15R SBFins—alt 25 swim SLSSS, 25 SIDchoice, 25 swim SLSSS (focus: weightless arm)

IHR or RPE

Total distance: approximately 1,500

Comments: Note that there are fewer 25s and some longer drills and swims. As you become more skilled, you should need less rest. Always try to apply a part of a drill you have mastered to your full-stroke swimming. Remember that on sets done on IHR or RPE, the goal is to stay in the target range assigned for the workout.

游泳高尔夫

4 × 25 狗刨式。这与越过酒桶的姿势正好相反。你需要完全放下肘部，并在水下进行恢复。练习快速游几圈；慢速游几圈；做一些头部露出水面的笨拙动作；以及一些保持紧绷姿势和平衡的动作。正确的姿势和平衡真的能让狗刨式更高效吗？只有真正自信的人才能在公共场合做这个动作。

备注：SGolf训练后，预计心率会升高。今天的练习结束后，请务必记录下你SGolf的最佳（最低）成绩以及取得这些成绩的方法——划水次数、用时以及你当时的重点。事实上，记录下你所有的SGolf成绩，在下一阶段的训练中会非常有用，届时你将重复这些游泳练习进行比较。记住，在较长的休息时间里进行轻松的活动或游泳，有助于你更快地恢复。你可以选择不同的练习重点或训练内容；每次练习都应该有所不同。

Swimming Golf

 

Training zone: High aerobic

Target RPE range: 11 to 14

Target heart-rate range: 80 to 95% of SLTHR

Warm-Up
 

1 × 100—alt 25 DPBDchoice, 25 swim (focus: tight line)

IHR or RPE

IHR or RPE

4 × 25 cavort—dogpaddle. This is the opposite of over the keg. Instead you swim with your elbows totally dropped and with an underwater recovery. Do some fast; do some slow; do some schlumpy with your head out of the water and some with full tight-line posture and balance. Does proper posture and balance make even the dogpaddle more efficient? Only truly self-secure people can handle doing this in public.

3 × 50 SGolf on 1:45 (or :45RMin) (focus: over the keg)

IHR or RPE

1 × 150 swim SLSSS (focus: 50 tight line, 50 the tube, and 50 two-beat kick)

IHR or RPE

Cool-Down
 

4 × 50 on :10R TS—alt 25 SGSS, 25 3R3S (focus: hand and hip connection and stealth)

IHR or RPE

Total distance: 1,600

Comments: Expect higher IHRs after SGolf sets. After today’s practice, be sure to write down your best (lowest) SGolf scores and how you got them—number of strokes, number of seconds, and what you were focusing on to get those scores. In fact, writing down all of your SGolf scores as you do them will come in handy in the next level, when you will repeat these swims for comparison. Remember that easy movement or easy swimming during those longer rests will help you recover faster. There are several places where you can choose your focus or drill; you should make a different choice each time.
