The maximum number of strokes that I’ve seen someone take in a 25-yard pool is 135 (with a full push and glide from the wall). How close can you come to that? What can this cavort teach you?

IHR or RPE

 

Comments: In the second set of SGolf, the fatigue of the LEnd set will make it more difficult to swim low scores. If you can swim the same low scores that you did on the first SGolf set, consider that an accomplishment.

7 24-Minute Lactate Endurance
 

Training zone: Alactic sprints and red line

Target RPE range: 9 to 18+

Target heart-rate range: 70 to 105+% of SLTHR

Warm-Up
 

8-minute set as follows:

4 × 50 swim on IHR or RPE desc 1-4 Fins (focus: tight line)

6 × 25 swim on :05R desc 1-6 Fins (focus: easy speed)

Fairly fast LAR Fins to finish 8 minutes

IHR or RPE

Main Set
 

6-minute set. Short sprints FinsOpt. Each short sprint starts from a push into a sprint LAR for at least three rotations. Add four strokes while keeping this fast-rotation tempo, and then swim easy until you recover before the next repeat. Before starting each sprint, drum your hands fast on the deck, tuning your kick to this tempo.

IHR or RPE

TEST (LEnd), 24-minute set. Swim 200s on 1:1 W/RInt :06Range [interval, fast2, slow, avgSPL, HHR]. What will you do instead of just standing there and breathing hard? Easy swim? Drill? Cavort?

IHR or RPE

1 × 100 EZ swim. Count your total strokes for this swim.

IHR or RPE

5 × 50 SGolf OACI (See following comments.)

IHR or RPE

1 × 100 swim. How fast can you swim using no more strokes than in the previous EZ 100?

IHR or RPE

Cool-Down
 

200 SLSSS or your choice of cavort

IHR or RPE

 

Comments: Before you start this practice, look up the results of your previous SGolf sets and calculate an average score per 50 repeat. Use this as your par score on the 5 × 50 SGolf set and see if you can swim through this 5-hole course, finishing under par.

8 Lactate Tolerance—50s
 

Training zone: Lactate threshold and red line

Target RPE range: 9 to 19+

Target heart-rate range: 70 to 110+% of SLTHR

Warm-Up
 

8-minute set. Drill or swim continuous TSOpt—alt 25 Dchoice, 25 swim

IHR or RPE

Main Set
 

8-minute set of 50s SGolf. First 50 should be swum at a moderate pace. Then see how many different combinations of stroke counts and time you can use to get the same score. Take only the amount of rest you need.

1 × 100 swim SLSSS BOYLFS

TEST (LTol), swim 8 × 50 on 3:00 (or 6 on 4:00, 1:00Cut) [fast2, slow, avgSPL, HHR]. Swim maybe an easy 50 plus add a bit of bobbing to ease your suffering between repeats.

IHR or RPE

1 × 100 swim SLSSS BOYLFS

IHR or RPE

12-minute set. Swim 150s @ CPace on :15R (or 100s @ CPace, :10R) LOFO. Try to reduce your stroke count throughout this set.

IHR or RPE

2-minute cavort—water-aided standing broad jump. In roughly chest-deep water, perform a standing broad jump for distance. You may use only a single sweep or scoop of your arms to assist you. A judicious use of your leap momentum plus the interplay of gravity and buoyancy can carry you quite a distance. Repeat several times and improve on your original leap.

Cool-Down
 

4-minute set. EZ 50s continuous FinsOpt—alt 25 SGB weak, 25 swim BOYLFS (focus: red dot)

IHR or RPE

 

Comments: The CPace set, which follows soon after the test set, offers an excellent opportunity to focus on efficient swimming while you are fatigued. Remember that when a focus point is not explicitly indicated, you should select a focus for your stroke. Focus on correcting and refining problem areas rather than on what you already do well.

9 Lactate Tolerance—100s
 

Training zone: Alactic sprints, lactate threshold, and red line

Target RPE range: 9 to 19+

Target heart-rate range: 70 to 110+% of SLTHR

Warm-Up
 

6-minute set. Swim 150s (or 100s) desc and NS on :15R SBFinsOpt

IHR or RPE

Main Set
 

12-minute set. Swim 2 × 500 NS (or shorter distance) @ CPace on 1:00R. Choose a distance in which CPace time is 5:30 or less.

IHR or RPE

6 minutes of short sprints. On the first one, push off and swim three long, easy strokes, and then turn and sprint back to the wall, counting your strokes. On each subsequent repeat, add one more full-length easy stroke before the turn. How few returning sprint strokes can you add for each easy stroke you add? Swim an easy 25 or 50 between each repeat.

IHR or RPE

4-minute set. 25s swim on :10R TSOpt—alt 25 @ NSPL, 25 @ -1SPL, 25 @ -2SPL, 25 @ -3SPL. Try to look like you are swimming rather than drilling.

IHR or RPE

TEST (LTol), swim 4 × 100 (or 75—2:00Cut) on 6:00 [fast2, slow, avgSPL, HHR]. Active rest early in the set will delay lactate accumulation; so does breathing out against some resistance. What will you do here between repeats? During the last repeat of the set, remember the following: Pain is weakness leaving the body.

Cool-Down
 

6-minute set. Reswim one repeat of the distance you swam in the CPace set. Swim it at a very easy pace, but negative-split it.

IHR or RPE

 

Comments: On the CPace set, negative splitting each swim is challenging, but it will help you swim your best time for the number of heartbeats spent. Be sure to take an IHR or RPE at the beginning of the 1-minute rest as well as at the end in order to see how well you recover.

10 Lactate Tolerance—200s
 

Training zone: Red line

Target RPE range: 9 to 19+

Target heart-rate range: 70 to 110+% of SLTHR

Warm-Up
 

8-minute set. Continuous swim TS—alt 75 fists, 50 fingers, 25 hands. First cycle is swum at a very easy pace; each cycle is swum faster than the one before.

IHR or RPE

Main Set
 

4-minute set. Swim 25s @ CPace on :05-10R. Maintain the same stroke count throughout.

IHR or RPE

1 × 200 swim fists SLSSS

TEST (LTol), swim 3 × 200 (or 150—4:00Cut) on 12:00 [fast2, slow, avgSPL, HHR]. For recovery work between these high-intensity repeats, I encourage you to mix easy swimming and your favorite cavorts.

IHR or RPE

1 × 200 swim fists SLSSS

4-minute set. Swim 25s @ CPace on :10-15R LOFO. Use one fewer SPL than in the previous CPace set.

IHR or RPE

Cool-Down
 

4-minute set. Swim 50s on IHR or RPE. Start @ CPace and swim each one 1-2 seconds slower than the preceding one. Try to decrease stroke count throughout the set.

 

Comments: Once you have swum each of the LEnd and LTol test sets with no fins or snorkel, you may swim some of them with equipment for more variety. Be sure to record these results separately from your no-equipment test sets.

 

第四部分
 
长期训练
 

第三部分介绍了一系列技术和体能训练活动，这些活动的时间和强度会逐渐增加。一旦你熟悉了技能练习、技术概念和练习符号，你就可以开启一段终身难忘的水上冒险之旅。第四部分将帮助你实现这一目标。在接下来的章节中，你将学习如何将练习安排成一个训练计划，以及如何记录你的进步。

Part III introduced you to a variety of technique and conditioning activities that became progressively longer or more intense. Once you have familiarized yourself with the skill drills, technique concepts, and practice notation, you are ready to embark on a rest-of-your-life aquatic adventure. Part IV will help you do that. In the following chapters, you’ll learn how to organize the practices into a training program and how to chart your progress.

第十三章将帮助你制定一个包含不同训练阶段和适当休息时间的季节性训练计划。此外，我还提供了许多游泳运动员（无论是否参加比赛）如何安排训练的具体示例。

Chapter 13 will help you put together a seasonal training program that incorporates different training phases and appropriate amounts of rest. In addition, I give specific examples of how many swimmers, competitive or otherwise, organize their training.

第十四章提供了一系列为期三周的训练计划示例，您可以将其作为整个赛季训练计划的基础。这些示例计划根据三种不同的兴趣和能力水平划分——健身游泳、预备竞技游泳和竞技游泳。如果您选择使用第十四章中的计划，您会发现它们循序渐进，并能持续考验您的技能、耐力和速度。

Chapter 14 offers a variety of sample three-week programs that you can use as building blocks for an entire season. The sample programs in chapter 14 are based on three levels of interest and ability—fitness swimming, precompetitive swimming, and competitive swimming. If you choose to use the programs in chapter 14, you will find that they are progressive and that they continually test your skill, endurance, and speed.

第十五章讲解了如何通过寻找训练伙伴、记录训练日志、变换游泳环境以及准确追踪每日、每周和每个赛季的游泳进步来保持高昂的训练动力。书中还提供了几个方便的进度图表，您可以复印后带到泳池使用。

Chapter 15 explains how to keep your motivation high by finding training partners, keeping a training diary, varying your swimming environment, and accurately tracking your swimming progress day to day, week to week, and season to season. Several handy progress charts are supplied for you to photocopy and take to the pool.

第十三章
 
全年游泳
 

健身游泳者往往习惯于以相同的中等速度进行长距离游泳，很少或根本不注重技术训练——这无疑会让他们养成用同样难看的泳姿慢速游下去的习惯。虽然竞技游泳者更有可能规划训练并更加努力，但他们通常每次只针对一次训练进行计划，而不是像竞技游泳者那样规划整个赛季的训练。如果你想成为一名更优秀、更快的游泳者——一名高效的游泳者——你需要不同的策略。

Fitness swimmers tend to make a habit of doing long swims at the same moderate pace, with little or no technique focus to their workout—a surefire plan for becoming better conditioned to swim slowly with the same ugly stroke they’ve always used. While competitive swimmers are more likely to plan their practices and to work harder, they often plan for only one practice at a time rather than for a season of practices. If you want to become a better and faster swimmer—a highly effective swimmer—you need a different strategy.

无论您是竞技游泳运动员还是健身游泳爱好者，制定赛季计划都能让您的训练更加高效且充满乐趣。本章将介绍训练赛季的不同阶段，指导您如何制定赛季计划，解释您的身体对训练的反应，以及如何避免过度训练的后果。您可以在赛季计划中使用第14章中的示例训练计划。这些计划会详细列出您在整个赛季中每天应该进行的训练内容。

Whether you are a competitive swimmer or a fitness swimmer, your training will be more productive and enjoyable if you do some seasonal planning. This chapter describes the different phases of a training season, shows you how to plan a season of training, explains how your body responds to training, and explains how to avoid the consequences of overtraining. You’ll be able use the sample programs in chapter 14 in your seasonal plan. They will tell you precisely which workouts you should do each day throughout your season.

游泳训练计划的各个阶段

Phases of a Swim-Training Program

 

赛季训练策略分为五个阶段：技术习得和一般耐力、技术精进和专项耐力、技术保持和比赛、大赛前减量训练以及赛季间歇期。根据你的最终目标，你可以在赛季计划中采用部分或全部阶段。每个阶段的训练组合方式将决定你的训练成果。

There are five phases of a seasonal training strategy: technique acquisition and general endurance, technique refinement and specific endurance, technique maintenance and competition, tapering for a big meet, and the break between seasons. Depending on your ultimate interests, you may use some or all of the phases in your seasonal planning. How you combine these workouts in each phase determines the outcome of your efforts.

技术习得与耐力基础游泳的基本耐力是指以低于最大速度的配速进行长时间有效游泳的能力。任何训练赛季都必须从这个阶段开始，运动员才能在赛季后期应对更高强度的训练。即使是精英游泳运动员，在每个训练赛季的最初几个月里，也需要学习新技能并提高对技能细微差别的敏感度。1至3级的训练课程旨在帮助你学习新技能，并通过技能练习和专注的低强度游泳来建立有氧体能基础。这些训练课程应占据赛季初期训练的相当一部分。

Technique Acquisition and General Endurance Basic endurance for swimming involves swimming effectively at submaximal paces for extended periods of time. Any training season must start at this level if the athlete is to negotiate more demanding training later in the season. Even elite swimmers spend the first several months of each training season learning new skills and increasing their sensitivity to skill nuances. The practices in levels 1 through 3 allow you to learn new skills while developing an aerobic conditioning base using skill drills and focused, low-intensity swimming. The practices should constitute a sizable portion of your early-season training.

技术精进与专项耐力训练在建立起整体耐力之后，我们将通过引入并逐步增加乳酸阈值训练（包括巡航速度和巡航间歇训练，见于第四阶段）来提升有氧训练强度。由于我们希望继续精进在整体耐力阶段所学的技能，因此我们将继续结合技能练习和技术导向的游泳训练。“熟能生巧”是本训练阶段的技术主题。对于那些没有竞技或冒险目标的游泳运动员来说，这或许就是他们所能达到的游泳体能训练的极限了。

Technique Refinement and Specific Endurance Once general endurance is established, we increase the intensity of the aerobic training by introducing and progressively increasing lactate-threshold training with cruise pace and cruise interval work found in level 4. Because we want to continue refining the skills we learned in the general-endurance phase, we continue to mix skill drills and technique-focused swimming sets. “Practice makes permanent” is the technique theme for this training phase. This may be as far as swimmers with no competitive or risk-taking aspirations ever want to venture into swim conditioning.

技术维护与比赛那些希望参加比赛或仅仅是为了测试身体极限的人，需要增加5级和6级的训练内容。这些训练引入了乳酸耐力、乳酸耐受力和无氧无氧训练。无氧速度是训练的重点，但同时也会安排足够的耐力训练来维持你的有氧能力。如果你参加比赛，请将大部分比赛安排在这个训练阶段。这些比赛将作为你高强度训练的一部分。通过继续进行技能练习，并增加使用实时反馈的完整泳姿练习，来保持你已经掌握和精进的技能。监控你有效游泳技能的执行情况是此阶段训练的技术主题。

Technique Maintenance and Competition Those who wish to compete or to simply test the body’s limits will add workouts from levels 5 and 6. These workouts introduce lactate endurance, lactate tolerance, and anaerobic alactic work. Anaerobic speed is the conditioning focus, but with enough endurance work to maintain your aerobic conditioning. If you compete, schedule most of your competitions during this training period. They will serve as a portion of your high-intensity training. Maintain the skills you have already acquired and refined by continuing your skill-drill work and by including more full-stroke swimming using real-time feedback. Monitoring your execution of effective swimming skills is the technique theme for this phase of training.

 

精心策划的训练赛季的每个阶段都包含技术和体能训练，旨在稳步提高运动表现。

Each of the phases of a well-planned training season incorporates a mix of technique and conditioning work aimed at steadily improving performance.

© AP Images

© AP Images

 

减量训练如果您是一名竞技游泳运动员，您可能正在为赛季末的某项赛事进行训练。整个赛季的训练计划旨在让您在比赛中发挥出最佳水平。减量训练是指减少训练量的时期，在此期间，身体会比平时获得更多的休息时间，从而使身体有机会充​​分适应训练。例如，在减量训练期间，游泳运动员可以将总训练量（包括泳道长度和训练时长）减少到减量训练前的三分之一。关键在于保持与减量训练前相同的相对强度，但减少训练量。竞技游泳运动员在减量训练后成绩显著提高的情况很常见。

Tapering If you are a competitor, you probably have a specific season-ending competition that you are training toward. A training season is planned to allow you to perform your best during this competition. A training taper is a period of reduced training, during which the body is allowed much more rest than usual and is thereby given the chance to fully adapt to training. For example, during a taper, a swimmer may cut his total training volume (yardage and duration) to as little as one-third of his pretaper volume. The key is to work at the same relative intensity as in pretaper practices but to do less of it. It is common for competitive swimmers to report dramatic improvements in their performance after tapering.

无论你游泳的目的是什么，偶尔从训练计划中休息一下——一周到一个月——对于保持状态和热情是必要的。当你重返泳池时，你会对训练有全新的认识。

Take a Break Regardless of your reasons for swimming, an occasional break from your training program—from a week to a month—is necessary in order to maintain freshness and enthusiasm. When you return to the pool, you will have a renewed outlook on your workouts.

规划一个有竞争力的训练赛季

Planning a Competitive Training Season

 

赛季规划要从最终目标出发。以下是一个典型的成人游泳大师赛赛季周期性训练计划示例，该计划的目标是在五月中旬的短池（25码泳池）全国锦标赛上达到最佳状态。我们将从五月中旬开始倒推规划。由于长池（50米泳池）全国锦标赛通常在八月中旬举行，而且游泳运动员在大赛后通常会休息一个月，因此我们最早也要到九月中旬才能开始短池训练赛季，这样我们就有35周的训练时间。

Planning a season begins with the end in mind. Here is an example of how we might build a periodized training schedule for a typical Masters training season, which is focused on a peak performance at Short-Course (25-yard pool) Nationals in mid-May. We’ll plan backward from that mid-May date. Since Long-Course (50-meter pool) Nationals usually take place in mid-August, and since swimmers often take a month off after the big meet, the earliest we might start a short-course training season would be in mid-September, which would give us 35 weeks to train.

减量期：根据训练赛季的强度和持续时间，你的减量期应该持续两到四周。我们将以四月下旬到五月中旬的三周为例。几个赛季的个人经验会让你更清楚地了解你的减量期应该有多长。

Taper Period Depending on the intensity and duration of the training season, your taper should last anywhere from two to four weeks. We’ll use the three weeks from late April to mid-May. Personal experience over a few seasons will give you a better idea of how long your taper should be.

技术保持期和比赛期：根据您的训练赛季长度，此训练期可能持续 6 至 12 周。这是集中、高强度训练的最佳范围。扣除减量期后，我们的赛季大约还剩下 32 周。我们希望每个耐力训练阶段都比比赛阶段持续时间更长，因此我们将从 2 月中旬到 4 月下旬的 9 周（不到剩余赛季的三分之一）安排为比赛训练。

Technique Maintenance and Competition Period Depending on the duration of your training season, this training period could last from 6 to 12 weeks. This is the optimum range for concentrated, high-intensity training. After deducting the taper period, we have roughly 32 weeks left in our season. We want each endurance training phase to last longer than our competition phase, so we’ll block out the 9 weeks from mid-February to late April, less than one-third of the remaining season, for our competition training.

技术精进与专项耐力训练期：剩余23周的耐力训练时间，我们希望每个耐力训练阶段都分配大约一半的时间。因此，在专项耐力训练期，我们将预留12周——从12月到2月中旬——考虑到假期期间可能会损失一周的训练时间。

Technique Refinement and Specific Endurance Period With 23 weeks left for endurance training, we want to spend about half of that time in each endurance phase. So for our specific endurance period, we’ll block out 12 weeks—December through mid-February—knowing that we’ll probably lose a week of training around the holidays.

技术习得和一般耐力训练期从 9 月中旬到 11 月底的 11 周时间，我们将进行一般耐力训练。

Technique Acquisition and General Endurance Period This leaves the 11 weeks from mid-September through the end of November for our general endurance training.

日程安排如下：

技术习得和整体耐力，11 周（9 月中旬至 11 月底）

技术精进和专项耐力训练，12 周（12 月至 2 月中旬）

技术维护和比赛，9 周（2 月中旬至 4 月下旬）

逐渐减量，3周（4月下旬至5月中旬）

短程全国赛

休息两周（至六月初）

The schedule would look like this:

Technique acquisition and general endurance, 11 weeks (mid-September through the end of November)

Technique refinement and specific endurance, 12 weeks (December to mid-February)

Technique maintenance and competition, 9 weeks (mid-February to late April)

Taper, 3 weeks (late April to mid-May)

Short-Course Nationals

Break, 2 weeks (until early June)

 
如果完成本次比赛后，您想参加八月中旬的长池全国锦标赛，那么您只有短短11周的备战时间。您可以这样安排：

缩短休息时间，只休息一周。这样你就有12周的时间来完成工作。

技术掌握和整体耐力训练，3周（5月下旬至6月中旬）

技术精进和专项耐力训练，4 周（6 月中旬至 7 月初）

技术维护和比赛，3 周（7 月初至 7 月下旬）

减量期，2 周（7 月下旬至 8 月中旬）

长距离全国锦标赛

休息 4 周（直到 9 月中旬，下一个短程赛季开始）

Cut break short, 1 week. This gives you 12 weeks to work with.

Technique acquisition and general endurance, 3 weeks (late May to mid-June)

Technique refinement and specific endurance, 4 weeks (mid-June to early July)

Technique maintenance and competition, 3 weeks (early July to very late July)

Taper, 2 weeks (very late July to mid-August)

Long-Course Nationals

Break, 4 weeks (until mid-September, when the next short-course season begins)

 
这种长池训练方案并非理想之选，但它说明了赛季规划的基本原则如何在极短的训练周期中得到应用。一些游泳运动员和教练更倾向于一年规划三个赛季，而不是两个。一个包含三个赛季的年度周期可能如下所示：
第一赛季：从九月初开始，持续15周，最终在十二月下旬举行一场精选比赛。
 

技术掌握和整体耐力训练，4 周（9 月初至 10 月初）

技术精进和专项耐力训练，5周（10月初至11月初）

技术维护和比赛，4 周（11 月初至 12 月初）

逐渐减量，2 周（12 月初至 12 月下旬）

选定的会议

休息 1 至 2 周

第二赛季：从1月1日开始，持续20周，最终在5月中旬举行短程赛全国锦标赛。
 

技术习得和整体耐力训练，6 周（1 月至 2 月中旬）

技术精进和专项耐力训练，6 周（2 月中旬至 3 月下旬）

技术维护和比赛，5周（3月下旬至4月下旬）

逐渐减量，3周（4月下旬至5月中旬）

短程全国赛

休息 1 至 2 周

第三赛季：如前所述，为期11或12周的长赛季训练，之后有3至4周的休息时间，然后是下一个短赛季。
 
Season 1: 15 weeks from early September, culminating in a selected meet in late December
 

Technique acquisition and general endurance, 4 weeks (early September to early October)

Technique refinement and specific endurance, 5 weeks (early October to early November)

Technique maintenance and competition, 4 weeks (early November to early December)

Taper, 2 weeks (early December to late December)

Selected meet

Break, 1 to 2 weeks

Season 2: 20 weeks from January 1, culminating in Short-Course Nationals in mid-May
 

Technique acquisition and general endurance, 6 weeks (January through mid-February)

Technique refinement and specific endurance, 6 weeks (mid-February to late March)

Technique maintenance and competition, 5 weeks (late March to late April)

Taper, 3 weeks (late April to mid-May)

Short-Course Nationals

Break, 1 to 2 weeks

Season 3: 11 or 12 week long-course training season as described earlier with 3 to 4 weeks break before the next short-course season
 
 

制定健身训练计划

Planning a Fitness Training Schedule

 
健身游泳者可以运用相同的训练计划框架，而无需受限于特定的比赛日程。有些人选择像竞技游泳运动员一样按部就班地进行训练，包括减量训练和休息。而另一些人则倾向于跳过比赛阶段或减量训练阶段，或者两者都跳过，具体取决于他们是否希望进行一段时间的高强度训练。以下是一些可能的健身训练计划示例：
为期6周的训练计划，不包含高强度阶段。
 

技术习得和一般耐力训练，3周；

技术精进和专项耐力训练，3周

6-week schedule without a high-intensity phase
 

Technique acquisition and general endurance, 3 weeks

Technique refinement and specific endurance, 3 weeks

 
由于该赛季的生理压力较低，因此可以多次重复，无需在每次循环之间休息。每个阶段的持续时间并不关键，但应大致相等。对于希望加入高强度训练期的游泳运动员，以下计划适用：
为期9周的训练计划，包括一个高强度阶段。
 

技术习得和一般耐力训练，3周；

技术精进和专项耐力训练，3周；

技术维持和比赛训练，2周；

减量或休息，1周

9-week schedule including a high-intensity phase
 

Technique acquisition and general endurance, 3 weeks

Technique refinement and specific endurance, 3 weeks

Technique maintenance and competition, 2 weeks

Taper or break, 1 week

 

再次强调，各阶段的实际持续时间并不像之前描述的相对时长那么重要。虽然你不会真的参加比赛，但第三阶段是高强度训练的阶段。之后进行一段短暂的减量期或休息（例如进行交叉训练），既可以作为奖励，也可以避免过度训练。

Again, the actual durations of the phases are not as important as following the relative durations as described earlier. Though you won’t actually compete, that third phase is when the high-intensity training takes place. Following it with either a short taper period or with a short break, perhaps for cross-training, serves both as a reward and as a method for avoiding overtraining.

当难以维持规律训练时（例如圣诞假期），计划休息一段时间是避免因错过训练而产生的内疚感的好方法。

Planning for a break when regular training is difficult to maintain—Christmas holiday, for instance—is a great way to avoid the guilt that often arises when one must miss training.

适应

Adaptation

 

人们普遍误以为训练中的付出能提升游泳水平。事实上，真正提升体能的是训练间隙——也就是恢复期——的锻炼。正常情况下，身体会根据体力需求进行适应性调整。身体会追求一种最佳的健康状态，在这种状态下，日常的体育活动不会造成太大负担。例如，搬运工的身体会增加肌肉量以帮助他们搬运重物；跑步者的身体会增强腿部肌肉的有氧能力并改善心血管系统。运动会向大脑和身体发出信号，触发一系列生理适应，例如增强力量、提高爆发力、增强耐力等等。

A common misconception is that the work you do in practice makes you a better-conditioned swimmer. In fact, it is what you do between work sessions—during your recovery periods—that actually improves your conditioning. Under normal conditions, the body makes adaptations in response to physical demands. Your body seeks a state of fitness for which the physical activities that you regularly engage in are not a great hardship. A furniture mover’s body adds muscle mass to help him lift heavy objects. A runner’s body increases the aerobic capacity of her leg muscles and improves the cardiovascular system. Exercise sends signals to the brain and body that trigger a variety of physiological adaptations, such as increased strength, more explosiveness, more endurance, and so on.

上一段的关键短语是“在正常情况下”。正常情况包括适当的营养、适当的水分、充足的高质量睡眠、极少或完全不使用文化污染物（例如酒精、尼古丁、可卡因、甜食）、无疾病以及相对较低的心理压力水平。

The operative phrase in the previous paragraph is under normal conditions. Normal conditions include proper nutrition, proper hydration, adequate amounts of high-quality sleep, minimal or zero use of cultural pollutants (e.g., alcohol, nicotine, crack, Twinkies), freedom from disease, and relatively low psychological-stress levels.

但是，当一种或多种身体状况异常时，身体对运动的正常适应能力会急剧下降。如果你今晚去锻炼，然后饮食不规律，尽情玩乐，睡眠不足，那么你的锻炼效果将微乎其微。而且这种效果也无法弥补。即使三天后你终于调整好状态，保证充足睡眠和健康饮食，你也无法获得今天锻炼带来的益处。

But when one or more conditions are abnormal, there is a dramatic decrease in the body’s ability to adapt normally to exercise. If you go to practice this evening, then eat poorly, party hearty, and don’t get enough sleep, you should expect very little adaptation to result from your workout. And you can’t get it back. Even if you finally get your act together three days from now by getting plenty of sleep and eating well, you will not reap the benefits of today’s workout.

睡眠不足可能是最常见也是最具破坏性的偏离理想适应状态的情况。如果你睡眠不足，最好把现在花在训练过程（比如旅行、训练、再旅行）上的两三个小时用来好好睡一觉。更好的办法是早点睡觉。睡眠不足再加上其他一种或多种不利因素只会让问题更加严重。虽然偶尔偏离理想适应状态不会对你的训练造成毁灭性打击，但持续地破坏理想适应状态会让你的竞争对手获得巨大的优势。

Lack of sleep is probably the most common and most destructive deviation from ideal-adaptation conditions. If you are not getting enough sleep, you’d probably be better off taking the two to three hours you now devote to the workout process (i.e., traveling, training, and traveling again) and investing it in a good nap. Better yet, get to bed earlier. Coupling lack of sleep with one or more of the other negative conditions just compounds the problem. Although an occasional deviation won’t devastate your training, consistently infringing on ideal adaptation conditions will give your competition a huge advantage.

休息和过度训练

Rest and Overtraining

 

过度进行高强度运动，同时又缺乏足够的休息（包括主动休息和被动休息），会导致所谓的适应失败。这种适应失败作为一种保护机制，实际上会降低你进一步运动的能力。这种情况通常被称为过度训练，其潜在后果可能比训练不足更为严重。因此，采取积极主动的措施来避免过度训练至关重要——包括制定计划、提高意识、进行监测以及保持灵活性。

Doing too much high-stress exercise while at the same time not getting enough rest, active and passive, will result in what is called failing adaptation, which, as a protective mechanism, actually decreases your ability to do further exercise. This is often referred to as overtraining, and it potentially has far worse consequences than not training enough. Taking a proactive approach to avoiding overtraining—through planning, awareness, monitoring, and flexibility—is essential.

计划安排：由于连续或一周内进行过多的高强度训练是过度训练的主要原因——无论你的能力水平、体能水平或兴趣如何——你应该计划每周至少休息一天，不要游泳。这有助于你在泳池中保持身心清爽。休息日进行其他体育活动是可以的，只要强度较低即可。你可以把这看作是另一种形式的积极休息。

Planning Because too many days of hard exercise in a row or in a week is the primary cause of overtraining—regardless of your ability level, conditioning level, or interest level—you should plan to take at least one day off from swimming each week. This will help keep both your body and your mind fresher when you are in the pool. Pursuing other physical activities on your day off is fine, as long as you keep the intensity level low. Consider this another form of active rest.

锻炼时，注意观察过度训练的迹象非常重要。以下一项或多项主观指标应被视为过度训练的警示信号：

• 感觉疲倦、精疲力竭或感觉没有精力

• Feeling tired, drained, or like you have no energy

• 多处肌肉和关节出现酸痛或疼痛

• General aches or pain in many muscles and joints

• 无法从一次锻炼中恢复过来，直接进入下一次锻炼

• Not recovering from one workout to the next

• 表现、训练能力或强度下降

• Decrease in performance, training capacity, or intensity

• 失眠

• Insomnia

• 头痛

• Headaches

• 情绪波动、易怒、热情减退、抑郁

• Moodiness, irritability, decreased enthusiasm, depression

• 食欲减退

• Diminished appetite

 

还有一些更客观的指标可以判断是否过度训练。如果你正在按照本书中的训练计划进行训练，那么你应该定期记录你的T泳心率——也就是你的SLTHR。如果你发现当心率达到这个水平时，你的训练速度开始下降，那么你可能正走向过度训练。记录每天的训练感受也能帮助你发现训练强度下降和热情减退的趋势。

There are more objective measures for overtraining. If you are following the programs in this book, then you are regularly recording your T-swim heart rates—your SLTHR. If you find that your training pace begins to slow down when you are at that heart rate, you may be heading toward overtraining. A training diary in which you include notes about how you feel each day can also help you spot downward trends and decreased enthusiasm.

监测：过度训练的另一个指标是静息心率 (RHR) 的异常波动。为了准确判断，您必须养成定期（甚至每天）监测 RHR 的习惯，以便了解其正常范围。佩戴心率监测器并将其设置为夜间平均心率是理想的选择。其次，最好在清晨醒来后立即进行测量。如果您手动测量 RHR，请在 60 秒内数出脉搏次数，并保持正常呼吸。如果您发现 RHR 超出正常范围几 BPM 以上（无论是偏高还是偏低），并且持续超过一天左右，这可能表明您开始过度训练或处于疾病的早期阶段。

Monitoring Another indicator of overtraining is an unexpected variation of your resting heart rate (RHR). To make this determination accurately, you must make a habit of checking your RHR regularly, even daily, so that you know its normal range. Wearing a heart-rate monitor and setting it to average your heart rate overnight is ideal for this. The next best option is to take a reading first thing in the morning when you wake up. If you check your RHR manually, count the number of pulses over a full 60-second period and breathe normally throughout. If you notice that your RHR is more than a few BPM out of your normal range, high or low, for more than a day or so, this could indicate either the beginning of overtraining or the first stages of illness.

灵活性：如果你在出现过度训练的警告信号后仍然继续训练，最好的结果是感觉疲惫，最坏的结果是生病或受伤。根据症状的严重程度，完全恢复可能需要几天到几周的时间。恢复应该包括合理的营养、减轻压力和高质量的睡眠。最好从一开始就避免过度训练。如果你怀疑自己可能处于过度训练的边缘，可以尝试调整训练计划几天到一周。减少高强度训练的量，增加休息和积极休息的时间。这样或许可以避免更严重的后果，最终只是训练出现小波动，而不是彻底崩溃。

Flexibility If you continue to train despite having the warning signs of overtraining, you will feel stale at best and sick or injured at worst. Depending on the severity of your symptoms, total recovery can take from a few days to several weeks. Recovery should include proper nutrition, stress reduction, and quality sleep. It would be better to avoid overtraining in the first place. If you suspect that you may be on the edge of overtraining, try altering your training for a few days to a week. Decrease the amount of high-intensity training you do and include more rest and active rest. You may be able to avoid more severe consequences and end up with merely a training blip as opposed to a train(ing) wreck.

第14章的示例训练计划详细列出了每日训练安排。这些计划通常交替进行强度较高和强度较低的训练日，并且每周至少安排一天休息。您可以按照这些计划执行，也可以将其作为参考来设计自己的训练计划，以确保在训练计划中安排充足的休息时间。

The sample programs in chapter 14 lay out training days. They typically alternate between less intense and more intense days and include at least one day of rest per week. Follow these programs or use them as a model for designing your own to ensure that you plan an adequate amount of rest into your training program.

第十四章
 
游泳课程示例
 

大多数经常游泳的成年人都会说，他们游泳的首要目的是为了健身。但每个人不同的是，当他们本可以做其他事情的时候，是什么动力让他们坚持回到水中。无论你是想增强有氧运动能力、提高游泳效率，还是备战全国锦标赛，请继续阅读，你会找到一系列可以帮助你实现目标的训练计划。本章中的训练计划分为三种兴趣或参与类型：

Most adults who swim regularly will say that they swim first and foremost for fitness. What varies from person to person is the motivation for continuing to come back to the water when they could be doing something else. Whether you simply want to be aerobically fit, increase the effectiveness of your swimming, or train for the national championships, read on and you will find a set of programs that can help you reach your goals. The programs in this chapter are divided into three interest, or participation, types:

初级和轻松游泳课程（泳道游泳或健身游泳）作为一名游泳初学者，您可能经常游泳以放松身心、享受乐趣，或将其作为有氧健身计划的一部分。初级和轻松课程提供各种学习活动，旨在提高您的有氧运动能力。这些课程主要包含1级和2级练习，侧重于技能训练。它们教授并巩固高效自由泳的基本技巧，同时每周提供三到四次有氧运动。虽然大多数练习旨在将您的心率保持在有氧训练心率范围的较低水平，但也包含一些强度稍高的3级和4级练习。

Beginning- and Easy-Swimming Programs (Lap or Fitness Swimming) As a beginning swimmer, you probably swim on a regular basis for relaxation and enjoyment or as part of an aerobic-fitness plan. The beginning and easy programs provide a variety of learning activities that will improve your aerobic fitness. These programs consist mainly of level 1 and level 2 practices that focus on skill drills. They teach and reinforce the fundamentals of efficient freestyle swimming while providing you with aerobic activities for three or four practices per week. While most of these practices are intended to keep your heart rate at the lower end of the aerobic-training heart-rate range, there are also a few level 3 and level 4 practices that are somewhat more intense.

经常游泳训练计划（赛前）：养成定期锻炼习惯的游泳者通常希望增加训练的频率和强度，这往往是为了将来参加比赛。经常游泳的人会超越最低有氧运动要求。他们训练更频繁、时间更长、强度更高。经常游泳者可能还会参加一些比赛，例如公开水域游泳或当地大师赛的长距离项目。如果您每周游泳四到五次，那么您很可能属于这一类。赛前训练旨在增加训练量、频率和强度，同时为比赛所需的更高强度训练奠定基础。

Frequent-Swimming Programs (Precompetitive) Swimmers who make a habit of working out regularly often want to increase the frequency and intensity of their workouts—often with an eye toward competing in the future. People who swim frequently go beyond the minimum aerobic-exercise requirements. They train more often, for longer periods, and at higher intensities. Frequent swimmers might also swim in an occasional competition, such as an open-water swim or a distance event at a local Masters meet. If you swim four or five times per week, you are most likely in this category. Precompetitive workouts increase training volume, frequency, and intensity while laying the groundwork for the more intense training that is necessary for competition.

高强度游泳训练计划（竞技型）如果您已经参加比赛，或者计划在不久的将来参赛，又或者只是想了解自己的身体极限，那么高强度训练计划将是您的理想之选。这些计划的前提是游泳是您的主要运动项目，并且您愿意每周投入更多训练时间。您是否参加比赛并不重要。竞技游泳运动员的乐趣和动力来自于不断挑战自己的速度和耐力，无论是与计时器较量还是与其他游泳运动员竞争。这些训练计划专为那些希望现在游得更快，下周游得更快的游泳运动员而设计。它们强度高，并提供循序渐进的挑战。

Intense-Swimming Programs (Competitive) If you already compete, if you want to compete in the near future, or if you just want to know what your body is capable of, a more intense program is for you. These programs assume that swimming is your primary physical activity and that you are willing to commit to more training time each week. Whether you actually compete in meets is irrelevant. A competitive swimmer is one who finds joy and motivation in testing her speed and endurance, whether against the pace clock or against other swimmers. The workouts in these programs are designed for swimmers who want to swim fast now and faster next week. They are intense and they provide a progressive challenge.

以下是针对上述三个类别分别设计的为期三周的训练计划示例。每个计划都侧重于游泳的特定方面——例如，提高技术、增强耐力或提升速度。此外，还包括对训练内容的解释以及如何最有效地使用这些计划。通过阅读解释并参考示例，您可以根据自己的时间安排调整计划，或者制定自己的训练计划。

The following is a sample of three-week programs for each of the three above categories. Each program focuses on a specific aspect of swimming—i.e., improving technique, building endurance, or building speed. Also included are explanations of the workouts and how you can use the programs most effectively. By reading the explanations and following the examples, you will be able to adapt the programs to fit your schedule or to put together programs of your own.

初级和轻松游泳课程（泳道游泳或健身游泳）

Beginning- and Easy-Swimming Programs (Lap or Fitness Swimming)

 

改进技术

IMPROVING TECHNIQUE

 

这两个训练计划以逻辑严谨的方式呈现了第一级和第二级的全部练习内容，循序渐进地引入新的技能训练，并逐步增加距离和难度。如果您是这套训练体系的新手，或者您是游泳初学者，又或者您对任何技能训练或训练概念不清楚，我强烈建议您从这两个计划开始。每个计划的最后一天，您需要重复一次难度较低的练习，并立即进行一次T-20米游泳（记录您的成绩）。本章所有计划都允许您调整列标题，以便在您选择的星期几进行该计划的第一次训练。例如，L1•4 表示进行第一级（第七章）的第4次练习。

These two programs present the complete set of level 1 and level 2 practices in a logical progression, slowly introducing new skill drills and gradually increasing distance and complexity. If you are new to this system, if you are a beginning swimmer, or if any of the skill drills or training concepts are unclear, I strongly encourage you to start with these programs. The last day of each program calls for you to repeat an easier practice and to follow it immediately with another T-20 swim (recording your results). With all of the programs in this chapter, you can shift the column headings in order to do the first workout of the program on the day of the week you choose. Note that L1•4, for example, means to do practice 4 in level 1 (chapter 7).

如果您的体能水平高于平均水平，但仍需按逻辑顺序学习技能训练，可以考虑减少休息天数或在某些日子进行两次训练，以加快进度。无论哪种方式，我都建议您按照指示的顺序进行训练。如果您的时间安排只允许每周进行三次训练，那么可以将训练计划延长至四周，但仍需遵循指示的顺序。

If your fitness level is above average but you still need to learn the skill drills in a logical order, consider accelerating the progression by taking fewer days off or by doing two practices on some days. In either case, I recommend that you do the practices in the order indicated. If your schedule allows only enough time for three practices a week, then lengthen these programs to four weeks, but follow the order indicated.

 

增强耐力

BUILDING ENDURANCE

 

在您至少完成一遍一级和二级的所有练习，并熟悉训练内容和重点之后，就可以开始提升耐力了。这两个训练计划在逐步引入更具挑战性练习的同时，也为您提供了更大的灵活性。请注意，例如 L1•1-5 表示您可以从一级练习中选择 1 到 5 中的任意一项。

After you have worked through all of the level 1 and 2 practices at least once and are familiar with the drills and focus points, it’s time to start building your endurance. These two programs give you more flexibility while gradually introducing more challenging practices. Note that L1•1-5, for example, means to select any one of the practices, 1 through 5, from level 1.

 

经常游泳计划（竞技前）

Frequent-Swimming Programs (Precompetitive)

 

改进技术

IMPROVING TECHNIQUE

 

这些训练计划每周安排五次训练，其中包括更多3级和4级训练，这些训练需要更长的距离和更高的强度。训练间隙穿插一些强度较低的1级和2级基础技能训练。每个计划的前两个周六是较长的训练日，以轻松的1级训练作为热身，为强度更高的3级或4级训练做准备。和之前一样，每个计划的最后一个周六安排一次T-20游泳测试。

In these programs, there are five practices per week, including more level 3 and level 4 practices, which require more distance and intensity. These are interspersed with lower intensity, fundamental-skill practices from levels 1 and 2. The first two Saturdays of each program are longer training days, using an easy level 1 practice as a warm-up for a more intense level 3 or 4 practice. As before, the final Saturday of each program calls for a T-20 swim.

 

增强耐力

BUILDING ENDURANCE

 

这些训练计划每周安排五次训练，并在1至4级训练的基础上，每周增加一到两次5级训练。周六的训练时间依然较长，包括更长的乳酸阈值组和一些乳酸耐力组。许多5级训练包含T-30测试组，需要更详细的记录来追踪训练进度。请注意，第二个计划的最后一个周六要求进行T-30游泳测试，而不是T-20游泳测试。

These programs call for five practices per week, and they add one or two level 5 practices a week to the mix of levels 1 to 4 practices. Saturdays continue to be longer training days. There will be longer lactate-threshold sets and some lactate-endurance sets. Many level 5 practices include test sets beyond the T-swims, requiring more record keeping to track your progress. Note the final Saturday of the second program calls for a T-30 swim instead of a T-20 swim.

 

加速

BUILDING SPEED

 

这些训练计划将通过增加乳酸耐力训练来提升你的速度，并通过乳酸耐受力训练来最大限度地测试你的速度。请注意，每个高强度训练日（5级，第4至10次训练；6级，第4至10次训练）之后都会安排休息日，或者安排一个低强度或中等强度的1级、2级或3级训练日。

These programs will build your speed with more lactate-endurance work, and they will maximize and test your speed with lactate-tolerance work. Note that each of the high-stress practice days (level 5, practices 4 to 10, and level 6, practices 4 to 10) is followed by either a rest day or by a low- or moderate-intensity level 1, 2, or 3 day.

 

高强度游泳训练计划（竞技类）

Intense-Swimming Programs (Competitive)

 

改进技术

IMPROVING TECHNIQUE

 

这些训练计划每周包含六次训练，其中包括更多来自5级和6级的训练，这些训练需要更长的距离和更高的强度。训练中穿插着强度较低的基础技能练习和1至4级的体能训练。如果您的时间安排不允许每周进行六次训练，您可以将这些计划分散到四周，每周五次训练，但保持训练顺序不变。这些计划中的所有T泳均为T-30米。

In these programs, there are six practices per week, including more practices from levels 5 and 6, which require more distance and intensity. These are interspersed with lower-intensity, fundamental skill drills and conditioning workouts from levels 1 through 4. If your schedule does not permit six practices a week, then stretch these programs across four weeks of five practices, but keep the same order. All of the T-swims in these programs are T-30s.

 

增强耐力

BUILDING ENDURANCE

 

和之前一样，我们增加了一些乳酸阈值训练和乳酸耐力训练。由于每周只有一天休息时间，因此密切关注过度训练的迹象至关重要。如果您发现高强度训练之间无法充分恢复，建议您将这些训练计划延长至四周，每周增加一天休息时间。

As before, we add more lactate-threshold activities and some lactate-endurance work. With only one day off each week, it becomes important to watch for signs of overtraining. If you find that you are not recovering between one high-intensity workout and the next, you might want to stretch these programs over four weeks, adding another day of rest each week.

 

加速

BUILDING SPEED

 

这些训练计划包含更多乳酸耐力和乳酸耐受训练，因此难度较高，压力也较大。请勿连续使用这些计划超过 9 至 12 周，之后应休息几周，过渡到压力较小的训练计划。

More lactate-endurance and lactate-tolerance workouts make these programs challenging and stressful. Do not use these programs for more than 9 to 12 weeks at a time without returning to a stretch of less stressful programs for a few weeks.

 

第十五章
 
保持正轨
 

大多数人在开始健身计划后六个月内就会放弃。如果你的计划也是如此，你就不会购买这本书了。然而，我们都知道，光有良好的意愿是不够的。人们放弃健身计划的主要原因是感到厌倦和缺乏动力。当你开始一项新的计划时，最初的两三个月里，新的环境、新的人和新的体验会让你对这项活动充满热情。但是，随着锻炼内容日渐单调乏味，你就很难避免厌倦，也很难保持动力。本章将教你如何记录和解读你的训练进度，鼓励你寻找训练伙伴，探索不同的游泳场所，并解释如何以及为什么要记录训练日志。这些方法中的任何一种或全部都可能是你坚持健身计划的关键。

Most people who begin exercise programs stop exercising within six months. If that was your plan, you wouldn’t have purchased this book. Yet we all know that good intentions are not enough. The primary reasons that people drop out of exercise programs are boredom and lack of motivation. When you begin a new program, there is a period of two or three months in which the stimulation of new surroundings, new people, and new experiences keeps you excited about the activity. But as the workout routine gets to be the same old, same old, it becomes more difficult to avoid boredom and to stay motivated. This chapter shows you how to chart and interpret your training progress, encourages you to hook up with a training partner and find different places to swim, and explains how and why to keep a training diary. Any one or all of these may be the key to your continued participation in an exercise program.

记录你的进度

Charting Your Progress

 

如果你能持续获得关于自身努力的准确反馈，你会发现保持动力并不难。你得到的积极反馈越多，你就越期待下一次回到泳池游泳。

If you have a constant supply of accurate feedback about your efforts, you will find that staying motivated is easy. The more positive feedback you can get, the more excited you will be about going back to the pool for your next swim.

在整个训练计划和练习过程中，您将经常测试游泳的各个方面。我强烈建议您从一开始就记录测试结果，并以条理清晰、逻辑严谨的方式保存，而不是仅仅依靠记忆。您的努力将会在短期和长期内都得到回报。您每天或每周都会看到成绩的提升。如果您在某些方面没有看到进步，您就会意识到哪些技能或体能需要额外加强。随着时间的推移，您会发​​现训练强度逐渐增加，因为您的大部分游泳速度都将直接根据之前的测试结果而定。这种具体、个性化的反馈将大大提高您坚持训练计划并取得理想成绩的几率。

Throughout the programs and practices, you often will test various aspects of your swimming. Rather than trusting the results to memory, I strongly encourage you from day one to record your results and to keep these records in an organized and logical fashion. Your efforts will pay off, both in the short term and over the long haul. On a daily or weekly basis, you will see improvements in your results. When you don’t see improvements in particular areas, you will become aware of skills or conditioning that need extra attention. As months and seasons pass, you will see a progressive pattern of increased training intensity, because you will do much of your swimming at speeds that are derived directly from the results of your previous test swims. This type of specific, personalized feedback will greatly improve the odds that you stick with the workout program and that you get the results you are looking for.

本节末尾附有几张表格，用于记录测试组和游泳成绩。首次填写前请先复印几份，以便在后续记录时使用干净的表格。建议每张表格多复印几份，以便追踪不同的训练组数、距离和器材。使用活页夹（最好带有内置计算器）可以帮助您整理和追踪游泳进度。

At the end of this section, there are several charts for recording the results of test sets and swims. Make copies of these charts before filling them out the first time so that you will have clean charts for recording results over an extended time. You may want to make several copies of each chart so that you can keep track of different set variations, distances, and equipment. A looseleaf binder (preferably with a built-in calculator) will help you organize and track your swimming progress.

T型游泳测试性能图表

T-Swim-Test Performance Chart

 
这是你首次记录第三章游泳体能测试中T-20游泳成绩时会接触到的第一个图表。之后，你需要记录后续T-20游泳的成绩。当你进行T-30游泳时，请启用新的图表。使用辅助器材进行的T-游泳训练，你应该单独使用图表。你需要根据相应的T-游泳图表查找每100米的巡航配速。以下任何一项都表明你取得了进步：

1. 每百公里巡航速度更快

1. Faster cruise pace per 100

2. 保持巡航速度，但降低心率

2. Same cruise pace but lower IHR

3. 保持相同的巡航速度，但平均划桨次数降低

3. Same cruise pace but lower average stroke count

4. 保持相同的巡航速度，但降低主观疲劳感知（RPE）。

4. Same cruise pace but lower RPE

 
 

记录和跟踪你的进步可以提供强大的反馈机制，让你保持动力并继续留在泳池中。

Charting and tracking your progress provides a powerful feedback mechanism that can keep you motivated and in the pool.

 

当你从T-20秒训练过渡到T-30秒训练时，如果你的巡航速度稍有减慢，请不要惊慌。假设你在T-20秒训练中尽了全力，那么你的T-30秒训练时间越长，对实际巡航速度的估算就越准确。

As you switch from T-20s to T-30s, do not be alarmed if your cruise pace slows a bit. The longer your T-swims are, the more accurate the estimates of true cruise pace will be, assuming that you give the T-swims your best effort.

游泳高尔夫（SGolf）成绩表

Swimming Golf (SGolf) Performance Chart

 
在第三章中，您学习了游泳高尔夫。在练习过程中，您将有很多机会进行游泳高尔夫游泳练习。此外，如果您想检验自己的技术水平，可以随时尝试几次游泳高尔夫重复练习。虽然练习中的游泳高尔夫游泳距离限制为 50 米，但您可以将相同的方法应用于任何距离。以下任何一项都表明您的进步：

1. 降低SGolf分数

1. Lower SGolf score

2. SGolf 得分相同但 IHR 较低

2. Same SGolf score with lower IHR

3. 相同的SGolf成绩，但RPE更低

3. Same SGolf score with lower RPE

 

计算游泳高尔夫成绩的方法是：将划水次数加上完成一段距离所需的总秒数。你会注意到有一列是你的ASGolf（高级游泳高尔夫）成绩。这其实就是你的常规游泳高尔夫成绩加上你的心率。比较高级游泳高尔夫成绩可以更准确地反映你游泳效率的变化。如果你使用心率监测器，可以在练习说明中用ASGolf代替所有出现的SGolf。你应该为使用器械进行的游泳高尔夫练习单独记录成绩。

Compute your swimming golf score by adding the total number of strokes to the total number of seconds that are required to complete a distance. You’ll note that there is a column for your ASGolf (advanced SGolf) score. This is simply your regular SGolf score plus your IHR. Comparing advanced SGolf scores will give you a more accurate reading of the changes in your swimming efficiency. If you use an HRM, you can substitute ASGolf for SGolf anywhere it appears in the practice descriptions. You should keep separate charts for SGolf swims that you do with equipment.

乳酸耐力（LEnd）测试组表现图表

Lactate-Endurance (LEnd) Test-Set Performance Chart

 
当你开始进行5级和6级训练时，你需要开始使用这张图表。你需要保留四张这样的图表——每张对应5级和6级训练中出现的四个LEnd组。这些图表比较复杂，但它们能为你提供丰富的进度反馈。你需要计算并记录加权平均游泳时间（将最快、次快和最慢的游泳时间相加，然后除以三），以及计算出的时间范围（用最慢的游泳时间减去最快游泳时间）。以下任何一项都表明你的进步：

1. 游泳加权平均时间更快

1. Swimming a faster weighted average time

2. 保持相同的加权平均时间，但缩小范围

2. Maintaining the same weighted average time but with a smaller range

3. 在不牺牲速度的前提下，降低平均击球次数

3. Having a lower average stroke count without sacrificing speed

4. 加快游泳速度

4. Swimming a faster interval

5. 达到新的最高心率 (HHR)，这意味着你比以往任何时候都更加努力。

5. Achieving a new highest heart rate (HHR), which means that you have pushed yourself harder than ever before

 

随着游泳水平的提高，你可以加快 LEnd 训练组的间歇训练速度。LEnd 训练组的目标是保持 1:1 的训练与休息比，无论你游多远。假设你一直以 2 分 30 秒的间歇时间游 100 米。随着时间的推移，你的加权平均时间从 1 分 15 秒缩短到了 1 分 13 秒。到目前为止，你的训练间歇时间是正确的。假设在接下来的几次训练中，你的平均时间达到了 1 分 12 秒或 1 分 11 秒。假设你所有的训练组成绩都在规定的范围内，那么现在可能是时候将间歇时间缩短到 2 分 25 秒了，因为这样更接近 1:1 的训练与休息比。你应该为使用器械进行的 LEnd 训练组单独记录训练计划。

As your swimming improves, you can move to faster intervals for LEnd sets. The goal for LEnd sets is to maintain a 1:1 work-to-rest ratio for whatever distance you swim. Let’s say you have been swimming 100s on a 2:30 interval. Over time, you have lowered your weighted average time from 1:15s to 1:13s. Until now, you have been swimming on the correct interval. Let’s say that on your next couple of performances, you average 1:12s or 1:11s. Assuming that you are swimming all of your sets within the specified range, it is probably time to drop your interval to 2:25, since this would now be closer to a 1:1 work-to-rest ratio. You should keep separate charts for LEnd sets that you do with equipment.

乳酸耐受性 (LTol) 测试组性能图

Lactate-Tolerance (LTol) Test-Set Performance Chart

 
强度最高的测试组出现在第 5 级和第 6 级训练中。你需要记录三个 LTol 测试组的成绩。与 LEnd 测试组一样，你需要记录平均游泳时间和成绩范围。使用器械进行的 LTol 测试组应单独记录成绩。共有四个进度反馈点：

1. 更快的加权平均游泳时间

1. Faster weighted average swim time

2. 相同的加权平均游泳时间，但范围更小

2. Same weighted average swim time but a smaller range

3. 在不牺牲速度的前提下，降低平均划水次数

3. Lower average stroke count without sacrificing speed

4. 达到新的最高心率 (HHR)，这意味着你已经比以往任何时候都更加努力了。

4. Achieving a new highest heart rate (HHR), which means that you have pushed yourself harder than ever before

 

寻找训练伙伴（或多个）

Finding a Training Partner (or Several)

 

无论你是学习游泳、健身游泳还是备战比赛，与他人一起训练都能极大地提升你的游泳体验。我鼓励你至少找到一位训练伙伴，你们可以一起游泳、交流心得、互相反馈、彼此激励。与伙伴一起训练有以下几个好处：

Whether you are learning to swim, swimming for fitness, or training for competition, your experience can be greatly improved by training with others. I encourage you to find at least one training partner with whom you can swim, compare notes, trade feedback, and cross-motivate. Training with a partner has several benefits:

 

学习：如果你给你的伙伴买一本这本书，你们就都有了同一份训练参考手册。观察和分析他人的动作，能让你从不同的角度思考自己的训练。缩短学习曲线的最佳方法之一，就是尝试教授你已经掌握得比较好的东西。这既能巩固你已有的理解，也能发现你理解上的不足。

Learning If you buy your partner a copy of this book, you’ll each have the same reference manual to base your workouts on. Observing and analyzing the movements of others allows you to think about your own efforts in a different light. One of the best ways to shorten learning curves is to try to teach something you have a fair grasp on. This will reinforce the ideas you understand and will reveal any remaining gaps in your understanding.

 

动力：伙伴之间互相鼓励，督促你坚持锻炼，这在你原本可能放弃游泳的日子里尤为重要。如果你和伙伴互相激励，这个训练计划高阶阶段的高强度训练组会更加有效。

Motivation The get-to-the-workout nudges that partners give each other can help on the days when you otherwise might skip the trip to the pool. The high-intensity sets in the upper levels of this program will be more productive if you and a partner push each other.

 

与志同道合的人一起游泳，能让锻炼事半功倍。即使你和你的伙伴只能偶尔一起游泳，这种伙伴关系也能提升你们各自的训练效果。如果能召集几个训练伙伴组成一个非正式的训练小组，效果会更好，尤其是在大家都遵循同一训练计划的情况下。

Camaraderie Swimming with like-minded people helps a workout go more quickly. Even if you and your partner can swim together only occasionally, the partnership can still enhance the overall effort for each of you. Gathering several training partners into an informal training group can be even more effective, particularly if you all follow the same program.

记录训练日志

Keeping a Training Diary

 

我鼓励你开始并坚持写一份专门的游泳训练日记或日志。我说的不是那种用来记录训练距离和偶尔个人记录的袖珍本子，而是一个正规的笔记本。每次训练结束后，用完整的句子写下你练习的游泳技巧、学到的东西、遇到的问题、这些问题的答案等等。安排至少10分钟的时间，带着笔记本和笔，用完整的句子持续记录你的训练体验。然后，每次训练前，至少重读最近两次训练的记录。无论你是铁人三项运动员、竞技游泳运动员还是健身游泳爱好者，这样做都能缩短学习或改进的周期，让你在水中的时间更加高效，并提高你的训练动力。写训练日记可以帮助你做到以下几点：

I encourage you to start and keep a dedicated swim-training diary or journal. I don’t mean a pocket-sized affair where you write down your workout distances and the occasional personal record. I mean a proper notebook where, after every practice session, you write in complete sentences about aquatic skills you worked on, what you learned, questions that arose, answers to those questions, etc. Plan to sit with a notebook and pen for at least 10 minutes, writing continuously in complete sentences about the practice experience. Then, before each practice, reread the entries from at least the last two practices. Whether you are a triathlete, a competitive swimmer, or a fitness swimmer, this will shorten the learning or refining cycle. It will make the time you spend in the water more productive, and it will increase your motivation level. Keeping a training diary helps you do the following:

 

提升你的锻炼意识。过去那些你几乎意识不到的事情，如果你的目标是收集有用的信息，就会变得格外清晰。如果你在锻炼时计划记录你的体验，你的注意力会更加集中——这正是你在学校被要求记笔记的原因之一。

Supercharge your workout awareness Things that were barely on the periphery of your consciousness in the past will come sharply into focus if your goal is to gather useful information. If, while you are practicing, your plan is to write about your experience, your attention will remain more focused —that’s half the reason you were told to take notes in school.

 

巩固你已经掌握的概念和应用。当你以一种能够与他人交流的方式组织思路时，抽象概念就会变得具体。强迫自己使用完整的句子和结构良好的段落，会迫使你将思维和认知中零散的信息联系起来。

Reinforce the concepts and applications you have a good handle on Abstract concepts become concrete when you organize your thoughts in a way that allows you to communicate them to others. Making yourself use complete sentences and well-constructed paragraphs will force you to connect loose ends in your thinking and awareness.

 

发现知识盲点：当你尝试用完整的句子表达你自认为理解的内容时，更容易发现通往水上运动巅峰之路上的障碍。那些你并不真正理解的概念，在你试图用语言表达想法的过程中，往往会变成问题。把这些问题写下来，然后寻找答案——或许可以通过更多练习、观察他人、阅读、观看视频，或者向教练请教。如果答案是你自己提出的问题，那么你的学习速度会更快。

Expose gaps in your knowledge When you try to use complete sentences to express something that you think you understand, it is easier to spot the potholes in your road to aquatic nirvana. Concepts that you don’t truly understand will tend to become questions as you try to verbalize your thoughts. Write the questions down and then find the answers—perhaps by practicing more, observing others, reading, watching videos, or cornering a coach. You learn faster if the answers are responses to questions you have formulated on your own.

 

调整好心态，然后下水。在下水前，重新回顾一下你之前认真思考过的内容。从划水的第一下开始，你就能更好地做好准备，更加专注于你的训练。

Get your mind right, and then get wet Before hitting the water, reread what you’ve already given great thought to. From the very first stroke, you’ll be better prepared for and more focused on your workout.

 

充分利用时间。当你在训练、比赛或与教练或其他游泳运动员的交流中学到宝贵的经验时，一定要把它写下来。然后定期阅读和重读你的日记。与其在泳池里重复过去的错误来重新学习同样的教训，不如利用日记来帮助你回忆起来之不易的经验。只需投入少量时间，就能避免你一次又一次地经历学习的过山车。

Leverage your time When you learn something valuable during a workout, a competition, or a conversation with a coach or another swimmer, write it down. Then read and reread your diary regularly. It is easier to use your diary to help you recall a hard-learned lesson than it is to relearn that same lesson by repeating your past mistakes in the pool. A small investment of time can save you from riding the learning rollercoaster again and again.

如果你能正确地坚持写日记，所花费的时间和精力将会得到丰厚的回报。以下是一些帮助你充分利用日记的提示：

• 准备一个中等大小的笔记本。如果它有口袋，你可以存放与你写作主题相关的文章。再准备几支不同颜色的防水笔——或许还可以准备一支荧光笔。

• Get a medium-sized notebook. If it has pockets, you can store articles that relate to what you are writing about. Include several different-colored pens with waterproof ink—and perhaps a highlighter pen.

• 将所有这些物品存放在一个结实耐用的带拉链的厨房保鲜袋或类似的防水容器中。我知道你不想让它沾水，但这种情况难免发生。妥善保管的日记本将成为一份无可替代的珍贵资料。在潮湿的环境中，一个塑料袋就是一种廉价的保障。

• Store all this in a heavy-duty, zippered kitchen storage bag or similar waterproof container. I know that you don’t plan on getting it wet, but it happens. Properly kept, your diary will be an irreplaceable asset. A plastic bag is cheap insurance in an inherently wet environment.

• 请完整地表达你的想法，并提出足够的问题（以及留白供你作答）。写作时要让不太了解游泳的人也能读懂你的内容，明白你的意思。

• Express your thoughts completely and include plenty of questions (and blank spaces for answers). Write in such a way that someone who is less knowledgeable about swimming would be able to read your work and get an idea of what you are doing.

• 尝试从不同的视角写作（今天用第一人称，明天用第三人称）。这样可以让你以其他方式无法实现的方式审视自己的游泳水平。

• Write from a variety of perspectives (one day writing in the first person, another day in the third person). This allows you to examine your swimming in ways that are not possible otherwise.

• 使用电子方式记录日记有一些优势（备份、文本搜索、与他人交流）。一位精通技术的游泳运动员可能会在电脑上写日记，然后同步到掌上电脑，这样她就可以在更衣室或泳池边下水前重读日记。

• Keeping your diary electronically offers some advantages (backup, text search, communicating with others). A tech-savvy swimmer might make diary entries on her computer and sync them to a PDA so that she can reread them in the locker room or at the pool’s edge just before hopping in.

• 考虑让其他游泳运动员或教练阅读你的文章并提出意见——比如写博客？

• Consider having another swimmer or coach read your entries and make comments—blogging, perhaps?

• 制定计划，确保你有足够的时间在下水前重读之前的记录，并在练习后尽快写下你的想法。

• Plan your schedule to ensure that you have enough time to reread prior entries before you hit the water and to write down your thoughts as soon after your practice as possible.

• 在练习时，在泳池尽头准备一个防水笔记本，以便随时记下笔记和偶尔的“啊哈！”，以便日后详细阐述。

• Have a waterproof notebook handy at the end of the pool during your practices so that you can jot down notes and the occasional “Aha!” that you can elaborate on later.

• 不要弄错方法。（提示：除了不记游泳日记之外，没有其他错误的记录方式。）

• Don’t do it wrong. (Hint: There is no wrong way to keep a swimming diary, other than not keeping one at all.)

重点内容

Focus Points

 

浮力压力——将肺部向泳池底部压紧。（第34页）

buoy pressure—Press your lungs toward the bottom of the pool. (page 34)

核心旋转节奏——用核心旋转来控制游泳节奏，而不是用手臂。（第154页）

core-rotation tempo—Set swimming tempo with core rotation instead of with your arms. (page 154)

顺坡游泳——利用浮力使臀部和腿部保持在水面，这样你会感觉整个身体略微向下倾斜。（第86页）

downhill swimming—Using buoy pressure to keep your hips and legs at the surface, which will make you feel like your whole body is tilted slightly downhill. (page 86)

向下倾斜手臂伸展——将引导臂以略低于水平面的角度伸展。（第40、61页）

downward angle arm extension—Extending the lead arm at a slightly-below-horizontal angle. (page 40, 61)

轻松的速度——速度要快，但要让人感觉和看起来轻松自如，而不是慌乱无章。（第166页）

easy speed—Going fast, but making it feel and look easy rather than frantic. (page 166)

完成你的划水动作——偶尔用拇指轻拂大腿，以确定手臂划水动作的结束位置。（第61页）

finish your strokes—Occasionally brush your thumb against your thigh to determine where your arm stroke finishes. (page 61)

前弓步——重点不要放在向后拉动一只手臂上，而是感受身体另一侧由于核心旋转而向前迈出的步伐。（第139页）

forward lunge—Focus not on pulling one arm backward, but on feeling the other side of your body lunging forward as a result of core rotation. (page 139)

手套动作——在击球时，想象一只假想的手套在身体前方从一只手传递到另一只手。（第56页）

glove—Transferring an imaginary glove from hand to hand out in front of your body as you take strokes. (page 56)

手与髋的连接——通过紧绷的体态，感知并运用手与髋之间的内部肌肉连接，从而为划水和入水提供动力。（第119页）

hand and hip connection—Awareness and use of the internal muscular connection of the hand to the hip via the tension of your tight-line posture to power both the stroke and the entry. (page 119)

换手——保持伸出的手臂在身体前方，直到另一只接替的手准备好接替它的位置。（第86页）

hand swapping—Keeping the extended arm in front of your body until the recovering, or entering, hand is ready to take its place. (page 86)

皮划艇划桨——肌肉张力将一只手从背部连接到另一只手，并将入水臂的动作直接传递到划水臂，很像使用皮划艇桨。（第139页）

kayak paddling—Muscular tension that connects one hand across your back to the other hand and that transmits the action of the entering arm directly to the stroking arm, much like using a kayak paddle. (page 139)

臀部发力踢腿——每次踢腿都应该主要依靠臀部发力，而不是膝盖。（第103页）

kick from hips—Each kick should come predominantly from your hips, not from your knees. (page 103)

激光束旋转触发——恢复的手穿过一道假想的激光束，这道激光束横跨你的泳道，位于你头部前方边缘，距离水面几英寸。穿过这道假想的激光束会触发下一次核心旋转。（第62页）

laser-beam rotation trigger—The recovering hand cuts through an imaginary laser beam that stretches across your lane at the front edge of your head, a few inches above the water’s surface. Passing the imaginary laser beam triggers the next core rotation. (page 62)

木偶式恢复——高肘、低手、向前运动（非迂回式）的恢复动作。（第62页）

marionette recovery—High elbow, low hand, forward-motion (not circuitous) recovery. (page 62)

中立肩——始终保持恢复侧肘部位于身体额状面的前方。（第62页）

neutral shoulder—Keeping the recovering elbow in front of the frontal body plane at all times. (page 62)

越过酒桶——在划水开始时，尽可能地向前伸出手臂越过一个假想的酒桶，以便接住水。（第61页）

over-the-keg—Reaching over an imaginary keg as far out in front of the body as possible in order to make the catch at the beginning of your stroke. (page 61)

臀部和臀瓣——始终保持一侧或两侧髋部或一侧或两侧臀部的一块皮肤暴露在空气中，尤其是在呼吸时。（第56页）

patches and cheeks—Keeping a patch of skin from one or both hips or from one or both butt cheeks exposed to the air at all times, especially when breathing. (page 56)

向下刺入（而非向下推）至完全伸展——穿刺的手臂应直接向下刺入至完全伸展的位置，而不是向前刺入后再向下推。（第56页）

pierce (not push) down to extension—Entering arm pierces straight down to a fully extended position, as opposed to piercing forward then pushing down. (page 56)

红点法——在水下时，始终在头顶中央想象一个红点，并使其指向池壁尽头。（第44页）

red dot—Keeping an imaginary red dot in the center of the top of your head underwater and pointed at the end wall at all times. (page 44)

危险呼吸法——呼吸时头部尽可能深地吸气——头部和躯干都不要抬起。（第43页）

risky breathing—Keeping your head as deep as possible as you breathe—zero head-lift, zero torso-lift. (page 43)

换脚滑行——模仿滑冰运动员用一只冰鞋蹬地加速，然后将重心转移到另一只冰鞋上滑行，并保持这个姿势直到下一次加速换脚。（第139页）

shift and skate—Emulate a skater’s surge of speed as he pushes off with one skate and shifts his weight into a glide on the other skate, which he holds until the next propulsive shift. (page 139)

侧滑——侧身滑行，手臂略微向下伸展，同时另一只手臂向前移动，越过头部，到达激光束旋转触发点。（第86页）

side skating—Gliding on your side with your arm extended at a slightly downward angle while the recovering arm moves forward, past your head, to the laser-beam rotation-trigger point. (page 86)

滑板式入场——将高肘恢复动作的势能转化为旋转和向前运动的动能。（第63页）

sliding-board entry—Recapturing the potential energy of the high-elbow recovery to the kinetic energy of rotation and forward motion. (page 63)

灵活的髋部动作——利用腿部力量带动髋部快速旋转。（第61页）

snappy hips—Using your legs to drive the snappy rotations of your hips. (page 61)

潜行——游泳时尽可能少地发出声音，尽可能少地扰动水面。（第120页）

stealth—Making as little noise as possible and disturbing the water as little as possible as you swim. (page 120)

划水次数——计算每次游完一个来回的划水次数。每次手入水都要计数，包括游到泳池尽头时最后一次入水。（第87页）

stroke count—Count the strokes you take during each length. Count each hand as it enters the water, including the final hand entry at the end of the pool. (page 87)

挺拔的姿势——高挑、紧绷、笔直的姿势与佝偻的姿势形成对比。（第31页）

tight line—Tall, tight, and straight posture vs. schlumpy posture. (page 31)

两拍踢腿——每次旋转和击打只用一个踢腿节拍，而不是像六拍踢腿节奏那样每次击打用三个踢腿节拍。（第120页）

two-beat kick—Using one kick beat for each rotation and stroke instead of the three kicks per stroke that are used in six-beat kick timing. (page 120)

管子——游泳时，你的身体和腿会滑过一个假想的管道。（第102页）

tube—An imaginary tube that your body and legs slide through as you swim. (page 102)

手臂无重力——当你转头吸气时，前导臂应保持无重力伸展状态。（第120页）

weightless arm—As you turn your head and breathe in, the lead arm should remain weightlessly extended. (page 120)

宽幅追踪——每只手都从自身肩部正前方进入并伸展。笔画的大致间距也应与肩同宽。（第56页）

wide tracking—Each hand enters and extends directly in front of its own shoulder. The general lines of the strokes should be shoulder-width apart as well. (page 56)

关于作者
 
 

埃米特·海因斯是全美顶尖的成人游泳教练之一。他是仅有的13位持有美国游泳教练协会（ASCA）五级成人教练认证的教练之一，该认证是ASCA颁发的最高成人教练认证。2002年，他荣获成人水上教练协会终身成就奖。1993年，他还被评为美国年度最佳成人游泳教练。海因斯从14岁起就开始从事各种形式的教练工作。作为H 2 Ouston Swims游泳俱乐部的总监兼总教练，海因斯拥有超过25年的成人游泳教学经验，指导对象涵盖初学者到奥运选手。他曾担任Total Immersion游泳训练营的高级教练，该训练营是全球最知名、最受尊敬的成人游泳教学机构，他的训练足迹遍布全美乃至世界各地。

Emmett Hines is one of the top masters swimming coaches in the nation. He is one of only 13 coaches to hold the level 5 Masters certification, the American Swim Coaches Association’s (ASCA) highest adult coaching certification. In 2002 he received the Masters Aquatic Coaches Association Lifetime Achievement Award. He also was honored as the U.S. Masters Swimming Coach of the Year in 1993. Hines has been coaching in some form since the age of 14. The director and head coach of H2Ouston Swims, Hines has coached adult swimmers for more than 25 years—from beginners to those with Olympic pedigrees. He has conducted clinics across the country and internationally as a senior coach for Total Immersion Swim Camps, the world’s most widely known and respected organization for adult swimming instruction.

海因斯的文章曾刊登于《游泳》杂志，他每月为《跑步者铁人三项新闻》撰写专栏，并在游泳和铁人三项杂志及通讯上发表过200多篇文章。他曾在ASCA世界教练研讨会和太平洋教练研讨会上发表演讲，这两个研讨会是全球规模最大的专业游泳教练盛会之一。在他的指导下，游泳运动员赢得了无数团体和个人全国冠军头衔，并创造了多项国家和世界纪录。海因斯曾担任美国游泳大师协会（USMS） 《游泳》杂志的助理编辑、美国游泳大师协会（MACA）通讯的编辑以及海湾游泳大师委员会（GMSC）通讯的编辑。

Hines’ articles have been featured in Swim Magazine, he writes a monthly column for Runner Triathlete News,and he has published over 200 articles in swimming and triathlon magazines and newsletters. He has spoken at the ASCA World Coaches Clinic and Pacific Coaches Clinic, two of the largest professional swim coaches’ gatherings in the world. Swimmers under his guidance have won numerous team and individual national championship titles and set numerous national and world records. Hines has served as the assistant USMS editor for Swim Magazine,editor of the Masters Aquatic Coaches Association (MACA) newsletter, and editor of Gulf Masters Swim Committee (GMSC) newsletter.

在所有与游泳相关的活动中，海因斯都力求运用他的创造力和幽默感来拓展成人游泳的世界，同时提高游泳者和教练的知识和技能。

Throughout all of his swim-related activities, Hines seeks to use his creativity and humor to expand the world of adult swimming while improving the knowledge and skill of swimmers and instructors alike.

他的妻子佩吉也是一名游泳教练，他的两个儿子都热爱游泳。除了游泳，他们全家还积极参与竞技射箭运动。

His wife, Peggy, is a swim coach as well, and both of his boys are fish. Aside from swimming, the whole family is actively involved in competitive target archery.
